stories.title: UP teachers can now take Special TET:5 lakh teachers to benefit; know application process
stories.summary: Teachers from schools recognized and aided by the Basic Education Council will now also be able to take the Special Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). Teachers at both primary and upper primary levels have been deemed eligible for the exam. This means that every teacher can now take the TET. Following this government decision, approximately 5 lakh teachers will now be able to take the TET. Until now, the TET was being organized only for special educators in Basic Education Council schools. Following instructions from the Basic and Secondary Education Department, the UP Education Service Selection Commission has issued an for the Special TET. No need to retake the exam if already TET/CTET qualified According to Parth Sarthi Sen Sharma, Additional Chief Secretary of Basic and Secondary Education, teachers who have already passed the TET or CTET will not be required to pass the Special TET again. Meanwhile, teachers who have not yet passed the TET or CTET have been asked to apply for the special TET and appear for the examination. The government has instructed Basic Education Officers to inform the concerned teachers at their level so that eligible teachers can complete the application process within the stipulated timeline. Applications from 5th September, Exam on 3rd November The Education Service Selection Commission released the for the special TET on 3rd September. Online registration, OTR, and the application process began on 5th September. Candidates will be able to submit the application fee until 4th October. The last date for making any kind of corrections in the application has been set for 8th October. The Special TET exam will be held on 3rd November. This means that after completing the application process, candidates will have about a month to prepare for the exam. There will be no negative marking in the Special TET Now, teachers who have not passed the UP TET will also be able to save their jobs by passing this special exam. Anil Yadav, State President of the UP BTC Teachers' Association, said that this will provide great relief to teachers working since before 2011. The Special TET will be of 150 marks. Objective questions will be asked in it. The exam will be of two and a half hours. Each question will carry one mark, but there will be no negative marking. Now, know how to apply for TET... Mandatory to pass TET by 2028 In an order issued on September 1 last year, the Supreme Court made it mandatory for all working teachers to pass the TET by August 31, 2028. Following this, teacher organizations protested, demanding special relief. The government had announced that a separate special TET would be conducted for working teachers. Now, its action plan has been approved. How many marks are required to pass? General category teachers will have to secure at least 90 marks, i.e., 60% marks, in the examination. Meanwhile, SC, ST, OBC, freedom fighter dependents, ex-servicemen, and disabled candidates will be considered passed if they secure 82 marks, i.e., 55% marks. For general candidates from the Economically Weaker Section (EWS), 82 marks will also be required to pass. There will be two papers just like the general TET Like the general UP TET, there will be 2 papers in the Special TET as well. Paper-1: This will be for teachers teaching classes 1 to 5. It will include questions on Child Development and Pedagogy, Hindi as the first language, a choice of either English, Urdu, or Sanskrit as the second language, Mathematics, and Environmental Studies. There will be 30 marks worth of questions from each subject. Paper-2: This will be for teachers teaching classes 6 to 8. In this, one will have to choose from Child Development and Pedagogy, Hindi as the first language, and English, Urdu, or Sanskrit as the second language. Apart from this, one subject will have to be chosen from Mathematics-Science or Social Studies, or Social Science. There will be 30 marks each for the first three subjects and 60 marks for the last subject.

stories.title: CJP worker Nishu Azad receives rape threat in Ghaziabad:Abusive messages sent to her father; says ‘I’m scared to step out of home’
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) worker Neeshu Azad has received a rape threat. On Wednesday, Neeshu claimed on X that she is being threatened with rape and death via messages. Her father, Sanjay Azad, is also being abused. Neeshu shared a screenshot of the threatening message in her X post at 4:27 PM. She said, "Some people are calling my statement false. Just think for yourself, if these people can use such indecent and offensive language against me through phone messages, then what will happen to my safety if I come face-to-face with them? How much fear and anxiety will I have?" Earlier, in a video released on X at 7:00 PM on Tuesday, she stated that her freedom has been curtailed due to media personnel constantly staying around her house. See 2 pictures... Nishu said - Recording is being done by installing cameras Nishu Azad said, ''The media is reaching right outside my house. They are installing cameras at the main gate of the society and recording. Some people from the society are going to the gate and giving interviews to the media. When I myself do not want to give interviews to the media and am not feeling comfortable with it, why is the media repeatedly reaching around my house? When some people arrived in the society in my support, the society members were troubled, and questions were raised regarding this. If any untoward incident happens to me, the society members will be responsible for it.'' Demanded security for family Prior to this, Nishu had released a video on social media X on Saturday night at 10:48 PM. She had said - Some people are surrounding her house, and stones and bricks were pelted at the house. She had demanded security for her parents and family from the Delhi and Ghaziabad police. She had said - if something happens to my parents, who will be responsible for it? However, the society members had outrightly rejected Nishu's statements to Dainik Bhaskar. Meanwhile, during the Jantar Mantar protest, she had also alleged that her father, Sanjay Azad, was assaulted. In this case, the accused content creator, Swatantra Bhardwaj, was arrested on Saturday. Swatantra Bhardwaj-Nishu Azad Case - Sequence of events from past few days A podcast video of Swatantra Bhardwaj went viral. In it, he allegedly said that he had "cracked the skull" of Nishu's father and claimed that despite this, he did not go to jail. He also mentioned his political connections. After this video, the old case once again came into national discussion. September 4: CJP leaders and supporters protested outside the Parliament Street Police Station in support of Nishu Azad and her father. On behalf of Nishu, advocate Rishav Ranjan demanded that the police add relevant sections of attempted murder, criminal intimidation, and the SC/ST Act. The police added these sections. Swatantra was taken into custody. September 5: A Hindu organization held a protest in Delhi in support of Swatantra Bhardwaj. This protest was called by Daksh Chaudhary. Daksh is known for assaulting and slapping high-profile individuals. He had also slapped Kanhaiya Kumar.

stories.title: HC rebukes Deoria SP, calls officials a ‘bunch of liars’:Asks why cop wasn’t suspended over illegal detention, says ‘Apologise to them, not me’
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court reprimanded the Deoria SP severely on Wednesday. The matter pertains to the alleged detention of four people between 13 April and 24 April, 2026. The petitioners allege that the police kept them illegally at the police station for 10 days. In the previous hearing, the court had sought information regarding the CCTV cameras at the Gauri Bazar police station and the footage for the relevant period. On Wednesday, the SP and the SHO stated that the police station's CCTV camera was faulty and not working. Justice Atul Sreedharan was displeased with the police officer's explanation. The court asked, "Why has the SHO not been suspended despite such gross negligence? Do not apologize to the court, but to the people who were kept in detention." During the hearing, he made an oral remark, even calling the police officers a 'bunch of liars'. The four individuals had filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court regarding this matter. It was during the hearing of this petition that the court raised questions about the functioning of the police. First, understand the entire case- The case of four people being kept in detention for several days at the Gauri Bazar police station in Deoria has reached the Allahabad High Court. Mahendra Gaur and three others alleged that the police kept them at the police station without following legal procedures. The four filed a habeas corpus petition in the High Court. They state that they were kept at the police station for varying periods between 13 April and 24 April, 2026. Some individuals have alleged being held in detention for about 10 days. The case is being heard by a bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Divesh Chandra Samant. To investigate the allegations, the High Court had sought the CCTV footage from the police station. CCTV was faulty, but there was no entry in the police station diary On 2nd September, the state government informed the court that the police station's CCTV had become faulty even before the incident. Following this, the High Court ordered the Deoria SP and the Station House Officer (SHO) to appear in court. The hearing took place on Wednesday. The bench asked the SHO, "If the camera was working since 14 April, then where is the recording? You have been the SHO for two months. Where is the recording?" The SHO stated that the CCTV had become faulty on 12 April, 2026 itself. The court again asked whether the information about the camera being faulty was recorded in the police station's diary or not. The Station House Officer (SHO) stated that no entry was made. The SP informed the court that he was not notified about the CCTV being faulty. On this, the court asked what action had been taken against the SHO. The court said - Apologize to the people The SP apologized to the court. To this, Justice Atul Sreedharan said, "Do not apologize to the court. Apologize to the people." The bench asked what action was taken against the SHO. Was he suspended or removed from service? Justice Sreedharan said that an SHO who does not even know how to record an investigation in the general diary should not remain in service. Such a person is not even fit to be a constable. The SP informed that the SHO has been transferred to the Crime Branch. However, the court was not satisfied with this action. The court asked why strict action was not taken against the SHO if he was found guilty. ₹46.46 lakh received for CCTV The court also referred to its order dated 2nd September. In this, questions were raised on the working style of the police. The High Court also cited the Supreme Court's instructions regarding CCTV. The court stated that the state government had released ₹ 46.46 lakh for the installation of CCTV in the police stations of Deoria. However, the government affidavit did not mention when this amount was released. The court considered this date important. The court also questioned the date of the police action. The action reported by the SP was from 14 August, 2026, whereas the relevant High Court order had already been issued on 4 August. The court prima facie observed that it appears the district officials initiated action only after the petition was filed in the High Court and the order dated August 4 was passed. Work not completed, yet full payment made On Wednesday, the court also raised questions regarding the payment made to the agency responsible for installing CCTV cameras. The bench asked why the full amount was paid to the agency when the CCTV work had not been completed. The court stated that instead of blacklisting the agency, the entire amount was released. Payment was made solely on the basis of assurances. In the case of illegal detention, the court ordered compensation to be paid to all four petitioners. Petitioners 2, 3, and 4 will receive ₹20,000 each. Petitioner number 1 will be given ₹5,000. A total compensation of ₹65,000 will be given to the four. This amount will be recovered from the salary of the concerned Station House Officer (SHO).

stories.title: Rapido rider sends ‘I love you’ message to girl:Says, ‘Complain wherever you want’; company apologises to Noida woman
stories.summary: A Rapido rider in Noida sent personal messages to a woman after she booked a parcel delivery through the platform. He first asked, “Hello, how are you?” and soon followed it with, “I love you.” The woman warned him that she would approach the police if he called or messaged her again. The rider responded, “Yes, go ahead. You can complain to Rapido as well.” The woman, Geetika Srivastava, shared screenshots of the conversation on LinkedIn and tagged Rapido co-founder Aravind Sanka, seeking action against the rider. Following her post, the company apologised to her. Digital communication expert had booked parcel through Rapido Digital communication expert Geetika Srivastava, who lives in Noida, spoke to Dainik Bhaskar over the phone. She said: “On Sunday at around 10 am, I booked two Rapido orders, both for delivery to my home. About two hours after the second order was delivered, I checked my phone and saw an ‘I love you’ message from the rider who had delivered the second order. I told my husband about it and showed him the message. He then replied to the rider. I spent a long time looking for an option to file a complaint on the Rapido platform, but could not find one. After this, my husband shared the matter in a LinkedIn group. Rapido apologised to me after being reminded twice.” Geetika asked - Will any action be taken against the rider? Geetika expressed surprise that the rider remained fearless despite being warned about complaining to the police or the company. He even told her to go ahead and file a complaint. She questioned whether any action would be taken against the rider for such behavior. She also questioned Rapido's recruitment and monitoring process for delivery partners. She asked: What kind of people is the company hiring as riders? Rapido company apologized by commenting on the post After the matter came to light on social media, Rapido responded to Geetika's post. Rapido apologized. The company stated that it understands the girl's concern regarding the delivery executive's behavior. Such matters are taken seriously. In its response, Rapido said that the safety, respect, and dignity of customers are its top priorities. Users said - Rapido's attitude is very poor

stories.title: Mayawati sets condition for Akash Anand’s return:Says Ashok put son-in-law’s political career at stake, must now retire from politics
stories.summary: Mayawati has set a new condition for Akash Anand's return to the BSP. She has accused former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth of working for personal gain and advised him to retire from politics. Akash Anand's return to the BSP can only happen once this condition is met. Akash Anand is the son-in-law of Ashok Siddharth. Mayawati had removed her nephew Akash Anand from his post on 3rd September, 2026. He is currently associated with the party as an ordinary supporter. Mayawati had stated that Akash Anand still needs to become more politically mature. Know what new signals Mayawati has given On 9th September, the BSP office issued a letter. In it, Mayawati stated that the elections in UP, Uttarakhand, and Punjab are important for the BSP. The party is dedicated with heart, mind, and resources to fulfilling Dr. Ambedkar's dream of transforming the 'oppressed into the ruling class'. Referring to the challenges being raised regarding the Bahujan movement and reservation, she appealed to the Dalit community not to do anything for personal gain that might harm the mission. She further added that misguided people in the party are being given a chance to improve, but disciplinary action is also being taken against those who become obstacles. In this context, the example of former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth was cited. Mayawati clarified that Ashok Siddharth prioritized his personal and family ambitions over the party's mission. The direct consequence of this has been borne by his son-in-law, Akash Anand. The BSP chief has said that Ashok Siddharth still has a chance to retire completely from politics. Only then will Akash Anand be able to work independently, and only then will the party sympathetically consider giving him back his old responsibilities. Got Akash Anand unfollowed on social media According to party sources, Mayawati first called Mewalal Gautam last Sunday and asked him to contact the party’s district presidents and office-bearers over the phone. She instructed them to unfollow Akash Anand and Ashok Siddharth on social media. Mewalal, who is in charge of the party office in Lucknow, is considered Mayawati’s eyes and ears. The move came amid growing social media activity surrounding Akash. Sources said Delhi-based YouTuber Samarraj had shared two posts about Akash Anand, one of which was retweeted by Ashok Siddharth. Satish Chandra Mishra reportedly informed Mayawati about this. Following this, Mayawati instructed Mewalal Gautam to ensure that both leaders unfollowed such posts. Will Akash's younger brother Ishaan now take his place in the BSP? The beginning of the changes in the BSP started to become visible from the national executive meeting on 3rd September. Mayawati had called for a national executive meeting. For the first time, her younger nephew and Anand Kumar's younger son, Ishaan (Ishu) Anand, also attended it. The significant point was that Akash Anand was not invited to this meeting. Following this, Akash himself gave an indication of being removed from the post of National Coordinator by changing his social media bio. This entire sequence of events in the BSP is not being considered just an organizational reshuffle. At its core is also the next generation of leadership for the party after Mayawati. On one hand, Akash Anand has long been the face of the party's youth politics. On the other hand, assigning Ishaan Anand the responsibility of overseeing the organization at the national level now indicates that Mayawati has increased Ishaan's role in the party's organizational structure. However, it would be premature to say that Ishan has been formally established as a replacement for Akash. But the changes in the responsibilities of those associated with Akash and the new role given to Ishan have certainly intensified discussions within BSP's internal politics. Akash Anand had raised questions on the party's internal structure in Jewar On 25th August, in Jewar, Noida, Akash Anand had said that he had put his career at stake the very day he announced that he would bring reforms and listen to everyone. He had said, "Some of our office bearers do not let us work. The wrong people are sitting in the wrong places. There are many strategies and technologies that we want to adopt, but we are unable to do so because of the way the structure is built. The people sitting there do not want to let anything happen, whom we cannot touch or remove right now." Akash Anand had said that he considers him elder and respects him. He had spoken about trying to make some improvements without causing any disruption. This same structure brought a party with 31% of the vote down to 9.4% in 2024. This was an even bigger shock than the 13% vote share received in 2022.

stories.title: Millionaire father-in-law murdered while daughter-in-law dances:Planned Kanpur murder, left for party and guided killers over phone
stories.summary: The daughter-in-law of a millionaire businessman in Kanpur was allegedly dancing with her husband at a party while her father-in-law was being murdered by two domestic workers, according to the police investigation. According to the police, the accused daughter-in-law Shalu had planned the murder before leaving home and continued to guide the killers over the phone during the attack. She was later arrested and sent to jail. The party had been arranged by her husband, Subrat, at Cosmozin Lounge in the city. It was scheduled for 11.30 pm, but Subrat and Shalu reached the venue at around 10.30 pm. Videos from the party, obtained by Dainik Bhaskar, show around 20-25 people, mostly couples, dancing to Bollywood songs. Shalu is seen wearing a dark purple gown, while her husband is wearing a grey shirt. In one video, the couple can be seen dancing to the song Tum To Dhokhebaaz Ho, Vaada Karke Bhool Jaate Ho. Her behaviour at the party appeared normal, and those present did not suspect that she had allegedly been involved in planning the murder. See the pictures Businessman found murdered in bedroom Vinod was murdered inside his flat at Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur at around 11.28 pm on Saturday, according to police. The family returned home at around 3 am on Sunday and found his body in the bedroom. CCTV footage reportedly showed two domestic workers, Vishal and Rajkishore, at the scene. Police later arrested the two following an encounter. During questioning, police said the men confessed to carrying out the murder at Shalu’s direction. Police arrested Shalu on Monday and sent her to jail.

stories.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Wednesday reprimanded a Noida Executive Magistrate for issuing a notice to a student who participated in a CJP (Cockroach Janta Party) protest, despite the Supreme Court having directed that no coercive action be taken against students over such demonstrations. The CJI said the Supreme Court had already quashed FIRs related to student protests and directed that no coercive action be taken against students in connection with such demonstrations in the future. “How dare an Executive Magistrate issue a notice to a student when the Supreme Court has passed such an order?” the CJI asked. He also made it clear that no Magistrate could violate the Supreme Court's directions. Magistrate issued notice seeking ₹5 lakh bond On 4th September, the Third Executive Magistrate's Court of the Noida Commissionerate issued a notice to student Akshat Tripathi, who had participated in a CJP protest. The notice asked him to furnish a personal bond of ₹5 lakh and produce two sureties for the same amount. The student later posted a video on Tuesday, alleging that he was being threatened for participating in the protest despite the Supreme Court's order. He also sought a fair investigation into the matter. During Wednesday's hearing in the Supreme Court, senior advocate Vishwajeet Bhattacharya verbally brought the matter to the attention of the bench headed by the CJI. He said the Executive Magistrate had issued a notice asking why the student should not be required to furnish a personal bond of ₹5 lakh to maintain peace. The notice was later withdrawn. Bhattacharya said the action was prima facie contempt of court and argued that officials in Noida and Uttar Pradesh could not create an atmosphere of fear among students. Student was booked under BNSS Section 130 Akshat Tripathi is a resident of Jhunsi in Prayagraj and is pursuing a BA-LLB at Gautam Buddha University (GBU). On September 4, 2026, the office of the Third Executive Magistrate of the Noida Commissionerate issued a notice to him under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The notice said there were sufficient grounds to believe that Tripathi was encouraging university students to participate in the proposed CJP protest. It also alleged that he was spreading anti-government and misleading information among students. According to the notice, such activities could create tension and affect public order. Tripathi was asked why he should not be bound to maintain peace for six months. He was directed to furnish a personal bond of ₹5 lakh along with two sureties of the same amount. The hearing in the matter was scheduled for September 5. SC says it will seek response from district magistrate Advocate Bhattacharya told the Supreme Court, “An experiment is being conducted with the students of India. Its impact will be felt across the country. First, contempt was committed and then withdrawn. Such contempt cannot be remedied in this manner.” He said the action amounted to contempt of the dignity of the court. “Officials in Noida and UP cannot create an atmosphere of fear among students,” he said. CJI Surya Kant assured him, saying, “We will seek a response from the district magistrate on this.” Notice issued on 4 September, cancelled the next day Akshat Tripathi, a resident of Jhunsi in Prayagraj, is pursuing a BA-LLB at Gautam Buddha University (GBU). He is also a member of the Uttar Pradesh state committee of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI). On 4 September, 2026, the office of the Third Executive Magistrate of the Noida Commissionerate issued a notice to him under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The notice said there were sufficient grounds to believe that Tripathi was encouraging university students to participate in the proposed CJP protest. It alleged that he was spreading anti-government and misleading information among students, which could create tension and affect public order. Tripathi was asked why he should not be bound over to maintain peace for six months. He was asked to furnish a personal bond of ₹5 lakh, along with two sureties for the same amount. The matter was scheduled for hearing on September 5. ACP Ravi Shankar said: “Akshat Tripathi’s name surfaced during the investigation. It was found that he had gone to participate in a protest at Jantar Mantar. The police sent the notice to the student through WhatsApp. The notice was cancelled on September 5 after the investigation found that the student was not present there at the time.” The ACP also said that in November, Tripathi had made a video claiming that he would commit suicide, which later went viral. He subsequently went missing, following which the police searched for him. Student asks in video: ‘Is speaking against government policies a crime?’ Tripathi posted a video on social media on Tuesday, claiming that he was being threatened despite the Supreme Court’s order in connection with the CJP protest. He questioned whether peacefully protesting against government policies or issues such as paper leaks amounted to a crime in a democracy. He said he had received the notice from the Greater Noida magistrate, which required him to furnish a personal bond of ₹5 lakh. “I am a student and have no personal income. How is such a large financial condition practical for me?” he asked. The notice alleged that by participating in the 20th July protest against paper leaks at Jantar Mantar, he had instigated university students against the government. Tripathi questioned how criticising government policies, questioning the government or raising one’s voice against paper leaks could be considered instigation. He also sought the basis and evidence for the allegations against him. He said he had not attended the university for three months and had returned to his home in Allahabad about a month and a half before the July 20 protest. “If I was not even in the university, how could I have instigated its students?” he asked, condemning the action and demanding a fair investigation.

stories.title: 'Will call in force and put you in your place':Gorakhpur cop threatens protesting university students
stories.summary: A police officer at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University allegedly threatened protesting students, saying he would call in enough force to “put you in your place”. In a video that has surfaced, the officer can be heard shouting at the students while gesturing with his hand: “I’ll call in the force and put you in your place, I’m telling you. This is Gorakhpur Police. This is not a peaceful protest. The students are ready to grab collars. Is this how a protest is supposed to be conducted?” The students have been on hunger strike since September 5 over a series of demands. On Monday, Assistant Proctor Ved Prakash Rai reached the protest site to speak to them. Students allegedly misbehaved with him and pushed him during the interaction. Police then escorted the proctor out of the area. During the incident, Aviral Mishra, the officer in charge of the university police outpost, became angry and confronted the protesting students. Police say students became aggressive After the video surfaced, Gorakhpur Police said the students had become aggressive during the discussion and that officers had intervened to protect the assistant proctor. Police said the situation was brought under control and legal action was being taken after an investigation. See 3 pictures- Students have been protesting since August 25 Around 20 students have been staging a protest at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University since August 25. They began an indefinite hunger strike on September 5, demanding action on six issues. Their demands include: Protest turns tense during talks with professors As the protest intensified, Assistant Proctor Ved Prakash Rai and other professors reached the site around 2.30 pm on Tuesday to speak to the students. They held talks with student leaders Satish Prajapati and Ujjwal Singh and asked them to call off the protest, saying the university was considering their demands. The student leaders, however, said they would continue the protest until they received a written assurance from the administration. An argument then broke out between the students and the professors. Other students sitting with the leaders began raising slogans against the university, and the situation soon escalated. According to people present at the site, pushing and shoving followed shortly afterwards. Police and university security guards reached the spot and escorted the proctor out of the group of students. The police then managed to calm the students. The commotion continued for around an hour, after which the students returned to their protest outside the administrative building.

stories.title: Government doctors in UP may work until 70 after retirement:Health dept begins process on Deputy CM’s instructions
stories.summary: Government doctors in Uttar Pradesh will be able to continue providing services until the age of 70 through reappointment after retirement, under a new initiative by the state Health Department. Government doctors currently serve until the age of 65. Following directions from Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak, the Health Department has begun the process of issuing an order to allow eligible doctors to continue working through reappointment until they turn 70. The move is aimed at making better use of experienced doctors and strengthening healthcare services across the state. Experienced doctors to support hospitals and health centres Government hospitals, community health centres (CHCs) and primary health centres (PHCs) across Uttar Pradesh receive large numbers of patients every day. The continued availability of experienced doctors is expected to help patients access specialist medical advice and better treatment. The arrangement could also ease the pressure on hospitals and health centres facing shortages of experienced medical professionals. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak said the Provincial Medical and Health Services cadre is the Health Department’s key medical cadre. It includes medical officers and specialist doctors who play an important role in providing healthcare at government hospitals, CHCs and PHCs across the state. He said allowing eligible and experienced doctors to continue working until the age of 70 after retirement would ensure that patients benefit directly from their years of experience. Focus on specialist shortages and rural healthcare Pathak said the new arrangement would be particularly useful in departments facing a shortage of specialist doctors. Experienced doctors could also play an important role in strengthening healthcare services in rural areas, he said. The Deputy CM said the Additional Chief Secretary of the Health Department has been directed to move forward with the process of issuing an order on the reappointment of doctors after retirement until the age of 70. The government aims to make the best use of the expertise of experienced doctors and make public healthcare services across Uttar Pradesh more capable, accessible and effective.

stories.title: Schools flooded in Varanasi, disrupting classes:Children spend days in relief camps; parents demand online classes
stories.summary: The Ganga’s water level is now receding in Varanasi, while floodwater from the Varuna is also gradually going down. However, the impact of the floods is far from over. Homes and residents have been affected, but children’s education has also suffered. Several schools remain flooded, preventing students from attending classes. In some cases, children have been unable to go to school because they have had to help their families manage household responsibilities. Sukumari, a Class 6 student at MBS Public School, said she had not attended school for 15 days. Students Nuraafreen and Deepak also said classes had been disrupted because floodwater had entered their school. Meanwhile, Ankita Jaiswal, a student of Chitrakoot Inter College, is currently staying at a flood relief camp set up at the school. She said she had not attended classes for eight days because her school shoes were left at home. Parents said alternative arrangements should have been made if regular classes could not be held. They suggested that schools should have conducted online classes so that children could continue their studies during the floods. Schools shut, students unable to attend classes Sukumari, a Class 6 student at MBS Public School, said floodwater had entered the school and no alternative arrangement had been made for teaching. She said she had not attended school for around 15 days and her studies had also stopped. Nuraafreen, a Class 5 student at the same school, said the school was flooded and students were unable to attend classes. She said the situation had affected their studies. Deepak, another Class 5 student, said he had been unable to attend school since the floods began because the premises were still flooded. Ankita Jaiswal, a Class 4 student at Chitrakoot Inter College, is currently staying at the flood relief camp set up at the school. She said she had not been to school for eight days because her shoes had been left at home. Another student, Lado, said she usually attends school every day but could not go because her family had to move household belongings to safety. Mother says children will return when teachers can teach Sanno Devi, who is staying at a relief camp, said children were not going to school because of the flooding. She said children would return when teachers were able to conduct classes and suggested that schools should make alternative teaching arrangements. “If classes were conducted on mobile phones, children could continue studying that way,” she said. Children taught at night at relief camp Staff deployed at Chitrakoot Inter College said children staying at the relief camp are being taught at night. The school principal said four rooms had been converted into a relief camp, while classes were continuing in the remaining rooms. However, she said the number of students attending classes had fallen. Relief camps set up in 20 primary schools Basic District Education Officer Bhopalendra said relief camps have been set up in 20 primary schools. One teacher has also been deployed at each of these schools to teach children staying at the camps. Flooding along the Varuna has affected around 11 neighbourhoods, impacting 328 families and 1,388 people. Of these, 935 people from 219 families are currently staying in 13 relief camps.

stories.title: Crorepati father-in-law’s murder mastermind cries in custody:Weeps for hours remembering son in Kanpur, inmates console her
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the first night in jail for the daughter-in-law accused of murdering her millionaire medicine trader father-in-law was spent in extreme restlessness. Accustomed to the comforts of home, the daughter-in-law was placed in a barrack after arriving at the jail on Monday evening. For the first two hours or so, she remained quiet and did not speak to anyone. When the female inmates asked her the reason for coming to jail, she began to cry. She also refused to eat dinner. On Tuesday morning around 6:30 AM, she was woken up like the other inmates. In the morning, she had porridge and jaggery for breakfast. For lunch, she was served lentils, rice, chapatis, and vegetables. In the afternoon, female inmates tried to console her. When asked if she had children, she began crying upon remembering her five-year-old son. She did not speak for a long time, then sobbed and fell asleep after two–three hours. In the evening, after having tea and biscuits, she ate lentils, vegetables, and chapatis at night. Why did the police suspicion deepen towards the son as well? How was the accused daughter-in-law caught? Read on in detail… In Ratan Orbit, Indira Nagar, 63-year-old millionaire medicine trader Vineet Minocha was murdered by domestic help Vishal Gautam (30) alongside accomplice Raj Kishore (30) at 11:28 PM on Saturday night. Around 3 AM on Sunday morning, when the son, daughter-in-law, and grandson arrived at the flat, they found the blood-stained body. On Sunday evening at 7:30 PM, the police arrested both men after shooting them in the leg during the encounter. Vishal revealed, "We committed the murder at the behest of the trader's daughter-in-law." Following this, on Monday evening, the police arrested the accused daughter-in-law, Shalu, as well. Without being asked, the daughter-in-law said: 'I don't know why Vishal killed him?' Fresh disclosures are coming to light daily in the Vineet Minocha murder case at Ratan Orbit in Indira Nagar. The police had to toil hard to extract secrets from the accused daughter-in-law, Shalu. Right on the first day of the incident, police suspected the involvement of someone close to the family. On receiving news of the incident, Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal arrived at the scene and began questioning Shalu alongside three female officers. She broke down crying profusely and feigned falling unconscious. Weeping, she said, "Papa was very good; he took care of my every small and big need. How will I live without him now..." The Police Commissioner asked Shalu if she knew Shivam. To this, she replied that yes, Shivam also goes by the name Vishal. She added that he used to visit the house for minor chores. "I don't know why Vishal killed Papa..." This remark by Shalu left the Police Commissioner and the investigating officers bewildered, wondering how she already knew that Vishal was the one who committed the murder. Daughter-in-law called accused Vishal 14 times, son called 25 times before murder Seeing Shalu's facial expressions change during questioning, police suspicions grew stronger, though officers did not let their doubts show. Following this, police began scrutinising the call detail records of Shalu, her husband Subrat, Vishal, and others who fell under the purview of suspicion. After the post-mortem proceedings were concluded and Vineet Minocha's final rites performed, the accused Vishal and his accomplice Raj Kishore fell into police hands late on Saturday night. Both confessed that they had carried out the murder at Shalu's behest. Meanwhile, when Shalu's call detail records reached the police, the entire matter became even clearer. The call detail records revealed that on the day of the murder, Shalu spoke to Vishal on the phone 14 times between 12 noon and 9 PM, while her husband Subrat made 25 WhatsApp calls to him. When Police Confronted Shalu and Vishal, Truth Was Confessed On Monday morning around 7 AM, police took Shalu into custody. Family members were left stunned by the police action. Shalu's sister also arrived at the Kalyanpur police station alongside her, pleading to stay with Shalu, but the police turned a deaf ear. When police began interrogating Shalu in a closed room, she said weeping, "I have done nothing; you people are trying to frame me forcibly." When police placed the call detail records before her, she said that Vishal is a good electrician and also helped with household chores, which is why she used to call him over. Police asked why she had called Vishal on the day of the murder, to which Shalu stated that she had to attend a couple's kitty party, for which she had ordered a gajra (flower garland) through Vishal. She claimed that after receiving the gajra, she left for the party with her husband and son, adding, "I do not know why Vishal killed Papa (Vineet Minocha)." Following this, when police brought Shalu and Vishal face-to-face, her body language changed. In front of police officers, Vishal confessed that he had carried out the murder solely at Shalu's behest. Vishal revealed that Shalu had instructed him, "If the police catch you, say that you killed him on the instructions of Bhaiya (Subrat)." After this, Shalu fell completely silent, following which police remanded her to jail late on Monday evening. Jail Superintendent Rajesh Kumar Pandey stated that Shalu has been kept in the observation barrack just like ordinary inmates. On arriving at the jail, she remained restless for a few hours, but later settled down. No clean chit for trader's son; police suspicion deepens There are still several secrets in the medicine trader's murder mystery that remain undisclosed. The police investigation revealed why, despite being sacked four years ago on theft charges, murder accused Vishal remained in continuous contact with the son, Subrat, and daughter-in-law, Shalu. Why did he speak with Shalu and Subrat on a daily basis? Between 29 August and the night of the murder, 25 WhatsApp calls took place between the trader's son Subrat and accused Vishal, whereas 14 conversations took place between Vishal and Shalu. Not only that, Shalu and Vishal also spoke via WhatsApp call three times while the murder was being committed. The probe further revealed that a few days before the murder, Vishal, Shalu, and Subrat had gone shopping together. Furthermore, despite being aware of his wife Shalu's involvement in his father's murder, Subrat did not open his mouth and maintained silence. When the police first showed Vishal in the CCTV footage, Subrat even refused to identify him. The police have yet to find answers to all these questions. Police Working to Recover 49 Deleted Messages The plot to murder the medicine trader was woven through 49 deleted messages. These messages were deleted between 1st May and the day of the incident. What were these messages and of what nature? Neither the murder accused Vishal nor the daughter-in-law who gave the contract provided this information to the police. Police are engaged in recovering data from the seized mobile phones of the contract killer, Vishal Gautam, and the daughter-in-law, Shalu. Between 1st May and the day of the incident, 309 calls took place between Shalu and Vishal Gautam. Police Find No Footage at Cosmojin Lounge Daughter-in-law Shalu had claimed that on the night of the incident, she went to a party at Cosmojin Lounge in Tilak Nagar alongside her husband Subrat and their 5-year-old son. Following this, on Tuesday, the Kalyanpur police reached Cosmojin Lounge to ascertain the truth. The police investigation revealed that no DVR was found attached to the CCTV cameras installed at the lounge. Upon questioning, the lounge manager stated that live recording of the party is conducted. Police subsequently obtained the guest list for the couples' kitty party. According to police officials, a list containing over 30 individuals has been acquired. Who was the party organiser? Were Shalu and Subrat present at the party on the day of the incident or not? To verify all these facts, guests who attended the party will be summoned for questioning.

stories.summary: Residents say they fear UP Police raids; family members worry some youths could take an extreme step The investigation into the murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan has now reached Shahpur village in Sonipat, the native village of gangster Rahul alias Bholu Shahpuriya. Bholu had allegedly claimed responsibility for the murder through a social media post. Since then, Uttar Pradesh Police have been conducting repeated raids in the village. Amid the police action, around 20 young men have reportedly left their jobs and businesses and gone underground. The lanes, which remain busy during the day, turn deserted at night. Residents say police vehicles and people in plain clothes are frequently seen moving around the village at night. Some vehicles allegedly do not have number plates, leaving villagers unsure about who is carrying out the searches. The Dainik Bhaskar team visited Shahpur to understand the situation on the ground. Residents described an atmosphere of fear and said some families are worried that their children could take an extreme step because of the pressure. Read the ground report… ‘It is difficult to tell who is police and who is not’ Shahpur is around 5 km from the Sonipat district headquarters. Villager Sumer said fear had increased since Bholu’s alleged claim of responsibility for Ankit’s murder came to light. “Vehicles keep moving around the village at night. Some do not have number plates and people in plain clothes are seen inside them. We cannot tell whether they are police personnel or someone else,” he said. Another resident, Karm Singh, said police sometimes arrive at night and drones are also used for surveillance. “The people who come in plain clothes are difficult to identify. This has kept the villagers constantly worried,” he said. 20-25 youths work outside the village Villager Dilawar said around 20 to 25 young men from the village work in government and private jobs. Several have left the village because they fear repeated police raids. “There is a fear that someone could be wrongly implicated in a case. No one in the village has anything to do with Bholu, and his family has also cut ties with him. The village was peaceful, but now the actions of one person are affecting everyone,” he said. ‘If Bholu committed a crime, he should be punished’ More than 60-year-old resident Jaikishan Sharma said Bholu should be punished according to law if he committed the crime. “Police coming through the village lanes repeatedly is troubling people. Bholu’s younger brother Ritesh has also left home. He was his mother’s main support. Bholu did not even return when his father died,” he said. Sharma urged UP Police to conduct their investigation in uniform and question people in the presence of local residents. “The village will fully cooperate with the investigation,” he said. ‘People open their doors at every sound’ Sharma said the situation had changed so much that residents now step outside whenever they hear even a small sound in the lanes. “Women are afraid to stay alone at home and children are also scared. The village has a population of around 2,500, with nearly 1,580 registered voters. People are also worried about vehicles without number plates because they do not know who is coming and why,” he said. Resident Dharamveer said the situation was affecting children as well. “If the police need to question someone or take action, they should do it during the day and bring the local police with them. We are not opposing the investigation. The villagers will cooperate, but innocent people should not be made to feel afraid,” he said. ‘We feel imprisoned in our own village’ Ajit Singh said his nephew runs a shop in RK Colony and is also questioned while returning to the village from Murthal. He recalled an incident in which a husband and wife were stopped by police personnel outside the village while they were out in the evening and were told to return home. “Sometimes people in uniform are seen and sometimes those in plain clothes. This has created a fear that our children could also be picked up and linked to a case,” he said. The post claiming responsibility for the murder of Bholu Shahpuriya... Bholu has not returned home for four years Bholu’s mother, Rajpati, said he studied up to Class 12 and was good at his studies. Around four years ago, he left the village for work. During this period, his name surfaced in a dispute in Kumasapur and was later linked to a murder case. He has not returned to the village since then, she said. Rajpati said her four daughters are married and her younger son Ritesh is also no longer at home. Her husband, Suresh, worked in farming. Ritesh was involved in property dealing but had stopped working around 10 months ago to look after his father, she said. According to Rajpati, Suresh died on July 26. Police remained around the cremation site throughout the night, due to which Bholu did not return for his father’s last rites. She said the family has now completely cut ties with Bholu. Village Panchayat says it stands with Ankit’s family At a village panchayat meeting on Tuesday, residents expressed grief over Ankit Baliyan’s murder and offered condolences to his family. The villagers said the entire community was saddened by Ankit’s death and stood with his family. The panchayat also decided that residents would help the police in apprehending those responsible for Ankit’s murder. At the same time, villagers urged the police to limit their action to the accused and not harass innocent youths merely because of their relationship with the suspect or their connection with the village.

stories.title: Transitioned from transgender to woman for lover, endured pain:Says man she trusted was father of 2; extorted ₹10 lakh
stories.summary: “My lover told me, ‘Get the surgery done, and then we will get married.’ I trusted him. For the sake of love, I transitioned from a transgender person to a woman and underwent three surgeries. I spent around ₹3 lakh and endured months of pain. I believed we would marry after that, but he backed out once the surgeries were completed. Later, I discovered that he was already married and had two children. He had hidden this from me for one and a half years. He also extorted around ₹10 lakh from me. Today, I have neither his love nor a marriage, and I have also lost the money I gave him. I am not highly educated, so I kept going from one police station to another seeking help. Now that an FIR has been registered, I hope I will finally get justice.” These are the words of a 20-year-old transgender woman from Agra, who has filed a case against her lover. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, she said she was born in Agra’s Rambagh and underwent surgery to transition to a woman. Mother died when she was two She said her mother died when she was just two years old. Her family later opposed her decision to undergo gender-affirming surgery. Unable to get their support, she eventually severed ties with them. ‘I trusted his promise of marriage’ According to the woman, her lover assured her that they would marry after her surgeries. Trusting him, she underwent three procedures and spent around ₹3 lakh. She said she endured significant pain for months, believing the surgeries would lead to their marriage. ‘He was already married with two children’ She later discovered that the man was already married and had two children. She alleged that he had deliberately concealed this from her for around 18 months and also took around ₹10 lakh from her. ‘I hope I will get justice now’ The girl said she struggled to seek help because of her limited education and repeatedly approached different police stations. With an FIR now registered against her lover, she hopes the case will bring her justice. Read her story in her own words... Met 18 months ago, man promised to marry her The girl said, “I used to earn a living by dancing at events in Lucknow. Around one and a half years ago, I met Trivendra, a resident of Lakhanpur village in Sikandra, at Gayatri Mod in Shastripuram. He worked at a shoe factory in Agra. I was introduced to him by another transgender person.” ‘He frequently visited my grandmother’s house’ She further said, “At the time, I was living at my maternal grandmother’s house in Lucknow. Trivendra would also frequently visit the house and knew my relatives. It was during these visits that he began talking about marriage. He repeatedly assured my family that he would marry me.” ‘I left Lucknow and came to Agra’ The girl further stated, “As my relationship with Trivendra grew closer, I left Lucknow and came to Agra. I trusted his promise of marriage. Trivendra coaxed me into going to hotels, where he sexually assaulted me.” Lover took ₹10 lakh in name of marriage The girl said, “Trivendra took around ₹10 lakh from me in the name of marriage. I gave him ₹4 lakh to buy a Bullet motorcycle. I also gave him ₹1.5 lakh during Diwali and another ₹1.5 lakh on Raksha Bandhan. I gave him money on several other occasions as well.” Some payments made through UPI She added, “I paid some of the money in cash, while some payments were made through UPI. I do not have a bank account of my own, so on several occasions, I asked other people to transfer money to Trivendra.” She further said, “I have photographs of some of these transactions and other evidence, which I have handed over to the police. I also have photographs with Trivendra from hotels, restaurants and outings.” Spent ₹3 lakh on gender-affirming surgery Speaking to Bhaskar she said, “When Trivendra and I started discussing marriage, he told me that I would need to undergo gender-affirming surgery. He assured me that we would be able to marry after the procedure. He said that society and our families would not accept us in our existing situation.” She added, “Trusting him and his promise of marriage, I went to Kanpur in January. I spent nearly ₹3 lakh from my own pocket on the surgery at a hospital.” Learn how the surgery was performed Experienced burning, anxiety, vomiting and breast pain during hormone therapy Endured pain for months after 3 surgeries and had difficulty eating and drinking She went to the man's house after surgery and discovered that he was married The girl said, “After the surgery, when I returned to Agra and brought up marriage, Trivendra's behavior began to change. He started evading the subject. After that, I went to his house to discuss marriage. It was there that I learned that Trivendra was already married and had two children.” She added, “Trivendra hid his marriage from me for about a year and a half. His family threatened to kill me. I then began to fear for my safety.” ‘I am not educated, so the police kept dismissing me’ She also stated, “About eight months ago, I began filing complaints with the police. I approached the police outpost in Agra, the Sikandra police station, the Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (City), and the Police Commissioner. Trivendra was brought to the police station several times, but he pretended to faint. He would then leave. I am not educated, and because of this, my complaints were not being heard. An FIR was registered only after the matter appeared in the media.” ‘I used to dance in Lucknow; now I seek alms in Rajasthan’ She added, “Now even my family and relatives have distanced themselves from me. My lover also turned out to be a fraud. After this, I began living with the transgender community. Even after the surgery, my work did not change. At present, I live with the transgender community in Rajasthan and seek alms. I occasionally come to Agra for work.” Police are now investigating the hotel and financial transactions Sikandra police station in-charge Rajiv Tyagi said, “The girl has photographs of several hotels. She is telling the police about these hotels. The police are investigating these locations. The photographs provided by the girl and evidence related to the transactions of money are also being examined. A case was registered on September 2. Further action will be taken based on the investigation.”

stories.title: Former Delhi Chief Secretary dies by suicide in Noida:Lived alone in rented flat; wife, also former IAS officer, was with son in Dehradun
stories.summary: Former Delhi Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta, 75, died by suicide at his rented flat in Noida. His wife, former IAS officer Sumanti Mehta, called him several times on Sunday (6 Sept) afternoon but received no response. She then sent the society’s security guard to check on him. The guard entered the flat and found Mehta hanging from a ceiling fan. Suicide note mentions illness Mehta lived in a rented flat in Kendriya Vihar-2 society in Sector 82. Police recovered a one-page suicide note from the spot. In the note, Mehta reportedly said he was distressed due to illness and did not hold anyone responsible for his death. 1975 batch IAS officer was close to Sheila Dikshit Rakesh Mehta was a 1975-batch IAS officer and was considered close to former Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit. His family performed his last rites in Delhi on Monday (7 Sept). The incident came to light after the family approached the police on Tuesday (8 Sept) and provided information about his death. Rakesh Mehta was originally from Dehradun Rakesh Mehta was originally from Dehradun and had been living in the Kendriya Vihar-2 Society in Sector 82, Noida, for around five years. His wife, Sumanti Mehta, was a Delhi-cadre IAS officer. The couple has two children. Their son is pursuing a PhD, while their married daughter lives in London. Wife was in Dehradun when she could not reach him At the time of the incident, Sumanti Mehta was in Vasant Vihar, Dehradun, with their son. She became concerned after Rakesh Mehta repeatedly failed to answer her calls, following which the police were informed. Held key administrative posts in Delhi During his administrative career, Mehta held several important positions in the Delhi government and municipal corporation. He served as Chief Secretary of Delhi and Commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, among other key posts. Mehta suffered from several health conditions Police recovered a one-page suicide note written in English from the flat. In the note, Rakesh Mehta reportedly said he was distressed by his health problems. He was suffering from hypertension, diabetes and tremors in his hands and feet. Served as Delhi Chief Secretary from 2007 to 2010 Rakesh Mehta became Delhi’s Chief Secretary in 2007 and continued in the post until November 2010, when he retired. His tenure coincided with that of then Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit and included preparations for and the hosting of the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi. Also served as MCD Commissioner Besides holding key positions in the Delhi government, Mehta served as Commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. During his more than three-decade administrative career, he worked on several major issues, including transport, electricity and civic amenities. Police call it a case of suicide According to police, “Information was received through Dial-112 that a 75-year-old man, Rakesh Mehta, had died by suicide.” Officials added, “Mehta, son of Kulwant Ram Mehta, lived in Kendriya Vihar-2 under the jurisdiction of the Phase-2 police station in Gautam Buddh Nagar. After receiving the information, local police immediately reached the spot. Teams from the forensic and field units also inspected the scene as part of the investigation.”

stories.title: Alok Kumar likely to be next UP Chief Secretary:Veena Kumari also in race; suspense over SP Goyal’s extension
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the state may get a new Chief Secretary. The current Chief Secretary, Shashi Prakash (SP) Goyal, is due to retire on January 31, 2027. Among the contenders for the post, Alok Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, is currently considered the frontrunner. Additional Chief Secretary of the Sugar Industry and Cane Development Department Veena Kumari Meena, CM Yogi’s Additional Chief Secretary Sanjay Prasad, and Census Commissioner of India Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan are also among the contenders. Government may push for an extension for SP Goyal Senior government officials believe that the Model Code of Conduct for the elections may already be in force when SP Goyal retires. In such a situation, to avoid administrative reshuffles, both the state government and the Election Commission may consider giving SP Goyal a three- to six-month extension. This could help ensure that the election process is completed smoothly. After the election results, the new government could choose a new Chief Secretary according to its own preferences. However, some officials believe that if SP Goyal does not seek an extension himself, or if CM Yogi does not write to the Centre requesting an extension for him, Uttar Pradesh could get a new Chief Secretary in the middle of the election process. Know the names being discussed for the next Chief Secretary Alok Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, is considered the strongest contender for the post of Chief Secretary. According to sources, Manoj Kumar Singh, CEO of the State Transformation Commission, is backing his candidature. Some Union ministers are also reportedly in favour of appointing Alok Kumar as Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary. Alok Kumar is regarded as one of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s trusted officers. This is why he has been handling key departments such as MSME and Industrial Development since December 2023. If he is appointed Chief Secretary, he would have nearly three years in office, giving him sufficient time to work. This is one factor that puts him in a stronger position than the other contenders. 1993-batch IAS officer Veena Kumari Meena is also a strong contender for the post. If the government chooses her, she would become Uttar Pradesh’s first woman chief secretary. Since returning from central deputation in 2019, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has consistently entrusted her with key responsibilities. She served as Principal Secretary of the Stamp and Registration and Geology and Mining departments from August 2019 to January 2020. From May 2020 to March 2023, she handled the Food and Civil Supplies Department. Since June 2023, she has been continuously heading the Sugar Industry and Cane Development Department. Sanjay Prasad is an influential 1995-batch officer. He is currently the Additional Chief Secretary to the Chief Minister. He also holds charge of the Home, Information and Estate departments. Since March 2019, he has consistently been among the key officials at the Pancham Tal (the Chief Minister’s Office). Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan is also an influential 1995-batch officer. He is currently the Census Commissioner of India. From 2017 to 2018, he served as Secretary to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath before going on central deputation. He is considered to be among the officers close to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, as well as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. Why have the other senior officers fallen behind? Several officers rank senior to the contenders after SP Goyal in terms of seniority. However, as per the rules, an officer must have at least six months of service remaining to be eligible for appointment as Chief Secretary. stories.title: Who owns Neem Karoli Baba’s birthplace?:Granddaughters accuse trust of grabbing it; grandson blames 6 brothers-in-law
stories.summary: A film based on Neem Karoli Baba, Hanuman Ansh, has earned more than ₹100 crore. However, the house where Neem Karoli Baba spent his childhood has now become the centre of a dispute between his family and a trust. 6 of Baba’s granddaughters have submitted a complaint to the District Magistrate, accusing trust secretary Sanjay Gupta of attempting to take possession of the property. Meanwhile, the Uttar Pradesh government is preparing to develop a corridor linked to Neem Karoli Baba there. In such a situation, questions over the ownership and management of properties associated with Baba’s legacy have become significant. So, who owns Neem Karoli Baba’s ancestral house? Why have his granddaughters accused the trust of taking possession of it? Read the full report… First, understand what the dispute is about… Neem Karoli Baba was born in Akbarpur village, around 15 km from Firozabad. House No. 154-V in the village panchayat is his ancestral home. It is maintained by the Shri Thakur Hanuman Trust. The ancestral residence has Baba’s meditation room, dining hall, guest room, and bedroom. This property is at the centre of the dispute. In a complaint submitted to the District Magistrate, Baba’s six granddaughters have accused trust secretary Sanjay Gupta of attempting to take possession of the property. Neem Karoli Baba was a householder saint. He had two sons and a daughter. His elder son, Aneke Sharma, has one son, Dhananjay Sharma, who lives in Firozabad. His younger son, Dharma Narayan Sharma, has six daughters. It was the granddaughters who filed the complaint alleging the encroachment. Baba’s daughter, Girija Bhatele, lives in Agra. Baba’s grandson says sisters’ husbands are behind the dispute We spoke to Neem Karoli Baba’s grandson, Dhananjay Sharma, about the entire dispute. He said, “When this temple was built, my father and uncle had said that after their death, the house should be handed over to the trust. No documentation was done at the time, so there is no proof. The house is built on just 450 square feet. It is not property worth crores. Maharaj Ji’s name is so revered that such a dispute will only tarnish his reputation.” Dhananjay said the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department is preparing to develop a corridor on 5 hectares of land in the village. The land has also been identified. It will be developed along the lines of Kainchi Dham. However, a dispute has now been raised over the property, with allegations that the trust has taken possession of it. “It would be considered encroachment if someone from outside the family had taken possession and refused to vacate the house. But here, the trust is responsible for its entire maintenance,” he said. Dhananjay said, “On August 14, all the sisters came to the village for the death anniversary of their aunt, their mother. There was no talk of any dispute at that time. Everyone sat together and had a meal in the same house. Later, a complaint was submitted to the DM. It is not the sisters but their husbands who are behind all this. Manoj Rawat is at the forefront. I find it strange that the DM accepted their letter when there is no dispute here. My aunt has been the president of the trust from the beginning.” Now, hear the side of Baba’s granddaughters… Baba’s six granddaughters are Sunita Sharma, Archana Sharma, Vandana Sharma, Bhavana Rawat, Ritu Tiwari and Richa Rawat. Manoj Rawat, whom Dhananjay Sharma mentioned, is Bhavana Rawat’s husband and lives in Agra. He is providing documents related to the case to the DM. We spoke to him and told him that Dhananjay had said the complaint was tarnishing Baba’s name. Manoj said, “I understand that too, but there is a limit to everything. When things went beyond the limit, we had to take this step.” Manoj said, “This is not a matter of land, but of emotions. It is our property, and it is not right that we should be stopped from entering it. We submitted documents related to the property to the DM on 7th September. Maharaj Ji’s name is recorded in the Gharoni (property record). After him, the names of his sons and then their daughters should be recorded. We have also submitted the family registers to the DM.” Speaking about the trust’s authority, Manoj said without naming anyone, “When one person has all the authority, there is a possibility of irregularities. They start thinking they are everything. We want the trust to be dissolved and the government to set up a new trust. The Firozabad DM should be its ex-officio president, along with the Tundla tehsildar and another official. Other people from Akbarpur should also be included. This would ensure that these officials keep changing and no one develops a permanent mindset of control.” Trust says dispute has been created deliberately Baba’s wife, Rambeti, established the Shri Thakur Hanuman Ji Trust in 1996. Baba’s daughter, Girija Bhatele, is currently its president. 17 other people are also members of the trust. It manages properties associated with Baba across the country. We spoke to an office-bearer of the trust about the matter. Speaking on condition of anonymity, he said, “There has never been any dispute within the trust so far, and there is no possibility of one in the future either. This dispute has been created deliberately. Truth always prevails. Those creating the dispute will eventually calm down themselves.” Government is developing Neem Karoli corridor The Tourism Department is giving special focus to Neem Karoli Baba’s birthplace. A modern convention centre is also being built here at a cost of around ₹9 crore. It will have a multipurpose hall, a cultural block and a modern exhibition hall. Items associated with Neem Karoli Baba will be displayed in the exhibition hall. Uttar Pradesh Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh visited Firozabad recently. He said the government was developing the area as a religious and cultural tourism centre. This would boost local employment and economic activity. “Our aim is to provide everyone visiting the area with easy connectivity, modern facilities and a spiritual experience,” he said.

stories.title: Crorepati father-in-law’s murder mastermind cries in jail:Weeps for hours remembering son in Kanpur, inmates console her; police suspect son too
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the first night in jail for the daughter-in-law accused of murdering her millionaire medicine trader father-in-law was spent in extreme restlessness. Accustomed to the comforts of home, the daughter-in-law was placed in a barrack after arriving at the jail on Monday evening. For the first two hours or so, she remained quiet and did not speak to anyone. When the female inmates asked her the reason for coming to jail, she began to cry. She also refused to eat dinner. On Tuesday morning around 6:30 AM, she was woken up like the other inmates. In the morning, she had porridge and jaggery for breakfast. For lunch, she was served lentils, rice, chapatis, and vegetables. In the afternoon, female inmates tried to console her. When asked if she had children, she began crying upon remembering her five-year-old son. She did not speak for a long time, then sobbed and fell asleep after two–three hours. In the evening, after having tea and biscuits, she ate lentils, vegetables, and chapatis at night. Why did the police suspicion deepen towards the son as well? How was the accused daughter-in-law caught? Read on in detail… In Ratan Orbit, Indira Nagar, 63-year-old millionaire medicine trader Vineet Minocha was murdered by domestic help Vishal Gautam (30) alongside accomplice Raj Kishore (30) at 11:28 PM on Saturday night. Around 3 AM on Sunday morning, when the son, daughter-in-law, and grandson arrived at the flat, they found the blood-stained body. On Sunday evening at 7:30 PM, the police arrested both men after shooting them in the leg during the encounter. Vishal revealed, "We committed the murder at the behest of the trader's daughter-in-law." Following this, on Monday evening, the police arrested the accused daughter-in-law, Shalu, as well. Without being asked, the daughter-in-law said: 'I don't know why Vishal killed him?' Fresh disclosures are coming to light daily in the Vineet Minocha murder case at Ratan Orbit in Indira Nagar. The police had to toil hard to extract secrets from the accused daughter-in-law, Shalu. Right on the first day of the incident, police suspected the involvement of someone close to the family. On receiving news of the incident, Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal arrived at the scene and began questioning Shalu alongside three female officers. She broke down crying profusely and feigned falling unconscious. Weeping, she said, "Papa was very good; he took care of my every small and big need. How will I live without him now..." The Police Commissioner asked Shalu if she knew Shivam. To this, she replied that yes, Shivam also goes by the name Vishal. She added that he used to visit the house for minor chores. "I don't know why Vishal killed Papa..." This remark by Shalu left the Police Commissioner and the investigating officers bewildered, wondering how she already knew that Vishal was the one who committed the murder. Daughter-in-law called accused Vishal 14 times, son called 25 times before murder Seeing Shalu's facial expressions change during questioning, police suspicions grew stronger, though officers did not let their doubts show. Following this, police began scrutinising the call detail records of Shalu, her husband Subrat, Vishal, and others who fell under the purview of suspicion. After the post-mortem proceedings were concluded and Vineet Minocha's final rites performed, the accused Vishal and his accomplice Raj Kishore fell into police hands late on Saturday night. Both confessed that they had carried out the murder at Shalu's behest. Meanwhile, when Shalu's call detail records reached the police, the entire matter became even clearer. The call detail records revealed that on the day of the murder, Shalu spoke to Vishal on the phone 14 times between 12 noon and 9 PM, while her husband Subrat made 25 WhatsApp calls to him. When Police Confronted Shalu and Vishal, Truth Was Confessed On Monday morning around 7 AM, police took Shalu into custody. Family members were left stunned by the police action. Shalu's sister also arrived at the Kalyanpur police station alongside her, pleading to stay with Shalu, but the police turned a deaf ear. When police began interrogating Shalu in a closed room, she said weeping, "I have done nothing; you people are trying to frame me forcibly." When police placed the call detail records before her, she said that Vishal is a good electrician and also helped with household chores, which is why she used to call him over. Police asked why she had called Vishal on the day of the murder, to which Shalu stated that she had to attend a couple's kitty party, for which she had ordered a gajra (flower garland) through Vishal. She claimed that after receiving the gajra, she left for the party with her husband and son, adding, "I do not know why Vishal killed Papa (Vineet Minocha)." Following this, when police brought Shalu and Vishal face-to-face, her body language changed. In front of police officers, Vishal confessed that he had carried out the murder solely at Shalu's behest. Vishal revealed that Shalu had instructed him, "If the police catch you, say that you killed him on the instructions of Bhaiya (Subrat)." After this, Shalu fell completely silent, following which police remanded her to jail late on Monday evening. Jail Superintendent Rajesh Kumar Pandey stated that Shalu has been kept in the observation barrack just like ordinary inmates. On arriving at the jail, she remained restless for a few hours, but later settled down. No clean chit for trader's son; police suspicion deepens There are still several secrets in the medicine trader's murder mystery that remain undisclosed. The police investigation revealed why, despite being sacked four years ago on theft charges, murder accused Vishal remained in continuous contact with the son, Subrat, and daughter-in-law, Shalu. Why did he speak with Shalu and Subrat on a daily basis? Between 29 August and the night of the murder, 25 WhatsApp calls took place between the trader's son Subrat and accused Vishal, whereas 14 conversations took place between Vishal and Shalu. Not only that, Shalu and Vishal also spoke via WhatsApp call three times while the murder was being committed. The probe further revealed that a few days before the murder, Vishal, Shalu, and Subrat had gone shopping together. Furthermore, despite being aware of his wife Shalu's involvement in his father's murder, Subrat did not open his mouth and maintained silence. When the police first showed Vishal in the CCTV footage, Subrat even refused to identify him. The police have yet to find answers to all these questions. Police Working to Recover 49 Deleted Messages The plot to murder the medicine trader was woven through 49 deleted messages. These messages were deleted between 1st May and the day of the incident. What were these messages and of what nature? Neither the murder accused Vishal nor the daughter-in-law who gave the contract provided this information to the police. Police are engaged in recovering data from the seized mobile phones of the contract killer, Vishal Gautam, and the daughter-in-law, Shalu. Between 1st May and the day of the incident, 309 calls took place between Shalu and Vishal Gautam. Police Find No Footage at Cosmojin Lounge Daughter-in-law Shalu had claimed that on the night of the incident, she went to a party at Cosmojin Lounge in Tilak Nagar alongside her husband Subrat and their 5-year-old son. Following this, on Tuesday, the Kalyanpur police reached Cosmojin Lounge to ascertain the truth. The police investigation revealed that no DVR was found attached to the CCTV cameras installed at the lounge. Upon questioning, the lounge manager stated that live recording of the party is conducted. Police subsequently obtained the guest list for the couples' kitty party. According to police officials, a list containing over 30 individuals has been acquired. Who was the party organiser? Were Shalu and Subrat present at the party on the day of the incident or not? To verify all these facts, guests who attended the party will be summoned for questioning.
