stories.title: ‘Rajpal Yadav, deposit ₹5 crore or go to jail’:Supreme Court gives him time till tomorrow; actor had said, ‘I’ll deliver the outstanding money home’
stories.summary: In the cheque bounce case, the Supreme Court has granted Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav interim relief from surrendering and going to jail. However, he received this relief subject to a condition. On Tuesday, a three-judge bench headed by Chief Justice Suryakant heard the case. The court made it clear that Rajpal Yadav would not have to go to jail for the time being if he deposited ₹5 crore with the court registry by tomorrow. Rajpal Yadav has challenged in the Supreme Court the Delhi High Court's July 10, 2026, judgment, which sentenced him to three months in prison and ordered him to repay ₹7.5 crore. The Supreme Court has issued notice to the other party on Rajpal Yadav's petition and sought its response. The next hearing in the matter has now been scheduled for 15 September. The entire matter dates back to 2010, when Rajpal Yadav borrowed ₹5 crore for one of his films. The dispute had been pending in court for a long time after he failed to repay the outstanding amount and the cheque bounced. High Court had said: Actor's conduct was suspicious, send him back to jail On July 10, the Delhi High Court ordered Rajpal Yadav to return around ₹7.5 crore to the complainant in a cheque bounce case. The court also sentenced the actor to three months in prison in case of non-payment. However, immediately after the verdict, the High Court granted him two months to approach a higher court. While hearing the case, the court raised serious questions about Rajpal Yadav's conduct. The court said that despite giving repeated assurances, the actor had not paid the outstanding amount. 13 days ago, Rajpal Yadav had said: "I will deliver the money owed to people to their homes" Amid cheque-bounce cases and debt disputes, actor Rajpal Yadav had claimed that he had personally suffered losses of around ₹200 crore over the past 13 years. Speaking to news agency ANI, the 55-year-old actor said that he is a responsible person and would repay the money owed to people or deliver it to their homes. Received lower fees, missed more than 50 overseas tours Rajpal Yadav said that he suffered the greatest financial losses between 2013 and 2016. He said that during this period, he missed at least 50 overseas tours and the fees he received also decreased considerably. Giving an example, he said that where he should have received ₹100, he received only ₹10. However, Rajpal said that he is a student of art and values perfection in his craft more than money. Speaking about his financial situation and debts, Rajpal Yadav said that he has repaid or will soon repay everyone from whom he borrowed money. He said that even if he had borrowed money from 200 people, he would return it. Rajpal said that no one can buy him for ₹5 crore or ₹250 crore. He also said that his financial difficulties do not define his entire career, and even today, 500 people take selfies with him at the airport. Bank Auctioning Property Worth ₹3.10 Crore Action is being taken against Rajpal Yadav for failing to repay a loan owed to the Central Bank of India. Rajpal Yadav had taken a loan of ₹16.61 crore from the Central Bank's Mumbai branch in the names of his wife, Radha Yadav, and mother, Godavari. In Shahjahanpur, the Central Bank of India has pasted an attachment notice on his ancestral home regarding the outstanding loan of ₹16.61 crore. Rajpal has already served time in jail in the cheque bounce case Rajpal Yadav's cheque bounce case began in 2010, when he took a loan of ₹5 crore from Murli Projects Private Limited to make his film 'Ata Pata Laapata'. The film, released in 2012, flopped. Following this, the cheque bounce case has been pending in court since 2013. He also surrendered at Tihar Jail in February 2026, after which he spent 12 days in prison. He is currently preparing for the films 'Haivaan' with Akshay Kumar and 'SVC 63' with Salman Khan. Rajpal Yadav's Career... Became the Comedy King with films like Hungama and Hulchul He gained recognition for his comedy through films such as Hungama in 2003, Garam Masala in 2005, Chup Chup Ke in 2006, followed by Hera Pheri and Bhool Bhulaiyaa in 2007. He has worked in nearly 8 to 10 films with comic director Priyadarshan. Rajpal has already won the Best Versatile Actor Award. Rajpal Yadav received the Yash Bharti Award, the highest honor of Uttar Pradesh. He received this award for the 2003 film Main Madhuri Dixit Banna Chahti Hoon. The honor was presented to him for his comic and serious acting roles. Before him, the award had been given to prominent names such as Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan. He was nominated for Best Comic Actor on platforms such as Filmfare and IIFA, but he could not win the award. In Mumbai, the first dream was simply to stay alive After completing his studies at NSD, Rajpal came to Mumbai. Initially, he received no support. In an interview, he said that his first dream in Mumbai was simply to stay alive. After struggling for some time, he began getting work. During his days of struggle, Rajpal fed 20-22 struggling actors at his home. In an interview, Nawazuddin Siddiqui said, "Rajpal's house was like a community kitchen-free food and accommodation." His school friends called him Chhotu and Batla Rajpal Yadav is approximately 5 feet 1 inch tall. In school, his friends used to call him Chhotu and Dwarf because of his short height. At the age of 20, he got a job at the Ordnance Clothing Factory in his village. Married at the age of 20 Rajpal Yadav said in an interview that when he was around 20 years old, his family arranged his marriage. At that time, he was living in the village and had just started working. Wife died 15 minutes after the birth of their daughter In an interview, Rajpal Yadav revealed that he was 20 years old when his family pressured him into getting married. His first wife's name was Karuna. A year later, their daughter Jyoti was born, but his wife passed away just 15 minutes after the delivery. He says, 'I was supposed to meet her the next day, but I carried her dead body on my shoulder. It is not easy to endure such pain at the age of 20.' After this, he became a single father, and Jyoti was cared for by his mother and sister-in-law. Rajpal revealed in an interview that he met his second wife, Radha, in Canada. At the time, he was shooting for the Sunny Deol and Preity Zinta film Hero: Love Story of a Spy. They met through a common friend, and the two got married on June 10, 2003. Formed his own political party in 2016 In 2016, Rajpal Yadav launched a new political party called Sarv Sambhav Party (SSP). The party was formed in Vrindavan. He was the party's general secretary and star campaigner, but did not intend to contest the elections himself. The party's motto was, "Politics of dialogue, not controversy." He took an oath to work honestly, placing his hand on the Gita, Quran, Bible, Guru Granth Sahib, Ramayana, and the Constitution. In the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the party announced that it would contest around 390-400 of the 403 seats. The party's headquarters was in Lucknow. His two brothers, Shripal Singh Yadav (Bislpur) and Rajesh Singh Yadav (Tilhar), contested the elections on behalf of the party, but the party did not achieve any significant success. Rajpal Yadav Escaped Death 3 Times In an interview, Rajpal Yadav said that he had survived three life-threatening accidents. Once, while bathing in the Ganges, he went into deep water and lost consciousness. Besides this, he narrowly escaped being run over by a bullock cart on one occasion and a situation resembling an attack by wild dogs on another.

stories.title: Woman undergoes gender transition for lover, suffers months of pain:Trans woman in Agra says man she trusted was father of 2; extorted ₹10 lakh
stories.summary: My boyfriend told me to undergo surgery, saying we would get married afterwards. I trusted him. For the sake of love, I underwent three surgeries to transition from a transgender person to a woman. I spent around ₹3 lakh on the surgeries and endured months of pain. I thought we would finally get married, but he backed out after the surgeries. I later found out that he was already married and had two children. He had kept this hidden from me for one-and-a-half years. He also took around ₹10 lakh from me. Today, I have neither his love, nor a marriage, nor the money I gave him. I am not highly educated, so I kept going from one police station to another. Now that an FIR has been registered, I hope I will get justice. These are the words of the 20-year-old woman who filed a case against her boyfriend in Agra, speaking to Dainik Bhaskar. She said she was born in Agra’s Rambagh. Her mother died when she was just two years old. When her family opposed her gender-affirming surgery, she had to cut ties with them as well. They met one-and-a-half years ago, he promised to marry her The woman said, “I used to make a living by dancing at events in Lucknow. One-and-a-half years ago, I met Trivendra, a resident of Lakhanpur village in Sikandra, at Gayatri Mod in Shastripuram, Agra. Trivendra worked at a shoe factory in Agra. A fellow member of the transgender community introduced me to him. “I lived at my grandmother’s house in Lucknow. Trivendra also used to visit my grandmother’s house and knew my relatives. That is where talks of marriage began. He repeatedly promised my family that he would marry me. As my friendship with Trivendra grew, I left Lucknow and moved to Agra. He would then lure me to hotels and sexually assault me.” Boyfriend allegedly took ₹10 lakh in the name of marriage The woman said Trivendra took around ₹10 lakh from her on the pretext of marriage. “I gave him ₹4 lakh to buy a Bullet motorcycle. I also gave him ₹1.5 lakh during Diwali and another ₹1.5 lakh on Raksha Bandhan. I gave him money on several other occasions as well. “Some of the money was given in cash, while some was transferred through UPI. I do not have a bank account of my own, so I sometimes asked other people to transfer money to him. I have screenshots of some of the transactions and other evidence, which I have given to the police. I also have photographs with the accused at hotels, restaurants and during outings.” Spent ₹3 lakh on three surgeries to transition for marriage The woman said, “When I started discussing marriage with Trivendra, he told me to undergo gender-affirming surgery. He assured me that we could get married afterwards. He said society and our families would not accept us otherwise. “Trusting Trivendra, I went to Kanpur in January. I spent around ₹3 lakh of my own money on surgeries at a hospital there.” Hormone therapy caused burning, anxiety, vomiting and breast pain The woman said she underwent counselling with a mental health specialist several times. “During this entire process, preparing myself mentally for the physical changes was not easy.” Before the gender-affirming surgery process began, she was given hormone therapy. On a doctor’s advice, she started taking oestrogen hormone medication. She experienced problems including a burning sensation, anxiety, vomiting and mood changes. Gradually, her skin changed, body hair decreased, and breast development began along with pain in the breasts. Endured months of pain after 3 surgeries; had difficulty eating and drinking First surgery: Implants were placed in her chest to develop breast size. She experienced pain and swelling in her chest for several days after the surgery, making everyday activities difficult. Second surgery: This was performed to alter her facial features, including the shape of her jaw and nose. Her face remained swollen for several days after the operation, and she had difficulty eating and drinking. Third surgery: This was performed for gender transition. It was the most difficult procedure. She underwent an orchiectomy and vaginoplasty. She had difficulty sitting and getting up for several weeks afterwards and endured considerable pain. An orchiectomy involves removal of the testicles, while vaginoplasty is a surgical procedure to create a vagina. Went to his house after surgery; discovered he was married The woman said, “After returning to Agra following the surgeries, I started talking to Trivendra about marriage, but his behaviour changed. He began avoiding the subject. I then went to his house to discuss marriage. That is when I found out that Trivendra was already married and had two children. “Trivendra had hidden his marriage from me for around one-and-a-half years. His family threatened to kill me. I then became afraid for my safety.” Says, ‘Police kept turning her away because she was not educated’ The woman said, “Around eight months ago, I started approaching the police. I complained at a police outpost in Agra, Sikandra police station, the DCP City’s office and the Police Commissioner’s office. Trivendra was brought to the police station several times, but he would pretend to faint and then leave. I am not educated, and because of this, no one was listening to me. When the matter came into the media spotlight, the FIR was finally registered.” Used to dance in Lucknow; now seeks alms with the transgender community in Rajasthan The woman said her family and relatives have now distanced themselves from her. “My boyfriend also turned out to be a fraud. After this, I started living with the transgender community. My work has not changed even after the surgeries. At present, I live with the transgender community in Rajasthan and seek badhai as a traditional livelihood. I sometimes come to Agra for work.” Police now investigating hotels and financial transactions Sikandra police station in-charge Rajiv Tyagi said, “The woman has photographs from several hotels. She is providing the police with information about these hotels, and the police are investigating these locations. The photographs and evidence related to the financial transactions submitted by the woman are also being examined. A case was registered on September 2. Further action will be taken based on the investigation.”

stories.title: Rajbhar tells Akhilesh to turn his cap blue:Says, ‘P for first time, D for second, A for this time’; predicts defeat in 2027 too
stories.summary: In Ghazipur, Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar hit back at SP chief Akhilesh Yadav's statement calling him "P se pagal" ("P for crazy"). Rajbhar gave a new meaning to PDA. He said, "P stands for first time, D for second time, and A for this time. They lost for the first time in 2017, lost for the second time in 2022, and will lose this time in 2027." Rajbhar also took a jibe at the Samajwadi Party's red color. He said Akhilesh should change the color of his cap to blue. Rajbhar said that he had formed the Rashtriya Suheldev Sena about eight months ago, giving one lakh people an opportunity to join it. Its uniform is also blue. Rajbhar claimed that his organization is ready to take on the Samajwadi Party. Now, read Minister Rajbhar's 3 major statements 1. Demolition of the mosque in Saharanpur was a court decision Minister OP Rajbhar said about the mosque demolition case in Saharanpur: The government has only followed the court's order. He alleged that when the court notice was issued, the SP and Congress were not concerned. But now, after the action, they are talking about going there to recite Fatiha. 2. Raised a question about the well near the mosque Regarding the old well found at the site, Rajbhar said that an investigation is underway to determine how such a large and old well existed there. He also questioned how a mosque was built there afterward. He said that there has traditionally been a practice of having wells around temples. The situation will become clear only after the investigation is completed. 3. Government is looking after Anganwadi workers and Shikshamitras Minister OP Rajbhar also spoke about the demands of Shikshamitras, instructors, cooks, and Anganwadi workers. He said the government wants to look after everyone's interests. He said the Chief Minister made several important announcements on Tuesday from Ayodhya for all 75 districts of the state. Rajbhar said that appointment letters had been issued to those appointed this year. He added that the honorarium of Anganwadi workers had been increased from ₹3,000 to ₹8,000 and then to ₹12,000. The honorarium of assistants had been increased from ₹1,500 to ₹4,000 and then to Rs 6,000. In addition, medical treatment facilities of up to ₹5,00,000 have also been provided.

stories.title: Two ₹50,000-reward accused arrested in Badaun chit-fund case:Were hiding in Lucknow after fleeing with money collected from thousands of investors
stories.summary: The STF has arrested two wanted accused, carrying a reward of Rs 50,000 each, in connection with chit fund-related cases in Badaun. Both accused had been hiding in Delhi for nearly eight months before residing in the Manas Nagar area of Krishnanagar. The Noida STF team arrested them at around 5:40 p.m. on Monday. The arrested accused have been identified as Badaun residents Shashikant (58) and Suryakant (50). Four cases were registered against both of them at the Kotwali police station in Badaun in 2025. They had been absconding for a long time in these cases. A reward of Rs 50,000 each had been announced for their arrest. According to the STF, Shashikant started a grocery shop in Badaun's Jalandhari Sarai area in 1988. After 2004-05, he worked as a field agent for a finance company. He later started his own company named 'Amar Jyoti Hire Purchase.' The company facilitated investments in shares and provided personal loans. Lured people with promises of doubling their money in a short time During the investigation, it came to light that in 2016, the accused set up a company called 'Amar Jyoti Universe Nidhi Limited.' It is alleged that through the company, people were encouraged to open deposit accounts and deposit money, while attractive offers-including doubling the amount in a short period-were made. According to the STF, thousands of people had invested their money in these companies, but the funds were not returned on time. The two accused then fled Bareilly. In this connection, four cases had been registered at the Badaun Kotwali police station. Accused had traveled from Delhi to Lucknow To evade arrest, the two accused kept changing their locations. During questioning, they told investigators that they had remained hidden in Uttam Nagar, Delhi, for around eight months. After that, they began living in the Manas Nagar area of Krishnanagar, Lucknow. The STF team received information that the two were hiding in Lucknow. They were subsequently arrested. The STF is now investigating the other activities of the accused and facts related to the case.

stories.title: Cyber fraud in Varanasi’s Nagwan:₹2.28 lakh siphoned from account in 3 transactions; FIR filed at Lanka police station
stories.summary: A case of cyber fraud has come to light in Nagwan, under the jurisdiction of Lanka police station in Varanasi. Cyber fraudsters withdrew more than ₹2,28,371 from the Bank of Baroda account of Bhanu Pratap, a resident of the area, through UPI. When the victim learned that money had been withdrawn from his account, he lodged a complaint at Lanka police station. The police have registered an FIR and begun an investigation. Amount withdrawn from the account in three transactions Bhanu Pratap said that three separate transactions were made from his bank account between August 31 and September 1, 2026. One transaction was made late at night, while two were made on September 1. An amount of ₹91,083 was withdrawn at 11:45 p.m. on August 31, ₹77,168.51 at 8:15 a.m. on September 1, and ₹60,120 at 10:31 a.m. on September 1. The three transactions together resulted in ₹2,28,371.51 being withdrawn from the account. Victim Was Unaware of the Transaction The victim said that he had not authorized the withdrawals made from his account. He learned about the cyber fraud after the money was transferred via UPI. He then submitted an application to the Lanka Station House Officer, requesting action in the matter and the recovery of the money. Police Register FIR, Begin Investigation Based on the victim's complaint, Lanka police have registered a case. The investigation has been assigned to Inspector Santosh Narayan Pandey. Lanka Station House Officer Rajkumar said that an FIR had been registered on the victim's complaint. The investigation has begun. Police are examining the UPI transactions made from the account and the details related to the transfer of the money.

stories.title: Youth killed for stopping men from urinating on road:Rowdies surround and beat him in Kanpur, crush his head with brick; dies after 2 days of treatment
stories.summary: In Kanpur's Kakadev police station area, 47-year-old Amit Kumar paid a heavy price for objecting to someone urinating in the middle of the road. It is alleged that youths who were under the influence of alcohol surrounded him and beat him when he protested, striking him several times on the head with a brick. Amit, who was seriously injured, was admitted to a hospital, where he died late on Monday evening after two days of treatment. The entire incident was captured on a CCTV camera installed near the scene. The incident took place at around 11 p.m. on Saturday near Om Chauraha. Amit Kumar, a resident of Naveen Nagar, ran a shop named Prem Aid in Kakadev and was returning home after closing it. Meanwhile, some youths were standing near the intersection drinking alcohol. It is alleged that one of them began urinating in the middle of the road. When Amit tried to stop him, the dispute escalated and the youths began assaulting him. Police have taken the CCTV footage into custody and begun efforts to identify and arrest the accused. They surrounded him and began assaulting him after he objected According to the deceased's son, Rudra Pratap Singh, when his father stopped a young man from urinating on the road, the youth began abusing him. After this, the other youths accompanying him also confronted Amit and surrounded him. It is alleged that when people nearby tried to intervene, the attackers assaulted them as well. During the incident, Amit was struck on the head with a brick. After suffering serious injuries, he collapsed on the road. People informed the police and had him admitted to the hospital According to the family, the accused fled the scene after the incident and also threatened people nearby while leaving. The locals then informed the police by calling 112 and notified Amit's family about the incident. When the family reached the spot, they found Amit in critical condition. He was first taken to a nearby private hospital. As his condition was serious, doctors referred him to Anurag Hospital, where he remained under treatment for two days. He died during treatment, throwing the family into turmoil Late Monday evening, Amit's condition deteriorated during treatment, and he died. As soon as the family received the news of his death, chaos broke out in the household. On Tuesday, the family members reached the post-mortem house and demanded strict action against the accused. The family members have demanded that the police arrest the accused soon. They alleged that Amit died after suffering serious injuries in the assault. Four youths seen assaulting him on CCTV After the incident, the police examined footage from CCTV cameras installed nearby. The footage shows four youths assaulting Amit. A crowd of people can also be seen at the scene. The police have taken the footage into custody and are trying to identify the youths based on it. No arrests even after three days; family members raise questions The family members say that despite the incident being captured on CCTV cameras, the accused have not been arrested. Questioning the police action, they have demanded that all the accused be arrested as soon as possible. The family members said they would meet the Police Commissioner and demand action. Meanwhile, after the post-mortem, the process of handing over the body to the family was carried out. Station House Officer says accused will be arrested soon Kakadeo Station House Officer Dharmendra Ram said that a case had been registered based on the complaint filed by the deceased's family members. Amit Kumar died during treatment. Efforts are underway to identify and arrest the accused based on the CCTV footage. The accused will be arrested and sent to jail soon.

stories.title: Rahul’s plane fails to land on first attempt:Flying from Delhi to Lucknow, lands 25 minutes later on second attempt; scuffle at airport
stories.summary: Air India flight AI-1717 from Delhi to Lucknow was unable to land on its first attempt at Lucknow airport on Tuesday afternoon and had to perform a go-around. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was also on board the flight. The aircraft was reportedly very close to landing when the pilot realised that it was not in a suitable position to land safely. He aborted the landing and took the aircraft back into the air. The sudden manoeuvre caused a strong jolt, briefly triggering panic among passengers. However, the pilot made another approach towards the runway and landed the aircraft safely on the second attempt. All passengers and crew members on board are reported to be safe. Rahul Gandhi is on a two-day visit to his parliamentary constituency, Rae Bareli. He will stay at the Bhuemau Guest House tonight and attend a Disha committee meeting on Wednesday. Flight departed Delhi at 2:20pm and remained airborne for another 25 minutes According to the information available, Air India flight AI-1717 departed from Delhi at around 2:20pm. It was scheduled to reach Lucknow at around 3:30pm. During the first landing attempt at Lucknow airport, the aircraft performed a go-around after the approach became unstable. After remaining airborne for around 25 minutes, the aircraft made another approach towards the runway and landed safely on the second attempt. So far, the airline has not issued an official statement on whether the emergency situation was caused by weather conditions or a technical issue. Scuffle during Rahul’s welcome at the airport A large crowd had gathered at the airport to welcome Rahul. Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai, former state president Brijlal Khabri, leader Asim Waqar and several others welcomed him. People wanted to meet Rahul, leading to some pushing and shoving. When a security personnel pushed a young man, Rahul intervened and objected. Rahul also stopped several times to avoid the crowd. See 3 pictures of Rahul at the airport… Rahul meets traders Rahul Gandhi reached Rae Bareli from Lucknow with his convoy at around 6pm. A large crowd of Congress workers gathered in Maharajganj town to welcome him. People were seen standing in a queue stretching for nearly one kilometre. At around 7:30pm, Rahul reached the house of bullion trader Fana Trivedi in Prabhu Town Area. He held a meeting with traders from the district and listened to their concerns. Amethi MP Kishori Lal Sharma was also present. On September 9, Rahul Gandhi will hold a Janta Darbar at the Bhuemau Guest House. At 11:30am, he will attend the DISHA committee meeting at Vikas Bhawan. What is a go-around? In aviation, a go-around is a standard safety procedure. When a pilot determines that it is not safe to land the aircraft on the current approach, they abort the landing and climb back to altitude. The aircraft then makes a new approach and lands safely.

stories.title: Umesh Pal’s wife threatened with RDX attack:Jaya Pal breaks down in Prayagraj court, says, ‘I’ll be killed the same way as my husband’
stories.summary: Arguments have begun in the Umesh Pal murder case at the district court in Prayagraj. At 3:15 p.m. on Tuesday, Umesh Pal's wife, Jaya Pal, reached the SC/ST court and recorded her statement. When Jaya was questioned about her husband's murder, she became emotional. She said that her life was under threat. Speaking to the media outside the court, she said, "I am receiving death threats on social media. I am being told that I will be blown up with RDX." Jaya Pal asked, "Where are the accused Guddu Muslim, Sabir and Armaan? Why is the police unable to find them?" Jaya had brought a social media poster with her, on which the threats were written. After presenting her statement in court, Jaya Pal met Police Commissioner Piyush Mordia and demanded that a case be registered against those issuing the threats. In Prayagraj, on February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal and his two government-appointed security guards were shot and killed and attacked with bombs in broad daylight. Umesh Pal was a key witness in the 2005 murder of BSP MLA Raju Pal. Mafia figure and former MP Atiq Ahmed, his brother Ashraf, his son Asad, and their accomplices were accused of plotting and carrying out the murder. Jaya says, ‘People from the Atiq gang conduct surveillance on me every day’ Jaya Pal said, "My life is in danger. I was surveilled even today. Some people linked to the Atiq gang are still active." She filed an application in court seeking enhanced security and submitted CCTV footage. The court immediately ordered the Police Commissioner to increase her security. Today, I am remembering the scene of my husband's murder Jaya Pal said, "I am remembering that scene today... My husband had left after returning from court, and he was brutally murdered on the way. I, too, will be killed, just as my husband was murdered. Why is the police still unable to arrest the accused, Guddu Muslim, Sabir, and Armaan?" Jaya Pal showed a poster of Atiq Ahmed's eldest son, Umar. Umar is pointing a finger and asking people to remain silent. Who is this gesture meant for? Every day, it is being said on social media that Umar will return, Ali will return, and Ahzam is out. My family is being tortured. I want justice. Security arrangements remained tight because of Jaya Pal's arrival at the court. Umesh Pal's wife reached the court along with several lawyers and supporters. Earlier, on September 1, Jaya Pal had also recorded her statement in court. Read the full sequence of events... 2005: Raju Pal Murder Case A BSP legislator, Raju Pal, was murdered in Prayagraj. Umesh Pal was among the key witnesses in the case. Later, this testimony became the reason for Umesh Pal's murder. February 24, 2023: Murder of Umesh Pal Umesh Pal was attacked in the Dhoomanganj area of Prayagraj while returning home. Umesh Pal and two government security guards deployed for his protection were killed in the attack. Following the incident, a case was registered on the complaint filed by Umesh Pal's wife, Jaya Pal, against Atiq Ahmed, Ashraf, Shaista Parveen, Asad, and several others. February 27, 2023: First Police Encounter Three days after the murder, the police reported that Arbaaz had been killed in an encounter. According to the police, Arbaaz was accused of driving the attackers' vehicle. March 2023: Investigation and Arrests Intensify The police began arresting the accused and alleged accomplices in the case. The investigation also revealed alleged contacts with Ashraf, who was lodged in Bareilly Jail, in connection with the conspiracy. The Bareilly Police later filed a charge sheet against nine people. See 4 photos related to the murder of Umesh Pal... April 13, 2023: Asad and Ghulam killed in an encounter Asad, son of murder case accused Atiq Ahmed, and shooter Ghulam were killed by the Uttar Pradesh Police in an encounter in Jhansi. Both were accused of being involved in the Umesh Pal murder case. April 15, 2023: Atiq and Ashraf murdered Atiq Ahmed and his brother Ashraf were shot dead in Prayagraj in the presence of the police. Both were in police custody at the time and were accused in the investigation into the Umesh Pal murder case. May 2023: First chargesheet Prayagraj Police filed the first chargesheet in the Umesh Pal murder case. Subsequently, as the investigation progressed, chargesheets were filed against other accused as well. June 17, 2023: Second Charge Sheet The police filed a supplementary charge sheet against Atiq's lawyer, Khan Saulat Hanif, Iqlakh Ahmad, and other accused. October 2023: Charge Sheet Against Vijay Mishra The police also filed a charge sheet against Vijay Mishra, the lawyer for the Atiq family. 2024: Action Against Atiq's Sons Umar and Ali After the investigation, the police also filed a charge sheet against Atiq's sons, Umar and Ali. According to the police, both were accused of having knowledge of the conspiracy behind the murder. October 2024: Charge Sheet Against Guddu Muslim, Sabir, and Armaan The police also filed a charge sheet against the absconding accused, Guddu Muslim, Sabir, and Armaan. All three were reported to have been absconding since the incident.

stories.title: Bike jumps over speed breaker, crashes into divider in Kanpur:Man killed; brother had undergone stone surgery
stories.summary: 25-year-old man died in a road accident on Tuesday afternoon in the Chakeri police station area of Kanpur. Near Love Park in Sanjeev Nagar, his motorcycle suddenly jumped over a speed breaker. After he lost control, the motorcycle skidded for about 10 meters before colliding with a divider. The motorcyclist, Aman Yadav, suffered serious head injuries in the accident. Acting on information from passersby, the police reached the spot and took him to Kanshi Ram Hospital, where doctors declared him dead during treatment. Aman was a resident of Geeta Nagar in Rawatpur and was on his way to Hathipur to deliver clothes to his elder brother. His elder brother, Ramniwas, lives in a rented room in Hathipur and works as a train guard. He underwent surgery for kidney stones at Regency Hospital on September 3. After the operation, he was discharged from the hospital and returned home. Aman had set out on Tuesday to take his clothes to him, but met with an accident on the way. Motorcycle jumped over a speed breaker near Love Park On Tuesday afternoon at around 2:30 p.m., Aman was traveling from the 60-feet road at Tiranga Square toward Hatheepur. As soon as he reached near Love Park in Sanjeev Nagar, his motorcycle suddenly bounced over a speed breaker. Before Aman could regain control of the motorcycle, he lost his balance. The motorcycle then skidded along the road for about 10 meters before crashing into the divider. The impact was so severe that Aman suffered serious head injuries and fell onto the road. Gathering of passersby, death at the hospital People from the surrounding area gathered at the scene after witnessing the accident. Passersby informed the police. The police arrived shortly afterward and took the seriously injured Aman to Kanshiram Hospital. The doctors began treating him at the hospital, but they could not save his life. The doctors declared Aman dead. Aman had gone out to collect his brother's clothes Aman's maternal uncle, Indrajit Yadav, said that Aman was going to Hathipur to collect the clothes of his elder brother, Ramniwas. Ramniwas lives there in a rented room and is a train guard. A few days ago, he underwent surgery for kidney stones at Regency Hospital. He had returned home after the operation. The family had hoped that Aman would return after collecting his brother's clothes, but as soon as news of the accident arrived, the household was plunged into mourning. Body sent for post-mortem The police took custody of the body and sent it for a post-mortem examination. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the accident. Chakeri police station in-charge Ajay Prakash Mishra said that the body had been sent for a post-mortem examination. The actual cause of the accident is being investigated. Further legal action will be taken once a complaint is received.

stories.title: Anganwadi workers’ honorarium increased by ₹4,000, will now get 12,000:₹5 lakh cashless treatment, smartphones and sarees announced by Yogi in Ayodhya
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi arrived in Ayodhya on Tuesday. He said, “We have come up with four types of schemes for Anganwadi workers and helpers. We have increased their honorarium, provided cashless treatment of up to ₹5 lakh, are increasing the number of sarees they receive, and are giving them smartphones.” Yogi said that Anganwadi centres are now smart. “Nine years ago, they were in a dilapidated condition. The government at that time indulged in corruption, while Anganwadi workers faced the blame. The nutrition programme was controlled by the liquor mafia. Its influence was such that it could affect any system. No one dared to speak against it.” As a result, Anganwadi centres were in a state of disorder. Nutrition was not provided on time. Someone else made the mistake, but others had to face the consequences. The government and the mafia ruined the system, while Anganwadi workers had to face the abuse. Yogi said that before 2017, innocent children themselves brought mats to Anganwadi centres. Even drinking water was not available. The central government provided funds, but the state government did not purchase anything. “And when it did make purchases, the money went into the hands of the mafia. Anganwadi centres remained deserted. Even if you wanted to work, you could not. Over the past nine years, we have given Anganwadi centres an organised structure.” Earlier, Yogi was welcomed at a felicitation ceremony for Anganwadi workers and helpers organised at the Government Inter College (GIC) in Faizabad. He handed over appointment letters to Anganwadi workers and helpers. Around 12,000 Anganwadi workers and helpers from Ambedkarnagar, Amethi, Barabanki, Sultanpur, Basti and Gonda were invited to the Chief Minister’s programme.

stories.title: Akhilesh launches blue dress for SP student wing:Says BJP fears colours, not God; calls people on the other side imposters
stories.summary: In Lucknow, Akhilesh Yadav launched a new blue dress for the SP's student wing, 'SP Chhatra Sabha', on Tuesday. Akhilesh said, "The color blue represents the Bahujan society as well as an ideology. The new generation has new thinking. That is why there should be a new uniform." When we are in uniform, all inequality disappears. A uniformity becomes visible. Uniform brings uniformity. Through the new uniform, students will take the ideology and socialist values among the students and youth. Akhilesh said that BJP people are often afraid of colors, but they are not afraid of God. Whoever steals offerings must be the biggest imposter. A large number of Chhatra Sabha members were present at the SP office on this occasion. Read the 5 big points of Akhilesh Yadav... 1. BJP people are afraid of colors, not God Akhilesh Yadav said that BJP people are afraid of colors. They are not afraid of God. They steal offerings and donations. That is why they should be afraid of God, not colors. In what guise must they have stolen the donations? Whoever is stealing donations and offerings must be the biggest imposter. The people on the other side are imposters. These are the same people running negative campaigns on social media. BJP members claim that running negative campaigns is not their job. Everyone, put your hand on your heart and tell me, who is running all the negative campaigns on social media? 2. A new battle on digital platforms, we will not back down The BJP is the one spreading negative propaganda. We will have to complain about this to Meta. Youth should not spend too much time on Instagram; it is an addiction. I want to tell my youth, if they are creating content, then we are also creating content. We have not given permission yet, they can create all this. Our people will continue to make and post videos. This is a new battle on digital platforms. We will not back down from this fight. 3. Janmashtami was not allowed to be celebrated, belongings were thrown on the road Regarding Janmashtami, Akhilesh Yadav said that this festival is celebrated in many countries of the world. In some places, Janmashtami was not allowed to be celebrated. Belongings were thrown on the road. Referring to the Jagannath Yatra, he said that even the British people there participated in it. Akhilesh targeted the government over inflation, electricity, and waterlogging. He said that there is a problem of traffic jams and waterlogging everywhere. Wherever there is BJP, there is waterlogging. Referring to Prayagraj, Akhilesh Yadav said that it is the most religious and mythological place for all of us, where the Triveni is located. About one lakh crore rupees were spent there in the name of development, but theft and robbery took place. 4. If the SP government comes to power, AI will be used in law and order Work should be done to create an AI ecosystem. AI can also be used extensively in law and order. The Samajwadi Party government had introduced the Dial-100 system. The Samajwadi Party government had invested in laying cables for the internet in UP. Cables were taken to every village, and it is a result of that, that we are getting good internet today. When the SP government comes to power, free Wi-Fi facility will be provided again in Hazratganj. Regarding the ambulance system, Akhilesh said that ambulances are not available today. A mother goes to Agra and the child dies, and that too in a district which is an international city like Agra. 5. Said - Wherever there is BJP, there is waterlogging Akhilesh targeted the government over inflation, employment, investment, and the power situation. He said that the government has no mechanism to curb inflation or provide jobs. There is also no answer regarding how much investment will come or how much has already come. He said that electricity is becoming expensive, but the government is unable to improve the power system. In a city like Kyoto (Varanasi), along with waterlogging and traffic jams, the rivers are not being cleaned, even though about one lakh crore rupees have been spent there.

stories.title: 80% of patients at SN Medical College have flu:Doctors stress masks as neglect leads to pneumonia; swine flu
stories.summary: With the change in weather, flu patients have increased rapidly. Currently, about 70 to 80 per cent of patients visiting the SN Medical College OPD have flu symptoms. Among these, complaints of fever, cough, cold, and sore throat are the most common. Some patients are also experiencing shortness of breath and chest congestion. Samples of patients with symptoms similar to swine flu are being sent for testing, although the reports have been negative so far. Doctors have advised wearing masks in crowded places and taking precautions to avoid infection. They stated that ignoring a viral infection for too long can lead to pneumonia or swine flu. Increase in flu and viral patients among children as well Dr. Neeraj Yadav from the Department of Pediatrics stated that 179 children visited the OPD on Monday. About 90 per cent of these children were suffering from jaundice, viral fever, and diarrhea. Due to their serious condition, 8 to 10 children have to be admitted to the emergency ward daily. Separate OPD for flu patients In view of the increasing number of patients, a flu OPD has also been set up at SN. Principal Dr. Prashant Gupta stated that suspected patients of viral fever and flu are being examined in room number 12-A of the Medicine Department. Wear a mask in crowds, wash hands before touching children and the elderly SN OPD physician Dr. Prakash mentioned that flu infections are on the rise. In such a situation, avoid going to crowded places, and if it is necessary to go, wear a mask. One should avoid going to crowded places without a mask. Always wash your hands before touching your eyes, nose, and ears. Also, clean your hands before going near children and the elderly at home. If possible, change your clothes after returning from outside. Children and the elderly are more susceptible to flu infections, so take special precautions before coming into contact with them. Consult a doctor if fever or cough persists for 5 days Dr. Prakash stated that one should not be negligent for a long time by considering fever or cough as normal. If the fever or cough persists for about five days, consult a doctor. If treatment is not received on time, the illness can become serious in some cases, and there may be a risk of complications like pneumonia or swine flu. Flu vaccine recommended for children up to five years of age Dr. Arun Jain, former president of the Indian Academy of Pediatrics, stated that cases of viral flu are being found more frequently in children. Delay in treatment or an incomplete course of medication can cause some children's conditions to worsen. With timely treatment, normal cases improve within 3 to 5 days. He advised getting the flu vaccine for children up to five years old. Take precautions to avoid infection 3,590 patients reached SN OPD

stories.title: ₹4-crore under-construction water tank collapses into river:Crumbles like pack of cards in Bareilly; boundary wall washed away 4 days ago
stories.summary: In Bareilly, UP, a water tank under construction worth 4 crore rupees collapsed into the Kichha river. Due to the strong current on Tuesday morning, the erosion happened rapidly. The tank started shaking and within 4 seconds, it collapsed into the river. Its boundary wall had been washed away just 4 days ago. Upon receiving the information, SDM Nidhi reached the spot and gathered details from the officials and villagers. The construction of the tank had been ongoing since 2023 under the Jal Jeevan Mission. Its structure was ready, while the work of installing the tank was pending. The pipeline had also been laid. The incident took place in Gram Panchayat Bairamnagar of Shergarh block, 50 km away from the district headquarters. See 3 pictures- River eroded 100 meters in a week The foundation, premises, room, and gate work for the water tank had been completed. Water taps had already been installed in 70% of the village homes. According to the villagers, engineers conducted a survey before building the tank, but they did not take the river's erosion into account. Village head Shamshul Khan said, "A week ago, the river was 100 meters away from the tank. But the erosion happened so rapidly that four days ago, the tank's boundary wall collapsed into the river." Following this, officials reached the spot and secured essential equipment, including solar panels, DG sets, SCADA, and generators. Village head said - Warned the officials, but they didn't listen The village head stated, "We had told the officials that if pitching (a protective layer to prevent erosion) was not done to stop the erosion, the tank would also be washed away, but the officials did not listen to us. Today, the tank has finally been washed away. If the work had been done in time, perhaps the tank could have been saved." When the tank construction began, the river was 500 meters away The village head said - When the land was selected for the tank, the Kichha river was about 500 meters away. Due to continuous erosion over the last two-three years, the river gradually moved closer to the tank. Currently, the river is in spate and erosion is happening rapidly. Villagers said - A new tank should be built soon Villagers say that the course of the river had been changing continuously for the last two-three years and the erosion was moving towards the water tank. In such a situation, the tank should have been built in a place where there was no danger of erosion, but this was not done. The villagers demand that the construction of the tank at a new location should be started soon so that people can get clean water. -

stories.title: Two UP students die in Delhi accident:Family donates Abhishek’s eyes; Pawan’s mother says, ‘Sent him to become an officer, got his body back’
stories.summary: Two students from Uttar Pradesh were among the seven people killed when a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi’s Satya Niketan area on Sunday. Chandauli’s Abhishek Kharwar (21) and Auraiya’s Pawan Singh (20) were studying in Delhi. Both had returned home around 10 days ago for Raksha Bandhan, where they celebrated with their sisters before returning to Delhi after promising to come home again during Dussehra. Instead, their families received their bodies in coffins. Abhishek cremated in Varanasi Abhishek’s family brought his body from Chandauli to Varanasi on Tuesday morning. His father performed the last rites at Manikarnika Ghat. His mother, Chaman Tara Devi, has been inconsolable since his death and has repeatedly fainted. When she regains consciousness, she looks for her son. Amid the grief, the family donated Abhishek’s corneas so that they could help restore sight to someone else. Abhishek’s aunt Anjani said he had already registered for organ donation. Following his death, the process to donate his eyes and other organs was initiated in Delhi. His corneas have since been donated. “Abhishek is gone, but his eyes can bring light to someone else’s life. For the family, it is a moment of both pride and pain,” she said. See pictures of Pawan's house Pawan’s mother: ‘Sent him to become an officer, got his body back’ Pawan’s last rites were performed in Auraiya on Monday. When his body reached home, his sisters hugged him and broke down. His mother repeatedly caressed his face, while his father sat silently near the door. As the funeral procession left the house, his sisters ran behind it. His mother kept saying, “We sent him to become an officer. His body has come back.” Pawan was the only son of retired homoeopathic pharmacist Vishambhar Singh and had four sisters. His elder sister Priyanshi is also studying at Delhi University and lives in a girls’ hostel. His mother Meera Devi is a homemaker. Pawan completed his Class 12 education this year from Saraswati Vidya Mandir Inter College in Dibiyapur. He secured admission to Delhi University’s BSc Computer Science programme on 20 July, around a month and a half before the tragedy. Mother spoke to Pawan twice every day According to the family, Pawan spoke to his mother on video calls every morning and evening. He had returned home for Raksha Bandhan and went back to Delhi on Saturday after celebrating Janmashtami. He spoke to his mother after reaching Delhi and also spoke to her on Sunday morning. However, when he did not call in the evening, his mother became anxious. The family soon learnt about the hostel building collapse. Pawan’s sister Priyanshi, who was staying in Delhi, immediately reached the hostel and searched for her brother for a long time. The family was informed late at night that Pawan had died. His father travelled to Delhi on Monday morning and returned home with his son’s body later that evening after the post-mortem. ‘If officials had acted earlier, my nephew might be alive’ Abhishek’s family lives in Jhansi village under Sadar Kotwali in Chandauli. His father, Santosh Kharwar, has worked as a crane operator at Hindalco in Sonbhadra for more than 30 years. His elder son Om Kharwar (26) has completed his BTech, while Abhishek was living in Delhi and pursuing a programming course. The deaths have left the family devastated. Abhishek’s mother has remained largely unconscious for the past two days, repeatedly fainting in grief. A sombre atmosphere has prevailed from the family’s ancestral village to the Hindalco colony in Renukoot. Abhishek’s maternal uncle Pankaj Kumar said the family initially learnt about the collapse through television reports. “When we saw the news, everyone panicked. When the family reached Delhi, we learnt that Abhishek had died in the collapse,” he said. After the post-mortem, the family had to make several efforts before the police handed over the body. His last rites were performed in Varanasi on Tuesday morning. Abhishek’s aunt Anjani alleged that the building was in a dilapidated condition and that local residents had informed the authorities about it. She said timely action could perhaps have prevented the tragedy. The family’s promising young son had gone to Delhi to study, she said, but returned home in a coffin.

stories.title: Woman constable dies after rifle fires while sitting on chair:Trigger pulled accidentally in Kaushambi, bullet exits through neck; posted 3 months ago
stories.summary: In Kaushambi, a 25-year-old woman constable died after being shot. She was on guard duty at the women's police station. While sitting on a chair, the rifle's trigger was accidentally pressed, causing it to fire. The bullet tore through her neck, ripped through her jaw, and exited. Chaos broke out at the police station as soon as the gunfire rang out. Police personnel stationed there took the constable to a medical college, where doctors declared her dead. The incident occurred at the city's women's police station. The woman constable was a resident of Ghazipur. She had completed her training just three months earlier. Her first posting was at the women's police station in Kaushambi. Priyanka had joined the women's police station in the last week of June. ASP says-No suicide note found in the room ASP Amita Singh said that at 10:30 a.m. on Tuesday, Priyanka was sitting on a chair at the gate outside the police station office. She got up to do some work and returned two minutes later. The preliminary investigation has revealed that as soon as she was about to sit on the chair, the sound of a gunshot was suddenly heard. She said-When fellow police personnel reached the spot, Priyanka was found seriously injured. A rifle was in her right hand. The constable's room was searched. No suicide note has been found so far. The forensic team collected evidence from the spot. The rifle has been taken into custody for examination. The spot has been sealed. CCTV footage is being examined. Information is also being gathered from fellow police personnel. A team has been formed under the leadership of CO Sadar Saurabh Samant to investigate the case. The cause of the incident will become clear once the investigation is complete.

stories.title: ‘I’d rather die than be called a cowardly judge’:UP judge who sentenced 36 to death wrote, ‘Better to resign than live in fear’
stories.summary: I would rather die than be called a cowardly judge. I will continue in service as long as I can follow my principles; otherwise, I will resign. As long as I occupy the judge’s chair, the authority to decide cases will remain mine alone. My parents taught me from the beginning to fear God and no one else. If I start fearing someone else, people will lose faith in the courts. If I begin to fear mafias, it would be better to resign from this sacred judicial institution. Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar made these remarks in his judgment on Monday while sentencing Nadeem to death in the Shahpur Shehzadi murder case in Muzaffarnagar. The court also imposed a fine of ₹1 lakh on Nadeem. Diwakar is the same judge who has sentenced 36 convicts to death during his 17-year judicial career. In Muzaffarnagar alone, he has handed down death sentences to 23 convicts in five months. Last month, the district judge recalled around 100 cases from his court and transferred them to other courts. Judge says Muzaffarnagar once faced gangster and mafia terror In his judgment, Diwakar referred to the murder of gangster Vicky Tyagi inside a courtroom in Muzaffarnagar. He wrote that the incident showed that criminals in the district had, at one point, little fear of the law. He also referred to the influence of the Shaukeen gang in the area. The court recently sentenced Shaukeen’s brother Shah Nawaz to death, he noted. Judge says family received threats after Gyanvapi case Diwakar said he and his family had received several death threats following the Gyanvapi case in Varanasi. He said threats had also come from outside the country. According to the judgment, an accused named Adnan Khan had allegedly threatened him through an Instagram account. The judge said his photograph had been used with the word ‘kafir’ written in red above his eyes. ‘It is not appropriate to speak now; the office has its dignity’ The judge wrote that he was deeply hurt by certain conduct but did not elaborate on the matter. He said a person might deceive the world but could not deceive their own conscience. He alleged that such conduct was aimed at protecting mafias, gangsters and criminals. “I know why this happened, but it would not be appropriate to speak about it at this stage because the office of a judge has its own dignity,” he wrote. Gangster allegedly threatened to get judge transferred Diwakar also referred to a message he allegedly received from a gangster from western Uttar Pradesh. According to the judgment, the gangster told him that only the cases had been removed for the time being and warned that if the judge continued to pursue them, his court could also be changed and he could be transferred outside the district. The message allegedly claimed that the gangster had influence “at the highest levels”. The judge wrote that it was a serious threat to any democratic country when judges became unable to deliver justice freely because of pressure or influence. What happened in the Shahpur Shehzadi murder case? On the night of July 23, 2018, at around 8.30 pm, Nadeem allegedly assaulted and abused his wife, Shehzadi. He then allegedly poured kerosene over her and set her on fire. Shehzadi died during treatment at Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi on July 28, 2018. Her parents and brother later retracted their statements in court. However, her dying declaration recorded before an Executive Magistrate at Safdarjung Hospital on July 24, 2018, proved crucial. In the statement, Shehzadi said that her husband Nadeem had poured kerosene over her and set her on fire. Additional Sessions Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar sentenced Nadeem to death on Monday, September 7. The court also imposed a ₹1 lakh fine. Shehzadi had not mentioned any demand for dowry or dowry-related harassment in her statement. Therefore, Nadeem was acquitted of the dowry-death charges. His sister Soni, who was also an accused, was acquitted of all charges. His mother, Shamshida, has died. Diwakar took charge in Muzaffarnagar in November 2025 Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar took charge at the Additional District and Sessions Court, Fast Track Court-3, in Muzaffarnagar on November 29, 2025. He began his judicial career in 2009 and had previously served in Sambhal and Bareilly before being posted to Muzaffarnagar.

stories.title: 3 friends swept away with bike in Bareilly river:Tried crossing bridge amid strong current, swam for long but couldn’t escape
stories.summary: Three friends were swept away along with their motorcycle by the strong current of the Aril River, in Bareilly. The three were crossing a small bridge on the motorcycle. Due to heavy rain, the river was flowing about two feet above the bridge. Suddenly, the motorcycle went out of control in the strong current, slipped, and fell into the river. All three friends fell into the water along with the motorcycle. They kept trying to swim to the shore for a long time but could not get out because of the strong current. The incident took place at around 5:30 p.m. on Monday in Ladpur village, under the jurisdiction of Aonla police station. The police have recovered the motorcycle and are searching for all three friends. Click on the image above to watch the spine-chilling VIDEO

stories.summary: Saharanpur police have arrested YouTuber Huda Zareewala. She had commented on Chief Minister Yogi over the demolition of a mosque on the collectorate premises. On Monday evening, she arrived at the Circuit House to protest the mosque's demolition. When she insisted on going inside, the police stopped her. As soon as they received information about her arrival, the police reached the spot and detained her. Huda had said two days earlier A mosque belonging to Muslims has been martyred. This is a criminal activity. Who gave them the right to demolish the mosque? The entire Muslim community stands against such people. We will not remain silent. After the video surfaced, lawyer Dushyant Singh filed a complaint against her at Sadar Bazar police station on Monday morning. Huda Zareewala has previously been a spokesperson for the Aam Aadmi Party. She has also worked as an anchor at a media organization in London. She currently describes herself as a social activist and YouTuber. Lawyer says Jariwala's statement has angered people Advocate Dushyant Singh, who filed the complaint against Huda Jariwala, said- Huda made comments against the administration over the action to remove the mosque from the collectorate premises. She also made objectionable remarks against the Chief Minister. A video of this has also surfaced. Her statement has angered people. That is why I filed the complaint. I appeal to the police to take strict action against Huda. Mosque demolished 3 days ago Find out why mosque was demolished

stories.title: ‘Sar Tan Se Juda’ incites violence:Allahabad HC says the slogan cannot be compared with religious chants like ‘Jai Shri Ram’; rejects Tauqeer Raza’s bail plea
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Monday said the slogan ‘Gustakh-e-Nabi Ki Ek Hi Saza, Sar Tan Se Juda’ openly challenges the law and unity of the country. The court observed that the slogan incites people to violence and against the country. Justice Ashutosh Srivastava said the slogan cannot be compared with religious chants such as ‘Jai Shri Ram’, ‘Har Har Mahadev’, ‘Sat Sri Akal’ or ‘Allahu Akbar’. The court rejected the bail pleas of Maulana Tauqeer Raza Khan and his close associate, Dr Nafis Khan. Tauqeer Raza is an accused in the riots that took place in Bareilly on September 26, 2025. He has been in jail since September 27, 2025. Police have described him as the alleged mastermind of the riots, while Raza has claimed that he was framed as part of a political conspiracy. Tauqeer Raza’s lawyer says he was framed due to political rivalry Tauqeer Raza’s lawyer told the court that the cleric was innocent and had been implicated because of political rivalry. The lawyer said Raza had never called for violence and was not present at the scene when the incident took place. He claimed that Raza had been placed under house arrest on September 26. The lawyer also argued that Raza had neither delivered a speech nor made any appeal that could be considered an attempt to incite violence, disorder or a breach of public peace. He said the call for a protest had been withdrawn after the administration refused permission and restrictions were imposed under Section 163. Government says Tauqeer provoked the crowd Additional Advocate General Anoop Trivedi, appearing for the state government, said the accused had held a meeting on September 19, 2025, and appealed to members of the Muslim community to gather at the Islamia Inter College ground. The appeal was made in connection with a protest against alleged atrocities and false cases, the government told the court. The local administration subsequently imposed restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), prohibiting gatherings of five or more people in public places. Despite the restrictions, around 200-250 people allegedly moved towards the Islamia Inter College ground. When police tried to stop the crowd, protesters allegedly raised slogans, threw stones and attacked the police with petrol bombs. Several police personnel were injured in the incident. After the violence, the main accused allegedly released a video through co-accused persons, thanking and praising those who had taken part in the protest. Court says violence and damage to public property cannot be justified The High Court observed that Tauqeer had called upon members of the Muslim community to gather after Friday prayers without obtaining permission from the administration. The court made it clear that violence against police personnel, rioting, damage to public property and acts that disturb law and order cannot be justified. What happened during the Bareilly violence? The violence in Bareilly on September 26 was linked to a dispute over ‘I Love Mohammad’ posters. Tauqeer Raza had called for a protest and appealed to people to gather in large numbers at the Islamia ground. The administration did not grant permission for the protest. Despite this, Raza allegedly challenged the police and administration through a video appeal and called on people to gather. Around 200-250 people reached the college following his appeal. When police tried to stop the crowd, protesters allegedly raised ‘Sar Tan Se Juda’ slogans and pelted stones. Petrol bombs were also allegedly thrown and shots were reportedly fired in the air. Several police personnel were injured and public property was damaged. Tauqeer Raza was named as the main accused in the case. Ten cases were registered against him at Kotwali police station. Police arrested him and sent him to jail, following which he approached the High Court seeking bail.

stories.title: Cement-laden goods train derails in Gorakhpur:Chaos at yard; leaves 7 hours later, DRM inspects site
stories.summary: A freight train loaded with cement derailed at Gorakhpur Junction late Monday night. The incident occurred at around 1 a.m. in the western yard of line number 8 at the junction. Late at night, three wagons of a freight train suddenly derailed, causing panic among the railway employees present at the site. As soon as railway officials received information about the incident, they were notified. Following this, a railway team reached the spot and began working to bring the situation under control. Freight train carrying cement bags It was reported that the freight train was traveling from Madhya Pradesh to Narayanpur Anant Railway Station in Bihar. The train was loaded with cement bags. Meanwhile, three of its wagons derailed in the western yard of Gorakhpur Junction. After the accident, railway employees first began the process of separating the derailed wagons from the freight train so that the remaining wagons could be safely sent onward. All three wagons were removed at 8:10 a.m. After several hours of work, the railway administration's team removed all three derailed wagons at around 8:10 a.m. on Tuesday. The freight train was then rerailed and dispatched onward. The railway authorities also conducted the necessary investigation and technical procedures at the site following the incident. DRM also reached incident site After receiving information about the incident, the DRM also reached the site on Tuesday morning. He inspected the area and sought information about the incident from the officials. At present, the actual reason why the three freight train wagons derailed has not been determined. Railway administration engaged in investigation Since the accident occurred in the western yard, the railway administration took immediate action and separated the derailed wagons. The freight train was then safely sent onward. So far, no casualties have been reported in the incident. The railway administration's team is engaged in determining the causes of the incident. Only after the technical investigation will it become clear exactly why the freight train's wagons derailed.

stories.title: 'Kill father-in-law, I’ll pay ₹6 lakh':Crorepati’s daughter-in-law called servant home on pretext of giving garland, got him entry under changed name
stories.summary: Twenty days ago, Shalu bhabhi called me and said, ‘Kill my father-in-law, Vineet Minocha, or arrange an accident. I will give you ₹6 lakh.’ When I refused, she said, ‘Don’t be afraid, I am with you.’ I was not ready to stage an accident, so she told me to suffocate him with a pillow while he was asleep. People would think he had died of a heart attack. She also promised to give me a job after the murder. This is the statement of Vishal, one of the accused in the murder of Kanpur medicine trader Vineet Minocha. According to police, Vishal told investigators that he later involved his friend Rajkishore in the plan and offered him ₹30,000. Shalu allegedly told them she would call the two men to the apartment on the pretext of delivering a gajra. She also allegedly instructed Vishal to give the name ‘Shivam’ to the security guard. After entering the apartment on Saturday night, Vishal and Rajkishore allegedly hid in Shalu’s bedroom. When Vineet entered the room, they allegedly attacked and killed him before washing the blood from their hands and feet in the bathroom and fleeing. Vineet was murdered at around 11.28 pm on Saturday at his flat in Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur. He was alone at the time, while his son and daughter-in-law had gone to a party. His body was found in the bedroom when they returned around 3 am on Sunday. Police arrested Vishal and Rajkishore following an encounter. During questioning, Vishal allegedly named Shalu as the person who had ordered the killing. Police arrested Shalu on Monday and sent her to jail. Accused claims debt led him to agree to murder During questioning, Vishal allegedly told police that he had worked at the home of Subrat, Vineet’s son, around four years ago before losing his job. He worked elsewhere for a short period but had been unemployed since 2022. He said Subrat occasionally called him for odd jobs. Vishal said he lives with his younger brother Akash and mother Sushila and had accumulated a debt of around ₹2 lakh. Around 20 days before the murder, he went to Subrat’s house for work, where Shalu was present. According to Vishal, Shalu told him she was troubled by her father-in-law’s behaviour and his constant restrictions. She allegedly said CCTV cameras had been installed in the house and that he monitored her movements. Vishal claimed Shalu first offered him money to arrange an accident involving Vineet, but he refused. She then allegedly asked him to kill him inside the house. ‘Bhabhi gave me the house key and ₹1,200’ Vishal allegedly told police that Shalu asked him to come to the flat when she and Subrat went out for a party. “She gave me one key to the flat and told me to get a duplicate made,” he allegedly said. According to him, Shalu gave him the original key around 12 days before the murder and ₹1,200 to make a duplicate at a local key shop. Vishal then approached his friend Rajkishore and offered him ₹30,000 for “a job”. He allegedly did not tell him initially that it involved killing Vineet. He bought a knife for the planned murder. The two had initially planned to carry out the killing on Janmashtami but abandoned the plan because of the crowds and activity around the apartment. Shalu allegedly arranged entry using a fake name Vishal told police that Shalu had already informed the security guard that a man named Shivam would arrive with a gajra and should be allowed inside. She allegedly instructed Vishal to identify himself as Shivam at the gate and not make an entry in the register. At around 9 pm on Saturday, Vishal and Rajkishore reached the apartment. The security guard did not stop them. Rajkishore stayed in the parking area while Vishal went upstairs and handed the gajra to Shalu. At around 9.38 pm, Shalu allegedly left for a kitty party at Cosmo Gym in Tilak Nagar with her husband and son. Police said she sent Vishal a message while travelling, telling him that the house was empty and asking him to go inside. At around 9.42 pm, Vishal and Rajkishore allegedly entered the flat and hid in Shalu’s bedroom. Accused claims they washed blood in bathroom and escaped At around 10.58 pm, Vineet returned home. According to Vishal’s alleged account, Vineet switched on the light in Shalu’s bedroom and was shocked to see the two men there. He allegedly asked them what they were doing in the house. Vishal claimed Rajkishore pushed Vineet to the floor, after which he attacked him repeatedly with a knife, striking his neck and chest. After Vineet died, the two men allegedly washed the blood from their hands and feet in the bathroom. Rajkishore covered his face with a black scarf, and the two allegedly escaped by jumping over the boundary wall of the society’s park. DCP West said CCTV footage helped police identify and arrest Vishal and Rajkishore. During questioning, Vishal allegedly named Shalu. Police questioned her at around 7 am on Monday. The DCP said she confessed during questioning. Medicine wholesaler ran business with son Vineet lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment. The four-bedroom flat with a dining room is reportedly worth more than ₹1 crore. He ran a wholesale medicine business under the name ‘Pharma Traders’ on Birhana Road. Vineet managed the business with his son Subrat. The firm reportedly had an annual turnover of ₹50–60 crore. Vineet is survived by his wife Punita, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Shalu and Subrat had been married for seven years. Punita works as a marriage counsellor and had travelled to Ghaziabad a week before the incident. Vineet’s daughter Subhani and son-in-law Gurugram-based engineer live in Gurugram.
