stories.title: UP’s ₹40 liquor kills 12:Families say victims tore their hair out, lost recognition and writhed in agony; village wept over funeral pyres
stories.summary: Uncle was pulling his hair and beating his forehead. His vision had blurred. His condition had deteriorated so much that he could not even recognise his family members. Uncle had turned blue... While saying this, Kirti Lodhi, the niece of Kartar Singh Lodhi, became emotional. Kartar returned home after drinking alcohol on Saturday evening and began vomiting a short while later. When his condition worsened, the family took him to the hospital, but he died during treatment. Kirti, a resident of Ghughra Khurd, said that the family had previously tried to stop him from drinking alcohol, but he did not listen. Kartar was the youngest of four brothers. The family is engaged in farming, and he leaves behind two young children. The family watched him suffer. Kirti says, "If only he had not drunk alcohol. We have lost our uncle." An FIR has been registered against around 30 people so far in the liquor scandal. A case has been registered against 20 people at Banda Police Station, while an FIR has been filed against more than five people at Vinayak Police Station. In addition, five officials have also been suspended. Read this report to find out how the liquor was supplied, who delivered it to the villages, and where it was prepared. Health deteriorated around 8 pm The deceased's uncle, Sardar Singh Lodhi, said, "His condition deteriorated around 8 pm. He kept losing consciousness repeatedly. He was referred to Sagar from Banda Hospital, where he died during treatment." While recounting this, Sardar Singh also broke down. Dizziness 20 minutes after drinking, followed by vomiting Kailash Lodhi, a resident of Nauraaj, said that he had consumed alcohol on Saturday night. About 20 minutes later, he began feeling dizzy. He went home and fell asleep, but later started vomiting. He had bought the alcohol from Jujhar Singh's place in the village. The alcohol was of the Sagar Gold brand. He had purchased a quarter for ₹90. His condition reportedly improved after treatment at the hospital. Received treatment first, condition deteriorated again in the morning Relatives of the deceased, Harnam Rai, said that his health deteriorated on Saturday afternoon. He was brought to the Banda hospital after he started vomiting. His blood pressure was checked, and after treatment, the family took him home. At around 6 a.m. on Sunday, his condition began deteriorating again. He was brought back to the hospital, where he died during treatment. Body turned blue after drinking alcohol Ramkumar Dangi, cousin of the deceased Sumer Singh Dangi, said that alcohol is sold in Bamura Bheda. Sumer had consumed alcohol, after which his condition deteriorated. His body had turned blue. He was taken to the hospital, where he died during treatment. According to Ramkumar, the condition of other people who had been drinking with him also deteriorated, and they died. Bottles lined the streets in Nauraaj; villagers revealed names Residents of Nauraj claim that illegal liquor has been sold in the village for a long time. According to the villagers, empty liquor bottles are lying in the village lanes and surrounding areas. They have accused several people, including Jujhar Singh, of being involved in selling liquor. According to the villagers, a quarter bottle of Sagar Gold is sold for around ₹40, while a quarter bottle of Bombay Whisky is sold for ₹90 to ₹100. These claims are yet to be confirmed by a police investigation. Claim of illegal liquor production in Tatarwara for years Villagers say that the illegal manufacture and sale of liquor has been going on in Gram Panchayat Tatarwara for several years. The police are also aware of it. Along with liquor coming from Uttar Pradesh, liquor prepared in Tatarwara has also been reaching nearby villages. Poisonous Liquor Connection from UP's Lalitpur to Sagar? Interrogation by the Lalitpur Police exposed a counterfeit liquor network. The accused revealed that they prepared fake liquor in collaboration with Ravi Lakhera, his wife Shivani Lakhera, Chandresh Lodhi, and Mona Raja. Methyl alcohol was used in it. Fake labels and caps resembling those of genuine brands were used To make the liquor bottles look genuine, the accused replicated the entire packaging. Fake wrappers and caps resembling those of genuine brands were placed on the bottles. They were then sealed. After this, fake QR codes were affixed to the bottles so that the packaging would appear to be that of genuine liquor and buyers would not suspect that it was counterfeit. Supply from Lalitpur to villages in Sagar The investigation revealed that the prepared liquor was brought from Lalitpur to Sagar by car and motorcycle. It was distributed in border villages, including Barethi, Banda, Shahgarh, Magardha, Vinayaka, Dalpatpur, and Baraytha. The police are now investigating the supply routes, local people involved in the network, and the extent of the entire operation. Investigation into the role of the contractor and liquor shop employee The investigation has also revealed the name of Akash Rai, a resident of Lalitpur, who works at a licensed liquor shop in Baretha, Sagar. The police are trying to determine whether he had any direct connection with the network. A contractor from Lalitpur has also been accused of being involved in the supply of liquor. The police are investigating the roles of both individuals. Raids to arrest the suspects are ongoing. Clues of liquor supply from Lalitpur SP Anurag Sujania said that FIRs have been filed against around 25 people in the liquor case. Of these, FIRs have been registered against 20 people at Banda police station. At Vinayak police station, FIRs have been registered against more than five people. So far, seven liquor shops have been sealed. The initial investigation has revealed that the liquor was supplied from Lalitpur in Uttar Pradesh. The people and network involved in the liquor supply are being investigated. Authorities are finding out where the consignment originated, who purchased it, through whom it reached the Banda area, and who sold it in the villages.

stories.title: Mayawati may expel Akash Anand from BSP:X bio now says ‘BSP supporter’; organisational reins to pass to younger nephew
stories.summary: The dispute surrounding Akash Anand in the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has now reached its final stage. Mayawati may expel Akash Anand from the party at any time. On Sunday, Akash Anand changed his bio once again, signalling this possibility. On September 3, he had described himself as a BSP worker. He has now changed it to ‘BSP supporter'. In addition, three major developments took place on Sunday. First, Mayawati instructed party office-bearers to immediately unfollow Akash and Ashok Siddharth on social media. Second, she assigned Ishan Anand the responsibility of reviewing the party organisation in all states across the country, except Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. This responsibility was previously held by Akash. Third, she elevated the stature of Ramji Gautam, Suresh Rao, Rajaram, and Atar Singh. Along with this, Randhir Singh Beniwal, who was overseeing the Saharanpur division, has now also been made in charge of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. Announcement of Akash's expulsion from party may come at any time Akash Anand has replaced 'BSP' with 'BSP supporter' on his social media profile. This is being viewed as a sign that Akash is growing increasingly distant from the party. However, no clear official announcement regarding Akash Anand's expulsion from the party has been made so far. According to party sources, Mayawati may announce it at any time. Instructions to unfollow Akash and Ashok Siddharth According to party insiders, Mayawati first directed Mewalal Gautam on Sunday to speak with the party's district presidents and office-bearers over the phone and instruct them to unfollow Akash Anand and Ashok Siddharth on social media. It is being reported that the activities taking place on social media concerning Akash are behind this. It has come to light that Ashok Siddharth retweeted one of two posts related to Akash Anand by Delhi-based YouTuber Samarraj. According to sources, Satish Chandra Mishra conveyed this information to Mayawati. Mayawati then instructed Mewalal Gautam to make both leaders unfollow each other. Mayawati upset over 'Akash of Hopes' trending on social media There is discussion of discontent among a section of BSP workers regarding Akash Anand. Phrases such as 'Akash of Hopes' are trending on social media. Akash's supporters are trying to create a favourable atmosphere for him. Some people presented the matter to Mayawati in such a way that Ashok Siddharth wanted to take control of the party through Akash. Since then, Mayawati has been making several decisions one after another. Ishan given major responsibility BSP chief Mayawati made major changes to the organisational structure on Sunday. She has divided the country into three sectors. Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand have been kept separate, while the remaining states have been divided into two large sectors, with senior leaders assigned responsibility. Ramji Gautam and Suresh Rao given responsibility for 10 states in Sector 1 Rajaram and Atar Singh Rao given responsibility for 9 states in Sector 2 Randhir Singh Beniwal given responsibility for Punjab again, also assigned Himachal Pradesh Randhir Singh Beniwal's role has also become important in the organisational reshuffle. Along with Ramji Gautam, he has been assigned responsibility for Punjab as well as Saharanpur. In addition, he has been given independent charge of Himachal Pradesh. One political interpretation of this change is that responsibility for Himachal Pradesh has been taken away from Nitin Singh, who is considered close to Ashok Siddharth. However, there is no information that Nitin Singh has been expelled from the party. Mayawati suddenly summoned Ramji Gautam, Anand Kumar, and Atar Singh Amid these changes, Mayawati's increased activity is also being discussed. It is being reported that Mayawati suddenly summoned Ramji Gautam, Anand Kumar, and Atar Singh on Sunday. Satish Chandra Mishra also arrived there. A meeting was subsequently held with the leaders. After the meeting, organisational orders of this nature were issued. Program to visit Delhi on September 9 According to sources associated with the party, Mayawati was scheduled to visit Delhi on September 9. It was reported that she had called Akash Anand's wife, Pragya, from London and was planning to meet Akash's daughter. Mayawati was also expected to make an organisational announcement regarding Ishan Anand in Delhi, but following the decision concerning Akash, she postponed her visit to Delhi. This is why she made decisions regarding Ishan on Sunday itself. Will Akash's younger brother Ishan now replace him in the BSP? The change in the BSP had begun to become apparent at the National Executive meeting held on September 3. Mayawati had called the meeting of the National Executive. For the first time, her younger nephew and Anand Kumar's younger son, Ishan (Ishu) Anand, also attended it. What was particularly notable was that Akash Anand was not invited to the meeting. After this, Akash himself indicated that he had been removed from the post of national coordinator by changing his social media bio. This entire development in the BSP is not being seen merely as an organisational reshuffle. At its core is the question of the party's next-generation leadership after Mayawati. On the one hand, Akash Anand has long been the face of the party's youth politics. On the other hand, the decision to give Ishan Anand the authority to oversee the organisation at the national level now indicates that Mayawati has increased Ishan's role in the party's organisational structure. However, it would be premature to say that Ishan has been formally established as Akash's replacement. But the changes in the responsibilities of those associated with Akash and the new role given to Ishan have certainly intensified discussions within the BSP's internal politics.

stories.title: UP cops allegedly torture jeweller, plant smack in bike:Poured petrol on private parts; released him after taking ₹2 lakh
stories.summary: In Shahjahanpur, four police officers planted smack in a jeweler's motorcycle trunk. They took him to a police outpost and brutally beat him. They poured petrol on his private parts. They then released the jeweler after taking ₹2 lakh. The trader had called his father from the outpost itself and asked him to bring the money. An audio recording of the call has also emerged. On Sunday, the jeweler filed a complaint at the police station. Following this, the SP ordered an investigation, which found all four police officers guilty. An FIR has been registered against all four, and two constables have been taken into custody. The incident took place at around 8 p.m. on the night of September 4 in Parshurampuri. Read the entire incident in sequence Called on the pretext of pledging a chain Rajesh Kshatriya lives in the Kanoon Goyan locality of Parshurampuri. He is a jeweler. He has four sons-Satyam, Shivam, Sundaram, and Mangalam. Satyam is a software engineer in Gurugram. Shivam, Sundaram, and Mangalam run jewelry shops. Sundaram said, I received a phone call at around 8 p.m. on the night of September 4. The caller said he wanted to pledge jewelry and borrow ₹10,000. After that, I left home. The caller told me that he had reached Jalalabad. Sundaram began waiting for him near Saraiya Turn around 9:56 p.m. Just then, constables Arun Chittaudiya, Pankaj, Tushar, and Virendra, posted at Tilhar police station, arrived on two motorcycles. All four were in plain clothes. Sundaram already knew them. Since they were acquaintances, he went with them. Took him to an isolated place and placed a polythene bag in the motorcycle's storage compartment The four constables took Sundaram to an isolated place. There, they took out a polythene bag they had brought with them and placed it in his motorcycle's storage compartment. They then took Sundaram to the Biriyaganj outpost of Tilhar police station, alleging that he was a drug trafficker. He was assaulted at the outpost. They tried to record a video showing the recovery of smack. They also threatened to send him to jail in a false case. Sundaram said, 'They poured petrol on my private parts.' He said the policemen released him after taking Rs 2 lakh Sundaram said that at around 1:30 a.m., the policemen demanded Rs 2 lakh in exchange for releasing him. They also threatened him, saying that if he told anyone about the incident, they would send him to jail. Sundaram's father, Rajesh Kshatriya, said, My son was beaten up. He called at 11:06 p.m. He told me that he had been detained in connection with a smack case. They demanded Rs 2 lakh from him. My son was released only after the money was paid. Meanwhile, Sundaram's brother Shivam said, The police took my brother away on the night of September 4. They poured petrol on his private parts, because of which he was in severe distress. I personally went to the Biriyaganj police outpost with ₹2 lakh and gave the money to the police officers. FIR filed against 4 police officers, 2 detained The allegations against the police personnel were confirmed during the investigation into the complaint. Following this, an FIR was registered against all four on the instructions of SP Saurabh Dixit. Constables Virendra and Pankaj have been detained. SP Saurabh Dixit said that the investigation into the matter is underway. Strict action will be taken. Read conversation between Sundaram and his father All four policemen made Sundaram call his father from the police outpost itself. They asked him to bring ₹2 lakh. Read the complete conversation verbatim... Sundaram: Hello? Father: Yes... Sundaram: Dad? They are saying, come to Beriya outpost. Father: Beriyaganj outpost...? Sundaram: Yes, Tilhar. Father: When? Sundaram: Now. Father: Should I come to the Beriaganj police post now? Sundaram: Yes, and bring two lakh rupees as well. Father: What...? Sundaram: They caught some goods in the vehicle. Father: We won't be able to pay that much. I don't have two lakh rupees. Sundaram: If you don't have it, arrange it, Dad. I'll sell the shop tomorrow and repay you. Father: At least tell me what happened. Sundaram: The police caught me at the Jalalabad intersection. Father: Were you selling smack? Sundaram: I'm not selling any smack or anything, but bring the money. Father: Then tell me why they took you away. Sundaram: Try to understand what I'm telling you. Father: Are they asking for two lakh? Sundaram: Yes... Father: We are talking-who is the policeman? Sundaram: Don't talk, just bring the money. Father: Have they arrested you? Sundaram: Yes... Father: Oh... why were you arrested? Sundaram: I had come to the intersection. Someone had called saying that a chain needed to be pawned. I came there because of that, and they picked me up. Father: Did they also find something on you? Sundaram: Yes, they are saying that the goods came out of the vehicle. Father: What was found? Sundaram: They haven't told me. You just bring ₹200,000, and the matter will be settled here.

stories.title: Lucknow head constable murders wife:Hits her on head with iron rod, then calls brother-in-law and sits beside body
stories.summary: A UP Police head constable from the 2011 batch allegedly killed his wife at their home in Lucknow’s Mahanagar area. The couple argued over an issue, following which the head constable hit his wife on the head with an iron rod. She collapsed unconscious and died. The head constable then called his brother-in-law and asked him to come over. When he arrived, he found the head constable sitting beside his wife’s body. Saurabh Srivastava, the victim’s brother and a resident of Malepura in Ambedkar Nagar, said his sister Rashmi Srivastava married Himanshu Srivastava, a resident of Niralanagar in Ayodhya, in 2015. He said Himanshu had allegedly been harassing her frequently since their marriage, but she continued to tolerate it to save the marriage. Brother-in-law says family would always counsel sister Saurabh said whenever the couple argued, the family would also counsel Rashmi to try to resolve the matter. On Sunday, his younger brother Adarsh called him at around 3pm and said Rashmi was unwell and asked him to go to her house. When they reached the house, Rashmi was lying on the floor of her room, while Himanshu was sitting nearby. She had suffered a serious head injury and was bleeding. She was not breathing. When they asked Himanshu what had happened, he failed to give a proper response, following which they alerted the police. DCP Central Vikrant Veer said, Himanshu Srivastava is a 2011-batch head constable. He is currently posted at the Right to Information Cell office in Daliganj. Police received information that a murder had taken place inside the house. When officers arrived, they found his wife Rashmi, 40, lying dead on the floor, with blood around her head. Was living in a rented house Himanshu had been living in a rented house belonging to Dr MM Srivastava in the Paper Mill area for the past two-and-a-half years. After the incident, he sat at the landlord’s house for quite some time. He later spent around three hours walking around with his child. Meanwhile, the police were informed about the incident. The Mahanagar police reached the spot after receiving the information. The woman’s body was taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examination. Himanshu, the accused husband, has been detained and is being questioned. This news is being updated…

stories.title: Stones thrown at CJP activist’s home over Swatantra Bhardwaj case:Ghaziabad neighbours say, ‘She is lying; nothing happened’
stories.summary: Nishu Azad, an activist of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), claimed that his house in Ghaziabad was pelted with stones. Nishu posted a video on social media platform X at 10:48 p.m. on Saturday night. He said that some people were surrounding his house and that stones and bricks had been thrown at it. He demanded protection for his parents and family from the Delhi and Ghaziabad police. He said, ‘If anything happens to my parents, who will be held responsible?’ In fact, during the Jantar Mantar protest, he had also alleged that his father, Sanjay Azad, was assaulted. In this case, accused content creator Swatantra Bhardwaj was arrested on Saturday. In this matter, a Dainik Bhaskar reporter tried to speak to Nishu Azad, but he has currently refused to speak to the media. Meanwhile, his neighbors said, No such incident took place here. The police should investigate the truth. Police say that if the family files a complaint, an investigation will be conducted on that basis; the video is also being examined. Nishu Azad lives in the Shalimar Garden police station area of Ghaziabad. See 2 pictures Neighbouring women said: We were awake, nothing like that happened Neighbour Pradeep said-If stone-pelting had occurred, we would have heard it first Pradeep Soni said that his house is right next to Nishu Azad's house. The society has tight security arrangements. A security guard is stationed at the main gate, and guards are also deployed in every building. No outsider can enter the society without making an entry in the register. He said that if there had been even the slightest disturbance or stone-pelting at Nishu Azad's house, the sound would have reached his house first. The atmosphere in the society is normal and safe. People continue to walk around until 11 or 12 at night after having dinner. There has been no stone-pelting or any such unpleasant incident here. Pradeep said that he learned about the matter in the morning, when the police arrived to investigate and were checking the CCTV footage. NSUI president visits home After the video surfaced, NSUI National President Vinod Jakhar visited Nishu Azad's home on Saturday and met with her family. Questioning the police action, he said that Swatantra Bhardwaj himself had admitted to attacking Nishu Azad's father, Sanjay Azad. Despite this, no action was taken initially. Jakhar claimed that the police became active after Rahul Gandhi raised the matter. Nishu accused of insulting Hindu gods and goddesses Two lawyers have filed a police complaint against Nishu and her father. They allege that both made objectionable remarks about Hindu gods and goddesses on social media. Lawyer Amita Sachdeva said that in an old X post, the activist used an offensive word for Goddess Durga and mocked Goddess Saraswati. The activist denied these allegations, saying, "There is an illegal demand to send my father to jail." Meanwhile, lawyer Prateek Jha filed a separate complaint alleging discrimination in the police action at Jantar Mantar. Swatantra Bhardwaj-Neeshu Azad case: Developments over last 2 days A podcast video featuring Swatantra Bhardwaj went viral. In it, she allegedly said that she had "smashed Neeshu's father's skull" and claimed that she was not jailed despite this. She also mentioned her political connections. Following this video, the old case once again became a subject of national discussion. September 4: CJP leaders and supporters staged a protest outside the Parliament Street Police Station in support of Neeshu Azad and her father. On behalf of Neeshu, lawyer Rishav Ranjan asked the police to add charges of attempted murder, criminal intimidation, and relevant sections of the SC/ST Act. The police added these charges. Swatantra was taken into custody. September 5: A Hindu organization staged a protest in Delhi in support of Swatantra Bhardwaj. The protest was called by Daksh Chaudhary. Daksh is known for assaulting and slapping high-profile people. He had also slapped Kanhaiya Kumar. Accounts of victim, the accused, and Delhi police in the assault case 1. Victim's side-Sanjay Kumar/Nishu Azad Sanjay Kumar, the father of CJP activist Nishu Azad, was injured during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on June 23. A case was registered at the Parliament Street police station based on Sanjay's complaint. Nishu alleges that her father was hit on the head and that even after one and a half months, the police have not taken adequate action. 2. Accused-Swatantra Bhardwaj Swatantra Bhardwaj claimed in a viral podcast that he had attacked Sanjay on the head, resulting in 60 stitches. He also said that he did not have to go to jail. Later, Bhardwaj retracted his statement, saying that it was not an attack but self-defense. He claims that 10-15 people had surrounded him and that if he had not acted in self-defense, the mob could have killed him. 3. Delhi Police's Version According to the police, Sanjay Kumar sustained an injury to his head on June 23 after being struck by a bangle (bracelet). Sanjay was taken to RML Hospital for a medical examination. The injury was described as simple in the medico-legal case. Police dismissed the claim that the skull had burst/fractured. Earlier, the police had called Swatantra in for questioning and then released him. Now, following pressure from the CJP, he has been taken into custody again, and new sections have been added to the case. Police said the family has not yet filed a complaint DCP of Ghaziabad City/Trans Hindon, Dhawal Jaiswal, said that a video of Nishu Azad has surfaced on social media. The video is being investigated. Nishu alleged that someone from outside had thrown some objects at their house during the night. The entire matter is being investigated. Neither Nishu nor their family has filed any complaint with the police. Further action will be taken based on whatever evidence emerges.

stories.title: BJP Minority Morcha chief stages shows strength with 250-car convoy:Basit Ali in Lucknow says, ‘We will puncture SP’s cycle’
stories.summary: The BJP Minority Morcha held a show of strength in Lucknow on Sunday, with its national president Basit Ali also taking part. Addressing the gathering, he said, “We will puncture the wheels of the Samajwadi Party’s cycle at every booth. There is neither distance nor a divide; Modi is our brother.” Basit Ali reached the government residence of minister Danish Azad at 2pm. Following a public meeting there, a roadshow began with a convoy of around 250 cars. The procession passed in front of the Samajwadi Party office before reaching Lal Batti Chauraha. Roadshow halted by heavy rain The convoy then travelled via Raj Bhavan to Christ Church College, where Basit Ali was scheduled to address party workers for around an hour. However, heavy rain began as soon as the convoy reached the college. Seeking shelter from the rain, the workers dispersed from the area. The convoy was supposed to continue to the BJP office, but with people leaving the area near Christ Church College because of the rain, Basit Ali, Danish Azad and other office-bearers were forced to return from there. During the roadshow, Basit Ali’s convoy could be seen stretching for around one kilometre along the road. stories.title: 85-year-old Padma Shri professor beaten by doctor at BHU:Face injured, eye turns red; PRO denies allegations
stories.summary: A case has emerged involving the alleged assault of Padma Shri awardee Professor T.K. Lahiri, who has been admitted to the ICU of Banaras Hindu University (BHU) Hospital. His niece, Ketaki, has alleged that on the night of August 29, Dr Arvind Pandey, an associate professor in the Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery, abused and slapped Professor Lahiri. Professor Lahiri suffered facial injuries in the alleged assault, while his left eye also became red following the incident. The 85-year-old professor has been in the ICU for eight months after being admitted with fluid in his lungs. Ketaki has filed a complaint with the Vice-Chancellor. Dr Pandey has denied the allegations, while the BHU administration has formed a medical board to investigate the matter. However, the medical superintendent has denied that any assault took place. He said the family had been informed several times about Professor Lahiri’s condition, but relatives did not come to care for him. Family learns about alleged incident later Professor Lahiri’s niece, Ketaki, has alleged that her uncle was mistreated in the ICU on the night of August 29. She claims Dr Pandey abused and slapped him, resulting in injuries to his face and eye. According to Ketaki, a department employee informed her about the incident on September 1. She was subsequently provided with photographs and videos showing the injury marks on Professor Lahiri. She emailed a complaint to the BHU Vice-Chancellor, IMS Director and Medical Superintendent, demanding an impartial investigation. Ketaki has also requested a medical examination of Professor Lahiri to determine whether he suffered any internal injuries in addition to the visible injuries. Dr Pandey denies slapping allegation According to Dr Arvind Pandey, Associate Professor in the Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery, Professor Lahiri was not allowing the ICU bed to be cleaned, creating a risk of infection spreading. Dr Pandey said Professor Lahiri was therefore forcibly removed from the bed as a last resort so that it could be cleaned. He denied the allegation that he had slapped the professor. Former Cardiology head demands FIR Dr Om Shankar, former head of the Department of Cardiology, has also demanded action in the matter. He said that regardless of a patient’s condition or behaviour, no one has the right to use force or assault them. He stressed that patients must be treated humanely under all circumstances and that nobody has the right to take the law into their own hands. Dr Om Shankar has demanded that an FIR be registered against the doctor accused of assault and that responsibility be fixed in the matter. Professor Lahiri admitted since January 27 Padma Shri awardee Professor T.K. Lahiri has been admitted to the BHU Hospital ICU since January 27, 2026. According to his family, he had been bedridden at home for around 15 days before being admitted to the hospital. The family alleges that the BHU administration did not provide timely information about Professor Lahiri’s illness or the alleged incident. They say they learned about the incident through a doctor from the department. Professor Lahiri admitted since January 27 Padma Shri awardee Professor T.K. Lahiri has been admitted to the BHU Hospital ICU since January 27, 2026. According to his family, he had been bedridden at home for around 15 days before being admitted to the hospital. The family alleges that the BHU administration did not provide timely information about Professor Lahiri’s illness or the alleged incident. They say they learned about the incident through a doctor from the department. Congress City President demands action At the request of Pradesh Congress Committee president Ajay Rai, city president Raghavendra Choubey visited BHU on Sunday and enquired about Professor Lahiri’s health. Choubey said that such treatment of an 85-year-old senior doctor raises serious questions about the dignity of the medical profession and human compassion. He demanded an impartial, time-bound investigation and strict action against anyone found guilty. Chanchal Sharma, Rohit Dubey, Prince Choubey and Ayush Patel were also present. Retired in 2003 but continued treating patients Professor T.K. Lahiri, born in Kolkata on January 3, 1941, retired from IMS BHU in 2003. Despite his retirement, he continued to serve patients. According to his family, he would walk from his home to the Super Speciality Block OPD to see patients. He would travel from Nariya Gate, through the lane near the NCC Battalion and past the Vice-Chancellor’s residence, before reaching the Super Speciality Block. Despite his advancing age, his dedication to serving patients remained unwavering. Received Padma Shri in 2006 Professor T.K. Lahiri was awarded the Padma Shri in 2006 for his contribution to medicine and service to patients. According to his family, he has donated a significant portion of his pension to various institutions. They also said that Professor Lahiri does not like accepting financial assistance from anyone and lives a simple life.

stories.title: SHO dies by suicide over woman’s alleged blackmail:Demanded ₹1 crore after having sex with him; she threatened to slit her wrist
stories.summary: In Basti, Station House Officer Surya Prakash Singh died by suicide after being harassed through a honey trap and blackmail. On Sunday afternoon, the police arrested the accused woman, her father, and a lawyer. The woman used to lure people into romantic relationships, make video calls to them, and engage in obscene conversations while chatting. She would then blackmail them and extort money. The accused woman also had a physical relationship with Station House Officer Surya Prakash and then began blackmailing him. She started demanding ₹1 crore from him and threatened to cut the veins in her hand if he did not pay. The police recovered a Bolero and three mobile phones from her possession. All three accused have been sent to jail. Look at the entire case Walterganj Station House Officer Surya Prakash Singh was originally a resident of Bhilampur Chhapra village in Azamgarh. He was due to retire in four years. Besides his wife, he has one son and two daughters in his family. His elder son is Sandeep Singh (30). Surya Prakash Singh had come to Basti after being transferred from Siddharthnagar. He was initially posted at the police lines here. On April 18, 2026, he was appointed in charge of Walterganj police station. On August 29, he was found hanging from a noose at his government residence near the Collectorate. Before taking his own life, he had posted a status on WhatsApp. It read: "Wealth and property are necessary, but nothing is more important than peace and love." Read the police disclosure Police caught all three in front of Sadar Hospital DIG Sanjeev Tyagi said that accused Priyanka Chaudhary, her father Ramnayan Chaudhary, and lawyer Vijay Prakash were arrested from in front of Sadar Hospital on Sunday morning. During questioning of the family members, surveillance, and examination of call detail records (CDRs), the police found that Station House Officer Surya Prakash Singh was in contact with all three accused. Lawyer Vijay Prakash collected the extortion money. Priyanka had been living separately from her husband for 10 years The police said that 32-year-old Priyanka Chaudhary, who lived in Gandhar under the jurisdiction of Walterganj police station, had separated from her husband 10 years ago. Priyanka worked at beauty parlors and spa centers in Mumbai. She lured wealthy people into romantic relationships. She would then make videos and audio recordings of them. After that, she blackmailed them through WhatsApp, video calls, and chats, demanding money. She frightened people by pretending to cut the veins in her hand According to the police, Priyanka would make video calls to people who had been lured into the trap. She would show them a scene of blood flowing after supposedly cutting the veins in her hand. In this way, she frightened people and extorted large sums of money from them. Priyanka's father, Ramnayan Chaudhary, and lawyer Vijay Prakash Yadav supported her in this. The two collected the blackmail money. They also received a share of the extorted amount, along with Priyanka. The investigation also revealed that the accused had extorted ₹2.4 million from three other people. A doctor was also among their victims. Walterganj police station in-charge Surya Prakash Singh was the accused's fourth victim. The police are now gathering information about other people who came into contact with the gang. They fell into station in-charge Priyanka's trap because they lived in the same area Station in-charge Surya Prakash Singh was posted in Walterganj. Priyanka also lived in the same area. Gradually, Priyanka and Surya Prakash Singh became acquainted with each other. They initially began meeting, and later entered into a relationship. After that, Priyanka started blackmailing Surya Prakash Singh. On the day of the incident (August 29), at 1:41 p.m., Priyanka's lawyer, Vijay Prakash, spoke to station house officer Surya Prakash Singh over the phone. She had demanded ₹1 crore. Surya Prakash Singh was unable to arrange that much money. That is why he committed suicide before paying the amount. Meanwhile, station house officer Surya Prakash Singh's son, Sandeep Singh, says that the accused should receive strict punishment.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan’s daughter Shalini ready to contest polls:‘Will definitely fight if I get the ticket’; says family ties are her strength
stories.summary: Shalini Singh, daughter of Uttar Pradesh strongman leader and former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Singh, has decided to enter politics. On Sunday, Shalini said in Bulandshahr that she has been active in the social sector in Noida for nearly 15 years. She believes in raising her voice on the right issues, rather than taking sides based on whether someone is in the ruling party or the opposition. Shalini Singh said that a leader is identified not by any position or party ticket, but by their leadership. If the party's top leadership asks her to contest an election, she will certainly enter the electoral arena. Shalini said that she is a third-year-trained member of the Rashtra Sevika Samiti (RSS) and recently completed her third-year training in Nagpur. She said that she does not want to distance herself from this ideology. On dynastic politics-family is not a weakness, but a strength Responding to criticism of nepotism because she comes from a political family, Shalini Singh said that children from political families face greater pressure to prove themselves. She said that if a family has done good work, being part of that family is not a weakness but a strength. She said that people also have higher expectations regarding the advantages that come with belonging to a political family, which is why such individuals have to work even harder to prove their capabilities. She said that from childhood, she had learned to sit among people, understand their needs, and work on their problems. Shalini said on Swatantra Bhardwaj's arrest-Let the law take its course Regarding the attack on the father of CJP worker Nishu Azad at Jantar Mantar and the arrest of the accused, Swatantra Bhardwaj, Shalini Singh said that the law is doing its work, and it is also listening to those who are raising their voices. She said that both sides should be heard in every case, and the appropriate action taken thereafter should be respected. A connection with Bihar, and love for Purvanchal too Speaking about her political future, Shalini Singh said that the place of work does not matter. If a person has the passion and ability to work, they can work anywhere. She said that she also has ties to Bihar and is Bihar's daughter-in-law. She also receives considerable affection from Purvanchal. However, she said that finding a political foothold in any particular area is not her objective. "We have come here to work. I believe we are in the role of the young leadership that the party needs." She said that the party is experiencing a generational gap, and she belongs to the generation that understands both young people and the elderly. On the Gen-Z movement: The party has brought about change, and that should be respected Speaking about the Gen-Z movement, Shalini Singh said that it could significantly narrow the gap between young people and political parties. She said that Gen-Z has put forward its voice effectively. He said that if a political party changes its policies, it should be respected. According to him, if there had been a dictatorship, the party would have stuck to its decision, but it changed its decision and tried to understand the people. He said that the narrative surrounding the issue has also changed on social media, and people are now listening to the youth. In-laws are former Bihar MPs Former MP Brij Bhushan Singh married Shalini Singh to Vishal Singh, the only son of late former MP Ajit Singh from Ara and former MP Meena Singh. Vishal Singh is a resident of Ara, Bihar, but currently lives in Noida. He is also a BJP leader. He is also the chairman of the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation (NCCF). Besides this, he is the president of the Bihar State Cooperative Marketing Union (BISCOMAUN). Shalini and Vishal have a 13-year-old son named Atharva. He has authored a book titled I Am Fearless, Not Rude.

stories.title: Well found beneath demolished mosque in UP’s Saharanpur:ASI called to examine age; Rajbhar asks Akhilesh, ‘Will you offer Fatiha there?’
stories.summary: A well was found beneath the site of a mosque after it was demolished in the Saharanpur Collectorate premises. The well is around 20 feet deep and 1.5 metres wide. It was covered with a stone slab. When the administration had the stone cut with a cutter, the well became visible. Police have covered it with an iron sheet to prevent debris from falling inside. The administration has called the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to determine how old the well is. Heavy police forces have been deployed at the spot. The area has been barricaded and no one is being allowed to enter. Vikas Tyagi, who had complained about the mosque, claimed that there might have been a temple at the site earlier and that the mosque was built after it was demolished. He demanded an investigation. Political controversy has also begun over the mosque. MP Chandrashekhar said, "We will fight this battle in the House, in court and on the streets. Why was there such a hurry to demolish the mosque?" Meanwhile, Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar wrote on X, "Akhilesh ji, will you go to Saharanpur and offer Fatiha in front of the debris of the illegal building? Uttar Pradesh is asking, Please tell us?" The mosque was demolished on Saturday after bulldozers operated for 16 hours. The debris was cleared by Sunday morning. The administration said the mosque was demolished following a court order. The mosque's side, however, alleged that it was not given an opportunity to appeal in the High Court. Advocate Babar Wasim said, “We will approach the High Court against the action.” See 3 pictures from today… Muslim clerics and representatives of the mosque claim that it was around 100 years old. They said it was mentioned in Waqf documents dating back 70 years.

stories.title: Woman returns home alive in Lucknow after 27 months:Fled in-laws' home, family had cremated unclaimed body mistaking it for missing daughter
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a family performed the last rites of a woman they believed was dead, but she returned home alive 27 months later. Twenty-eight-year-old Shivani reached her maternal home in Navikot Nandana village of BKT tehsil on September 5. Her family members were shocked to see her. About a year and a half ago, the body of an unidentified woman was found in a drain behind IIM Road. Her maternal family members identified it as Shivani. The last rites were subsequently performed at Bhainsakund. A case of dowry death was also filed against her in-laws. Now that Shivani has returned alive, the case has become complicated. The question is, whose body was found in the drain? The police have taken Shivani to the police station and are questioning her. Now, know the full story According to her maternal family, Shivani was married on April 22, 2020, to Anand Singh, a resident of Saktapur in Sitapur, at the Bhuiyan Devi Temple in BKT. After the wedding, Anand's family had a house built in Bhikhapur village of BKT. Shivani then began living there. It is alleged that after some time, Shivani's in-laws began demanding a plot of land from her. Her family refused to fulfil the demand. Meanwhile, Shivani's grandmother passed away. She came to her maternal home and told her mother about her in-laws' demand. After this, the family refused to send her back to her in-laws' home. Shivani had gone out to get her Aadhaar card, then suddenly went missing At around 9 a.m. on May 2, 2024, Shivani told her mother that she was going to the new house of her in-laws in Bhikhapur to get her Aadhaar card. She then said she would go to the Indora Bagh CHC for treatment for stomach pain. However, she did not return home until late evening. Her father, Sarvesh Singh, also known as Heegu, said, "I asked Shivani's in-laws about her. Her mother-in-law, Sheela Devi, said that Shivani had probably gone to the rented room of Anand's maternal uncle, Sushil Singh, in Bharat Nagar, Madiyaon. The family also searched for Shivani there, but she could not be found." Woman's body found in a drain after one and a half months On May 4, 2024, the family filed a missing person report for Shivani at the BKT police station. On July 16, 2024, a woman's body was found in a drain behind IIM. The body could not be identified. The police informed Shivani's family. The family went to the medical college. They identified the body as Shivani's based on the sacred thread tied around her hand and the ring on her finger. The body was cremated at Bhainsakund in the presence of the police. After this, the family filed a dowry death case against her in-laws. On September 5, Shivani suddenly arrived at her parents' home in Navikot Nandana. The family was shocked to see her. She said that she had been living in the Para area all this time. Her family informed the police. The police took Shivani to the station, where she is being questioned. Shivani had been living with Javed According to the police, Shivani had been living with a young man named Javed in Para. Javed looks after a municipal corporation toilet. Shivani said that she had met Javed in Para itself. Javed had repeatedly asked her to return home, but she did not go back. The police are now trying to contact Javed. They are also investigating where Shivani had been staying all this time. At the same time, they are trying to determine whose body was found in the drain. The BKT police station in-charge said- The family members themselves had identified the woman's body as that of Shivani. The body was subsequently cremated. Now that Shivani has appeared, the entire case is being reinvestigated.

stories.title: SP leader protests by standing in pothole:Says Hindu-Muslim politics ruined the city, fills pothole himself
stories.summary: Akhlas Ahmed alias Sonu, president of the Jajmau Traders' Association, staged an unusual protest against the poor condition of roads in Kanpur and the negligence of the departments concerned. He climbed into a nearly six-foot-deep pothole on Jajmau's VIP Road and protested for 30 minutes. Even after the protest, officials took no notice of the issue. Taking a dig at the government, he said that the city had been turned into hell by focusing on Hindu-Muslim issues. Responsible officials from all departments, including the Municipal Corporation and the Jal Nigam, have maintained silence. When no action was taken even after the protest, he spent ₹12,000 from his own pocket to get the pothole repaired. Pothole had appeared on VIP Road leading to Circuit House The six-foot-deep pothole near Purani Chungi on the VIP Road from Jajmau to Circuit House had existed for the past four months. Local residents had complained several times to officials of the Municipal Corporation and the Jal Nigam, but no permanent solution was found. Two-wheelers and e-rickshaws were frequently overturning because of the pothole. Several pedestrians had also been injured as a result. Because of this problem, Akhlas Ahmed climbed into the pothole on Saturday and protested for about 30 minutes. He claims that his health deteriorated due to the gas emanating from the pothole during the protest. His colleagues immediately took him to a nearby private hospital, where he received treatment. Despite this, instead of backing down, he decided to have the pothole filled himself. According to Akhlas, he spent around ₹12,000 from Saturday night until 7 a.m. Sunday. He had two tractor-trolleys of soil dumped into the pothole and then had the road paved with cement and sand. He says this will provide relief to pedestrians and reduce the risk of accidents.

stories.title: CM Yogi reprimands leaders on stage in Chitrakoot:Video surfaces as local politicians jostle for photos during flood relief check distribution
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath strongly reprimanded leaders on stage during a programme in Chitrakoot on Sunday, September 6, after they began competing to get their photographs taken with him while he was distributing relief cheques to the poor. Seeing this, the Chief Minister gestured to the leaders to move back so that the poor would not face difficulty moving around. The CM said – "The people of Chitrakoot will not be left alone. The government stands with you in this hour of crisis. Families whose homes have been completely washed away will be provided houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana or the Chief Minister Housing Scheme. Needy families who do not have land will be given residential leases." Earlier, CM Yogi conducted an aerial survey of the flood-affected areas of Chitrakoot and assessed the rising water level of the Mandakini River. He then met flood victims staying in relief shelters. He distributed relief kits weighing 50 kg each to 800 affected families. The kits contained lentils, rice, flour, potatoes, buckets, and umbrellas. He listened to the problems of the affected families and gave chocolates to the children. He told the officials that there must be no negligence of any kind in delivering relief. See 3 pictures – 2 major things said by CM Yogi- 1- The flood was devastating, but by the blessings of Kamta Nath, no one lost their life The CM said, "This time, the water level of the Mandakini River had reached a dangerous level. The severity of the flood can be gauged from the fact that a bridge built over the river in the neighbouring state of Madhya Pradesh was also washed away. Despite this, no one lost their life in Chitrakoot. This is due to the blessings of Kamta Nath. The government and administration began relief and rescue efforts in time and provided assistance to the affected people." 2- Before 2017, people received very little relief during floods No person affected by the floods will be left without assistance. Before 2017, people received very little relief during floods. Now the government has expanded relief arrangements. Our aim is not only to provide immediate assistance but also to rehabilitate affected families. Floods in Chitrakoot affect 14,000 people in 36 villages

stories.title: Ghat dome collapses in Gorakhpur, killing a lawyer:Advocates stage 2-hour protest at district hospital, vandalise ambulance; another victim critical
stories.summary: A dome-shaped canopy on the banks of the Rapti River in Gorakhpur collapsed at around 11:30 am on Sunday, killing a lawyer and seriously injuring another. People nearby removed the debris and pulled both men out, but it is alleged that an ambulance called after the incident did not reach the spot for nearly half an hour, following which they were placed on a sheet and taken to the district hospital in an e-rickshaw. Doctors later referred Alok Asthana to the medical college after finding his condition critical. Alok Asthana died on the way. After his body was brought to the district hospital in an ambulance, a large number of lawyers arrived and began protesting. Angry lawyers also vandalised the ambulance. The protest has continued for around two hours. The city SP, CO, and police personnel from several police stations are present at the scene. The accident occurred at Gorakhnath Ghat, built along the Rapti River, about 4 kilometres from the district headquarters. More than eight platforms have been constructed here for people attending funeral ceremonies to sit. These platforms also have dome-shaped shelters. On Sunday, one of the shelters suddenly collapsed. The deceased lawyer has been identified as 45-year-old Alok Asthana. His wife filed a complaint at the police station, accusing the doctors of failing to provide timely treatment. He said, “When I called the CMO, he said, ‘Ten people die here every day. What difference will it make if one more dies?’” See the pictures... Know the full story... Advocate Alok Asthana (45), a resident of Raptinagar in Gorakhpur, originally hailed from Santhu village in Kushinagar. He had been practising at the civil court for nearly 20 years. His family includes his wife, Shalini, son Aditya, daughter Siddhi, and younger brother. His son, Aditya, is pursuing a B.Tech degree at NIT Punjab, while his daughter, Siddhi, is in the first year of her graduation. His younger brother lives in Basti and works as a medical representative (MR). According to family members, at around 10 a.m. on Sunday, Alok went by motorcycle to the house of his associate, advocate Vinod Tiwari. Vinod's mother had passed away. After this, he reached Gorakhnath Ghat on the Rapti River to attend the funeral. During the funeral, Alok Asthana was sitting with advocate Sanjay Singh, a resident of Shaktinagar, under the dome-shaped awning built over the platform at the ghat. Meanwhile, the awning suddenly collapsed onto both of them. The two advocates were buried under the debris. People present nearby removed the debris and pulled them out. People said that an ambulance was called immediately after the accident, but it did not arrive at the scene for nearly half an hour. After that, both injured men were placed on a sheet and taken to the district hospital in an e-rickshaw. Wife accuses doctors of negligence in treatment Shalini Asthana, wife of advocate Alok Asthana, submitted a complaint at the Kotwali police station. In it, she alleged that her husband Alok and advocate Sanjay Singh were brought to the district hospital in critical condition, but the doctors did not treat them and referred them directly to the medical college. Alok died while being taken to the medical college. After Alok's death, his family members reached the district hospital with his body. A large number of his fellow advocates also gathered there. As soon as they learnt of the death, the enraged advocates began protesting and vandalised an ambulance. Shalini Asthana alleged that her husband died due to lack of treatment. She also claimed to have contacted the CMO several times. According to the wife, the CMO allegedly said, "Ten people die here every day; what difference would it make if one more died?" She alleged that the CMO and doctors at the district hospital deliberately failed to provide treatment, resulting in her husband's death. Protest continues for 2 hours Meanwhile, the protest by advocates at the district hospital has continued for nearly two hours. The protesters remain firm on their demand for action against the CMO and doctors. The city SP, CO, and police from several police stations are present at the scene. DM Says Lightning Strike Suspected DM Deepak Meena said that a family had arrived at Rajghat for a cremation. During this time, advocates Alok Asthana and Sanjay Singh were sitting at a dome-shaped seating area. According to local residents, a strong jolt occurred there due to a lightning strike, causing the slab to collapse and injuring both advocates. The DM said that Alok Asthana was seriously injured, while Sanjay Singh also sustained injuries. Alok Asthana died during treatment. Sanjay Singh is still undergoing treatment. He said that local residents and family members had complained about a delay in the ambulance's arrival. The ambulance's response time is being investigated. If any negligence is found at any level during the investigation, action will be taken against those responsible. The Chief Minister inaugurated the ghat in 2021 The dome that collapsed and caused the accident was constructed by the Irrigation Department. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated Guru Gorakhnath Ghat on February 16, 2021. Questions have also been raised in the past about the quality of the ghat's construction. This is reportedly why the Municipal Corporation has not yet taken over the ghat. However, the Municipal Corporation carries out cleaning work here. The ghat was beautified at a cost of ₹27.85 crore The proposal for the beautification of Guru Gorakhnath Ghat was prepared in 2019. The ghat was beautified at a cost of approximately ₹27 crore 85 lakh 71 thousand. Ram Ghat was also constructed on the other side of the Rapti River at a cost of approximately ₹21 crore. At Guru Gorakhnath Ghat, domed-roof platforms had been built at various places for people attending cremation ceremonies to sit. On Sunday, one of these domes collapsed, trapping two advocates beneath it. Films have also been shot at the ghat Several films have been shot at Guru Gorakhnath Ghat. The shooting of MP Ravi Kishan's film 'Mahadev Ka Gorakhpur' also took place at this ghat. In addition, the ghat has been used for shooting other films as well.

stories.title: House collapses in Kanpur, killing father and 3 daughters:One daughter injured, only family member left; her wedding is in 2 months
stories.summary: Four members of the same family were killed and one person was seriously injured after a mud house collapsed in Kanpur on Sunday amid heavy rain. The house suddenly collapsed at around 9:30 am, trapping the father, Mukesh (45), and his four daughters under the debris. After hearing an explosion-like sound, nearby residents rushed out, began clearing the debris and informed the police and administration. After about two hours, all five were rescued and taken to a Community Health Centre, where doctors declared Mukesh and his daughters Maya (16), Neetu (12) and Pallavi (7) dead. The eldest daughter, Kajal (19), remains in critical condition and is undergoing treatment. She is now the only surviving member of the family. She is due to get married in two months. Her mother had died of an illness long ago. The incident took place in Hirni village under the Saadh police station area, 40 km from the district headquarters. Father lived with his four daughters in a two-storey mud house According to the police, Mukesh, who lived in Hirni village, supported his family by working as a labourer. His wife had passed away. He lived with his four daughters in a two-storey mud house. Everyone was at home on Sunday morning when the house suddenly collapsed. Villagers, together with the police, rescued all five people and took them to the nearest community health centre. However, by then, four of them had died. The eldest daughter, Kajal, was referred to Kanpur District Hospital because of her critical condition. She is currently undergoing treatment there. Called the police, but they did not arrive on time Villagers said, ‘The accident occurred due to continuous rain’ The villagers said that it had been raining continuously for the past several days. As a result, the walls and roof of the mud house had weakened. The accident occurred during the rain on Sunday. The police and administration teams also reached the spot and gathered information about the incident.

stories.title: BRICS chief justices visit Taj Mahal:Delegation also visits Agra Fort; 65-member team arrives in Agra
stories.summary: Amid rain on Sunday, a 65-member judicial delegation from more than 10 countries, including the Chief Justices of the BRICS nations, visited the Taj Mahal in Agra. The foreign guests arrived carrying umbrellas and admired the monument’s architectural design and intricate carvings despite the rain, later visiting Agra Fort and taking photographs with the Taj Mahal; the cool weather also allowed them to enjoy Agra’s climate. The delegation came to India to attend the BRICS Chief Justices Forum. The forum was held in New Delhi from September 4 to 6 under India's chairmanship. Chief justices and senior judicial officials from BRICS and participating countries took part in it. The forum was hosted by the Supreme Court of India. Discussion Held on the Justice System and Judicial Cooperation Meetings held in New Delhi included discussions on the justice systems of different countries, the rule of law, judicial cooperation, and the use of modern technology. Representatives shared judicial experiences from their respective countries. The meeting also focused on strengthening legal and judicial cooperation at the international level. Representatives from Russia, China and these countries The 65-member delegation that arrived in Agra included chief justices and senior judicial officials from more than 10 countries, including Russia, China, the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, South Africa and Indonesia. After meetings in Delhi, the delegation arrived in Agra on Sunday. Despite the rain, they visited the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort. Security arrangements were made at both monuments in view of the foreign guests' visit.

stories.title: Moving AC bus catches fire in Lucknow:Tyre bursts on Shaheed Path; carrying 30 passengers from Gorakhpur to Delhi
stories.summary: A double-decker AC bus caught fire while travelling on Shaheed Path in Lucknow, with the flames engulfing the entire bus within minutes and triggering panic among passengers. The bus was travelling from Gorakhpur to Surat with 30 passengers on board, all of whom hurriedly got off and ran to safety. The incident occurred at around 12:30 a.m. in front of Medanta Hospital. A police investigation revealed that the bus's rear tire had burst. Sparks then flew out, causing the fire to flare up. Upon receiving the information, three fire brigade vehicles reached the spot. At that time, the entire bus was ablaze. Flames rising about 20 feet high could be seen. The firefighters brought the fire under control in 30 minutes. See pictures of the fire- Driver said-He heard a breaking sound from the back of the bus, then it caught fire Driver Rahul Patel, a resident of Orai, said, "I left Gorakhpur with the bus at 5 p.m. on Saturday. As soon as I reached in front of Medanta Hospital, I heard something breaking from the rear section of the bus. Shortly afterward, it caught fire. I stopped the bus and asked all the passengers to get off. All the passengers got out safely. The police were then informed." Upon receiving the information, ADCP Rallapalli Vasanth Kumar arrived with his force. The police stopped traffic in both directions. Fire engines brought the blaze under control, but by then the bus had been completely burnt. SFO Mabad Chand Gujjar said that the fire was extinguished in time. No passenger was injured in the incident. The driver's quick thinking prevented a major accident. Traffic jam on highway after accident The accident caused a traffic jam on the highway. Traffic police diverted the vehicles and sent them via an alternative route. After the fire was extinguished, the police called a crane and had the bus removed from Shaheed Path. The traffic jam was cleared afterward. A passenger on the bus said, We were sleeping when the fire broke out. We woke up only after the driver shouted. After that, we got off the bus. All the passengers are safe.

stories.title: Crorepati medicine trader murdered in Kanpur:2 suspects seen entering flat; wife is marriage counsellor, son and daughter-in-law were at party
stories.summary: In Kanpur, a millionaire pharma businessman was allegedly killed by his employee and an accomplice. Police arrested both after an encounter in which they sustained bullet injuries to their legs. The arrested accused have been identified as Vishal Gautam and Raj Kishori. Vishal worked as the businessman’s employee. During questioning, he allegedly told police that they had killed the businessman at the behest of his daughter-in-law, who had promised them money. Earlier, the businessman’s body was found lying in a pool of blood on the floor of his flat. Blood was splattered across the room. According to police, his throat had been slit with a sharp weapon and he had suffered multiple injuries from a pointed object. The incident took place at Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur, an upscale area of the city. The murder occurred between 10.30pm on Saturday and 3am. At the time, the businessman’s son, daughter-in-law and grandson had gone to a party. When the family returned at around 3am, they found the main door of the flat open. They went inside and found the 63-year-old businessman’s body. The family informed police, who reached the spot. Police examined CCTV footage from inside the flat, which showed two suspects entering the premises. Based on the footage, the two were detained for questioning. Investigators also examined CCTV footage from the apartment’s main entrance and surrounding areas and seized the apartment’s entry register. See 2 pictures related to the incident… Know the full case... The medicine trader, 63-year-old Vineet Vinocha, lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment in the city. He was a wholesale medicine dealer. He ran a medicine firm named 'Pharma Traders' on Birhana Road in the city and managed the business along with his son, Subrat. His family includes his wife Punita, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Vineet's wife Punita is a marriage counsellor and had travelled to Ghaziabad around a week earlier. His daughter Subhani and son-in-law live in Gurugram. Both are engineers. Returned from party to find father's body lying on the floor Vineet's samdhi, Naresh Arora, a resident of Thakurganj in Lucknow, said, "At around 10:30pm on Saturday, my daughter Shalu, Subrat and their son Shrijay went to a party. When the three of them returned home at around 3am, they found Vineet's blood-soaked body lying on the floor inside." There were marks of knife attacks on Vineet's body. Subrat then informed the police. As soon as they received the information, Kalyanpur police reached the spot. A forensic team also examined the crime scene and collected evidence. Vineet was a wholesale medicine distributor, ran business with son The deceased businessman, Vineet Vinocha, lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment. The four-bedroom flat, which also has a dining room, is reportedly worth more than ₹1 crore. Vineet ran a pharmaceutical firm called ‘Pharma Traders’ on Birhana Road and managed the business with his son, Subrat. His family includes his wife Puneeta, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Puneeta is a marriage counsellor and had been in Ghaziabad for a week. Their daughter Subhani and son-in-law, who are both engineers, live in Gurugram. Neighbours had no idea the murder had taken place Naresh Arora, the father-in-law of Lucknow resident Vineet, said his daughter called him early on Sunday to inform him about the incident. She told him that she had left home with her husband and son at around 10.30pm. When the three returned at 3am, they found Vineet’s body lying inside the flat. Her husband then called neighbour Pankaj Tiwari and others. When the neighbours arrived and saw the body, they were shocked. Pankaj said they had no idea the incident had taken place, even though his house was right next to Vineet’s. Signs of struggle found inside room The forensic team collected evidence from the scene. Vineet’s body was found in the room where he slept. The bedsheet was stained with blood, while blood was also found on the floor. Signs of a struggle were found inside the room. During the initial investigation, police suspect that Vineet was attacked suddenly. After being attacked, he may have tried to escape, leading to a struggle inside the room. The attacker then allegedly killed him. No other belongings in the room appeared to have been disturbed, leading police to suspect that the attacker’s sole motive was murder. Police suspect businessman opened door for someone he knew Police suspect that Vineet may have opened the door himself for someone he knew. This is because when his family returned from the party at around 3am, they found the main door of the flat open. Police are now trying to determine who had come to meet Vineet and whether the same person was responsible for the murder. Two suspects seen on CCTV ACP Dileep Singh said police had found several important leads during the investigation. CCTV footage showed two people entering the house, and both have been detained. Police are also questioning domestic staff. The accused allegedly slit the victim’s throat and stabbed him multiple times across his body. This indicates that the murder was not committed with the intention of robbery. Police suspect the killing may have been carried out due to an old enmity. The DVR has been seized and the footage is being examined. A case has been registered based on the victim’s son’s complaint. Police said the case would be solved soon. Pharma business spans three generations Rajendra Saini, president of the Kanpur Drug Traders Association and state general secretary of the UP Retail Chemists and Distributors Association (RCDA), said businessman Vineet was among Kanpur’s top five pharmaceutical traders. He said Vineet’s family had been in the pharmaceutical business for three generations. His father ran the business first, followed by Vineet, and his son Subrat now manages it. The family has operated a shop under the name Pharma Traders in the Birhana Road medicine market since 1968. Saini condemned Vineet’s brutal murder and said the incident had sparked anger among pharmaceutical traders over their safety. He urged police to solve the murder soon and send the accused to jail. Employees says, ‘Boss never deducted even a rupee from our salaries’ Twenty-two employees work at Vineet’s firm. As soon as they learnt about his murder, several employees, including Aditya and Anurag, reached the post-mortem house. “Our boss Vineet never deducted even a single rupee from our salaries. He was very cheerful by nature. Even when he scolded us, there was always warmth and affection in his words,” the employees said. Businessman’s mother cries, ‘Bring my Vineet back’ The businessman’s body was taken to Bhairav Ghat for the last rites. Seeing her son’s body, his elderly mother, Chanchal, broke down in tears. “Bring my Vineet back. Why is my son sleeping? Wake him up. Why is my Vineet sleeping?” she cried. Vineet is survived by his younger brother, Puneet, who lives in Nawabganj’s Signature City and runs a laptop shop on Mall Road.

stories.title: 6 killed including siblings in Sambhal:Youth decapitated in head-on collision between dumper and tempo on highway
stories.summary: A sand-laden dumper collided with a tempo in Sambhal, Uttar Pradesh, on Sunday. Six people, including two young siblings, were killed in the accident, while four others were injured. The collision was so severe that the front portion of the tempo was badly damaged and the driver became trapped inside. The dumper also went out of control, hit a roadside tree and overturned. According to eyewitnesses, the tempo was travelling in its lane. An e-rickshaw travelling ahead suddenly took a U-turn. As the dumper driver tried to avoid it, he lost control and collided with the tempo. The tempo was thrown around 10 feet away by the impact. Bodies were scattered across the road. One young man's head was severed from his body. Hearing the screams, local residents rushed to the spot. They pulled the injured to the side of the road. Police reached the spot and sent the injured to Bahjoi CHC by ambulance, where doctors declared four more people dead. The deceased were identified as siblings Aaradhya, 3 months, and Dhruv, 6, their maternal aunt Rohini, 20, tempo driver Saudaan Pal, 40, Ruvaid, 30, and Rampal, 35. The accident took place at around 9am on the Agra-Moradabad National Highway in the Bahjoi police station area, around 2 km from the district headquarters. See the pictures of the accident- Now, understand the full case step by step- SP Vikas Chandra Tripathi said, The accident took place on the Bahjoi-Chandausi road. Police reached the spot immediately. The deaths of six people have been confirmed. The other four injured people are undergoing treatment. An investigation into the matter has been launched. Further legal action will be taken based on whatever emerges from the investigation.

stories.title: Technical education service exam begins in Varanasi:Over 16,000 candidates appear; entry allowed after three-layer security check
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) Technical Education (Teaching) Service Examination-2025 has begun in Varanasi. A total of 16,129 candidates are appearing for the examination. For this, 36 examination centres have been set up across the city. The examination is being conducted in two shifts. First shift examination underway The first shift is being held from 9am to 11am. Candidates were required to reach their centres by 7:30am. Before being allowed to enter through the centre gates, candidates underwent security checks and biometric verification. Thousands of candidates to appear in the second shift The second shift will be held from 2:30pm to 5pm. Candidates are required to reach their centres by 1pm. A total of 16,129 candidates are appearing across both shifts. Entry only after three-level security checks Special security arrangements have been made at the examination centres. Candidates are being checked at three levels. They are being allowed inside only after biometric verification and approval from the police and examination inspectors. 36 sector magistrates and 36 static magistrates deployed To monitor the examination, 36 sector magistrates and 36 static magistrates have been deployed. Surveillance is also being maintained around the examination centres. Photocopy shops closed within 200-metre radius To maintain the confidentiality of the examination, photocopy shops within a 200-metre radius of the centres have been ordered to remain closed.

stories.title: Technical education teaching exam today at 44 centres in Gorakhpur:19,496 candidates to appear in two shifts; CCTV surveillance
stories.summary: The Gorakhpur district administration has completed preparations for the Technical Education Teaching Examination-2026, with 19,496 candidates set to appear for the exam at 44 centres across the district on Sunday, September 6. The examination will be conducted in two shifts, with arrangements made for security, monitoring, traffic management and essential facilities to ensure it is held peacefully, fairly and transparently. In view of the large number of candidates appearing, separate sector magistrates have been appointed for both shifts. The sector magistrates will continuously inspect the examination centres in their respective areas. Officials will also visit the centres before the examination begins to check the arrangements. If any problem arises during the examination, the concerned officials will take immediate action. Monitoring to Be Conducted Through CCTV Cameras To maintain transparency in the examination, surveillance through CCTV cameras has been arranged at all examination centres. Activities taking place inside the centres during the examination will be monitored. A centre superintendent, room invigilators, and other staff have been deployed at each centre. Officials have been instructed to ensure that there is no negligence in maintaining the confidentiality of the examination and enforcing the prescribed rules. Gajendra Kumar, Nodal Examination Officer and ADM City, said that all necessary arrangements have been made to conduct the examination with complete transparency and integrity. The responsibilities of the officials and staff associated with the examination have been explained to them. Adequate Police Force Will Be Deployed at the Centers Considering that more than 19,000 candidates will take part, adequate police personnel will be deployed at all examination centres. Police officers will also manage security arrangements around the centres. Instructions have been issued to control crowds and monitor any suspicious activity. Security arrangements have also been strengthened to prevent cheating or any other improper activity. Police and administrative teams will also monitor the areas outside the examination centres. Special arrangements have been made to prevent unnecessary crowds from gathering around the centres due to people accompanying the candidates. The administration has appealed to people not to gather around the examination centres and to cooperate in maintaining order. Traffic arrangements also under watch to avoid congestion The arrival of thousands of candidates at examination centres at the same time and their return after the examination could increase traffic pressure on the city's major roads. In view of this, the traffic police have also made special arrangements. Police personnel will be deployed at major examination centres and on nearby routes to prevent traffic jams as candidates arrive and depart. The administration has appealed to candidates to reach the examination centre well in advance so that last-minute crowds and traffic problems can be avoided. Arrangements for Electricity, Water, and Cleanliness Also Made Arrangements for electricity, drinking water, and cleanliness have been ensured at all examination centres. The concerned officials have also been instructed to monitor these arrangements on the day of the examination. If any problem arises at a centre, it will be resolved immediately. Candidates have been advised to reach the examination centre well before the scheduled time. They must carry valid identification and all prescribed documents related to the examination. They should not bring any prohibited items to the centre and must follow all rules from entry until the examination concludes. ADM City Gajendra Kumar said that conducting the examination peacefully, fairly, and transparently is the district administration's priority. All departments have been instructed to work in coordination with one another. There must be no negligence at any level in security, traffic management, or examination arrangements. If any irregularity or inappropriate activity comes to light, action will be taken in accordance with the rules.
