stories.title: 400-metre bypass submerged in UP’s Shravasti:Funeral pyres burn on road in Prayagraj; rain in Meerut-Ghaziabad; alert in all 75 districts
stories.summary: Monsoon rainfall continues across Uttar Pradesh. Intermittent rain has been reported in 10 cities, including Ghaziabad, Meerut, Agra and Bareilly, since Sunday morning. In Shravasti, so much rain fell that a 400-metre stretch of the bypass was submerged. In Bijnor, roads and lanes have turned into ponds, with water entering homes to a depth of 2-3 feet. Rivers are in spate due to the continuous rainfall. As many as 26 districts, including Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur and Ayodhya, are affected by floods. In Prayagraj, people are having to wait to perform last rites at the Daraganj crematorium because it is flooded. They are being forced to cremate bodies at elevated spots along the roadside. In Varanasi and Kanpur, rising water levels in the Ganga have caused floodwater to enter people's homes. Residents are being forced to stay on rooftops. Yogi had conducted an aerial survey of the affected areas of Kashi on Saturday. A rain alert has been issued across all 75 districts of the state today. Bijnor has been witnessing intermittent heavy rain for the past three days, disrupting normal life. The rising water levels of the Ganga and Malan rivers have increased concerns among residents, while several roads across the district have been waterlogged by one to two feet, causing inconvenience to commuters. Power supply was also affected in several areas. On Saturday, a teenager drowned in a drain in Kiratpur, while two livestock died after being struck by lightning in Chandpur. See pictures of the rain and flooding... Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, The monsoon system formed near Rajasthan, close to eastern Uttar Pradesh, will turn eastward after 24 hours. As a result, some areas of eastern Uttar Pradesh will receive heavy rain between September 6 and 8. After September 8, this system responsible for the rain will weaken. Consequently, heavy rain will stop across the state. However, light rain or showers may continue in some places.

stories.title: Power minister says ‘Enjoy when electricity goes out':Smiles and walks away when asked about wire theft in UP's Mau
stories.summary: Energy Minister A.K. Sharma arrived in Mau on Saturday (5 Sept). When asked a question related to electricity, he said, “If the power goes out, enjoy it.” After saying this, the minister moved on. He was asked about the theft of wires from a 33,000-volt high-tension line in the Gontha substation and Dargah area. However, the minister did not answer the question. A.K. Sharma had attended an educational seminar and teacher felicitation ceremony organized at the Gontha Primary School. Read what A.K. Sharma said in response to questions related to electricity... Reporter: Minister, the wire on the poles has gone missing for up to 3 kilometers in the district. A.K. Sharma: Where is your home? Reporter: Right here in Mau. A.K. Sharma: Does the electricity go out? Reporter: Yes, sir, it does. A.K. Sharma: Enjoy the electricity. Wires from a 33-kilovolt high-tension line had been stolen. After this, he moved on. In fact, wires from the 33-kilovolt high-tension line were stolen from the Gotha substation on August 20. The Energy Minister was questioned at 5 p.m. on Saturday (5 Sept) as he was leaving the event. Villagers Anurag, Surendra, and Ramesh say that when electricity department officials themselves claim to be unaware of such a major incident, it is right to question the Energy Minister. Since the matter concerns the minister's home district, it is necessary to demand an explanation from him about the system.

stories.title: Former UP Dy-CM Dinesh Sharma appointed Andaman Nicobar LG:BJP Rajya Sabha MP replaces Admiral D.K. Joshi
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and current Rajya Sabha MP Dr Dinesh Sharma has been appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. He will replace Admiral D.K. Joshi (Retd.). Sharma’s current Rajya Sabha term has around two months remaining and is due to end in November 2026. Sharma thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for appointing him to the post. Tenure as Lucknow mayor and UP deputy CM Sharma served as Mayor of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation from 2007 to 2017. He was appointed Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 2017 and held the post until March 2022. He was elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2023. BJP’s prominent Brahmin face in Awadh Sharma has been actively involved in politics since 1998 and has held various organisational and political positions over the years. His appointment as Lieutenant Governor is also being viewed as an outreach to Uttar Pradesh’s Brahmin community. In the Awadh region, Sharma is considered one of the BJP’s prominent Brahmin leaders. BJP UP in-charge Vinod Tawde congratulates him Uttar Pradesh BJP in-charge Vinod Tawde congratulated Dr. Dinesh Sharma. Writing on social media platform X, he said: “Heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to Dr. Dinesh Sharma ji, former Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, current Rajya Sabha MP, and senior BJP leader, on being appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. I am confident that your able leadership and experience will give new direction and momentum to the development of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.” Who is Dr. Dinesh Sharma? Dr. Dinesh Sharma was born on January 12, 1964, in Lucknow, the state capital. He comes from a traditional Brahmin family in Lucknow. His father, Kedar Nath Sharma (Padha Ji), was an RSS and Jan Sangh worker. Dr. Dinesh Sharma studied at Lucknow University and later served as a professor there. During his tenure as a professor, he supervised more than 20 students for their PhDs and authored six books. Dinesh Sharma Remained in Office Continuously for Three Decades Former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and Rajya Sabha member Dr. Dinesh Sharma has been actively involved in politics for the past three decades. Since then, he has held various positions in the government and the party organization. He served as the state president of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha from 1993 to 1998. He served as the chairman of the National Youth Commission. He also held various other positions, including vice-chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Corporation. He served as the mayor of Lucknow from 2007 to March 2017. In 2014, he was appointed national vice-president of the BJP. That same year, he was appointed national convener of the BJP's membership drive. He served as Uttar Pradesh's Deputy Chief Minister from 2017 to 2022. In 2023, he was elected to the Rajya Sabha again. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, he was appointed the BJP's election in-charge for Maharashtra.

stories.title: Muslim clerics to move HC over demolition in Saharanpur:100-year-old mosque razed; Maulana asks, 'Are only masjid, madrasas, or shrines illegal?'
stories.summary: A mosque built on the Saharanpur Collectorate premises was completely demolished after a bulldozer operation that lasted around 16 hours. The demolition began at around 4 am on Saturday and continued until about 9 pm. The administration said the mosque had been illegally built on government land and was removed after following due legal procedure. Muslim clerics and members of the mosque committee, however, have questioned the action. They claim the mosque was more than 100 years old and existed before the present Collectorate building was constructed. They also claim that the mosque and the Collectorate premises are recorded under the same khasra (land survey) number. The Muslim side has cited old revenue records and other documents to challenge the administration’s claim that the mosque was an illegal structure. They have also questioned the timing of the demolition and the legal process followed. They claim they were not given enough time to approach a higher court after the City Magistrate’s order. According to them, six bulldozers were brought in at night, and the mosque was demolished before the matter could be taken to the High Court. The mosque’s legal representatives have now said they will approach the High Court. Read the report on this entire action... Mosque committee claims it existed before 1911 Muslim clerics and the mosque committee claim the structure was more than 100 years old and existed before the present Collectorate building. The mosque side reportedly presented a power bill dated January 1, 1911, as an old record. It has also claimed that the mosque has been registered with the Sunni Waqf Board for around 70 years. Congress MP Imran Masood also claimed that the mosque existed before 1911. According to him, old records show the land ownership in the names of Waheed Khan and Yakub Khan. Administration questions authenticity of 1911 power bill The administration has questioned the claim regarding the 1911 electricity bill. Officials said electricity supply began in Saharanpur around 1922, raising questions about the authenticity of a bill dated 1911. The mosque side, however, says the bill was obtained from a government website and had been presented before the court as an old record. The mosque side has also raised questions over the khasra number of the land. Maulana Qari Ishaq Gora claims that the mosque and the entire Collectorate premises are recorded under the same khasra number. The mosque committee has questioned how only the mosque could be declared an illegal structure if both properties fall under the same land record. It has demanded that this aspect also be examined. Muslim side cites 1926 revenue record Advocate Babar Wasim, who represented the mosque side, said a 1926 Fasli Khewat revenue record was presented before the court. According to him, the document lists Yakub Khan as the owner of the land and the Collectorate as the occupant. Wasim said the land covered around 24 bighas at the time. The area included the present Collectorate premises. Around eight bighas were used for the Collectorate building and its premises, while the remaining 16 bighas included the kotyard and mosque area, he claimed. According to the mosque side, the record described the Collectorate as an occupant rather than the owner of the land. Rent receipts and 1995 agreement also cited According to advocate Babar Wasim, records show that the post office operating from the Collectorate premises had paid rent for the mosque. He said the post office initially paid Rs 500 per month, which was increased to Rs 1,500 per month after an agreement in 1995. However, rent receipts from before 1995 were not presented as part of the records, he said. The mosque side argues that if the structure was completely illegal, the existence of rent payments and other government records over such a long period should also have been examined. The mosque side further claims that municipal tax had been imposed on the mosque since the municipality was formed in 1962 and that the tax was regularly paid. It says municipal documents were also presented before the court, but alleges that they were not accepted as evidence. Another key claim relates to Waqf records. According to advocate Babar Wasim, the mosque property has been registered with the Waqf Board since 1955 and has a Waqf number. An affidavit was also submitted by Tanveer, the mosque’s mutawalli (caretaker), according to the mosque side. Five other witnesses also submitted affidavits. Wasim alleged that these witnesses were not formally examined by the court. Dispute began with Bajrang Dal complaint in February 2025 The mosque was spread across around 3,300 square feet within the Collectorate premises. The two-storey structure had five rooms and two large halls. The ground floor had a large hall and two rooms, while the first floor had a hall and a large room. The post office was operating from the room, according to the report. On February 10, 2025, former Bajrang Dal state coordinator Vikas Tyagi complained to the District Magistrate, alleging that the mosque was an illegal structure. The complaint also alleged that rent was being collected from rooms on the mosque premises and from the post office. Following the complaint, the District Magistrate ordered a probe by a magistrate. The investigation concluded that the mosque was illegal, according to the administration. City Magistrate declares mosque illegal on July 16 On March 24, 2025, the administration filed a petition before the City Magistrate’s Court. On July 16, 2026, the court declared the mosque illegal and ordered its removal. It also ordered recovery of Rs 6.41 crore as compensation. The occupants were given 30 days to comply. On July 20, the mosque side filed a petition in the District Court challenging the magistrate’s order. On July 24, the District Court stayed the magistrate’s order and continued with the hearing. On September 2, District Judge Satendra Kumar upheld the City Magistrate’s demolition order and dismissed the mosque side’s petition. The administration then began preparations for the demolition. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers around the Collectorate premises to prevent any possible protest or law-and-order situation. Six bulldozers brought in after night-time security operation Security was increased around the Collectorate at around 11 pm on September 4. Around 300 police and Provincial Armed Constabulary personnel were deployed around the mosque. The demolition began at around 4 am on Saturday, September 5, with around six bulldozers brought to the site. After around 16 hours of work, the mosque was completely demolished and the debris was removed from the premises. Around 200 security personnel were deployed during the operation, according to the report. The surrounding borders were also sealed to prevent opposition leaders from entering the area. Local opposition leaders were placed under house arrest during the night, the report said. Mosque side plans to approach High Court The demolition has ended the physical structure but not the legal dispute. Advocate Babar Wasim, who represented the mosque side, said a writ petition would be filed in the High Court. The petition will seek consideration of the documents and evidence that were presented before the lower court. The mosque side will also seek action in accordance with the law, he said. Maulana Qari Ishaq Gora asked: Are only mosques, madrasas, or shrines illegal? Maulana Qari Ishaq Gora: ‘Are only mosques, madrasas and shrines illegal?’ Question: What do you have to say about the mosque that was demolished? Answer: The City Magistrate’s Court declared it illegal. I do not know on what basis it did so or what evidence the committee was able to present. This is certainly a day of grief not only for Saharanpur but for the entire country. There could also be a political angle behind the demolition of a mosque that was around 100 years old. We should have been given time to present our case before the court, but we were not given enough time to follow the legal process. The bulldozers were brought in so quickly. The question is: are only mosques, madrasas and shrines illegal? Are Muslims being treated unfairly? Question: It is being claimed that the mosque and the entire Collectorate premises have the same khasra number. Does that mean the Collectorate is also illegal? Answer: Everyone knows that the entire Collectorate area has the same khasra number. According to the information available, the Collectorate was built later and the mosque was already there. Despite this, we were not given time to appeal before a higher court. The bulldozers were brought in immediately. This has given politicians an opportunity to turn the matter into a political issue, which is unfortunate. Question: Do you feel that the mosque or the Muslim community is being targeted? Answer: There are some politicians who, by taking action against one community or targeting its religious places, are trying to please certain extremist groups. I believe this is the wrong approach. People have become more aware and we need to move beyond such issues. We respect people of every religion. Question: What will you do next? Will you continue the legal battle? Answer: Does the government see only mosques, madrasas and shrines as illegal across the state and the country? What kind of justice is this? This is a major question, and who will answer it? For now, we have appealed to everyone to remain calm and not act emotionally. We should follow the law and decide what legal step the panel handling the matter will take next.

Did Akhilesh’s Saharanpur rally get postponed due to factionalism?:Why did SP chief visit on 2 September; met some leaders, and brought others along?
stories.summary: A major Samajwadi Party (SP) public meeting was scheduled to be held in Saharanpur on September 6, 2026. It was named the ‘Yuva Yoddha Sammelan’ (Young Warriors’ Conference). However, the event was suddenly postponed. The SP officially cited bad weather and the possibility of heavy rain as the reason. However, there was speculation that two factors were behind the decision. 1- Internal factionalism within the party. 2- Opposition to remarks made about the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD). Interestingly, shortly after the public meeting was postponed, Akhilesh Yadav arrived in Saharanpur. During his nearly five-hour visit on September 2, he had lunch at the Chaudhary family home and held a closed-door meeting. He also met leaders from different factions in an attempt to manage the political equations. Read the report… What was the factionalism and real reason behind postponing the rally? Party national general secretary Chaudhary Rudrasen and his brother Chaudhary Indrasen said the event had been postponed in view of the possibility of rain. A new date could be fixed in October-November. Meanwhile, the RLD linked the postponement of the rally to Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘from a 25-paise coin to a rupee’ remark about Jayant Chaudhary. The RLD claimed that 36 communities in western UP had decided to boycott the rally. The SP rejected the claim, saying the rally had not even been officially announced. The party said that whenever the rally was held, it would be historic. How did factionalism emerge during preparations for the rally? Rudrasen and Indrasen, sons of the late Chaudhary Yashpal Singh, were given responsibility for organising the rally in Saharanpur. Chaudhary Rudrasen is the SP’s national general secretary. The family began preparations for the event as an opportunity to demonstrate its strength. However, questions also arose over who would get credit for the rally’s success. Some hoardings put up during the preparations did not feature pictures of local leaders. Some leaders complained in Lucknow that not everyone was being involved in the preparations. In other words, differences within the party had begun to come out into the open even before the rally. Akhilesh personally took charge of damage control During his Saharanpur visit, Akhilesh Yadav met leaders from different factions instead of siding with any one group. In other words, during his nearly five-hour visit, Akhilesh tried to bring together different political factions in Saharanpur. Chaudhary brothers came to Lucknow in a special aircraft To understand the importance of the late Yashpal Chaudhary’s family in Akhilesh’s eyes, it is important to look at what happened before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Rudrasen wanted a Lok Sabha ticket from Saharanpur or Kairana. However, the Saharanpur seat went to the Congress. In Kairana, the ticket went to Ikra Hasan, daughter of the late Munawwar Hasan. This left Rudrasen and Indrasen unhappy. At a panchayat of their supporters, the two had even spoken of leaving the party. When Akhilesh learnt about this, he called both of them. He described them as members of the family and persuaded them not to leave the party. The two leaders were then flown to Lucknow on a special aircraft. Rudrasen and Indrasen travelled to Lucknow with Ashu Malik. They met Akhilesh, who addressed their grievances and resolved their differences. Expert says RLD would have benefited if Akhilesh had not acted Senior journalist Naved Shikoh, speaking about the shifting political equations in Saharanpur, says, The electoral mood in western UP is determined by the direction of the political wind in Saharanpur. In such a situation, if factionalism had surfaced during the public meeting and voices of dissent had emerged within the party, it could have caused greater damage to Akhilesh Yadav. This is why he sensed the sensitivity of the situation in advance. He not only postponed his rally but also went there himself before Jayant’s rally and managed the situation. Had he not done so, the RLD would perhaps not have hesitated to use the issue to its advantage at its public meetings. Understand the political significance of the entire episode SP spokesperson Fakhrul Hasan Chand says, No rally had been proposed in Saharanpur. This was propaganda created by the RLD. Akhilesh Yadav was initially scheduled to visit someone’s home in Saharanpur on September 6, but the programme was rescheduled and brought forward. Everyone in the party is united; there is no factionalism here. In fact, the sudden visit by Akhilesh Yadav is now being discussed more than the postponement of the rally itself. On one hand, he sought to win over the Chaudhary family, while on the other, he sent a message of maintaining a balance among local leaders. At the same time, he also appeared to be trying to manage the resentment caused by the war of words with the RLD.

stories.title: Will Cockroach Party help SP?:CJP spokesperson on 1.5-hour meeting says, 'Akhilesh invited me'; party to protest over youth issues
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka met in Lucknow on 3 September (Thursday). The two held a closed-door meeting that lasted around one and a half hours. The SP said Ashutosh Ranka had come to meet Akhilesh to convey thanks on behalf of CJP’s Abhijit Dipke. The SP had supported CJP during its protest in Delhi. The question is that several Opposition parties had supported the protest, so why did the meeting take place only with Akhilesh Yadav? What does the meeting mean ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections? Read about it in today’s Sunday Big Story... 1. Full story behind the meeting CJP national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka answered Dainik Bhaskar’s five questions. Question: Did you come to meet Akhilesh yourself, or did he invite you? Ashutosh: CJP’s protest was underway at Jantar Mantar. During the protest, Akhilesh Yadav and the SP had supported us. Akhilesh Yadav had also been inviting me to meet him, so I came to Lucknow. Question: What is your connection with Uttar Pradesh? Ashutosh: My in-laws are in Varanasi. I studied at IIT Kanpur. So I have always had a connection with Uttar Pradesh. Question: What role will CJP play in the UP elections? Ashutosh: The party will not contest the elections. We will not enter active politics. Question: Then what is the purpose of coming to UP? Ashutosh: Uttar Pradesh is the largest state in the country. We will expand our organisation here. Question: What will be the main issues? Ashutosh: Education and employment are our key issues. Young people should have access to good education and adequate employment opportunities. We will work on these issues in Uttar Pradesh as well. 2. Will CJP bring votes or just shape the narrative? CJP began on social media. It does not have a strong grassroots cadre, but it has a significant reach on social media. The party is claimed to have around 2.55 crore followers. Uttar Pradesh has around 2.07 crore Gen-Z youths aged between 18 and 29. During CJP’s protest in Delhi, large numbers of young people from several cities in UP travelled to the capital. Student protests were also held in Prayagraj, Agra and Kanpur. In such a scenario, CJP’s biggest utility for the SP may not be vote transfer but raising issues on social media and among young people. It is believed that if CJP becomes active in UP on issues such as education, employment and recruitment, it could have an impact among the youth. The social media battle between the SP and BJP is already underway. In such a situation, CJP’s support could help create a favourable atmosphere for the SP. How effective will CJP be in UP? Recruitment, unemployment and paper leaks are major issues among young people in Uttar Pradesh. There has been no basic teacher recruitment drive in the state for the past eight years. Candidates have been protesting continuously. CJP leaders have also repeatedly said they want to make development, education and employment the main issues in UP. Ashutosh Ranka has said that if a major youth movement emerges over paper leaks and unemployment, CJP will join it. 7.7% of young people unemployed in UP According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025, the unemployment rate among young people aged 15 to 29 in UP is 7.7%. In urban areas, it is 10.1%. The government claims to have provided 9 lakh jobs over nine years. Meanwhile, data has emerged showing that more than 55,000 posts in basic education and for lekhpals are vacant. In recent years, several recruitment examinations, including UPTET, RO/ARO, UP Police recruitment and the assistant professor examination, have been hit by paper leaks or other controversies. Millions of candidates have been affected by these examinations. Political ambitions of CJP leaders? Sonam Wangchuk had spoken about political ambitions among CJP’s leadership. He said political ambition was not wrong, but a student platform should not be turned into an individual political vehicle. He suggested that if CJP leaders wanted to enter politics in the future, they should form a separate political party. Alternatively, they could enter politics through an existing party. Responding to this, Ashutosh Ranka says CJP’s political ambition is not to gain power but to change the way politics in the country works. Met Opposition leaders at different times CJP currently has 12 prominent members. Six of them have been associated with the Aam Aadmi Party at some point in the past. Abhijit Dipke and Ashutosh Ranka are among them. After CJP came into existence and began its protest in Delhi, Aam Aadmi Party leaders were the first to support it. Senior party leader Manish Sisodia posted a video on social media expressing his support. During the protest, AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal also met CJP leaders. Apart from him, TMC MPs Mahua Moitra and Kirti Azad, Shiv Sena (Uddhav faction) leader Sanjay Raut, CPI(M)’s John Brittas, and SP leaders Priya Saroj, Iqra Hasan and Dimple Yadav, among others, met CJP leaders. However, Congress leaders stayed away from the protest. CJP leaders have also not met any Congress leader so far. CJP’s possible model in UP CJP says it will not contest the UP elections, but is preparing to expand its organisation and become active on issues concerning young people. In such a scenario, CJP’s strength could lie less in winning seats and more in shaping issues and the narrative among the youth. The question now is whether it will remain merely a partner of the SP in protests or also help create an anti-government mood among young voters ahead of the elections.

stories.title: Elderly man stabbed to death outside Lucknow police station:Deceased had confronted a street vendor for driving on the wrong side
stories.summary: An elderly man was stabbed to death in front of Madiyaon police station in Lucknow on Saturday afternoon. His grandson was taking him on a bike to pay a bill when a handcart vendor came towards them from the wrong side. As soon as the grandson asked him, "Where are you coming from on this side?" the vendor became angry and attacked him with a knife. The grandfather, who was seated behind his grandson on the bike, got off to save him. The handcart vendor stopped attacking the grandson and began stabbing the grandfather instead. He stabbed the elderly man five times in the stomach and chest with full force, causing chunks of flesh to protrude. He collapsed and died at the scene. The incident took place at 1 pm under the flyover in front of Madiaon police station. See 2 pictures- Retired from the municipal corporation 16 years ago The elderly man was Magan Bihari Tiwari of Bharatnagar. He had retired from the municipal corporation around 16 years ago, in 2010. He had been a supervisor in the RR department. At around 1 p.m. on Saturday, he was heading to the power house with his grandson, Sankalp Tiwari, to pay a bill. On the way, Sankalp got into an argument with a scrap dealer who was arriving on a three-wheeled cart, in front of Madiyaon police station. During the argument, the scrap dealer attacked Sankalp with a knife. Magan Bihari stepped forward to save his grandson. The scrap dealer repeatedly stabbed him as well. The knife penetrated several places in his abdomen and chest. Chaos broke out at the scene. People informed the police. The scrap dealer fled before the police arrived. Eyewitnesses said Rajkumar alias Malai committed the murder Madiyaon police said eyewitnesses reported that 40-year-old Rajkumar alias Malai stabbed the grandfather and grandson. He currently lives around Markandeya Dharamshala in Keshavnagar and buys scrap from neighbourhoods. According to police, teams have been deployed to apprehend the scrap dealer. He will be arrested and questioned about the motive for the murders. Pradeep Tiwari, the son of Magan Bihari, is also a supervisor in Zone 2 of the municipal corporation. He said, "I was in the office when my mother called and told me that my father was unwell. She asked me to come to Highway Hospital. When I reached the spot, I learnt that someone had stabbed my father. He had gone out with his son, my nephew, to pay the electricity bill." Injured Grandson Is Studying in Intermediate, Daughter Reached Hospital Magan Bihari's family includes his wife, Maya Tiwari, son Pradeep Tiwari, daughter-in-law Pushpa, and three grandchildren. At the time of the incident, his eldest grandson, Sankalp Tiwari, was with him. He is currently studying in intermediate. The family has been inconsolable since the incident. After receiving the information, his elder daughter Poonam also reached the hospital. She broke down after seeing her father's body there.

stories.title: Ajay Rai picked up on way to meet trader’s family:He questions why Dhananjay was not arrested in the codeine case
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai was stopped by police while travelling to Gonda to meet the family of businessman Vinod Sahni, who was killed. He was travelling with a convoy of six vehicles on Saturday afternoon. Police stopped him beyond the Shahabpur toll plaza at the Barabanki border and did not allow him to proceed. Ajay Rai became angry and argued with the police. Angrily, he said: "If there is a written order, show it. Why are you stopping me from meeting the family? I am going to share the family's grief. What have you done to the strongman Dhananjay Singh in the codeine cough syrup case? You have not been able to arrest him to this day. You are stopping me." Ajay Rai remained adamant about proceeding. The police then detained him and brought him to Masoli police station. As soon as he reached the station, he sat on a sit-in protest. On learning this, around 200 Congress workers from Gonda and Barabanki also reached the police station. Congress workers continued the sit-in for around one and a half hours. At 3:30 p.m., Ajay Rai ended the protest after the police persuaded him and returned to Lucknow. See 3 pictures- Congress leader says - We will definitely meet the family Ajay Rai had announced on Friday that he would travel to Gonda. The police became alert after this. Barricades were put up at the Shahabpur toll plaza and 100 police personnel were deployed. When Ajay Rai's convoy arrived at 1:20 p.m., Circle Officer Colonelganj Narendra Pratap Rai and Kotwal Narendra Pratap stopped it. In addition, several Congress leaders in Gonda were placed under house arrest. Pramod Mishra, former Gonda Congress district president, said, "We will meet the family, but before that, the police have started harassing us. Under no circumstances will we be prevented from visiting the victim's family home." Now, understand the full matter Videos and photos of Dhananjay with a drug smuggler had emerged Photos and videos of strongman former MP Dhananjay Singh with drug smuggler Amit Tata, who was arrested in Lucknow around nine months ago, had surfaced. However, Dhananjay Singh later issued a clarification, saying that a conspiracy was being hatched against him and that the CBI should investigate the smuggling of codeine-mixed intoxicating syrup. Ajay Rai has targeted Dhananjay over this case.

stories.title: Man hung upside down and beaten after visiting girlfriend:Saharanpur attackers tied him to a pole for 12 hours, freed him after taking ₹5 lakh
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, the family members of a man who had gone to meet his girlfriend caught him. They tied him up with a rope and hung him upside down. They beat him for around half an hour, then tied him to a pole. His family learnt about the incident in the morning and reached the spot. A village council was then held. The council took ₹5 lakh from the man's family in exchange for releasing him. A video of the incident emerged on Saturday. It shows the man hanging upside down from a rope, with several people standing nearby. The man repeatedly tries to hide his face. The incident took place in the Mirzapur police station area. Based on the video, police are trying to identify and arrest the accused. See 2 pictures... Now, the sequence of events in detail... The young man went to meet someone on the night of 9 September The young man is from the Mirzapura police station area. He is married. On Wednesday night (9 September), he went to the nearby village of Kasimpur to meet his girlfriend. During this time, the girl's family members caught him. The young man was first tied up with a rope and then beaten while being hung upside down. Someone recorded a video of the entire incident. Family began searching when he did not return home overnight The young man's family became worried when he did not return home overnight. They began searching for him. During this time, they learnt that the young man was in Kasimpur village and was being beaten. The young man's family then reached the spot. Discussions began to pacify the situation between the two sides. During this time, money is reportedly said to have been discussed in the name of releasing the young man and ending the dispute. The victim's family claims that ₹5 lakh was demanded. Of this, ₹3 lakh was taken by the girl's family and ₹2 lakh by intermediaries. Case reaches senior police officials Despite talks and a settlement, the young woman's family handed the young man over to the police. The police then began questioning him. It is alleged that despite a video emerging of the young man being hung upside down and beaten, a case was not immediately registered against the accused. Senior police officials have been informed about the entire sequence of events. On the officials' instructions, the victim has been called to Saharanpur and details of the entire matter are being gathered. Mirzapur police said the man is being questioned. Further action will be taken if a written complaint is received and the allegations are found to be true during the investigation.

stories.summary: The protest by panchayat assistants at Lucknow's Eco Garden continued on Saturday. Protesters arrived at the sit-in carrying umbrellas to protect themselves from the harsh sunlight. Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad also reached the protest site to support the panchayat assistants. Some of his supporters climbed trees to see him. Chandrashekhar Azad said, "Until my brothers' demands are met, I will not marry anyone." Panchayat assistants from different districts across the state have been sitting in protest over their demands for a week. They are seeking an increase in their honorarium and the fulfilment of other service-related demands. The panchayat assistants said they handle online and administrative work at the gram panchayat level. In return, they receive an honorarium of ₹6,000 per month. They are demanding that it be increased to ₹30,000 per month. They alleged that despite the low honorarium, they are being made to do more work and are being exploited. stories.title: Mayawati to promote niece Deepika, not nephews, in politics:Says she stands against dynastic politics like Kanshi Ram; 50% tickets for Gen Z in 2027
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) supremo Mayawati may hand over the reins of the party to her niece, Deepika Anand. Mayawati herself said this on Saturday. She stated that neither of her nephews, Akash and Ishan, will hold any political post in the party. In the future, her nephews' children will not receive any posts either. If her brother Anand Kumar requires a member's assistance, he can take the help of his only daughter, Deepika Anand (Mayawati's niece). Based on her honesty, loyalty, and competence, she may be entrusted with responsibilities in the party in the future. Mayawati said that, like Kanshi Ram, she will remain firm against dynastic politics. Deepika is currently studying law. Playing the Gen-Z Card to Counter the Fallout from Akash To hedge against potential losses from Akash Anand's expulsion, Mayawati announced plans to allocate up to 50% of tickets to Gen-Z in the 2027 Assembly elections. Mayawati stated that in the upcoming Assembly elections in UP, Uttarakhand, and Punjab, priority will be given to dedicated, young, and capable candidates from all sections of society. Mayawati said—BSP's objective will be to rapidly strengthen Ambedkarite politics and constitutional values in the country through the new generation. She appealed to party workers to prioritize the youth along with worthy individuals from all sections of society while selecting candidates, emphasizing representation for both women and men. If the Daughter is Unwilling, Responsibility Will Go to a Dalit Missionary Worker Mayawati clarified that if Deepika is not ready for this responsibility, her brother Anand may hand over the charge to another missionary worker from the Dalit community with the party's general consensus. However, this responsibility will not be given to his sons or their future children. "If I were not a woman, I would not have kept even my brother with me" Mayawati said—If I were not a woman, I would not have kept even my brothers and sisters with me. Due to being a woman, to avoid safety and other issues and to work in the party with dignity, I had to keep my youngest brother Anand with me. However, despite the circumstances now emerging regarding my brother's family members, I will not fall into any attachment. I will not let the party suffer any loss. "Like Kanshi Ram, I too stand firm against dynastic politics" Mayawati linked herself to Kanshi Ram's political legacy. She said—Just as Kanshi Ram stayed away from dynastic politics, I too stand firm on this principle. In the BSP, an individual may be given an opportunity based on their merit. However, under that pretext, other members of their family will not be given political benefits. The purpose of this is to keep the BSP free from dynastic politics and to connect as many people from all sections of society as possible with the movement for social change and economic liberation. Focus on Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha for 2027 Mayawati has indicated plans to increase the participation of youth in the party organisation as well as prioritize young faces in the Assembly elections. In this, particular emphasis has been placed on keeping the needs of Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha at the centre of politics. She also referenced the tenures of previous BSP governments. She stated that along with roads, electricity, water, education, health, government jobs, employment, schools, hospitals, and urban and rural development, work was also done on the needs of the youth. Mayawati claimed that during BSP governments, facilities such as schools, colleges, universities, hostels, training centres, and parks were expanded. As a result, forced migration was also largely curtailed. Blamed Rivals for Not Returning to Power in 2012 Mayawati also referred to the 2012 Assembly elections. She stated that owing to the alleged casteist attitude of opposition parties, the BSP could not form the government for a 5th time in 2012. People across all sections of society still regret this today. Following the BSP government, 'rule of law by law' could not be established in the state. People's lives remain full of hardships. Questioning the government's claims of development, Mayawati said that merely blowing the government horn does not fill people's stomachs. Advised Caution Against Social Media Propaganda Mayawati asked party workers to remain cautious of propaganda running across opposition parties, organisations, and media-social media. She alleged that tactics such as persuasion, bribery, division, and force (Saam, Daam, Dand, Bhed) could be employed to prevent the BSP from forming a government in UP. She appealed to the workers to remain dedicated to the Ambedkarite mission with their complete body, mind, and resources. Dismissed Reports of Expelled Leaders' Return as ‘Fake News’ Mayawati also rejected discussions circulating on social media regarding the return of leaders expelled from the party. She stated that for the past few days, propaganda has been spread claiming that individuals expelled due to indiscipline and anti-party activities would be taken back into the BSP. Such people will not be readmitted into the BSP.

stories.title: Bus crushes child to death in front of mother:Was waiting for school bus in Gorakhpur; female teacher held hostage, 3-hour uproar on road
stories.summary: A school bus ran over a five-year-old child in front of his mother in Gorakhpur on Saturday morning. The mother was waiting for the bus to drop her child at school. The speeding school bus then arrived and, after running over the child, continued on out of control. Family members took the child to CHC Pipraich, where doctors declared him dead. Meanwhile, after the accident, the driver tried to flee with the bus. When villagers chased him, he stopped the bus around 200 metres away and fled. Angry villagers held the schoolteacher travelling in the bus hostage and vandalised the vehicle. The commotion continued for around 3 hours. The people calmed down after officials who reached the spot assured them of action. The accident took place at 8 a.m. in Naiyapar Buzurg village, under Pipraich police station limits, 20 kilometres from the district headquarters. See the pictures... Read the full story now... Soni lives with her family in Naiyapur Buzurg in Pipraich. Her in-laws also live with her. Soni's husband lives in Mumbai, where he works in painting and polishing. Soni, the child's mother, said, "My five-year-old son Himanshu studied in Class 1 at SD Public School in Chauri. He woke up on Saturday morning to go to school. I prepared his lunch and then began waiting outside the house for the school bus to arrive." At 8 a.m., an SD Public School bus (UP52T0177) suddenly arrived at high speed. It ran over my child right in front of me and drove away. I raised the alarm. The villagers nearby then surrounded the bus from the front and stopped it around 200 metres away. The children also began shouting. The villagers held the teacher who was sitting in the bus hostage, while the driver fled the spot. The villagers smashed the bus windows and began creating a commotion. Pipraich police, who arrived after receiving the information, tried to pacify the people. When the police arrived around three hours later, they took the teacher to the police station along with the bus. Family demands ₹1 crore and a government job After the accident, SDM Gyan Pratap Singh, Tehsildar Dr Bhagirathi Singh and Naib Tehsildar Anu Singh reached the spot. During the commotion, the family members handed a memorandum of demands to the SDM. The mother, Soni, said, "A compensation of ₹1 crore should be paid, and one family member should be given a government job." CO Chauri Chaura Kundan Singh said: “We received information about the accident at around 8:30 a.m. today. A five-year-old boy, Himanshu, was waiting for a bus to go to school when the accident involving a school bus occurred. A case is being registered in this matter.”

stories.title: Woman dies six months after love marriage in Ghaziabad:Footage shows her falling from roof; brother alleges husband pushed her for Scorpio
stories.summary: A woman died in Ghaziabad six months after her love marriage. Her brother has alleged that her husband beat her for not receiving a Scorpio as dowry and then pushed her from the second floor. She died on Friday after undergoing treatment at a hospital for four days. As soon as they learned of the woman's death, her husband, parents-in-law and two sisters-in-law fled. Police have registered an FIR against all five and begun searching for them. A video of the incident also emerged on Saturday afternoon. It shows the woman suddenly falling from the roof at night. People nearby can be seen taking her to hospital. The incident took place in the Muradnagar police station area. The deceased has been identified as Akriti Singh. Her husband, Gaurav (25), works at a factory in Noida. Two images of the woman falling from the roof... Now read the full case in detail... The accused, Gaurav, owns a three-storey house in Muradnagar. He lives there with his parents and two sisters. Prabhat, the brother of Aakriti, a resident of Bhangel, said, "My sister's marriage to Gaurav was fixed on 20 February. At the time, Gaurav had demanded ₹30 lakh in cash and a Scorpio as dowry." "We could not afford to give such a large dowry, so we refused. The two sides also reached a settlement at Muradnagar police station in the matter. The marriage was subsequently called off, but Gaurav and Aakriti continued speaking on the phone." Brother said Sister had married against the family's wishes The brother said, "Two months later, the couple married at a temple against the family's wishes. Gaurav then brought Aakriti to his home. The family was initially upset but later accepted the marriage." Everything was fine between the two for a few days. Gaurav then started demanding a Scorpio from Aakriti again. He would ask her to get a Scorpio from her family. When Aakriti refused, he would assault her. Brother said: Sister told him over the phone, ‘All these people are beating me.’ Prabhat said that Aakriti called him on 7 September and said, "All these people are beating me." Shortly afterwards, Gaurav called and told him that Aakriti had fallen from the roof. He asked them to reach a hospital in Ghaziabad quickly. When they reached the hospital, Aakriti was in a critical condition. After four days of treatment, she died on the night of 11 September. Case registered against five, including husband After Aakriti's death, her family lodged a case at Muradnagar police station against her husband, Gaurav; father-in-law Ramesh, mother-in-law Saroj, and sisters-in-law Soni and Neha. Police reached the spot, conducted an investigation and sent the body for post-mortem. DCP (Rural) Surendranath Tiwari said that police were investigating the circumstances surrounding the woman's death. An FIR had been registered against her in-laws on the basis of the complaint.

stories.title: Three-star hotel gutted in Meerut fire:People flee to save lives, 2 cars parked outside burn; flames reach Indian Bank
stories.summary: A fire broke out at a three-star hotel in Meerut around 11.30am on Saturday (12 Sept). The blaze started in the parking area of Abika Hotel under the Partapur police station area and quickly spread to the hotel, engulfing 12 rooms. The sight of flames and thick smoke triggered panic among people in the surrounding area. As the fire began spreading towards the adjoining Indian Bank branch, chaos also broke out there. Six fire brigade vehicles reached the spot after receiving information about the incident, and firefighters began efforts to bring the blaze under control. The entire hotel was evacuated and everyone inside was brought outside. Hotel furnishings and two cars gutted in blaze The fire completely destroyed the hotel’s luxury furnishings and two cars parked in the parking area. A short circuit is being cited as the immediate cause of the fire. No casualties have been reported so far. See three pictures of the fire... Hotel fire spreads towards Indian Bank, eight fire tenders deployed Avika Hotel, located on Delhi Road under Partapur police station limits, is owned by advocate Arvind Bhati, who had rented it to Kumari Nandwani aka Bunty. Around 11.30am, a fire suddenly broke out in the hotel’s parking area. Fire spreads from cars to hotel rooms and party hall The fire initially reached the cars parked in the parking area. An Eon and a Brezza were gutted in the blaze. The fire then spread rapidly, with flames reaching the first floor from the ground-floor party hall. Within a short time, the entire hotel was engulfed. All 12 rooms and the belongings inside were destroyed. Thick smoke and flames could be seen from a distance, triggering panic among people in the surrounding area. Flames move towards adjoining Indian Bank branch During the blaze, flames also began spreading towards the Indian Bank branch adjoining the hotel. Panic broke out as the fire moved towards the bank. Preventing the flames from spreading to the bank became a major challenge for firefighters. Eight fire tenders bring blaze under control Eight fire brigade vehicles reached the spot after receiving the alert. Firefighters began operations from different sides and managed to prevent the flames from spreading towards the bank. The blaze was brought under control after around 30 to 60 minutes of efforts. No major damage to the bank has been reported. Short circuit triggers fire, flames spread from sofas to upper floors Hotel guard Ratan Pal Singh said the fire started in the parking area due to a short circuit. The fire first broke out in the sofas before the flames spread upwards. The tin sheets above also caught fire, after which the blaze spread to the vehicles parked in the parking area. Guard and owner suffer burns while trying to douse fire Ratan Pal said he and the hotel owner were the only people present when the fire broke out. Both tried to extinguish the blaze but suffered burns to their hands in the process. When they failed to bring the fire under control, they alerted the fire brigade. Six fire tenders rushed to the spot Six fire brigade vehicles reached the hotel after receiving the alert and began efforts to control the blaze. No customers at hotel, estimated loss of nearly ₹1.75 crore He said no customers or other people were present at the hotel when the fire broke out. The hotel has 25 rooms, including three store rooms. At present, only 12 rooms are being rented out. According to Ratan Pal, property and other belongings worth nearly ₹1.75 crore were damaged in the fire. It took around two hours to bring the blaze under control. Police confirm no one was trapped inside SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosle said police reached the spot as soon as they received information about the fire. The hotel has 12 occupied rooms, and all staff members and guests were evacuated in time. He said all the rooms were checked. There were rumours that some people were trapped inside the hotel, but the search found no one trapped. No casualties were reported in the incident.

stories.title: Youth murdered in public, accused’s house bulldozed:Meerut father sits with son’s body on road; married 4 months ago
stories.summary: The family has staged a sit-in after their only son was murdered in broad daylight in Meerut. They are raising slogans against the police and administration. They say they will not perform the last rites until the alleged killers are killed in a police encounter. On Friday, six attackers who arrived on two motorcycles shot dead 22-year-old Nitin in broad daylight, 200 metres from Hastinapur police station. He was shot in the leg and collapsed, bleeding heavily. He died after losing a large amount of blood. The father's health deteriorated after he saw his son's body, and he collapsed unconscious. His wife was inconsolable. When the police arrived at the scene to take the body into custody, the family refused to hand it over. Police personnel tried to persuade them throughout the night, but they did not agree. From 7 a.m. on Saturday, around 500 people joined the family in blocking the road at Ganeshpur Tirahe in Hastinapur, with the body placed there. They said, "We will not leave this place until bulldozers are used at the accused's homes and they are killed in a police encounter." After receiving the information, Hastinapur MLA and Minister of State Dinesh Khatik reached the spot and began trying to persuade the family members. He assured them that strict action would be taken against the accused. Immediately afterwards, the police began demolishing one of the accused's houses with a bulldozer. At present, police forces from five police stations, including Rural SP Abhijeet Kumar, are present at the spot. See three pictures... First, let us understand the entire case in sequence- Nitin killed in friend Prince's dispute His family members said Nitin's friend Prince lived in Hastinapur. Two days earlier, he had a dispute with his neighbour, Vivek Vardhan alias Pinky Chaudhary, over a route. The two sides had fought. A settlement was then reached in the presence of the police. On Friday, Pinky's elder brother Satya alias Miththu attacked Prince along with his associates. Prince escaped, but Nitin was killed. The police are searching for the killers. The father of accused Miththu is reportedly a clerk in the Education Department. Meerut SSP BBGTS Murthy said: “Four teams have been deployed to arrest the accused. The attackers will be arrested soon. The reason for the murder appears to be a two-day-old road-rage incident. The accused have been identified. Police teams are conducting raids to trace them.”

stories.title: Wife and daughters refuse last rites of former CRPF jawan:Say 'will immolate if killers not gunned down'; sit with petrol cans
stories.summary: After the murder of former CRPF jawan Amaresh Bahadur Singh in Ballia, his wife and three daughters have refused to perform his last rites, keeping his body at home for 16 hours while demanding action. His eldest daughter, Kritika Singh, is sitting beside the body with a can filled with petrol. She said the killers should be killed in an encounter and their house demolished with a bulldozer. "If the bulldozer is not brought in by 12 noon today, all three of us sisters will pour petrol on ourselves and self-immolate alongside our father." SDM Sharad Chaudhary and police personnel are trying to persuade the family. The wife said- "Blood must be avenged with blood. My husband was brutally murdered in front of my eyes. The accused fled. The police have not been able to arrest them yet. My husband was the family's only breadwinner. The family is now facing a financial crisis. We should be provided financial assistance." In fact, neighbours murdered former CRPF jawan Amaresh Bahadur Singh (45) on Thursday night. His brother, who came to save him, was also attacked in an attempt on his life. He is in a critical condition. The body arrived home from Mau on Friday evening. The family then began protesting, demanding action. Amaresh had taken VRS from the CRPF on 31 March this year. The incident took place in the area under the jurisdiction of Ubhaon police station, 70 km from the district headquarters. See three pictures – Daughter says, "There is no one left in my family to perform the last rites" The elder daughter, Kritika Singh, said, "It was dark at the time of the incident. My sister Ritika and I kept screaming. Our father fell to the ground injured right in front of our eyes. The accused also beat my uncle Manjesh Singh so severely that he is fighting for his life. There is no one left in my family to perform the last rites." Kritika said around 24 hours had passed since the incident, but there had been no update on the action taken so far. Two of the accused are still absconding. If the accused are not being arrested, their house is right here-why is it not being demolished with a bulldozer? "I saw my father get injured and collapse before my eyes" The younger daughter, Ritika, said her father was attacked in front of her. She demanded strict action against the accused. Ritika said she could not save her father. The accused also assaulted her and threatened that they would return and harm the family. Neighbours had torn open the abdomen of the former CRPF jawan Former CRPF jawan Amresh was a resident of Doth Sonadih village in the Belthara Road area. His family comprises his wife, Kanchan Singh, and three daughters: Kritika (21), Ritika (18) and Roshni (16). His brother, Manjesh Singh (35), also lived with them. The two brothers ran a dairy farm near their home. Amresh was at the dairy farm on Thursday. His neighbour Girish Singh then arrived with his wife, Sheila, their two sons, Karan and Suraj, and daughter Khushi, and began hurling abuses. When he objected, the entire family attacked Amresh. They knocked him down, beat him and stabbed him, leaving him seriously injured. Brother on ventilator support, 3 arrested, 2 still absconding When Mangesh went to save him, he too was attacked. Amresh died in hospital. Mangesh is undergoing treatment on ventilator support at BHU in Varanasi. After the murder, police arrested Khushi, the daughter, Sheela Singh, the wife, and Suraj, the son of named accused Girish. Girish and his son Karan are absconding. Three police teams have been formed to arrest the two absconding accused. The teams are conducting raids at likely hideouts. SP meets family, says strict action will be taken SP Omkar Singh went to the family's home to meet them on Friday evening. He said strict action would be taken against the accused. He added that he would speak to the SDM to arrange financial assistance from the Chief Minister's Discretionary Fund for the family's upkeep.

stories.title: IIT engineer’s body lay in flat for 4 days:Lived alone in Gorakhpur; younger brother in US, father was irrigation department officer
stories.summary: The body of a 45-year-old IIT engineer was found on the sofa in his flat in Gorakhpur on Friday morning (11 Sept) after neighbours alerted police when a foul smell began coming from the flat. Police broke open the door and found the body, which they said was three to four days old; however, the post-mortem examination also failed to establish the cause of death. The incident took place at Malhar Apartment in Sahara Estate. As soon as he learnt of engineer Abhishek Tripathi's death, his younger brother Ambreesh set off for Gorakhpur from the United States. The last rites will be performed after he arrives. Abhishek lived alone in the flat. He had lost his job four years ago and had been struggling with mental health issues since then. His younger brother, who lives in the United States, supported him financially. He had not married. His father, Sabha Tripathi, had retired as an executive engineer from the Irrigation Department. Their parents are dead. Their younger brother, Ambreesh, is an IT engineer in the United States. Their elder brother, Ashutosh, was a security guard for former Bihar Chief Minister Rabri Devi. He died of an illness in Chennai in 2014. Their sister, Gudiya, lives in Gorakhpur with her husband. Lost his job at a multinational company and slipped into depression Archana, who reached the spot after the incident, said, "Our father was originally from Mahason village in Kushinagar, but he was posted in the Irrigation Department in Gorakhpur. That is why we all studied here. Our father died 16 years ago. Three years later, our mother also passed away." Abhishek was academically bright. He studied engineering at IIT and worked for a multinational company in Noida. During the COVID-19 period, he moved to Gorakhpur because of work from home. He lost his job four years ago. After that, he began to remain distressed and gradually slipped into depression. His family arranged treatment for him in Lucknow, but the problem did not go away completely. His illness changed his behaviour, prompting people to distance themselves The sister said that Abhishek's behaviour had changed because of his illness. At times, he would speak to people in abusive language. This affected his relationships, and visits from relatives and acquaintances became less frequent. His younger brother, Ambareesh, used to send him money, which covered Abhishek's expenses. Ambareesh and I would visit him from time to time. Neighbours said he had become isolated and spent most of his time in his room According to neighbours, Abhishek had become isolated. He spent most of his time in his room and did not speak much to anyone. He had not been seen for three to four days. On Friday, the neighbours informed the police after a foul smell began coming from the flat. When the police broke open the door, they found his body inside. CO Keerti Nidhi Anand said- Abhishek had not left the flat for three to four days. The door was locked from the inside. The cause of death has not yet been established. The post-mortem report and other evidence are being examined. The room was found in disarray. The mobile phone is locked, and attempts are being made to unlock it.

stories.title: Programme held to ensure youth participation:Students take part in Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue in Varanasi
stories.summary: The Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) quiz was organised at Jagatpur PG College in Varanasi on September 11. The programme aimed to connect as many young people as possible with the campaign and encourage their participation. College students enthusiastically registered for the quiz during the event. Focus on youth participation The programme encouraged students to understand the role of young people in building a developed India and participate actively in the campaign. Organisers stressed the need to involve more young people in the quiz, while student registrations were also conducted on the college campus. Faculty members encourage students Dr Sanjay Pradhan, Lieutenant Dr Suresh Kumar Singh, Dr Chandrashekhar Pandey, Dr Ankur and Dr Anamika, among other faculty members, attended the programme. They encouraged students to participate enthusiastically. Students also showed keen interest in the quiz during the event.

stories.title: Azam Khan’s close aide, SP leader Dakku left isolated:Raids underway to trace close aide, city president; he writes letter detailing his pain
stories.summary: Jafar Amin, aka Dakku, never held a major post in the Samajwadi Party, but his political stature remained significant because of his close ties with the party’s Muslim face, Azam Khan. Although he never appeared to stake a claim to the posts of district president or city president, Dakku remained influential whenever the SP was in power, with his influence clearly visible within the party. He is currently in jail. Azam Khan is also in jail. This close aide of Azam has now been left isolated within his own party. A letter he wrote from jail has gone viral, and it also reflects his pain that his party is not standing by him. His close aide, Shabbir Qureshi, is the city president and is absconding in the same case; police are conducting raids in search of him. The matter is also within the knowledge of the SP national president, but no public statement has yet been issued by him either. In Dakku's letter, current district president Brajesh Kumar Gautam is in the crosshairs. Taking a sharp swipe at his efforts, he even said that Gautam should not come to meet him in jail. He also said that three councillors should not come either. One of them is considered his opponent. Dakku now wants to somehow manage the matter and get out of jail. For this, he has been knocking on the doors of some BJP-linked leaders from time to time. The Samajwadi Party's district president has also hinted at this. First, find out the case in which Dakku is in jail Dakku is in jail for allegedly attempting to seize land and threaten his opponent. However, he claims that he purchased the land in question through a registered sale deed and has the documents to prove it. Even on the day the incident took place and the video went viral, he remained unconcerned until 9:30 p.m. The police had also summoned both sides in the case with their documents. Until then, there was no indication that any action would be taken. Then, suddenly, an FIR was filed late at night, and Dakku was arrested from his home at midnight. Ten days have passed, but he remains in jail. Samajwadi Party city president Shabbir Qureshi had accompanied him in the same case. Shabbir is also named in the case but is absconding. Raids are continuing to locate him. On the first day, he was searched for in every corner of his house, including the fridge, cooler and wardrobe. Why has the SP been unable to speak out? Both leaders caught up in this case are prominent faces of the Samajwadi Party. Dakku is a senior SP leader, while Shabbir is the current metropolitan president. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is aware of the matter and has been kept informed at every stage. He has also been informed about the letter sent by Dakku from jail on Thursday. The SP leader also knows that someone had gone to Gorakhnath Temple with a recommendation on his behalf. The SP leader has returned after meeting the SP chief in Lucknow, but no instructions were issued from his side. If there had been any instructions, they would have been visible on the ground. A senior Samajwadi Party leader explained the reason. He said the party considers the matter a personal issue involving Dakku. Secondly, while he remained influential, his relations with most leaders were strained. Because of his outspoken image, he no longer had good relations with several leaders. The most important reason is that the family involved in the dispute is also Muslim. Akhilesh Yadav, who is conducting his entire political campaign around PDA, is staying away from the issue for this reason. He has not issued any statement regarding his metropolitan president either. SP leaders say the organisation fears that if the matter is given too much publicity, it will give the BJP an opportunity. It will not be easy for the party to respond to allegations such as grabbing a Muslim's land. The party has therefore maintained silence for now. What did the SP district president say? After the letter went viral, the SP district president reacted sharply. In an emotional outburst, he had said that Dakku had not gone to grab land after asking either him or the party. By Friday evening, his tone had softened, but the sting of the letter remained. Describing Dakku as his elder brother, he said that if he was instructed not to visit him, he would follow that order. He said he had not spoken to the metropolitan president either. Every possible effort has been made for the party leaders. He said the matter was in the knowledge of the national president. The person with whom there is a dispute is also from the Muslim side. This is Dakku's personal matter. However, a leader named Janardan Chaudhary has criticised the SP district president on social media over the issue. He called the district president's statement childish. Dakku has contested elections twice Dakku is a heavyweight leader. In 1991, he contested the Assembly election from Gorakhpur City on a Janata Dal ticket and received 20.10 per cent of the vote. Shiv Pratap Shukla won the election, held amid the Ram temple wave, after securing more than 55 per cent of the vote. Dakku contested the election from the newly formed Gorakhpur Rural Assembly seat in 2012 and received 22.27 per cent of the vote. BJP candidate Vijay Bahadur Yadav won that election. Dakku was highly influential in the Samajwadi Party government from 2012 to 2017. Azam Khan was the Urban Development Minister, and Dakku held sway over Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation and the municipal councils in the district.

stories.title: LIC agent shot at repeatedly in Lucknow, condition critical:Bullet grazes head and hits hand; attackers flee scene
stories.summary: Two youths allegedly surrounded an LIC agent and opened rapid fire at him in Malihabad, Lucknow, leaving him seriously injured. The attackers fled after repeatedly firing at the insurance agent outside a shop in front of a petrol pump near Dhendhemau village; one bullet grazed his head, while another struck his hand. LIC agent Samendra Yadav (36) is a resident of Saifalpur village. He had gone to a mobile shop in Dhendhemau, 10 km from his home. The two youths, who were lying in wait there, surrounded him and opened fire. After receiving information about the shooting, the agent's family members also reached the spot. They took Samendra, who was found injured by the roadside, to the Malihabad CHC. After providing first aid, doctors referred him to the trauma centre. See 3 pictures- CCTV footage related to the incident has also emerged. In one clip, the attacker is seen shooting Samendra in the forehead and fleeing on foot, while in another, he is seen fleeing on a motorcycle with an accomplice. Police reach the scene after being informed of the incident; atmosphere of fear The firing in the middle of the road has created an atmosphere of fear among local residents. As soon as the police were informed of the incident, personnel from the Malihabad police station reached the scene. After inspecting the site, the police launched a search for the attackers. ACP Malihabad Gyanendra Singh said that the youth had sustained a gunshot wound. His family was with him. The family members were being spoken to. Legal action was being taken after obtaining a complaint from them. The person seriously injured in the shooting is married. Link being drawn to the death of a brother-in-law's pregnant wife On 25 May, Rupanshi Yadav, the wife of Samendra's brother-in-law Sudhir Yadav, died under suspicious circumstances. She was three months pregnant. The police are also linking the firing at Sumendra to that incident. It is suspected that after Rupanshi's death, her maternal family may have developed an enmity not only towards her in-laws but also towards Samendra. The investigation is under way. It may be noted that Samendra's brother-in-law's in-laws' home is near Dhendhemau, close to the scene of the incident. Today, Samendra had gone there from his home, around 10 km away. This gave those holding a grudge an opportunity, and they fled after shooting him. CCTV footage of the incident also emerges Some CCTV footage related to the incident has also emerged. In one clip, the attacker is seen shooting Samendra in the forehead and fleeing on foot, while in another he is seen fleeing on a bike with an accomplice. In the first clip, the attacker shoots Samendra in the forehead. A youth was waiting for him some distance away. After the firing, the attacker ran away, and the other youth also fled with him. The attacker youths had parked their bikes some distance away. They ran there, mounted the bike and fled the scene of the incident. Married five years ago, has a four-year-old son Insurance agent Samendra is one of three brothers. Amarendra is the eldest, the injured Samendra is the middle one and Narendra Yadav is the youngest. Samendra married Neha Yadav of Bhulbhula village around five years ago. They have a four-year-old son. After the incident, Samendra's father Umashankar Yadav, his wife Neha and his brothers have been inconsolable. Liquor shop salesman was murdered in the same village on 11 May On 11 May, Ajay Kumar Jaiswal, aka Rinku Jaiswal (35), a salesman at a country liquor shop in the same Dhendhemau village under the jurisdiction of Malihabad police station, was beaten to death with an iron rod. Exactly four months later, on 11 September, an LIC agent was shot in the same village.

stories.title: BJP to build narrative against SP, Congress in UP:BL Santosh, Vinod Tawde meet in Lucknow; Mission 2027 roadmap prepared
stories.summary: BJP Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde and national general secretary BL Santosh held a meeting with the party’s core group at the BJP headquarters in Lucknow on Friday (11 Sept). Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was also present at the meeting. It was decided that the BJP would complete the first phase of its election campaign through the Seva Sankalp campaign, which will begin on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday on September 17. The campaign will continue until October 17, with the government and party organisation reaching out to people with the achievements of the Modi-Yogi government. Ground situation to be assessed during campaign The party will assess the ground situation in Assembly constituencies during the campaign and mobilise workers for the upcoming election. The meeting, which lasted more than two hours, also focused on preparing a roadmap for Mission 2027. The BJP and its organisation will work together to form the party’s government in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term. BJP plans counter-narrative against Opposition Two key issues were discussed during the meeting. The party plans to build a narrative against the Samajwadi Party and Congress among young people, Dalits and backward communities during the campaign. A strategy was also discussed to target the Opposition over issues including the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram temple, the UGC and the Gen-Z movement. Tawde, Santosh on two-day Uttar Pradesh visit BL Santosh and Vinod Tawde are in Lucknow on a two-day visit. This is Tawde’s second visit to Uttar Pradesh in the past seven days. stories.title: 24 gay men blackmailed with obscene videos, robbed:AMU student helps catch one accused; app-based gang active in Aligarh
stories.summary: A gang allegedly involved in blackmailing and robbing young men through a dating app has been busted in Aligarh, with the police investigation so far finding that 24 young men were targeted. Police have arrested one suspect, whose mobile phone contained obscene videos of 10 young men. The case came to light on Friday when a 19-year-old BBA student of Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) filed a complaint. The student alleged that he was assaulted in a hostel and blackmailed after an obscene video of him was recorded. Meanwhile, another victim also approached the police. As the modus operandi in both incidents was found to be similar, the police suspected that a gang was active. The police arrested one suspect based on the identification by the victims. Obscene videos of 10 young men were recovered from his mobile phone. The police are investigating the case. Now read the details... The student says, 'Friendship on app', then called to AMU hostel According to the BBA student, he received a friendship request on his Grindr app account. After they spoke, he was called to Vikar-ul-Mulk Hall at Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) to meet. The student alleges that after he reached the room, he was held captive and assaulted. An obscene video of him was also recorded. The accused blackmailed him by threatening to make the video viral and extorted ₹5,600 from him. Police have registered an FIR at Civil Lines police station on the student's father's complaint and begun an investigation. Another young man also fell victim through the app While the investigation into the student's complaint was under way, another young man from the Bannadevi area also approached the police. He too reported being blackmailed after coming into contact through the Grindr app. In both cases, the method was found to be the same: first contacting the young men through the app and then luring them to meet on the pretext of a meeting. The police subsequently expanded the scope of the investigation. So far, the police have obtained the names and addresses of 10 young men who were victims. First friendship, then a VIDEO... this is how the blackmailing was carried out How did the gang reach the AMU hostel? The biggest question in the case concerns how the gang gained access to the AMU hostel. According to the complaint, the BBA student was called to a room in Vikrarul Mulk Hall, although he himself lives in G.M. Hall. The police are therefore investigating how outsiders gained access to the hostel and with whose help the room was used. The police are also finding out whether the gang received assistance from any student or another person. The role of some outsiders and people linked to AMU is also being investigated. The investigation has been expanded to determine whether the gang's activities were limited to a single hostel room or whether its network extended further across the university campus. CO Sarvam Singh said: One accused has been arrested. Videos of 10 victims were found on his mobile phone. Digital evidence is being examined in the case.
