stories.title: Daughter-in-law drank heavily on night of father-in-law’s murder:Danced with husband for 1.5 hours while drunk; Kanpur hotel owner says they ate grilled fish, mutton tikka
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the daughter-in-law and son of millionaire pharmaceutical businessman Vineet Minocha drank heavily on the night of his murder. While contract killers were allegedly murdering the businessman inside his home, his accused daughter-in-law Shalu was partying at a lounge with her husband Subrat. The lounge manager and waiter told Dainik Bhaskar that the couple spent around five hours there. After drinking, Shalu danced with her husband on the DJ floor for around one-and-a-half hours. She also ate grilled fish and mutton tikka. The staff said Shalu and Subrat appeared normal and happy throughout the party. When they learnt about Vineet’s murder the next day, the lounge staff were also shocked. Here is what else emerged from the conversation. Shalu told waiter to make food less spicy Pharmaceutical businessman Vineet Minocha was found murdered inside his flat on the night of September 5 after his throat was slit. Police said his daughter-in-law had allegedly hired domestic worker Vishal Gautam, a resident of Harbans Mohal, and his associate Rajkishore to carry out the murder. While the alleged contract killers were murdering the businessman at home, his daughter-in-law and son were partying at Cosmojin Lounge in Tilak Nagar. Lounge general manager Saurabh Tripathi told Dainik Bhaskar that Subrat had booked a couple’s party there for the first time on September 5. A regular customer of the lounge had introduced him to Subrat. The party was scheduled to begin at 11.30 pm, but Subrat and Shalu arrived an hour early at 10.30 pm. They then went to the first floor of the lounge, where they ordered starters to check the taste. The waiter served them Hariyali kebab, veg seekh kebab, grilled fish and mutton tikka. Shalu reportedly praised the grilled fish and asked for the food to be made less spicy. Shalu and Subrat danced to songs from the 1990s General manager Saurabh said Subrat’s guests began arriving at around 11.15 pm. Around 35 guests attended the party. After the party began, Shalu and Subrat started playing games with their guests. Drinks were also served during this time. Shalu and Subrat also drank heavily while playing the games. At around 1 am, everyone moved to the DJ floor and requested songs from the 1990s. Shalu and Subrat were seen dancing enthusiastically. Saurabh said the couple continued dancing on the DJ floor until around 2 am. As it got late, the staff told them that the food was getting cold. However, Shalu said she wanted to dance for some more time and asked the DJ to play her favourite songs. They began eating after around 2.30 am and left the lounge at around 3.30 am. Waiter said Shalu did not appear to be plotting father-in-law’s murder Sam, a waiter from Shuklaganj, was responsible for looking after all the guests at the party. He said he had been working at the lounge for the past four years. Both vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes were served at the party. Sam said Shalu and Subrat particularly liked the grilled fish and chicken tikka and praised the food. He said the couple appeared very happy throughout the party. “Looking at Shalu, it did not seem at all that she was allegedly having her father-in-law murdered,” he said. The lounge staff were shocked when they learnt about the incident the next day and wondered what had happened. Domestic worker allegedly offered ₹6 lakh to carry out murder According to police, Vishal had been unemployed since 2022 and had a debt of ₹2 lakh. Around 20 days earlier, he had gone to Subrat’s house looking for work. Police said Shalu told him that she was troubled by her father-in-law’s behaviour, claiming that he constantly interfered in her affairs and had CCTV cameras installed in the house. She allegedly asked Vishal to either kill her father-in-law or arrange for his accident. He was a wholesale pharmaceutical trader and ran the business with his son Businessman Vineet Minocha lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Arbit Apartment. He ran a pharmaceutical firm named Pharma Traders on Birhana Road. Vineet managed the business along with his son Subrat. The firm had an annual turnover of ₹50-60 crore. His family includes his wife Puneeta, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Puneeta is a marriage counsellor. Shalu and Subrat got married seven years ago. Police said Vishal initially did not agree to arrange an accident. Shalu allegedly then suggested that he should suffocate Vineet with a pillow while he was asleep so that people would believe he had died of a heart attack. She allegedly promised to give Vishal a job after the act and also offered him ₹6 lakh for carrying out the murder. Vishal then allegedly agreed to kill Vineet Minocha. Police said Vishal offered his friend Rajkishore ₹30,000 to join him, following which the two allegedly murdered Vineet Minocha on the night of September 5.

stories.title: Elections to be fought more on mobiles than on ground:BJP, SP devise strategies to expand reach in UP; Mayawati has better X strike rate
stories.summary: This time, the Uttar Pradesh Assembly election will be fought more on mobile phones than on the ground. People are understanding issues through reels, short videos and social media posts rather than long speeches by political leaders. The political power of social media became even more visible after the Gen-Z protests held in Delhi from June 6 to July 25. This is why BJP, SP and BSP have put their full strength into social media. Here are three reasons behind it: After SIR, the state has a total of 13.39 crore voters. Of these, 12.28 crore have smartphones. According to mobile network companies, around 90% of voters in urban areas and 65% in rural areas have smartphones. An average voter spends around 4-5 hours a day on social media. 1. BJP (UP): More followers, but low reach on routine posts X (Twitter): Looking at data from July 26 to September 10, normal posts from the @BJP4UP handle generally receive between 5,000 and 40,000 views. However, posts targeting Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi perform better. A ‘The Priest King’ video posted on September 6 received 7.49 lakh views. Facebook and Instagram: The Facebook page generally receives between 100 and 300 reactions. On Instagram too, more than 90% of posts remain below 1 lakh views. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is BJP’s biggest and most influential digital face. 2. SP: Strong reach despite fewer followers X (Twitter): Posts featuring press releases and government statements remain limited to 4,000-12,000 views, while videos related to Akhilesh receive 15,000-45,000 views. These figures are from July 26 to September 10. Facebook and Instagram: Clips of Akhilesh’s speeches on Facebook receive between 9,600 and 36,000 likes. On Instagram, SP has fewer followers than BJP, but its average likes per post are higher. 3. BSP: Mayawati’s direct hold on X X (Twitter): The @bspindia handle only retweets Mayawati’s posts. Its reach does not even cross 100. Facebook and Instagram: We could not find BSP’s official Facebook page. However, it posts on Instagram around once every seven days on average. Posts related to Akash Anand and Mayawati receive between 5,000 and 15,000 likes. Akhilesh has strong engagement, Mayawati has hold on X 1. Yogi Adityanath: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s social media accounts appear to have the highest reach among the three leaders. His posts on political statements, development projects and cultural issues receive lakhs and even crores of views. An Instagram post on September 7 received more than 1.2 crore views and over 10 lakh likes. 2. Akhilesh Yadav: Most posts by SP president Akhilesh Yadav are getting more than 1 lakh views. However, photo posts and short updates receive only 3,000-18,000 views. On Instagram, his reels and videos are reaching lakhs and crores of views. 3. Mayawati: BSP supremo Mayawati’s strongest hold is visible on X. Between September 1 and 10, most of her posts featuring statements received more than 1 lakh views. An Instagram post on September 6 received more than 10 lakh views. How BJP and SP are increasing their reach, what is their strategy BJP focuses on 30-second reels On September 10, BJP IT Cell national coordinator Deepak Mhaskey held a major meeting with the state team in Lucknow. BJP’s future strategy is as follows: People no longer watch entire speeches. Therefore, selected and sharp excerpts from leaders’ speeches will be turned into reels and made viral. BJP has prepared a large team of digital influencers. They are being paid according to their reach and number of followers. The party has acknowledged that the opposition was getting ahead in setting the narrative. New IT teams are now being formed at district level, which will respond to SP and Congress in their own style without using abusive language. SP focuses on real-time response SP’s social media team operates from the party headquarters in Lucknow, with office-bearers posted in every district. Whenever an incident takes place anywhere in the state, the local team immediately sends information and videos to the Lucknow team. SP leaves no opportunity to target the government. Through Akhilesh’s official pages, it directly sets an aggressive narrative. Social media is not just publicity, but also a test of claims Social media expert Anup Mishra says, “Digital content will play the most decisive role in the 2027 UP Assembly election. Gen-Z is checking the reality of every promise and claim on social media. If an issue gets support on digital platforms, it becomes an agenda for television channels and newspapers.”

stories.title: Why HC released properties of Mukhtar’s relatives:Is UP Gangster Act weak; what changes can govt make to law?
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has released properties of Mukhtar Ansari’s relatives that were attached under the Gangsters Act. In a ruling in another case, the Supreme Court described the Act as ‘stillborn’, meaning a ‘dead law’ that died at birth. Comparing the Gangsters Act with Maharashtra’s MCOCA and Gujarat’s GCOCA, the court pointed out the legal shortcomings of the Gangsters Act. Read in today’s UP Explainer why the properties were released, what legal loopholes make the Gangsters Act weak, and what changes the government can make to the law… Question-1: Why did the Allahabad High Court release the properties of Mukhtar’s relatives? Answer: We will understand this in two parts. First, let us know which properties were released and in whose names they were… 1. September 2026: A bungalow worth around ₹2.5 crore in Dalibagh, Lucknow. It was in the name of Farhat Ansari, Mukhtar’s sister-in-law and wife of SP MP Afzal Ansari. The then Ghazipur DM had attached it in October 2022. 2. August 2026: Around 25 bighas of agricultural land, orchards, and a farmhouse in Machha and Shakarpur mauzas of Ghazipur, worth around ₹12 crore. These properties were in the names of nieces Nusrat, Nooria, and Maria, and sister-in-law Farhat Ansari. They were attached in 2022. 3. March 2026: 18 shops in Ghazipur worth around ₹28 lakh. These were in the name of cousin Mansoor Ansari and were attached in March 2023. Now, let us understand why the properties were released… Under Section 14 of the Gangsters Act (UP Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities Prevention Act, 1986), the DM can attach property even without a case being decided or the crime being proved, on the basis of a preliminary inquiry and police report. According to the Act, the DM must have ‘reason to believe’ that the movable or immovable property has been acquired with money obtained through crime. What constitutes ‘reason to believe’ has not been clearly defined. However, in court, it has to be proved that there is a direct link between the date of the crime, the illegal income generated from it, and the money used to purchase the property. This is called the ‘money trail’. In all these cases, the police could not establish this link. Question-2: What kind of legal loopholes did the SC point out in the Gangsters Act? Answer: In a judgment in a case on 21 August, 2026, the Supreme Court made several serious observations about the Act. It also explained why the law is technically weak… Definition of crime is not clear: The Supreme Court said the offences mentioned in this law are already punishable under the IPC and BNS. Therefore, the law does not define any separate offence; instead, it declares a person a ‘gangster’ and punishes them. This is its biggest shortcoming. A law made in the name of preventing violence appears, in several cases, to promote violence and repression against innocent people. Treating a person as guilty without a verdict: The court said that once provisions of the Gangsters Act are imposed, the process of arrest, prolonged judicial custody, trial, and punishment begins. In such a situation, the trial appears to become a mere formality, and the verdict seems to have been decided in advance. The person is defamed, and people begin to consider them guilty. Against the general legal principle: According to Supreme Court lawyer Virag Gupta, under MCOCA and other central laws, action to attach property is taken after the crime has been proved. However, under the Gangsters Act, property can be attached even before the trial begins, merely on the basis of the Act’s provisions being added to an FIR. The accused or property owner is not given a notice before the attachment. At the same time, the owner has to prove that the property is not ‘illegal’. This goes against the general principles of law. Loose standard for proving a crime network: Maharashtra-Gujarat laws continuously monitor the illegal activities of a crime network (gang). In contrast, the Gangsters Act is also imposed on petty or individual offenders. This takes the law away from its basic objective of dealing with ‘organised crime’. The Supreme Court had given a judgment in a similar case on August 21. Question-3: How is the Gangsters Act weaker than the Maharashtra-Gujarat laws? Answer: A comparison with Maharashtra’s MCOCA (Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999) and Gujarat’s GCOCA (Gujarat Control of Terrorism and Organised Crime Act, 2019) shows… Question-4: What changes can the government make to the Gangsters Act? Answer: No official draft for amendments to the law has been presented yet. However, considering the recent court judgments, Supreme Court lawyer Virag Gupta suggests that the following changes could be considered… Shortcoming 1: Clear definition of crime Technical point: The law needs to clearly specify which ‘act’ constitutes an offence. Sections 2(b) and 2(c) of the Gangsters Act only explain ‘gang’ and ‘gangster’, meaning they describe a ‘status’, not an act. Impact: Police can register an FIR by declaring the accused a ‘gangster’, even if there is no concrete or provable allegation. Possible reform: Section 2 could be amended to clearly specify (a) which acts constitute offences, and (b) how many incidents/FIRs are required at minimum to establish ‘continuity’. Shortcoming 2: Standards for property attachment Technical point: Under the existing procedure, the DM can attach property by declaring it ‘benami’ or ‘acquired through gangster activities’. Impact: According to the legal principle, the burden of proving that property is criminally acquired lies with the prosecution (police), not with the accused to prove their innocence. The existing procedure works in the opposite manner. Possible reform: (a) Before issuing an attachment order, the DM could be required to record a ‘preliminary evidence report’ showing a direct financial link (money trail) between the property and the crime. (b) If concrete evidence is not found within a specified time limit, a provision could be added for the attachment to be automatically cancelled. Shortcoming 3: Using only a family relationship as a basis Technical point: The Allahabad High Court has clearly said that property cannot be attached merely on the basis of an allegation or the owner’s relationship with a criminal. Possible reform: Mafias often purchase properties in the names of their drivers, employees, or relatives. A new amendment could create a legal mechanism for coordination with the Income Tax Department and the Benami Property Act to seize such ‘benami’ properties.

stories.title: Russian police ties up Kanpur engineer and abducts him:Threaten to kill him; tortured him for 48 hours, he says he will never go abroad again
stories.summary: A Russian police officer in Moscow detained a Kanpur-based engineer for 48 hours and tortured him. The engineer returned home to Kanpur with his wife and 10-year-old son on Thursday night. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, engineer Chandan Gupta said, “The police tied my hands and my friend’s hands and took us away in a police van. The officers abused us and threatened to kill us. “They took my friend to a separate room and beat him with sticks. We were not allowed to speak to our families. They did not provide us with a phone or a translator. The police falsely accused me of breaking the glass of an ambulance while drunk. Chandan said, “After this incident, I have no intention of going back to Russia for work. In fact, I will not go abroad for work again. I have been living in Moscow with my wife and son since 2023. Before that, I had also lived in Moscow for two years.” His wife, Sneha, said, “If the ambulance’s glass was broken, then where is the evidence?” Read the special report based on Dainik Bhaskar’s conversation with the engineer and his wife… Police tied my hands and took me away, seized my passport Engineer Chandan Gupta was working in Moscow on a high-qualified visa through a polyfilm company based in Noida’s Sector 62. He is a resident of Yashoda Nagar in Kanpur. His wife, Sneha, has studied LLB. Chandan said that on September 5, he went out for a walk with his friend Ashish and another friend after dinner. They were heading towards Kitay-Gorod Metro Station via the Hanging Bridge and Red Square when the police caught Ashish and him. Their other friend was a little farther away and managed to escape. The police then tied one hand of each of them and took them to a police vehicle parked around 400 metres away. During this, they also took Chandan’s mobile phone, passport, and other documents. Chandan said they repeatedly asked the police why they were being detained, but the policemen did not give them any answer. Police said I was drunk and had broken an ambulance window Chandan said that after making him sit in the vehicle, the police told him that he had broken an ambulance window. The policemen repeatedly said, “You broke the ambulance glass.” He asked them when and where he had broken the ambulance window. He was not shown any video or other evidence. The police also claimed that he was drunk, but he said he had not consumed alcohol. “The behaviour of the policemen was extremely inappropriate. They pushed me and threatened to beat me when I asked questions. My friend, who was detained with me, repeatedly asked the policemen why we had been arrested. He was then taken to a separate place and beaten several times with sticks.” No phone or translator provided until we went to court Chandan said the police vehicle carrying the two of them drove around for about an hour. On the way, the policemen stopped at one place and spoke to an officer. After this, they were taken to the Basmanny police station. Until around 1 a.m., they did not know what action was being taken against them. Chandan said they were not allowed to speak to anyone over the phone at the police station. They did not have their phones, and no translator was provided. He said they were not allowed to meet anyone until they went to court. According to Chandan, the language barrier made the situation even more difficult for them. However, he was confident that his family and company would be trying to help them. Police made us write and sign documents as they wanted Chandan said that before releasing them, the Russian police made them sign some protocols and documents. “The policemen said we had to write exactly what they told us. The police threatened me that if I did not cooperate, I would be released for now, but they could detain me again and seek a long remand.” “I was afraid that if I stayed in Moscow, I could be implicated in another case. That is why I decided to return to India with my family.” Chandan said he had been hearing about incidents of Indian nationals being harassed by police in Russia for around the past five months. His acquaintances and people from his company had told him that police stopped Indians, made them sit for several hours, and took their documents and money. Chandan says Indian Embassy did not even speak to him Chandan has also questioned the Indian Embassy in Moscow. He said that during the nearly 48 hours he was in custody, no official from the Indian Embassy contacted him. His wife, Sneha, had appealed to the Indian government for help through social media. Despite this, neither did any embassy official come to meet him nor did anyone speak to him over the phone about the incident. “What hurts me the most is that the Indian Embassy issued information based on the Russian police’s statement without even hearing my side.” Sneha asks: Where was the evidence before issuing the statement? Chandan’s wife, Sneha Gupta, has also questioned the Indian Embassy. She said that before issuing a statement about her husband, the embassy did not seek complete information about the incident from either her or her husband. “If Chandan had consumed alcohol, was he medically examined? If he broke the ambulance window, where is the video or photograph? What was the ambulance’s location and what was my husband’s location?” She said these questions should be answered. Sneha said that if Chandan has been accused of breaking the ambulance window, the evidence should be made public. She demanded that the Indian Embassy issue a clarification on the entire matter. Sneha said, “I want this matter to be investigated.”

stories.title: Village chief's son dies of swine flu in Kanpur:Postmortem confirms cause; second patient on ventilator at Hallet Hospital
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man from Kannauj, identified as Shivam, has died of swine flu while undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Kanpur. His family had alleged negligence in his treatment and demanded a post-mortem. After the post-mortem and the investigation report, it became clear on Saturday that Shivam did not die due to medical negligence but because of swine flu. The officer in charge of the post-mortem house has sent a report to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO). Following the death of the swine flu patient, the health department has gone on alert. Meanwhile, another 55-year-old swine flu patient is undergoing treatment on a ventilator at the LLR Hospital (Hallet Hospital). His condition remains extremely critical. Post-mortem report reveals the cause of death, health department issues alert Village Chief Ram Raj, a resident of Tera Jaket village in Kannauj's Gursahaiganj area, said that on the afternoon of August 28, his son suddenly experienced severe stomach pain. When his condition worsened, he was taken to Dr. Tomar's clinic in Kannauj. After examining him, the doctor said that fluid had accumulated in his lungs and that he had an abdominal infection. As his condition was described as critical, he was admitted for better treatment to Anurag Hospital in Sharda Nagar, Kanpur. When his condition deteriorated, the hospital management admitted him to the ICU, where he remained under treatment for four days. He died on September 1. The family members created a disturbance, alleging negligence in treatment, and demanded that the body be post-mortem examined. After an investigation, police from Rawatpur police station sent the body for a post-mortem examination, which was conducted on September 2. During the post-mortem, samples were sent for testing after suspicions arose. The test report received on September 5 made it clear that the youth had not died due to incorrect treatment, but because of a swine flu infection. As soon as the information was received, the officer in charge of the postmortem house sent a report to the CMO. Along with this, an investigation report was sent to the CMO of Kannauj. Now, all family members will also be tested to determine whether any of them have contracted swine flu. Meanwhile, the health department was also put on alert as soon as it learned of the death of the first swine flu patient. CMO Dr. Haridutt Nemi took cognizance of the matter and issued an alert. The staff at the hospital where the patient died will be tested. In addition, the employees of the postmortem house will also be tested to determine whether anyone has been exposed to the infection.

stories.title: SP MLA’s uncle says offering namaz is matter of pride:'I'm not afraid of FIR'; had offered prayers at Moradabad Circuit House
stories.summary: Offering namaz is not a matter of shame, but of pride. I am not afraid of legal proceedings. Saraswati Vandana is performed in schools, and Bhoomi Pujan is conducted before government construction projects. In such a situation, filing an FIR or raising questions only about namaz is discrimination. This was said on Saturday by Haji Mohammad Usman, the uncle of Samajwadi Party MLA Mohammad Faheem Irfan, in Moradabad. A video of Mohammad Usman offering namaz at the Circuit House in Moradabad on Friday (September 4) had surfaced. An FIR was registered against Mohammad Usman in the matter that same Friday. After this, Usman said that he did not know when or where the video was recorded, or who had recorded it. SP leader says-I did not block anyone's way Mohammad Usman said, I can be seen offering prayers behind cars in the parking lot. I am not seen blocking anyone's way. If any law has been violated, there should be an impartial investigation. However, the case registered over offering prayers should be dismissed. The Constitution has given everyone the right to worship. People who believe in the Constitution will not be intimidated by such cases. Usman appealed to people not to respond to hatred with hatred and to raise their voices while staying within the framework of the Constitution and the law. FIR registered for offering namaz at circuit house An FIR was registered against Samajwadi Party district vice president Haji Mohammad Usman at the Majhola police station late Friday evening on the complaint of Anit Kumar, the junior engineer in charge of the Circuit House. City SP Ranvijay Singh said, Haji Usman parked his car on the Circuit House road and offered namaz illegally behind it. This obstructed the movement of vehicles and people. The police have registered a case and begun an investigation. Video posted on Facebook on September 3 A video of Haji Usman offering prayers was posted on September 3 by a Facebook user named Malik Sharif. The caption of the post read: ‘Mohammad Usman Pradhan ji offering the Asr prayer today.’ Photos and videos related to the programs and activities of SP MLA Mohammad Faheem have been regularly posted from this account. Several photos and videos of the MLA and his uncle, Haji Usman, together have also been posted on this account. After the matter came to light, the video of the prayer was deleted from the social media account. Bajrang Dal also demands an investigation from the administration The police are now investigating when and under what circumstances the video was made, and who posted it on social media. Meanwhile, Rohan Saxena, state president of the Rashtriya Bajrang Dal, has demanded that the administration conduct an impartial investigation into the matter. He said, The Circuit House is government premises. In such a situation, the administration should clarify whether religious activities of any religion are permitted on government premises. The administration should also investigate the intention behind offering namaz at the Circuit House on the day of Shri Krishna Janmashtami. High Court had said-No one has the right to offer namaz in public places In May 2026, the Allahabad High Court delivered a ruling regarding offering namaz on public land. A bench of Justice Saral Srivastava and Justice Garima Prasad had said: Everyone has equal rights over public land. Its one-sided use is not legally acceptable. Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Barelvi had supported the High Court's decision. The Maulana had said, Islam clearly states that prayers should not be offered at a place where there is any dispute, where a spectacle is being created, or where someone has an objection or opposition. Mohammad Usman has been involved in controversies before Haji Mohammad Usman has also served as a former district panchayat member. He has previously been the head of his ancestral village, Ibrahimपुर. Haji Usman is the younger brother of former Bilari MLA Haji Mohammad Irfan and the uncle of the current Bilari MLA. Haji Mohammad Usman's name had earlier surfaced in a caste certificate controversy as well. Following a complaint, the district-level verification committee investigated the matter. The investigation found that the Other Backward Class (OBC) certificates belonging to MLA Mohammad Faheem and his uncle Mohammad Usman, identifying them as members of the Jhojha caste, did not comply with the rules. Following this, the administration cancelled the OBC caste certificates of MLA Mohammad Faheem, Haji Mohammad Usman, and his two daughters, Farheen Jahan and Samreen Jahan.

stories.title: 7 daughters carry mother’s bier:Youngest daughter performs last rites, says ‘She raised us like sons’
stories.summary: In Auraiya on Saturday, after their mother's death, seven daughters took turns carrying her bier on their shoulders. When they reached the cremation ground, preparations for the last rites began. Meanwhile, when the question of lighting the funeral pyre arose, everyone was left wondering who would perform the ritual. After a discussion, the youngest daughter decided that she would light her mother's funeral pyre. Why rely on a male relative? Her elder sisters also supported her decision. At around 3 p.m., the youngest daughter lit her mother's funeral pyre. The incident took place in the Dibiyapur area. Complete incident details Mother raised them alone after the father's death Krishna Devi (59), a resident of Durga Nagar, was married to Ramkishore Savita, who had served in the army. He died a few years after retiring. At the time, due to social customs, the family sought the help of a nephew for Ramkishore's last rites, as they had no son. After her husband's death, Krishna Devi raised her seven daughters all by herself. Their mother was their sole support and guide. Krishna Devi had been ill for quite some time. Her daughters jointly bore the expenses of her treatment and the household. Her youngest daughter, Soni Savita (25), was living at her maternal home to care for her mother. Her husband works in a private job in Agra. All seven daughters shouldered their mother's bier Krishna Devi passed away on Saturday morning. During preparations for the funeral, there was a discussion about who would perform the last rites. The villagers and family members discussed whether a male relative should take on this responsibility. Meanwhile, Krishna Devi's youngest daughter, Soni Savita, interrupted everyone. She said, "Our mother raised us like sons. She used to say that all of you daughters are sons to me. We also never let her feel the absence of sons. Now, we will not depend on anyone else for our mother's last rites." Daughter performed the last rites for her mother following all traditions Setting aside social customs, Krishna Devi's 7 daughters took turns carrying their mother's bier on their shoulders. The villagers and family members also helped them. Everyone reached the cremation ground in Dibiyapur with the deceased's body. There, Krishna Devi's youngest daughter, Soni, lit her mother's funeral pyre following all the traditional rituals. This decision conveyed a message about the role of daughters in society. According to the villagers, their mother made her daughters self-reliant throughout her life. She stood by them through every difficulty. The daughters, too, fulfilled their responsibility toward their mother at the end of her life.

stories.title: Part of machine collapses at Mirzapur crusher plant, 4 dead:Workers trapped in debris; SDM, SP reach spot
stories.summary: At a crusher plant in Mirzapur, a heavy part of a machine suddenly broke off and fell while dust was being removed. The accident caused chaos at the site. Four workers died. The accident occurred at around 3 p.m. at Pintu Singh Patel's crusher plant in the Ahraura area. As soon as they learned of the incident, nearby residents reached the site and informed the police and administration. Four workers from Chunar trapped After receiving the information, a police team reached the site and inspected the scene. According to Chunar Circle Officer Mohammad Faheem, Bargawan resident Lal Bahadur, son of Dulaare, Ashok, son of Basant, Rakesh, son of Ram Ji, and Duryodhan, son of Jhingai, all under Chunar police station limits, are feared to be trapped in the debris. No plant owner or employee was present at the site at the time of the accident. However, the police have begun gathering information by questioning people connected with the incident. SDM and SP reached the spot SDM, SP Rajkumar Meena and CO Gayatri Yadav reached the spot to investigate the incident. They inspected the site and gathered information. The officials have begun examining all the facts related to the accident. At present, it will become clear only after the administration's investigation under what circumstances the heavy part of the machine fell and how many workers were present at the plant at the time of the accident. The police have not confirmed the death of any worker or that anyone was trapped under the debris. The news is being updated continuously...

stories.title: Vinod Tawde on Akhilesh’s PDA:‘Someone else’s wealth is ours’; reaches Lucknow for first time as BJP’s UP in-charge to meet Yogi
stories.summary: BJP’s Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde on Saturday said the party would “thwart Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA”, interpreting the Samajwadi Party leader’s acronym as “Paraya Dhan Apna” (someone else’s wealth is one’s own). Addressing his first visit to Lucknow after being given charge of Uttar Pradesh, Tawde said the BJP had become the world’s largest party under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, while the pace of development in Uttar Pradesh had accelerated under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. He further said- Every worker of the BJP and NDA will contest and win the upcoming Assembly elections with full strength. After that, we will remain dedicated to serving the people of Uttar Pradesh for the next five years. Earlier, Vinod Tawde received a grand welcome at Lucknow airport. Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, state organization general secretary Dharampal Singh, state general secretary Sanjay Rai, and state office in-charge Govind Narayan Shukla were present on the occasion. BJP president Nitin Nabin appointed Vinod Tawde as the new state in-charge of Uttar Pradesh on December 18. Jagdish Ishwarbhai Patel was given the responsibility of co-in-charge. Tawde is the BJP's national general secretary and a Rajya Sabha MP. He has previously served as the in-charge of Haryana and Bihar. In 2025, under his charge, the BJP registered a landslide victory in Bihar. Will hold a review meeting behind closed doors, meet the CM and Deputy CM as well Vinod Tawde, who has arrived in Uttar Pradesh for a two-day visit, will begin a series of meetings to strengthen the organisation and sharpen the strategy for the upcoming elections. First, he will hold a closed-door review meeting with Pankaj Chaudhary and Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh. After this, he will meet with the BJP's state office-bearers to receive feedback on organisational activities, campaigns, and future action plans. He will then hold a core committee meeting with CM Yogi, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, and Brajesh Pathak. The meeting will deliberate on the current political climate, coordination between the government and the organisation, and the strategy for the upcoming elections. How important is Vinod Tawde's visit before the elections? Find out Vinod Tawde's visit to Lucknow before the assembly elections is considered highly significant. According to political analysts, the party will seek to infuse new enthusiasm among its organisation and workers through this visit so that preparations for the upcoming elections can be strengthened. The visit could also prove crucial in further consolidating the party's hold at the grassroots level. Elected as an MLA in 2014, became BJP's national secretary in 2020 Vinod Tawde is originally from Mumbai. He remained active in the party organisation in Maharashtra for a long time. He has also served as a minister in the Maharashtra government and as the leader of the opposition in the Legislative Council. In 2026, he was appointed in-charge of the Kerala Assembly elections. His political career began with the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). In 2014, Tawde was elected as an MLA from Maharashtra's Borivali constituency for the first time. On September 26, 2020, the BJP appointed him as its National Secretary. With this, his role expanded beyond Maharashtra into the national organisation. Why did the BJP give Tawde the most crucial state? The reason... Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh next year In Uttar Pradesh, which has 403 assembly seats, elections are likely to be held in February-March next year. The BJP suffered a setback in the state in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The Samajwadi Party emerged as the largest party with 37 seats, while the BJP was reduced to 33 seats. In this context, the 2027 elections are being seen as a major test for the BJP – not only to retain power in the state but also to strengthen its position following its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

stories.title: 81 teachers honoured on Teachers’ Day:CM Yogi felicitates them in Gorakhpur; retirement age raised by 2 years, 4,000 km free bus travel annually
stories.summary: During a Teachers' Day ceremony in Gorakhpur, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath broke with protocol and invited all 81 teachers to the stage to honour them. He said he had been told that only 10 teachers would come on stage, but he knew that all the teachers had travelled from faraway places. "Some have come from Meerut, while others have come from Hamirpur and Mahoba," he said. He further said, "It is fine. If they instil values in children, they are themselves well-cultured. They may not say anything, but they too have feelings. It may have taken up some of my time, but I called everyone to the stage and honoured them." Taking a dig at previous governments, CM Yogi said: "Before 2017, cheating was carried out on a contract basis. Children from other states used to come here and pay money to pass examinations. The education system was in a poor state and the youth were facing a crisis of identity. Questions were being raised about Uttar Pradesh, and the state with India's largest population was being put in the dock." The ceremony was held at the Yogiraj Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium. Of the 81 teachers honoured, 61 are from the Basic Education Department and 20 are from the Secondary Education Department. The group also includes 33 women teachers. At the ceremony, 76 teachers from the Basic and Secondary Education Departments were honoured with the 'State Teachers' Award 2025', while five teachers from self-financed secondary schools received the 'Chief Minister's Teachers' Award 2025'. See the pictures... CM Yogi Adityanath felicitating teachers. Also present on stage are Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh, Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi, Fisheries Minister Sanjay Nishad, MLC Dhruv Kumar Tripathi and others. Yogi says, 'We have stopped making cheating hubs examination centres' CM Yogi said that the ‘Nipun Abhiyan’ would now be implemented up to Class 5. He said that before 2017, children did not even have basic knowledge of letters. He said, "If a child does not know letters and numbers, how will they study mathematics and science, and how will they understand the meaning of a sentence?" He said the result was that schools had turned into hubs for cheating. “Cheating was carried out on a contract basis, and students from distant states used to come here to take examinations.” He added, "Contracts were run in the name of examinations, and another person would appear for an examination in place of a candidate. I instructed that such schools should not be made examination centres, and subsequently, such schools were stopped from being made centres." Yogi says, ‘For the first time, teachers have been guaranteed social security’ CM Yogi said, "For the first time, teachers have been guaranteed social security so that, in the event of any unfortunate incident, a teacher's family does not feel that it has been left alone. This is also a part of respecting teachers." He added, "The government has taken several steps in this direction so that students can receive quality education and a better environment can be created for it."

stories.title: Bulldozer action at mosque in Saharanpur Collectorate:Mayawati urges govt to stop action, Iqra placed under house arrest; MP Masood vows HC move
stories.summary: 70-year-old mosque in the collectorate complex in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, is being demolished. Six bulldozers have been carrying out the demolition since 4am on Saturday. As a precautionary measure, five companies of PAC and RAF personnel, along with 200 police officers, have been deployed. Police are not allowing anyone to approach the mosque. So far, around 70% of the mosque has been demolished. The action is being carried out on the orders of a magistrate after a court declared the mosque illegal. Before the demolition, rumours spread around 11pm on Friday that the administration was planning to demolish the mosque, drawing a large crowd. The administration team immediately reached the spot and dispersed the crowd. Kairana MP Ikra Hasan, who was travelling to Saharanpur to oppose the action, was placed under house arrest by police. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said in Lucknow that a true Hindu can never insult another religion. He alleged that the action was being taken because people had been caught stealing from the Ram temple. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi questioned whether Muslims still have their constitutional right to religious freedom. He asked why places of worship were repeatedly being demolished over what he called weak and fabricated reasons. BSP chief Mayawati appealed to the government to immediately stop the demolition. stories.title: SP launches PDA Pathshala in Lucknow:Free bags, books featuring Akhilesh Yadav distributed; spokesperson says 26,000 schools shut across UP
stories.summary: Today (5 Sept) on the occasion of Teachers’ Day, the Samajwadi Party organised a PDA Pathshala in Gomtinagar, Lucknow. SP leaders and workers taught children as part of a protest against the closure of primary schools across Uttar Pradesh. Notebooks and books were also distributed among the children. SP says 26,000 schools have been shut SP leader Fakhrul Hasan Chand said, “PDA Pathshalas were organised in all 75 districts of the state following a call by party national president Akhilesh Yadav. The campaign was launched in protest against the closure of around 26,000 primary schools.” According to Chand, “Children from PDA communities have been most affected by the closures, particularly those from backward, Dalit, minority, Muslim and farming families. The disruption was affecting their education.” Party vows to continue raising education issue Chand said, “The Samajwadi Party would continue to raise issues related to education through PDA Pathshalas and oppose measures that, according to the party, are disrupting access to schooling for children from disadvantaged communities.” SP workers to teach children daily and provide study materials SP workers said the PDA Pathshala will continue to operate, with a Samajwadi Party worker teaching the children for an hour every day. Study materials will also be provided to them. Facilities to be added soon At present, the children study while sitting on mats spread on the ground. SP workers said chairs, desks and other necessary facilities would soon be arranged for them. Promise to reopen closed schools The workers said that if the Samajwadi Party forms the government in Uttar Pradesh, all schools that were shut down will be reopened.

stories.title: Student’s father beats principal in Gorakhpur:Tears shirt, vandalises school; daughter was made to do squats for arriving late
stories.summary: The father of a Class 6 student allegedly assaulted a government school principal after the teacher punished his daughter for arriving late in Gorakhpur. The principal was reportedly beaten in front of the staff, and his shirt was torn. Other teachers intervened and defused the situation. According to reports, the teacher had made the student perform the ‘murga’ (rooster) punishment for coming late to school. After learning about it, her father became angry, reached the school and allegedly assaulted the principal. The principal has filed a complaint against the man, accusing him of assault and vandalising school property. The incident took place on 1st September at Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya in Khirkita Dubey, under the Gola police station area. The complaint was filed on 3rd September. Student was made to perform the 'murga' pose for arriving late Jitendra Kumar (56), the principal of Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya Khirkita Dubey in the Gola area, filed a complaint against a student's father, Dilip Kumar, on September 3. In his complaint, Jitendra Kumar stated that on the morning of September 1, a class 6 student arrived late to school. Students who arrive late to school are punished to maintain discipline. Under this policy, the student was made to perform the 'murga' (rooster) pose for a short time. When the student's father, Dilip Kumar, learned about this, he became angry. It is alleged that Dilip Kumar then reached the school and started a dispute. Jitendra Kumar stated that he tried to reason with Dilip, but he began to assault him. Beaten in front of staff, shirt torn Jitendra Kumar alleged that Dilip Kumar assaulted him in front of other school staff. Other teachers stepped in to save him and calmed the situation by reasoning with the accused. It is alleged that during the assault, Dilip Kumar also tore his shirt. Additionally, government property was damaged due to vandalism in the school. Accused works as a painter Dilip Kumar works as a painter. It is being reported that he had gone to the school earlier as well to secure a contract, which had also led to a dispute. The accused has been absconding since the incident, and the police are searching for him. Fear among staff after the incident After receiving information about the incident, the police reached the spot. The head teacher has demanded strict action against the accused from the police. He expressed apprehension that the accused might repeat such an incident with him in the future as well. After the incident, the school teachers and staff are also scared. The matter is a topic of discussion in the area. Gola Police Station In-charge Inspector Chandraprakash Pandey said that a case has been registered against the accused based on the complaint of the headmaster. The matter is being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Floods hit 26 UP districts, 3.5 lakh affected:17,000 rescued so far; rainfall quota nearly met, alert in 71 districts
stories.summary: Due to continuous monsoon rains in UP, 26 districts, including Varanasi and Prayagraj, are affected by floods. This has impacted 3.53 lakh people. So far, 17,544 people have been moved to safe locations, while approximately 5,000 people are staying in relief camps. On Saturday morning, light rain occurred in 10 cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Hardoi, and Sitapur. The rest of the districts are experiencing mild sunshine. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for rain with thunderstorms in 71 districts today. Heavy rain is expected in Western UP. The rainfall quota for this monsoon season in the state has almost been met. As of September 4, an average of 612 mm of rainfall has been recorded in the state, whereas 619.7 mm of rain was recorded by September 4 last year. This means that so far, there has been only 1% less rainfall compared to last year. See pictures of the flood... Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh stated- Due to the weather systems formed near Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, Western UP will experience heavy rainfall in the next 24 hours. After this, the system will move towards Eastern UP. This will cause heavy rainfall in some areas of Eastern UP between September 6 and September 8. After September 8, this rain-bearing system will weaken, leading to a cessation of heavy rainfall across the state. However, light rain or drizzles will continue in some places.

UP MLAs caught taking bribes:Bhaskar exposes BJP, SP MLAs insisting on 35% commission - Part I
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, MLAs themselves are allegedly engaging in corruption in the name of development. They reportedly write recommendation letters for roads, drains and street lights only when they receive a 35% to 40% commission. A recommendation letter is a letter from an MLA based on which the CDO (Chief Development Officer) releases money from the MLA development fund. With 40% of the money allegedly going into the MLA's pocket, it can be imagined what the quality of the work would be. Dainik Bhaskar has made its biggest expose so far, catching two MLAs allegedly taking bribes on camera. A Bhaskar reporter posed as an NGO manager and negotiated with the MLAs for the release of funds. The MLAs were focused on just one question: how much commission would they get? The MLAs were caught taking commissions on a hidden camera and subsequently issued recommendation letters for the release of MLA funds. Of the two MLAs, one is from the BJP and the other from the Samajwadi Party (SP). Read the full investigation… First, we conducted a sting operation on BJP MLA Jai Mangal Kannaujiya. Kannaujiya has previously faced allegations of bribery. We registered an NGO and then underwent training related to solar lights because we intended to seek funds from the MLA specifically for installing solar lights. To build a rapport with the MLA, we travelled with him from village to village for 30 days. We held a total of eight rounds of negotiations with the MLA for funds for solar lights. In the fourth round, MLA Kannaujiya agreed to sanction work worth ₹10.50 lakh in return for a 35% commission. During the subsequent meetings, he took the bribe and signed the recommendation letter and handed it to us. Read our conversation with him word for word… "Others are giving me 40% commission. How much will you give me?" - Kannaujiya Kannaujiya: "The other solar people are giving 40% commission." Reporter: "We can give you up to 35%." Kannaujiya: "Fine. I want the money on the same day we write the letter." Reporter: "How much should we pay as an advance?" Kannaujiya: "Why pay an advance? Pay the full amount. Get the letter written by me and finish the matter." Reporter: "If you say so, we can pay 20% of the 35% commission now. Once the letter is issued, we will pay the remaining 80%." Kannaujiya: "Fine. Come tomorrow morning at 11am." Kannaujiya: "Is the proposal for ₹10.50 lakh?" Reporter: "The 35% commission will be ₹368,500. Twenty per cent of this will be ₹73,500." (While handing over the money) "We have brought ₹50,000 in cash for now. We will pay the rest later." Kannaujiya: "Fine. Bring it tomorrow." (Two days later, we reached the MLA's house and handed over the remaining amount.) "Give me some more money. We had agreed that you would give me 20% of the total payment," - Kannaujiya Kannaujiya: "How much is this?" Reporter: "₹23,500." Kannaujiya: "How much does it come to?" Reporter: "Thirty-five per cent of ₹10.50 lakh comes to ₹367,500, which we will give you. We had agreed to pay 20% of this amount upfront, which comes to ₹73,500. We had already given you ₹50,000." Kannaujiya: (surprised) "₹73,500. No, brother." (He took out the calculator on his mobile phone and spent some time adding up the figures.) "You are giving me 20%, aren't you? You had said you would give us 20% of the 35%." Reporter: "We are giving you 20% of the 35%. We have already given you ₹73,500. Now ₹294,000 remains." Kannaujiya: "Give me something more, brother. We had agreed that you would give me 20% of the total payment." Reporter: "You were upset, so we have come to give you something more." Kannaujiya: "I am not the kind of person who gets upset. If you want to give something more, then give it." Reporter: "Sir, this is ₹10,000." Kannaujiya: (while taking the money) "Go, enjoy yourself. Come tomorrow and collect the letter." In this way, MLA Kannaujiya took a total bribe of ₹83,500 from us. The following day, he handed over the recommendation letter. SP MLA Pooja Saroj from Mehnagar in Azamgarh district has also faced allegations of taking bribes. We developed a relationship with the MLA's relative and representative, Vikas Saroj. Posing as an NGO manager, we presented the MLA with a proposal to install solar lights and water coolers. When the MLA asked for a sample, we purchased and installed a solar light to demonstrate it. For 15 days, we went from village to village with her associates and selected the locations where the solar lights were to be installed. We held a total of 15 meetings with the MLA. During the 12th meeting, the MLA raised the issue of commission. ‘Our only rule on bribes is 50% in advance,’ - MLA Pooja Pooja: "What was discussed?" Reporter: "Please give us the work order. We will make some advance payment." Pooja: (laughing) "Not some. We have only one rule: 50% commission first and 50% later. Vikas can discuss the matter accordingly. How much commission are we getting?" Reporter: "We will be able to give up to 35%." Pooja: "How much will you give as an advance, 50% or…?" Reporter: "We will pay 10% of the 35% as an advance." Pooja: "Before the paper, the recommendation letter, is prepared; that is, when I sign it, 50% of the advance must have reached me." (At a rate of ₹13,500 per unit for 200 solar street lights and ₹20,000 per unit for 20 water coolers, the total budget came to ₹31 lakh.) Pooja: "The amount is very low. Around ₹10 lakh. Only ₹5 lakh has to be given as an advance." Reporter: "Take 10% of ₹10 lakh now. We will make the remaining 90% later." Pooja: "First, arrange the commission for the solar lights." Reporter: "Fine. The budget for 200 lights comes to ₹27 lakh. Thirty-five per cent of this is ₹9.45 lakh." Pooja: "How much is 50%?" Reporter: "It will be around ₹5 lakh. When you sign the letter, we will give you ₹1 lakh. As soon as the money is released, we will give you ₹8.45 lakh." Pooja: "No." (Showing ₹5 lakh on the calculator on her mobile phone) "Bring this amount and I will sign the letter and give it to you." Pooja: "Don't do this. Give the full amount after two days. It is not such a large amount." Reporter: "This is our NGO's policy." Pooja: "Who is it? Let me speak to them. Call them. They are following some nonsensical policy." Reporter: "We can arrange 25% for you tomorrow, which comes to ₹236,650. The rest will be paid after the letter is issued." Pooja: "No. You see how you want to do it." Reporter: "Ma'am, it is just a matter of two days." Pooja: "Their policy will not work with me. We are getting entangled for no reason. This is not right." A few days later, Vikas called. He said, "You haven't come." We said, "Madam, the MLA is insisting on 50% in advance. We can give 25%. If you get the MLA to sign the letter and send it to us on WhatsApp, we will come with ₹5 lakh." Seven days later, Vikas sent four recommendation letters. Vikas said, "Bring ₹14,17,500, which is half of the 35% commission, and take the hard copies of the letters." Since we had already exposed the MLA, we did not go to collect the hard copies. MLAs' close associates are also taking money MLA Pooja Saroj's representative Vikas took ₹10,000 from us three times: ₹10,000, then another ₹10,000, and then ₹5,000. That means these people are allegedly taking 1-2% of the MLA development fund. Similarly, Sanjeev Shukla, a close associate of Maharajganj Sadar MLA Jai Mangal Kannaujiya, took ₹5,000 from us on four occasions, totalling ₹20,000. Now know where MLAs can use the MLA fund In Uttar Pradesh, every MLA receives ₹5 crore every year under the MLA development fund. That means ₹25 crore over five years. The funds can be used for various works, including roads, drains, brick-paved roads, community buildings, drinking water and lighting. Taking commission from the MLA fund is a serious matter and can lead to a seven-year sentence Atul Singh, AGM-1 (Additional Government Advocate) at the Lucknow High Court, said, "If an MLA takes a commission or bribe, Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita will apply. It provides for a sentence of three to seven years. The accounts containing approved or remaining MLA funds in the name of the accused MLA can be frozen immediately. At the Assembly level, the Conduct Committee or Ethics Committee investigates the matter." The chain of bribery in the MLA fund does not end here. When an MLA's recommendation letter reaches the CDO office, a commission is allegedly fixed for everyone there, from employees to officers. Read Part 2 of Bhaskar's biggest expose tomorrow for the rate list of bribes allegedly demanded by officers and employees at the CDO office.

stories.title: Will Jayant Chaudhary field wife Charu in elections?:Just 2-minute speech in Saharanpur, but her reply to Akhilesh steals the show
stories.summary: At the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD)’s ‘Swabhiman Rally’ in Saharanpur, Charu Chaudhary, wife of Jayant Chaudhary, is drawing more attention for her speech than her husband. Charu directly hit back at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘chavanni’ (quarter-rupee coin) jibe at Jayant Chaudhary. Charu said, ‘No one has the right to insult you or lecture you.’ She added that such remarks reflect the other person’s mindset and arrogance. In a democracy, she said, it is the people who decide which government comes to power and who enters or leaves office. Following Charu’s assertive speech, speculation is growing in political circles that Jayant could field his wife in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. If that happens, Charu would become the second woman from the Chaudhary family to enter electoral politics. Jayant’s grandmother, Gayatri Devi, wife of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, was active in politics. She served as an MLA from Iglas in 1969 and Gokul in 1974, and was elected MP from Kairana in 1980. Will Jayant field Charu in 2027? Charu has three key advantages: a political family legacy, years of election campaign experience, and the ability to deliver political speeches openly and confidently. She has regularly addressed rural women at village gatherings in Mathura and Baghpat with ease. Charu’s association with politics is not new. She has been active in election campaigns and RLD activities since 2009 and has regularly appeared at her husband Jayant Chaudhary’s rallies. Her late father-in-law and former Union minister Ajit Singh also made her a star campaigner for the party, recognising her political involvement. During the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, Charu held a roadshow for Jayant Chaudhary in Chhaprauli, Baghpat. The event was scheduled to last around six hours, but the huge crowd and enthusiasm kept it going until around 1 am. In 2021, she also joined the farmers’ protest in Delhi and was seen supporting women farmers. She has a strong presence in rural areas of western Uttar Pradesh. During the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, she also shared the stage with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at rallies in Baghpat and Baraut. If the RLD fields her from a Jat-dominated constituency in 2027, it would not simply be a decision to field another candidate. It could be part of a strategy to simultaneously target women voters in western UP, Jat pride, and the political legacy of the Chaudhary family. Charu shows an aggressive side in Saharanpur The ‘Swabhiman Rally’ in Saharanpur on 3 September 2026 is being seen as significant in Charu’s political journey because this time, her speech directly targets the Opposition. Charu is invited to the stage before Jayant Chaudhary speaks. She is introduced in a distinctly political manner and then addresses the crowd directly without reading from a written speech. She says no one has the right to insult the people. Elections come and go, and it does not matter whether a party is in power or in Opposition. Commitment towards the people, she says, will always remain. She also links the regional identity and ‘chaudharahat’ (influence of the Chaudhary community) of western UP with electoral politics and appeals to voters to send RLD and its alliance candidates to Lucknow with overwhelming support. ‘Chavanni’ jibe heats up western UP politics The controversy in western UP politics begins with Akhilesh Yadav’s remark targeting Jayant Chaudhary. He says, ‘You turned a chavanni into a rupee, and still left us.’ The RLD turns the remark into an issue of political and social respect in western UP. Reactions emerge in Jat-dominated areas, amid which the ‘Swabhiman Rally’ is organised in Saharanpur. Charu and their two daughters also join Jayant on the stage at the rally. Jayant also hits back at Akhilesh Amid the political confrontation, Jayant Chaudhary also responds to Akhilesh Yadav. He says he generally tries to ensure that nobody becomes his enemy. Jayant says he has not even provoked Akhilesh, yet the SP chief keeps making remarks against him. Jayant plays videos of SP leaders at the rally and takes a political swipe, saying, Forget ABCD politics. We will trap you in G for sugarcane and J for Jat, and then SP will not come to power. Charu and Jayant’s love marriage Charu Chaudhary comes from a business family and is originally from a Punjabi family in Delhi. Her family has been associated with a fashion and jewellery business called ‘Juki’ in South Extension, south Delhi. Charu and Jayant are classmates at Delhi University’s Sri Venkateswara College. Their friendship develops into a relationship, and they marry on 14 August 2003. After marriage, Charu continues her professional career and works in the corporate sector for around two-and-a-half years. She later leaves her job to pursue her interests in fashion designing and jewellery. She studies at the Jewellery Product Development Centre (JPDC) in Delhi and also attends the Gemological Institute of America. From fashion designer to entrepreneur Charu runs a multi-brand, multi-product store called ‘Zuki’, featuring jewellery, clothing and other design-related products. According to Charu, the idea for a multi-brand store came to her several years earlier, but family responsibilities delayed the plan. She eventually turns the idea into a business. In October 2019, she also showcased her designer fashion collection at Toronto Fashion Week. Charu is conscious of fitness and regularly goes to the gym. She enjoys watching detective shows and has also appeared on the covers of several magazines. Charu and Jayant have two daughters, Sahira and Elisha.

stories.title: Mirzapur’s damaged school now rivals convent schools:Fewer than 50 students earlier, now AI-computer classes; principal says, ‘We won parents’ trust’
stories.summary: In the smart classroom, children are learning how artificial intelligence (AI) works through a digital screen. The children are sitting in front of computers, wearing headphones and speaking into microphones. Paintings explaining the syllabus adorn the classroom walls. Outside, the campus is surrounded by greenery. This is not a scene from a high-end private school. We are talking about the PM Shri Composite School in Mirzapur. More than 200 children come to the school to study every day. The learning environment seen at the school today was not the same before 2016. Back then, the building was in ruins, and there was not even enough space for children to sit in the classrooms. With no boundary wall, the premises would become a hangout for drunkards after sunset. Gradually, parents also became afraid to send their children to school. That was when Madhurima Tiwari became the school's principal. She sought help from officials to turn the school into a smart school. She went door to door, assuring parents that their children would get a good education and a better learning environment. She then delivered on those promises. The school is now giving convent schools in Mirzapur a run for their money. Madhurima received the President's Award in 2025. Only two teachers from Uttar Pradesh received the award, Madhurima and Ramlal Yadav from Bhadohi. On Teachers' Day, read the story of how this school changed, step by step Broken ground, no boundary wall, children sat on mats Principal Madhurima Tiwari recounts the school's transformation: It was 2009. I got a job as an assistant teacher. My first posting was at a primary school in the Madihan area of Mirzapur. Two years later, I was transferred to this school in the city. What was the condition of the school at the time? Madhurima says, School operated from two separate campuses. The primary school was on one side and the upper primary school on the other. There was no boundary wall. Inside the school, children sat on the ground on mats. The school premises were also in poor condition.Within two to three years, I realised that children were not coming to school to study. Parents were also not coming for new admissions. By then, fewer than 50 children were left in the school.When we visited the homes of children who were not attending school, we found that parents were unhappy with the lack of facilities. Many parents told us, ‘Why should we send our children to your school when it gets flooded during the rains and there is no proper seating arrangement? What will you people teach them?’ Met MPs and MLAs, secured grants from officials, then repaired the building Madhurima says, In 2016, we met MPs and MLAs and showed officials photographs of the dilapidated building. After the grant was sanctioned, we got the building repaired. First, we brought the primary and upper primary schools together on the same campus. A year later, I became the principal here.We then started visiting parents with photographs of the new building and classrooms. We requested them to send their children back to our school. The impact was visible in the very first year. The number of children increased from 56 to 132. This felt like a major achievement for us. We continued our efforts, installing projectors in every classroom and increasing greenery across the school. First recognition in 2018, then experiments with teaching methods In 2018, Mirzapur BSA Praveen Tiwari visited the school. He praised the classrooms and campus and also presented a certificate of appreciation. This was the first recognition for the school and its principal. Madhurima says, After this recognition, I felt that we needed to make the school even better. My fellow teachers began working on new ways of teaching children. We started trying to explain every topic in an interesting way and make greater use of screens to display and explain the syllabus. Children receive ID cards arranged at their own expense Children at the school can now be seen in clean uniforms, shoes, ties and ID cards. Madhurima explains, There are several private schools around our school. Government schools do not charge fees, and we do not want children to develop an inferiority complex about studying in a government school rather than a private one, so we ask them to follow a dress code. Several things are not provided by the government, so my staff and I arrange them and provide them to the children.I learnt computers from my son and daughter and now teach them here.The school has a computer lab, a modern library, smart classrooms and computer systems. How are children being taught about these facilities? Madhurima says, We studied for a BSc, followed by BEd and BTC. Indeed, we did not get the opportunity to study computers. But I have a son and a daughter at home, and I learnt many things through them. Apart from that, the department provides us with training from time to time, and we use that training to teach the children here. ‘Parents withdrawing children from private schools and bringing them here’ There are currently 221 children enrolled at Madhurima's school. We asked whether parents were now withdrawing their children from private schools and bringing them here. Madhurima says, A parent came and asked us to enrol his child. We registered the name, but later found out that he had admitted the child to UKG at a private school just two months earlier. We told him to get the child's name removed from that school before it could be registered here on U-DISE. When he went there, the school refused to remove the child's name. We sought the help of officials, after which the school charged the poor parent ₹1,600. When I found out about this, I felt very sad. Now, hear from the students We asked a student named Khushi, who was studying in the computer lab, whether people in the neighbourhood ever asked her why she studied at a government school. Khushi says, When people ask us that, we tell them that our school provides much better education than theirs. Our school is even better than private schools. We have everything here that they have in expensive private schools. During the conversation, we learnt that Khushi's father is a carpenter and his financial situation does not allow him to afford private schooling for his daughter. ‘The facilities here are no less than those in private schools’ Samya, a Class 8 student sitting in the computer lab, says, I have been studying here since Class 1. My father is a carpenter, and my mother stays at home. We do not have to pay any fees here. Our school is very good. We have digital classes and a digital library. Whenever we do not understand something, we ask our teachers, and they explain everything to us. Tamanna, a Class 8 student attending an online class, says, My father is a tailor. Our family's financial situation is not good enough for us to study at a private school, so I study here. The facilities here are no less than those at any private school. Everything is very good. We keep telling our teacher to develop the school further, otherwise we will have to go to Arya Kanya Vidya Mandir for Class 9. After speaking to the students and staff at the school, it becomes clear that the school has now developed into something resembling a model school. It has almost every facility required for teaching. The only major problem is a shortage of staff. Apart from Madhurima, there is one assistant teacher and one Shiksha Mitra. In other words, just three people are managing the school. More staff are needed so that the children can be taught and guided even better.

stories.title: JE beaten with kicks, punches after being thrown to ground:Went to check power theft; pleaded, “Let me go, I’m a heart patient”
stories.summary: In Farrukhabad, a junior engineer (JE) who had arrived to investigate electricity theft was chased and beaten. The homeowner and his son knocked the JE to the ground on the road and assaulted him with kicks and punches. He had reached Loco Road in Fatehgarh with his team at 2 p.m. on Monday to investigate electricity theft. The electricity department's sub-divisional officer (SDO), a lineman, and a Bijli Mitra were also accompanying the JE. As soon as the JE raised an objection regarding the electricity theft, the homeowner and his son began beating him. To protect himself, the JE repeatedly pleaded, "Don't hit me... I am a heart patient." Slapped suddenly while the JE was making inquiries The junior engineer (JE) was talking to the landlord and his son. Suddenly, the landlord slapped the JE's cheek 3-4 times in quick succession. After this, his son also began punching the JE. The JE kept running to protect himself. The landlord and his son chased him down and continued beating him. They knocked the JE to the road and beat him with kicks and punches. Meanwhile, the CDO and lineman accompanying the JE were seen trying to intervene. While beating the JE, the landlord was saying, "My nose is bleeding. How could he punch me...?" JE says-Those who beat him also snatched government documents According to JE Mukhtar Hussain, he had reached Loko Road at around 2 p.m. on Monday along with SDO Ajay Kumar and a lineman to investigate electricity theft. When the team inspected a premises, electricity theft was detected there. They were collecting evidence related to the electricity theft and proceeding with action. During this time, the house owner and his son began abusing them and got into a scuffle with the team. They knocked the JE to the ground and beat him. It is alleged that government documents were also snatched during the incident. "I told them I am a heart patient, but they continued beating me" According to the JE, he sustained serious injuries in the assault and is suspected to have suffered a fracture. He said that he is a heart patient. We have demanded action against the accused at Fatehgarh Kotwali. The police also sent us to Lohia Hospital for a medical examination. Fatehgarh Station House Officer Vijay Singh said- The electricity department employees have been sent for a medical examination. No written complaint has been received in the case so far. Further action will be taken as soon as the complaint is received.

stories.title: Anganwadi workers’ salaries to rise by ₹4,000:Helpers to get ₹2,000 hike; Yogi to announce it in Ayodhya today
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government is set to give a major boost to the honorarium of anganwadi workers and helpers ahead of the Assembly elections. The monthly honorarium of around 3.28 lakh workers will be increased by ₹4,000, while helpers will get a ₹2,000 hike. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will announce the increase in Ayodhya on Tuesday. He will also hand over appointment letters to newly recruited anganwadi workers and helpers at the event. The Ayodhya administration has completed preparations for the programme. The government is expected to present the honorarium hike as a major benefit for workers paid an honorarium rather than a regular salary. Women and Child Development Minister Baby Rani Maurya said 71,310 anganwadi workers and helpers have been recruited. Of these, 21,804 are workers and 49,506 are helpers. Direct relief for more than 3.25 lakh families Political analysts believe the government is focusing on women workers with a strong presence at the grassroots level ahead of the elections. 1. Strategy to strengthen women’s support The government had earlier increased the honorarium and benefits for cooks working in Basic Education Council schools, most of whom are women. The latest move focuses on anganwadi workers and helpers. 2. Impact on more than 3.25 lakh families The increase in honorarium for 1.89 lakh anganwadi workers and 1.39 lakh helpers is expected to directly improve the household budgets of more than 3.25 lakh families across the state. 3. Strong grassroots network Anganwadi workers have direct access to households in both rural and urban areas. Their network is considered important for implementing government schemes on the ground and building support during an election campaign. 15,000 women expected at GIC ground; programmes planned across UP Around 12,000–15,000 anganwadi workers and helpers from the Ayodhya division are expected to attend the main event at the GIC ground in Ayodhya. Women from self-help groups (SHGs) involved in ration distribution will also participate in the programme. The main event will be held in Ayodhya in the presence of the Chief Minister, while similar programmes will be organised simultaneously in all other districts of the state. Preparations for the main event have been completed under the supervision of Ayodhya Chief Development Officer Krishna Kumar Singh. Yogi’s minute-by-minute schedule Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will spend around three hours in Ayodhya on Tuesday.
