stories.title: Prayagraj court includes Bhaskar Investigation in probe:Ashutosh Maharaj allegedly conspired against Shankaracharya; FIR scope to widen
stories.summary: Prayagraj's Special POCSO Court has ordered that a sting operation by Dainik Bhaskar be made part of the police investigation as digital and electronic evidence. The case is related to allegations of sexual abuse of two young disciples by Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Swami. Dainik Bhaskar found in its investigation that this was a conspiracy by Ashutosh Maharaj. P.N. Mishra, the lawyer for Shankaracharya's disciple Swami Mukundanand, presented the sting operation before the court. Following this, the court directed that all electronic evidence and the sting operation be included in the investigation. Read the impact of the news... Bhaskar's sting operation gives a new twist to the investigation P.N. Mishra, the lawyer for Shankaracharya's disciple Swami Mukundanand, presented Dainik Bhaskar's four-month investigation report and evidence related to the sting operation on a pen drive before the court. P.N. Mishra said, "We had filed an urgent application in court. Along with it, the investigation report by Dainik Bhaskar and digital evidence related to the sting operation were submitted to the court on a pen drive. Taking our arguments and evidence seriously, the court has directed that they be included in the investigation of FIR No. 58/2026." So far, action had been taken against only two people in this case. However, following the emergence of this evidence, the role of other people involved in the conspiracy will also be investigated impartially. How the conspiracy was exposed Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was accused of sexually assaulting two minors in Prayagraj between the Maha Kumbh in January 2025 and the Magh Mela in February 2026. On the order of a special judge, an FIR was registered against the Shankaracharya and his disciple at Jhunsi police station under various sections. In this case, the Shankaracharya had filed an application for anticipatory bail in court. The court accepted his application and granted him anticipatory bail. To uncover the truth, the Dainik Bhaskar team conducted an investigation for four months. The team reached the young boy and his family in whose name the FIR had been registered. The statements made by the boy and his family members in front of a hidden camera gave the case a new twist. In a sting operation, Batuk and his family claimed that they did not even know Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand, nor had they ever gone to his ashram to study or stay. The investigation revealed that Ashutosh Maharaj was behind the entire matter. He had allegedly used an ordinary rural family as a pawn in the case. Why did Ashutosh Maharaj choose two ordinary village Batuks? According to Dainik Bhaskar's investigation, Ashutosh Maharaj had contacted these Batuks about a year ago during a yajna held in two different cities in Uttar Pradesh. Both Batuks received ₹60,000 each as dakshina at the yajna. According to the report, these same Batuks were later allegedly made part of the conspiracy. Three reasons were cited for this- 1. Financial compulsion- Both Batuks came from extremely ordinary and impoverished rural families. Their families had no permanent source of income. 2. Exploiting religious faith- Batuk and their families believed in religious practices. Taking advantage of this faith, they were influenced in the name of religion and divine service. 3. Prior acquaintance- Ashutosh Maharaj was already acquainted with both Batuks. For this reason, he believed that he could persuade the families to accept his demands through money or pressure. What will happen next? Following this order by the Special POCSO Court in Prayagraj, the Jhunsi police will now have to expand the scope of their investigation. In addition to examining the role of Ashutosh Maharaj and his associates, the police will also have to investigate allegations such as kidnapping, preparing fake documents, and criminal conspiracy. Following the court's directions, the police will decide on further action based on new facts and digital evidence that emerge during the investigation. If sufficient evidence is found of any individual's role and involvement in the crime, legal action may be taken against them.

Man breaks legs after jumping from 30-ft height for reel:Friends film stunt at Pahuj Dam in Jhansi
stories.summary: In Jhansi, a young man jumped into a river from a height of 30 feet to make a reel. Since the water level was low, he hit a rock below and fractured both his legs. When he began to drown, he was rescued with the help of local divers. The incident took place on Sunday evening at Pahuj Dam, about 10 kilometers from the district headquarters. The young man is undergoing treatment at a private hospital. A video of the incident has also surfaced. It was filmed by the young man's friends. In the 31-second video, the young man can be seen climbing over the railing and getting into position to jump. His friends then laugh and say, "May God rest your soul." Immediately afterward, the young man performs the stunt and jumps into the dam. See the pictures... Here's the complete incident... Pushpendra Kumar (32), son of Rajkumar and a resident of Parwai village in the Raksa police station area, had arrived at Pahuj Dam on Sunday with his friends. According to eyewitnesses, the youths were making reels there. Pushpendra reached the viewpoint built on the left side of the dam, while his friends were recording a video from the other side. There was a railing at the viewpoint. Pushpendra climbed over the railing in his clothes and shoes and began positioning himself to jump. Before anyone realized it, he leaped into the dam from a height of about 30 feet. His friends recorded the incident. Fell on a rock in shallow water, fractured both legs Where Pushpendra fell in the dam, the water was very shallow and there was a rock below. He landed on the rock, breaking both his legs. Because of the injuries to his legs, he was unable to swim and began to drown. At one point, he also held his legs with his hands. He then tried to swim using his hands. Nearby divers somehow pulled him out. After receiving information about the incident, Grassland outpost in-charge Ranvijay Singh also reached the spot with a police team. The injured Pushpendra was taken to the hospital. His family members also arrived at the hospital after being informed. Three and a half feet of water where he fell Pushpendra's cousin Rajiv said, “My brother Pushpendra had gone to the dam with his friends. He then jumped into the dam. There was around three and a half feet of water where he fell. As a result, both his legs were fractured. The doctors have operated on both his legs. He is currently in stable condition.”

The accused was wanted in a case involving a minor in Mirzapur. In this matter, a sub-inspector from the Mirzapur police filed a case at the Agra GRP Fort police station regarding the accused's escape and the negligence of the three police personnel deployed with him. In his complaint, Sub-Inspector Jaiprakash, posted at Padri police station in Mirzapur, stated that Sub-Inspector Vijay Shankar Yadav, female head constable Geeta, and constable Neeraj Kumar had gone to Umra police station in Surat on September 2 to search for the minor victim and the accused, Suraj Kumar Pandey alias Harsh Pandey, in connection with the investigation of a case registered at Padri police station. With the assistance of Surat Police, both the victim and the accused were recovered. The police team was bringing them to Mirzapur from Udhna station aboard the Madhubani Express on September 4. According to the complaint, at around 12:30 a.m., between Shringarpor and Kirawali railway stations in Agra, the accused, Suraj, jumped from the moving train and escaped. Sub-Inspector Vijay Shankar Yadav conducted an extensive search, but he could not be found. After this, Constable Neeraj Kumar and Woman Constable Geeta reached Padri with the victim on September 5. The complaint states that the accused escaped due to the negligence of all three police personnel. GRP Fort police station has registered a case regarding the accused's escape and the negligence of the police personnel and has begun searching for him.

stories.title: 13-year-old dies of suspected heart attack in Meerut:Body found in school bathroom; Parents say he had no heart condition
stories.summary: 13-year-old boy died of a heart attack in Meerut. His body was found in the school bathroom at around 2:15 p.m. on Monday. He had gone to the toilet after school ended but did not come out. Meanwhile, an e-rickshaw driver was waiting for the boy outside the school. When all the students had arrived and the boy did not, the driver went inside the school to look for him. A search was launched with the school staff. When the boy was not found in the classroom, everyone went toward the bathrooms. The student was found lying there. The school staff informed the boy's family. His parents took him to a nearby private doctor, where he was declared dead. The student was in seventh grade. His parents said that he had no previous heart condition. The incident took place at Basant Valley Public School in the Mawana police station area. He was the second-born son among three siblings 13-year-old Kunal was the son of Dharmendra Sharma, a resident of Mohalla Kabili Gate on Kalawada Road in the Mawana area. He was the second-born among three siblings. His elder sister is Sakshi, while his younger brother is Sanchit Sharma. Kunal traveled to and from school every day by e-rickshaw. On Monday afternoon, after school ended, the e-rickshaw driver was waiting for the children outside the school. The other children came out and boarded the rickshaw, but Kunal did not come. After waiting for about 15 minutes, the driver went inside the school himself. He first looked for Kunal in the classroom, but he was not there. One child said that Kunal had gone to the washroom. The driver then went toward the washroom. Door was locked from the inside; when they looked from the roof, the child was found lying on the floor Family took him to Meerut after consulting two doctors As soon as he received the information, Kunal's father, Dharmendra, reached the school. He took the child to two different private doctors in Mawana itself. Both declared him dead. After this, family members took Kunal to Sushila Jaswant Rai Hospital in Meerut. There too, doctors examined him and pronounced him dead. According to the family, the doctors attributed the death to a sudden heart attack. Kunal's mother, Anita, and father, Dharmendra, said that their son had never experienced any heart-related problems before. They cannot understand what suddenly happened. When the police arrived, the family refused to take any action After receiving information about Kunal's death, the police also reached the house. However, the family refused to have a post-mortem conducted or take any kind of police action. The family then returned home with the child's body. Kunal’s father, Dharmendra Sharma, said, “My son had gone to school. He collapsed while using the toilet and suffered cardiac arrest. The school called us and said that our child had fallen. We rushed him to a doctor, but he was declared dead.” School manager says, ‘The child was very active since morning’ Amit Rana, manager of Basant Valley School, said, “Kunal Sharma, a Class 7 student at our school, went to the washroom just before the school was about to close for the day. After some time, when we called out to him, we found that he had latched the door from inside. He did not open it, so we had the door opened from inside.” The child was immediately taken to Dr MD Sharma and Dr Anil Khanna, who reportedly said he had suffered cardiac arrest. The school also informed his parents. “Kunal had been very active since morning and showed no signs of any problem. He had eaten his lunch properly. We do not know what suddenly happened,” Rana said. Understand the symptoms of a heart attack and how to take care of your heart… Heart specialist Dr. Ajit Bana said that cardiac arrest in children is quite rare. In some cases, there is a hole in the heart, which may not be detected during initial examinations. If such children go running or do any exercise, their heart may start pumping much faster than normal, which can lead to cardiac arrest. In addition, a child may already have an underlying illness that gradually begins to affect the heart. In such cases, children should undergo regular checkups.

stories.title: 1-year-old kept searching for his mother all night:Head constable who killed wife in Lucknow suspended; Faced a case earlier
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a head constable murdered his wife. The couple has a one-year-old son. After his mother's death, the one-year-old innocent boy, Tanmay, kept looking for her throughout the night. He repeatedly cried for his mother. His family had no answer other than trying to comfort him. What could the innocent child know-that his mother would never return and his father would be behind bars? On Sunday, following an argument, Head Constable Himanshu Srivastava struck his wife Rashmi on the head with a spice-grinding pestle. Rashmi died from her severe injuries. After the incident, her brother demanded strict punishment for the accused and termination of his job. Late at night, the police also suspended Himanshu. Further action is being taken against him. Rashmi was troubled by her husband's alcohol addiction Rashmi's brother Saurabh, who reached Lucknow, said that his sister was troubled by her husband Himanshu's alcohol addiction. He would often drink alcohol and assault and quarrel with her. He had not allowed his sister to live peacefully ever since their marriage. According to Saurabh, the dispute between the two had escalated to such an extent that it reached the point of divorce. Later, the family mediated a settlement. Despite this, Himanshu's behavior did not change, and he started assaulting her again. Rashmi had also filed a domestic violence case against Himanshu in Jaunpur. However, they later reached a settlement in that case as well. Saurabh said that his sister had a son about a year ago. The family hoped that everything would get better after the child's arrival, but the situation deteriorated further. See 3 pictures from the scene... Fearing that something might happen to his sister, Saurabh Srivastava came to Lucknow from home with a few people. Accused kept wandering around with the child in his arms According to the family, after the murder, the head constable sat beside his wife's body for some time. After that, he wandered outside carrying his one-year-old child in his arms. At around 3 p.m., Rashmi's brothers reached the house. They were stunned to see their sister's body. When they asked Himanshu the cause of her death, he began making excuses. The matter was then reported to the police. Himanshu had become a constable in 2011 The accused head constable, Himanshu Srivastava, is a resident of Niralanagar in Ayodhya. He married Rashmi Srivastava, a resident of Malepura in Ambedkar Nagar, in 2015. In Lucknow, Himanshu had been living as a tenant in the house of Dr. M.M. Srivastava in the Paper Mill area for the past two and a half years. He was the family's only tenant. Himanshu joined the police force as a constable in 2011. He was promoted to head constable last year. He was posted at the Right to Information Cell office in Dali Ganj. DCP Central Vikrant Veer said, We received information about a murder inside the house. When the police reached the spot, Rashmi's body was lying on the floor. Blood had pooled around her head. The police have detained the accused, Himanshu. He is being questioned. The motive for the murder has not yet been established.

stories.summary: The weather in Lucknow has changed since morning. Torrential rain occurred amidst dark clouds. Lightning struck, and due to the heavy downpour, darkness descended upon several areas. Motorists had to drive with their headlights on even during the day. Rain occurred in several areas including Hazratganj, Gomti Nagar, Vibhuti Khand, Indira Nagar, and Cantt. Now that the rain has stopped, there is waterlogging in many parts of the city. A neem tree fell on a Swift Dzire passing through Atal Tiraha in Cantt. There were 2 people inside the vehicle. Water has accumulated on the roads in Gomti Nagar. Students had to cross this drain water to reach school. The Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for rain today and has predicted moderate to heavy rainfall. During the monsoon, from June 1 to September 6, a total of 609.5 millimeters of rainfall was recorded, while the average normal rainfall is 556.6 millimeters. This has been 10 percent above normal. 5.8 millimeters of rainfall was recorded during the day on Sunday. The maximum temperature was 32.5 degrees, which was 0.6 degrees below normal. The minimum temperature was 25.5 degrees, which was 0.6 degrees above normal. The maximum humidity was 92 percent and the minimum humidity was 73 percent. See 8 photos of the weather...

stories.title: Waiter’s delay in serving salad enrages youths:Assault him and break his shoulder; FIR filed against 4 in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a waiter's shoulder was fractured over a delay in serving salad. It is alleged that at around 7 p.m. last Friday evening, four young men arrived at a canteen located in Transport Nagar. They ordered food. The waiter was serving all the dishes one by one. When they did not receive the salad, the youths became enraged and began hurling abuses at him. When he objected, the dispute escalated and turned into a physical altercation. The victim alleged that the youths brutally assaulted him with chairs and kicks and punches. They fled after threatening to kill him when others intervened. An FIR has been registered against four accused at Cantt police station. The police are investigating the matter. Waiter delayed salad order, lawyer allegedly abused him Thirty-year-old Sonu Chauhan, a resident of Baijnathpur village under Kothibhar police station in Maharajganj district, submitted a complaint at Cantt police station on Sunday. He stated that he works as a waiter at a canteen located in Transport Nagar under the jurisdiction of Cantt police station in Gorakhpur. He supports his family through this work. He said that at around 7 p.m. on Friday, four people arrived together at their canteen. They ordered food items. It is alleged that the waiter, Sonu, was delivering all the orders one by one. Meanwhile, one of them, a young man named Nishad, who is a lawyer, asked him to bring salad. The waiter had just gone to get the salad when the young man angrily called out to him again. When the waiter hurriedly reached the table, the young man became furious at the delay and began abusing him. When the waiter objected, the others accompanying the young man also became enraged. Beaten severely with a chair According to the waiter, they all slapped him repeatedly and knocked him to the ground. They then picked up a canteen chair and brutally assaulted him with it. They also kicked and punched him. Seeing the dispute escalate, the people present there and the owner intervened and rescued him. After considerable effort, the waiter was somehow freed. The four young men then fled, threatening to kill him. The waiter's left shoulder was fractured in the attack, and he is undergoing treatment. Based on the complaint filed by the victim waiter, an FIR was registered against the accused at Cantt police station on September 6. The police are proceeding with further investigation and action.

stories.title: Akhilesh asks why mosque was demolished in Saharanpur:UP government does not know what a green corridor means; says AI video will get a response
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference at the party's state office in Lucknow on Monday afternoon. During the event, he launched a scathing attack on the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh. Akhilesh said that a mosque in Saharanpur was demolished within 12 hours-what was the need for such haste? The government is wasting public money like water on "political makeup" to divert people's attention from basic issues. Akhilesh said that whatever spreads goodness in society is the real AI. It should be used only for good purposes, not to defame opposition leaders. If fake videos are made using AI, remember that videos can also be created from this side. He criticized the government over infrastructure, healthcare, education, and communalism. 5 major points from Akhilesh Yadav's press conference: 1. Government does not even know the meaning of a green corridor Questioning the government's technical understanding, Akhilesh said, "The real meaning of a green corridor is that the body organs of critically ill patients can be transported from one hospital to another in the shortest possible time. But this government assumes that simply planting trees along the roadside constitutes a green corridor. Our entire planning and design are heading in the wrong direction." 2. Ram Gaman Path sinks at 118 places, police searching for journalist The Ram Gaman Path has sunk at 118 places. The government has resorted to authoritarian measures to hide its failure. Police are searching for journalists who reported on the alleged corruption. Akhilesh said that while the government claims it will turn cities into “Spain and Kyoto”, the Chief Minister himself turns into an engineer. On the ground, a ₹1 lakh crore project is reduced to a shambles. Asked about Deputy CM Keshav Maurya, Akhilesh said, “He would know better, because his department has been taken away.” 3. ‘If an AI video is made from there, there will be a response from here too’ On the growing use of AI in elections and politics, Akhilesh said bluntly, “The real AI is whatever spreads goodness in society. It should be used only for good purposes. Those who create fake AI videos to defame opposition leaders should remember that videos can also be made from this side.” 4. ‘What was the hurry to demolish the mosque within 12 hours?’ The SP chief questioned the government’s intentions, saying some people want to make society completely communal. “They were communal in their speeches, and now they have become communal in their actions as well. When the country has High Courts and the Supreme Court, where justice could have been sought, what was the need to demolish the mosque within 12 hours? We will put an end to this communal path once and for all,” he said. 5. ‘The poor are not getting treatment, but police are reaching politicians’ homes’ The poor in the state are unable to get proper medical treatment, and people are losing their lives due to incorrect treatment. Schools are being shut down. The entire government machinery is spending ₹10,000 crore merely on branding. Instead of catching criminals, police are conducting raids at the homes of our party leaders. He also alleged that people from the ruling side were involved in the illegal trade of narcotic drugs, including codeine, uncovered in Varanasi.

stories.title: Daughter-in-law gets millionaire father-in-law killed in Kanpur:Hides servant in bedroom, guides him by phone; cries to avoid suspicion
stories.summary: 36-year-old daughter-in-law allegedly had her 63-year-old millionaire father-in-law, medicine trader Vineet Minocha, murdered in Kanpur. The alleged motive was the restrictions he imposed on her. Vineet kept an eye on his daughter-in-law through CCTV cameras and gave her only as much money as he considered necessary. Upset over the restrictions on her lifestyle, Shalu allegedly paid domestic help Vishal (30) ₹6 lakh to kill him. Vishal allegedly stabbed Vineet 26 times. Following the accused domestic help’s confession, police detained Shalu. She initially tried to mislead investigators but allegedly confessed after sustained questioning. During interrogation, Shalu reportedly broke down and said, “Despite being the daughter-in-law of a millionaire family, my father-in-law had complete control over my and my husband’s expenses. I had to ask him even for small expenses and plead with him for every penny. That is why I got him murdered through the domestic help.” Police also obtained Shalu’s call detail records. She and Vishal spoke 14 times on the night of the murder. Preliminary investigation has found no role of her husband, Subrat, in the murder. However, police have kept him at the police station for questioning. The murder took place at around 11:28 pm on Saturday inside Vineet Minocha’s flat in Kanpur. He was alone at the time, while his son and daughter-in-law had gone to a party. When they returned around 3 am on Sunday, they found Vineet’s blood-soaked body in his bedroom. Shalu allegedly pretended to cry and faint after discovering the body. The incident took place at Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur, an upscale area of Kanpur. CCTV captures domestic help and accomplice; both arrested in encounter Kanpur police checked CCTV footage and found domestic help Vishal and his accomplice Raj Kishore (30) entering the apartment and later leaving the flat. Police arrested both in an encounter late on Sunday night. When media personnel asked Vishal why he had killed the businessman, he said, “I killed him at the behest of daughter-in-law Shalu. She had asked me to kill him for money.” Vishal’s statement gave the murder case a new twist. Police picked up Shalu overnight and brought her to the police station. During questioning, she confessed to the crime. Guard says, ‘Shalu madam told me to let them in’ Madan, the security in-charge at Ratan Orbit Apartment in the Kalyanpur area, where the businessman’s flat was located, said Shalu and Subrat had gone out at night on the day of the murder. A few minutes after they left, Vishal Gautam arrived with his accomplice Raj Kishore. He asked for permission to go to Flat No. C-104. When I refused, they spoke to Shalu madam over the phone. She told me to let them in, saying, “They have come with medicines.” Shortly afterwards, Vineet’s son Subrat and daughter-in-law Shalu left with their son. Vineet Manocha was alone in the flat at the time. When the son and daughter-in-law returned around 3 am on Sunday, they found his body inside. They called the police, who arrived to find the businessman’s blood-soaked body lying on the floor. Blood was splattered throughout the room. The murder is believed to have taken place after 10:30 pm on Saturday. Father-in-law reprimanded her on July 28, daughter-in-law planned his murder the same day The accused daughter-in-law told police that she had attended a party on July 28 and returned home late. Her father-in-law objected to her going to and returning from late-night parties. An argument broke out between them over the issue, after which she allegedly began planning his murder. During questioning, Shalu told police that she had also called Vishal to her house on Janmashtami (September 4), under the pretext of giving him some items. The plan to kill the medicine trader was finalised that day. Shalu told Vishal that she would go to a party in Yashoda Nagar with her husband and child on Saturday, and that he should carry out the murder discreetly while they were away. Shalu had arranged a duplicate key to the house and handed it to Vishal around 15 days earlier. Vishal told police that they had initially planned to suffocate the businessman with a pillow while he was asleep, so that his death would appear to be a heart attack. However, on the night of the murder, he and his accomplice Raj Kishore hid in the businessman’s son’s bedroom. When the medicine trader entered the room, Vishal and Raj Kishore attacked him and stabbed him to death. They then fled the flat. Shalu allegedly struck a deal with Vishal for ₹6 lakh to carry out the murder. She was supposed to pay ₹2 lakh on Sunday, September 6, and the remaining ₹4 lakh 15 days later. Vishal told police that he involved Raj Kishore in the plan on the promise of paying him ₹3 lakh. Shalu had also promised to employ Vishal after the medicine trader’s death. DCP says, ‘Plan was to make the murder look like a heart attack’ Kanpur West DCP SM Qasim Abidi said Shalu had planned to make the murder appear like a heart attack. She allegedly told domestic help Vishal Gautam to suffocate her father-in-law with a pillow after he fell asleep, so that his death would appear to have been caused by a heart attack. Vishal had been visiting the businessman’s house for around 12 years. Shalu allegedly provided the accused with a duplicate key to the flat. At 9:38 pm, she messaged Vishal that the house was empty and told him to come over. The two accused then entered the flat and hid in the bedroom. Around an hour and 15 minutes later, the businessman arrived at the flat. Later that night, businessman Vineet felt hungry. He got up, ate sweets kept in the refrigerator, drank water and began checking and locking all the rooms in the flat. While locking the rooms, Vineet reached his son Subrat’s bedroom. When he switched on the light and looked inside, he found Vishal and Raj Kishore hiding there. Shocked, Vineet angrily asked Vishal what he was doing there. As soon as he asked the question, Vishal and his accomplice Raj Kishore attacked the medicine trader. When Vineet tried to flee, Vishal took out a knife that he had brought from outside in a plastic bag and slit his throat, killing him. The businessman had installed CCTV cameras in the house, which allegedly restricted Shalu’s freedom. Police said she was upset about this and allegedly got her father-in-law murdered. Shalu and Vishal spoke 14 times on the day of the murder When police began examining the CDRs (call detail records) of Shalu and Vishal, several startling details emerged. The records showed that the two had spoken on the phone around 35–40 times between July 1 and the day of the incident. The CDRs revealed that most of their conversations were brief, lasting only one-and-a-half to two minutes. On the day of the murder, Saturday, they spoke 14 times. Shalu first called Vishal at 9 am, and their conversations continued until late at night. Vishal was fired in 2022 over theft allegations Police officials said Vishal had been working at the medicine trader’s shop on Birhana Road since 2010. In 2022, businessman Vineet caught him stealing from the shop. After reprimanding him, Vineet dismissed him from the job. After that, Vishal continued visiting the businessman’s house to do odd jobs at the request of his son, Subrat. 3 clues that exposed the daughter-in-law in the businessman’s murder The accused domestic helps, Vishal and Raj Kishore, stabbed businessman Vineet to death. According to the post-mortem report, they stabbed him 26 times. The brutality of the murder led police to suspect that it stemmed from a personal grudge. The killers did not touch any valuables or other belongings in the house. They only killed the businessman and fled. This led police to suspect that they had been hired specifically to carry out the murder, suggesting the involvement of someone close to the victim. The apartment security guard’s statement also made it clear that Shalu had allowed both men to enter the building. She then left with her husband. This further strengthened police suspicion against her. Wholesale medicine distributor, ran the business with his son Businessman Vineet lived with his family in Flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment. The four-bedroom flat with a dining room is reportedly worth more than ₹1 crore. Vineet ran a medicine firm called ‘Pharma Traders’ on Birhana Road. Vineet managed the business with his son Subrat. The firm had an annual turnover of ₹50–60 crore. His family included his wife Punita, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Shalu and Subrat had been married for seven years. Subrat’s in-laws live in Lucknow. His wife Punita is a marriage counsellor and had travelled to Ghaziabad a week earlier. Their daughter Subhani and son-in-law live in Gurugram. Both are engineers. Businessman feared something might happen to him Police believe medicine trader Vineet feared that something might happen to him following his dispute with daughter-in-law Shalu. Minocha had CCTV cameras installed in his 3-BHK flat on July 1. One camera was installed facing the main gate and covered the entire dining hall, while the second was installed on the balcony leading to the other rooms and captured their entry and exit points. 16 employees and family members were troubled by him Police questioning revealed that Vineet Minocha’s firm had 16 employees. As he grew older, Minocha had reportedly become increasingly irritable. He allegedly spoke abusively to everyone and viewed people with suspicion. As a result, everyone at his firm was troubled by his behaviour, and no one wanted to confront him. Shalu’s father is a textile businessman in Lucknow Shalu Minocha’s father, Naresh Arora, is a textile businessman who lives in Thakurganj, Lucknow. Naresh got his daughter married in Lucknow. Shalu has a son, Shrijay. DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said, Vineet Minocha was among Kanpur’s top five medicine traders. He ran a medicine firm called ‘Pharma Traders’ on Birhana Road, with an annual turnover of ₹40–50 crore. The accused have been arrested. The involvement of the daughter-in-law is being investigated. 45 security guards deployed, yet no one noticed the murder The security arrangements at Ratan Orbit Apartments have also come under scrutiny following the murder. The complex has 1,056 flats and 27 bungalows. Assuming an average of five members per family, around 5,500 people live there. Around 45 security guards, including a security in-charge, are deployed at the complex. As many as 650 CCTV cameras are installed across the campus, from the entry gate to various other locations. Residents have also installed cameras inside their flats. Four guards are usually deployed at the main gate every day, but one guard was on leave on Saturday. As a result, three guards were stationed at the main gate, while the others were deployed across different blocks. Police found an entry in the main gate register at 8:28 pm, followed by the next entry at 10 pm, which was that of a milkman. No other person’s entry was recorded during this period. Police are now examining the register, CCTV footage and all aspects of the security arrangements.

stories.title: Gen Alpha stages protest for road:250 govt schoolchildren protest in rain in Mirzapur; say they use 1.5ft-wide ridge to commute
stories.summary: At a government school in Mirzapur, Gen Alpha children (up to 13 years old) began protesting at 10 a.m. on Monday, demanding that a road be built. The children wanted a paved road to be constructed so they could reach the school. They have to make their way to school with great difficulty along the ridges between fields. Impressed by the children's determination as they protested outside the school, getting drenched in the rain, their parents and teachers also joined them. Villagers arranged a tarpaulin and stretched it out to create shade for the children, who sat beneath it in protest. The sit-in, which lasted about two hours, ended after the Naib Tehsildar and the Block Development Officer assured them that road construction would begin. The incident took place at Cheruiram Composite School in the City Block, about 8 kilometres from the district headquarters. Around 470 children study there. After leaving the main road, they have to cover approximately one kilometre along the ridges between the fields to reach the school. The ridges are about one and a half feet wide, so two children cannot walk on them side by side. According to the parents, children face even more difficulties on rainy days. Water and mud accumulate on the way, creating a risk of slipping and falling. Many times, children fall and reach school covered in mud. This has been the only route to and from the school since it was built. See the pictures... Children sat in protest after closing the gate once school opened The government school in Cheruiram village began at 8 a.m. on Monday as usual. Around 250 students from Classes 1 to 8 had arrived. At around 10 a.m., all the students came outside the school, closed the gate, and began a sit-in protest outside. The children began raising slogans such as "Fulfil our demands" and "Give us a passage, give us a passage." As news of the children's protest spread, a large number of villagers arrived. The teachers also came out of the school. Meanwhile, it began to rain. However, the children continued their protest. Seeing the children's determination, the villagers brought a tarpaulin and stretched it out with the help of bamboo poles. The children were asked to sit underneath it and continue their protest. Parents, villagers, and teachers also joined them in the sit-in. After receiving the information, Samajwadi Party leader Rohit Shukla "Lallu" also arrived to join the children in the sit-in. Children insist on calling officials to the spot The children and parents are demanding that officials be called to the spot. They said that they have complained several times to officials and public representatives about the road problem, but no permanent solution has been found so far. Parents say the problem is not limited to the children. School teachers and other staff also travel along this poor road. The condition of the road worsens further when it rains continuously. Children say, ‘We have slipped and fallen several times, so we had to return home’ Class 8 student Rohit Chauhan said, “We come to school from about 1 km away. The road is in very poor condition. We have to walk through muddy paths and have slipped and fallen several times.” Aakash, also a Class 8 student, said, “We often have to make our way to school while falling on the unpaved road. Sometimes, we have no option but to return home midway.” Srishti Vishwakarma, a Class 6 student, said, “I have fallen several times during the rains. It is very difficult to travel to and from school. My schoolbag gets wet and my books are damaged.” Headmaster says, ‘We have been facing this problem since 1983’ School in-charge Headmaster Om Prakash Vishwakarma said the village has five hamlets, and children come to the school from all directions. Around 450 students are registered at the school. It was established in 1983, and the road problem has existed ever since. “We have been facing this difficulty for around 33 years,” he said. Meanwhile, SP leader Rohit Shukla Lallu said, “We also staged a protest last year demanding the construction of the road. We were given assurances at the time as well. This time, officials have sought 24 hours to begin the work. If work does not start, we will launch a protest. This time, the road will be built.” Protest ends after 2 hours; Naib Tehsildar assures road construction Following information about the children’s protest, Naib Tehsildar of Sadar Tehsil Surendra Pratap Singh and BDO Ravindra Shukla reached the spot. The officials assured the protesters that road construction would be started. Following the assurance, the children ended their two-hour-long protest. Protest ends after 2 hours, Naib Tehsildar assures that the road will be constructed After receiving information about the children's protest, Naib Tehsildar of Sadar Tehsil Surendra Pratap Singh and BDO Ravindra Shukla reached the spot. The officials assured them that road construction would be started. Following this, the children's two-hour-long protest came to an end.

stories.title: Lucknow has cleanest air in India:Beats Indore to rank No. 1 among cities with over 1 million population
stories.summary: Lucknow has secured the first position in the country in the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026 (Clean Air Survey 2026). Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), Lucknow was named the best-performing city in the survey. The Municipal Corporation received a prize of ₹1.5 crore for the achievement. Ward No. 70, Papermill Colony, in Zone 4, was also named the best ward in the country. It secured the first position among wards with a population of more than 30,000. The ward received a prize of ₹50 lakh. At an event held at the Indira Paryavaran Bhawan in New Delhi, Mayor Sushma Kharkwal, Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar, Additional Municipal Commissioner Pankaj Srivastava and Environmental Engineer Sanjeev Pradhan received the awards. Lucknow leaves Indore behind Indore ranked second in the category of cities with a population of more than 1 million. Lucknow overtook Indore to secure the top spot, while Jabalpur ranked third. Lucknow is the only city from Uttar Pradesh to receive the award this year. Notably, Lucknow was ranked 15th in the previous survey in 2024-25. This year, the city jumped straight to the top spot. Mayor says, ‘This is an achievement for all of Lucknow’ Mayor Sushma Kharkwal said securing the top position at the national level was a matter of pride for the entire city. She credited the achievement to the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the guidance of the Urban Development Minister, the Municipal Corporation team and the cooperation of city residents. She said the achievement belonged not just to the Municipal Corporation but to the people of Lucknow as a whole. The civic body will continue working to make the city cleaner, greener and more beautiful.

stories.title: Car hits transformer, 3 friends burnt alive:Fire breaks out after blast in Lakhimpur, Body found stuck to the driver’s seat; 3 critically injured
stories.summary: Car caught fire after crashing into a transformer in Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri. Three friends travelling in the car were burnt alive in the accident, while three others suffered burn injuries. The collision was so severe that it sounded like an explosion. The electricity wires broke and fell onto the car, causing sparks. Within moments, the car caught fire, trapping all the occupants inside. Hearing their screams, nearby residents rushed to the spot. Police and fire brigade teams arrived shortly afterwards and brought the fire under control. By then, half of the car had been badly burnt. The driver was completely charred and stuck to his seat. The other five occupants suffered severe burns. They somehow managed to get out, but lay writhing in pain on the road due to their injuries. All the victims were taken to hospital, where doctors declared two more people dead. Police said the accident may have occurred after the driver dozed off. However, the exact cause will be known only after the investigation. The accident took place around 2:30 am in Oyal town, under Kheri police station limits, about 8 km from the district headquarters. See 3 pictures... 6 friends were travelling to Sitapur in a Verna when the accident occurred According to police, Ayush Kumar, a resident of Shiv Colony under Kotwali Sadar police station, was travelling to Sitapur in a Verna car (UP14BV4127) with five friends. Near Oyal town, the car went out of control, crossed the pavement and entered a field, where it crashed into a transformer. Ayush was burnt to death on the spot. Outpost in-charge Dimple Singh, who reached the scene, got the power supply switched off and had the car windows broken to rescue those trapped inside. Police personnel took the injured to the district hospital in a private vehicle. There, doctors declared Ayush (21), Akash (19) and Shiva (16) dead. Utkarsh, Aman Verma and Piyush Singh are undergoing treatment. 1 died on the spot, 2 succumbed in hospital Piyush Singh, Aman Verma and Shiva Singh, all residents of Shiv Colony, along with Akash Verma from Pipariya Bypass and Shiva Singh from Rajapur, suffered severe burns. All the injured were taken to Oyal District Hospital, where Akash and Shiva also died during treatment. The condition of the remaining three is critical. Their families have been informed. Bodies sent for post-mortem, investigation into cause of accident underway Police said they are trying to ascertain whether any of the youths travelling in the car owned the vehicle or whether they had rented it. The three bodies have been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. The cause of the accident is also being investigated. Additional SP East Pawan Gautam said that at around 2 am on Monday night, an out-of-control car crashed into a transformer near the Oyal outpost in Kheri police station limits. The car caught fire following the collision. Six people were travelling in the car and were headed towards Sitapur. Three people died in the accident, while the three injured were referred to KGMU in Lucknow for better treatment. Police reached the spot and carried out rescue and relief operations. The law-and-order situation is currently normal, and necessary action is being taken in the case.

stories.title: 12 devotees killed in Baghpat, bodies scattered up to 30m:Pickup overturns after crash on expressway; 19 injured
stories.summary: Pickup van carrying 32 devotees overturned after being hit by a speeding canter on the Eastern Peripheral Expressway in Uttar Pradesh’s Baghpat. Twelve people were killed in the accident, including six men, three women and three children, while more than 19 others were injured. The devotees were returning to Badaun after visiting Bagad Dham (Gogamedi) in Rajasthan. According to eyewitnesses, the accident took place around 1 am on Sunday when the speeding canter rammed into the pickup. The impact sent the pickup out of control and into the divider. It was then dragged several metres before overturning in the middle of the expressway. The crash was so severe that bodies were scattered up to 30 metres from the spot. Screams filled the area after the collision. Hearing a sound like an explosion, nearby residents rushed to the spot and alerted the police. Locals moved the injured from the expressway to the roadside. Police later took them to the district hospital. The accident occurred between Basi and Bada Gaon in the Khekra Kotwali area, around 15 km from the district headquarters. CM Yogi Adityanath expressed deep grief over the loss of lives in the accident. He directed officials to provide financial assistance of ₹2 lakh each to the families of the deceased and ₹50,000 each to those injured. 2 pictures of the accident… Returning home to Badaun after visiting Rajasthan DM-SP visit hospital to assess injured, inform families As soon as they learnt about the accident, District Magistrate Asmita Lal and SP Suraj Rai reached the district hospital. Both officials met the injured and directed healthcare workers to ensure they received the best possible treatment. Police are investigating the cause of the accident. The families of the deceased and injured have been informed over the phone. Those killed in the accident include Sadhu (60), his wife Munni Devi (55), and his brother Prem Singh (40). Fellow villagers Sugadpal (40), Rameshwar Yadav (60) and Jitendra (7) also died in the accident. Meanwhile, a total of 19 patients were taken to Meerut Medical College, of whom six died. The deceased were identified as Premwati (50), Diksha (2), Bhanumati (52) and an unidentified 45-year-old person. Murti (35) and Saurav (4) also died during treatment. SP leader says, ‘Victim families should receive adequate financial assistance’ Former Samajwadi Party district president Billu Pradhan said all the deceased belonged to Yadav families. SP MPs Dharmendra Yadav and Aditya Yadav called to enquire about the accident. Following this, SP workers and office-bearers visited the bereaved families. He said the injured should receive the best possible treatment and the post-mortem process should be completed at the earliest. He also demanded that the victim families be provided adequate financial assistance. He said all SP workers stand with the affected families in this difficult time. Injured undergoing treatment in Baghpat and Meerut Vimlesh Kumar Yadav, a relative of deceased Rameshwar Yadav, said, “People from the village had travelled to Rajasthan in a single vehicle and were returning when the accident occurred. They all belonged to the same village. Following news of the accident, the entire village is in mourning. People from the village have been travelling to Rajasthan on this pilgrimage for the past 20 years. The accident has devastated several families.” The injured admitted to a hospital in Meerut said most of the devotees were resting late at night when the accident suddenly occurred. No one could understand what had happened or how. When they opened their eyes, they found themselves lying on the road. Local residents took them to hospital in ambulances.

stories.title: Lucknow’s Prabhati wins crown:Class 12 student becomes Miss Teen India winner on national stage
stories.summary: Lucknow’s Class 12 student Prabhati Pandey has won the prestigious Miss Teen India 2026 title, making her mark on the national stage. Prabhati brought pride to Lucknow by achieving the feat through her talent, confidence and impressive presentation. After an outstanding performance in this prestigious national-level pageant, Prabhati was crowned the winner. Her success has brought immense joy to her family, teachers, and well-wishers. Prabhati prepared for the pageant and received grooming training at Catwalk Academy in Lucknow. Under the guidance of the academy's founder and director, Amit Samson Nanu, she received training in ramp walking, posing, communication skills, public speaking, personality development, styling, and media presence. Prabhati's achievement is also a special milestone for Catwalk Academy. The academy has established a new identity in the field of fashion and pageant grooming by producing its fourth pageant winner in just eight months. Amit Samson Nanu said that success in any competition comes not only from talent but also from consistent practice, discipline, and proper guidance. He said that Prabhati prepared with complete dedication and commitment and displayed remarkable confidence and maturity suited to the national stage. At Catwalk Academy, emphasis is placed not only on runway walking but also on the overall personality development of participants. The academy operates prestigious pageant platforms such as Femina Miss India Uttar Pradesh and Mrs. India Icon. Meanwhile, Mrs India Icon, scheduled to be held in Lucknow in December 2026, is being regarded as a significant opportunity for the city's fashion and pageant industry.

stories.title: Dog saves 8 lives in Gorakhpur:10 people were sitting under collapsing balcony, 8 moved away after smelling dog’s foul odour
stories.summary: Two lawyers, Alok and Sanjay, died in Gorakhpur after the roof slab of a platform on the banks of the Rapti River collapsed while they were attending a friend's mother's funeral. The two were sitting beneath the slab with others to shelter from the rain when it suddenly collapsed; according to eyewitnesses, around 10 people had been sitting there shortly before the accident, but eight moved away after a dog from the cremation ground arrived and sat there, as they were troubled by its foul smell, while Alok and Sanjay remained seated. Meanwhile, the rain intensified and lightning suddenly flashed. A few moments later, the slab collapsed. Both men were pulled out of the debris and taken to the hospital, where they died during treatment. People present at the scene are now discussing that if those eight people had not moved away because of the dog, the accident could have been even more horrific. Eyewitness Chana Devi said: ‘8 people moved away when a dog arrived’ Chana Devi's kiosk is just 6 to 10 metres from the scene. Items used in last rites, along with water, are available here. Chana Devi herself was present at the shop at the time of the incident and witnessed the entire accident. Chana Devi said that it was raining. Ten people had come and sat beneath the awning when a dog came and sat there. A strong foul odour was coming from its body. Troubled by the stench, 8 people got up and left, while two people remained seated there. They said that shortly afterward, lightning struck and the awning came crashing down. Both people were trapped beneath it. This dog keeps roaming around the cremation ground. It eats the remains of corpses, which is why its body gives off a foul odour. Alok Mishra had also been sitting there shortly beforehand The woman for whose funeral advocate Alok Asthana and Sanjay Singh had gone there was the maternal aunt of Alok Mishra, a resident of Krishnanagar Private Colony. Alok Mishra had also been sitting beneath the same platform shortly before the accident. Alok Mishra said, "Sanjay, Alok, two other people, and I were sitting there when the dog arrived. Troubled by its foul smell, I cursed it and climbed down from the platform to the other side. Meanwhile, the rain also intensified." He said that after some time, the body arrived there. They took the body and headed toward the river. Suddenly, lightning struck and the awning collapsed with a crash. We left the body and ran back, pulling both of them out of the debris. They were then taken to the hospital, but both died during treatment. Discussion taking place at the scene about the dog Following the accident, people at the scene have been discussing the dog. They say that if the dog had not come there and eight people had not moved away because of its foul smell, more people might have been standing under the awning when the accident occurred. However, it is difficult to say that the dog alone saved people's lives. What is certain is that eight people had moved away from there shortly before the accident, and only two lawyers were under the awning when it collapsed. Proposal to provide financial assistance of ₹9 lakh each to both families The deaths of both lawyers in the accident have left their families devastated. Both families depended on them, and their children were also pursuing their education. The families of both deceased lawyers have already been given checks for financial assistance of Rs 4 lakh each by the Disaster Management Department. District Magistrate Deepak Meena said that a proposal had been sent to provide an additional Rs 5 lakh each to both families from the Chief Minister's Discretionary Fund. According to the District Magistrate, this assistance is also expected to be provided soon. After this, both families will receive total financial aid of Rs 9 lakh each.

stories.title: M.Sc student’s murder accused arrested after 20 days:Killed her after marriage was fixed; strangled her with friend
stories.summary: Twenty days after the murder of M.Sc. student Shreya Upadhyay in Varanasi, accused Vivek Chaubey was arrested by Rajatalab police during an encounter at 5 a.m. on Monday (7 Sept). Police said Vivek was trying to flee after firing at them when he was shot in retaliatory action and subsequently admitted to hospital, while several teams had been deployed to search for him; police had earlier sent his friend Puneet Mishra to jail. ADCP Rajatalab Nripendra Kumar said that Rajatalab police have arrested Vivek Choubey, the main accused in the murder of MSc student Shreya Upadhyay. The main accused in the murder case, Vivek Choubey, has described the motive and sequence of events. His statement makes it clear that Shreya was murdered after a romantic relationship because Vivek wanted to marry her. Vivek was distressed after the young woman's marriage was arranged with another man and had been constantly pressuring her to marry him, although she continued to refuse. After this, Vivek planned to kill her with his friend Puneet Mishra. The two called her to a room and killed her. On Monday morning, after receiving information that accused Vivek was heading toward Jagatdevpur, the police surrounded the area. When Vivek saw the police team, he began to flee, so they pursued him and tried to apprehend him. Seeing the team behind him, Vivek opened fire, but the policeman escaped unharmed. In retaliatory action, the accused was shot in his right leg, causing him to fall injured. Vivek Chaubey, son of Ram Sahay Chaubey, was immediately sent to the Community Health Centre in Jakhini for treatment. A country-made pistol was recovered from the accused's possession. The police are taking further action. Searched across 6 districts and 2 states; examined 150 CCTV recordings Before his arrest, Vivek Chaubey, accused of murdering MSc student Shreya Upadhyay in Bachhaon, Rohania, kept changing his location. After the murder on the 18th and the recovery of the body on August 20, police examined footage from around 150 CCTV cameras. The accused switched off his mobile phone and sought shelter at the homes of different relatives and friends. He kept changing his hideouts. By questioning his relatives, acquaintances and people who remained in contact with him, police also learned about his movements. While searching for Vivek Chaubey, police are gathering information about his possible hideouts in six nearby districts. In addition, a search is being conducted for him in two states. Four teams, including the SOG, continued working on different leads. Murder committed for a ₹22 lakh contract According to police, Puneet Mishra, Vivek's friend who was arrested earlier, confessed to the crime and said that he had agreed to receive ₹22 lakh in exchange for helping murder Shreya Upadhyay. Vivek Chaubey was his long-time friend and had offered him the contract. Driven by greed, Puneet carried out the murder of Shreya Upadhyay along with Vivek Chaubey. Police said that the arrested accused, Puneet Mishra, was sent to jail after receiving treatment. Now his friend Vivek will also go to jail. Read the sequence of events now... Shreya left home for college on August 18. When she did not return home by evening, her family began searching for her. After questioning relatives and acquaintances, the police were informed. Her mobile location pointed to Bachhaon. Meanwhile, Vivek Chaubey's name came up. He lived in a rented room in Bachhaon and was reportedly already acquainted with Shreya. They found the key to the room; when they opened the lock, the body was found in the bathroom When the family members gathered information about Vivek, they traced him to Bhuawalpur village in the Seekhar area of Mirzapur, his maternal grandparents' village. When he was not found there, they learnt about the key to the room. The family took the key and reached the room in Bachhaon. As soon as they opened the lock, a strong stench came from inside. Shreya's body was found lying in the bathroom. The police, who arrived after being informed, sent the body for post-mortem and began investigating the murder. She wanted to prepare for NEET, but her parents did not want to send her away from home Shreya was the only daughter in her family. According to her relatives, she wanted to prepare for NEET and pursue medical studies. Her parents did not want to send her away for her education. She subsequently enrolled at Jagatpur PG College in Varanasi. She was a first-year MSc student. The family had many dreams for their daughter's education and future. Now, the same house is steeped in mourning. Father alleges the accused wanted to marry her out of greed for property Shreya's father alleges that his daughter would have inherited the family's property in the future. He alleges that the accused wanted to marry her out of greed for the property and killed her when she refused. Police are currently investigating the actual motive behind the murder and whether anyone else was involved in the incident. Post-mortem Indicates Injuries from a Sharp Weapon According to information that emerged after the post-mortem, Shreya died due to excessive bleeding. It has also come to light that injuries caused by a sharp weapon were found on the body. Samples have been sent for investigation into other aspects. What happened in the room at the time of the murder, what the motive was, and whether anyone else was involved – answers to these questions will become clear only as the investigation progresses. After the body was found on August 20, the accused could not be arrested by August 23. Four police teams have examined more than 150 CCTV recordings, and the search is underway across six districts and two states. The family is now waiting for the accused to be arrested and for the police to take further action. Vivek had threatened us, saying, "I'll see how she gets married." Her father, Sunil Upadhyay, said, "Vivek must have been counselled by his relatives. He remained well-behaved for some time, but after a while, he started coming around again. He continued talking about marrying Shreya. We arranged Shreya's marriage in a nearby village. The engagement took place, and the wedding was scheduled for February 2027. After this, Vivek became aggressive. He had threatened Shreya's mother, saying, "I will also see how this marriage takes place." Vivek has now killed my daughter. Shreya's aunt said that Vivek had already threatened to kill Shreya's father. Vivek simply wanted to marry Shreya, but she remained silent because of fear and pressure. Brother said-we asked them to break the lock, but the police refused Shreya's cousin, Anshuman Upadhyay, said, "Vivek escaped due to police negligence. When Shreya had not returned by the evening of August 18, I went to the police station. I asked the police to trace Shreya's phone location. Its location was showing in the Bachhaon area. This was the same area where Vivek had a rented room." After getting the location, I went there myself. Nothing could be found. I later informed the police as well. The station in charge reached the spot again with police personnel. The room was locked. We told the police that the mobile phone's location was showing this place. We asked them to break the lock, search inside, and retrieve the phone. But the police did not agree. Police told the family: Both are adults; they may have gone somewhere The family alleges that the police did not break open the lock. The police said they were not authorised to do so. They also said that both individuals were adults and might have gone somewhere. The family members questioned people living nearby. It emerged that the girl had already left the place. After this, the police team returned. The cousin said, "If the police had broken down the door that night, they would have found out that Shreya might still have been alive. Even if something had happened, the perpetrator would not have had so much time to escape. We could have caught him quickly." The family searched themselves and then found Shreya's body The family members said that they continued searching for Shreya the following day as well. They kept gathering information about Vivek and visiting his possible locations. During this time, the family went to Vivek's relatives' home, where they found his bag. It contained the key to his rented room. They took the key and returned to the same room in Bachhaon, which they had previously visited with the police. Her mother hoped that they might find some clue about her daughter. However, as soon as they opened the door, a strong foul smell began coming from inside. The family entered and found Shreya's decomposed body lying in the bathroom.

stories.title: Ram Van Gaman Path caves in at 118 spots:Built by same company that constructed Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway
stories.summary: 210-km-long Ram Van Gaman Path is being constructed from Ayodhya to Chitrakoot in Uttar Pradesh, with a four-lane highway being built along the routes taken by Lord Shri Ram during his exile. However, before it could open, the highway began sinking at Shringverpur in Prayagraj, with the road sinking at 118 spots across both lanes over a stretch of around 500 metres, cracks measuring 1 to 1.5 feet appearing and the approach section leading to the bridge tilting nearly 30 degrees to one side. Viewed from beneath the bridge, the approach walls also appear to have bulged outward by about half a foot. Work is now being carried out hurriedly to fill the cracks. Dainik Bhaskar inspected the highway in Shringverpur, about 35 kilometres from Prayagraj. See 2 pictures – In some places, the road has sunk by up to one foot We reached the Ram Van Gaman route to Chitrakoot in Shringverpur and entered the left lane of the four-lane highway. From here, up to the bridge over the Kanpur Highway, about 500 metres ahead, the road was found to have caved in at several places. The bridge's approach road has also sunk downward by nearly 30 degrees. Then, to return from the same bridge, we moved to the right lane and found the same condition on this side for the next 500 metres. The road has caved in across both lanes, with cracks one to one and a half feet wide. When we counted some of the larger potholes, we found that the road had sunk at 118 places over 500 metres in both the left and right lanes. In some places, the road has settled by up to one foot. About 300 metres beyond this bridge, a bridge is being constructed over the Ganga. However, the road farther ahead is in good condition. Vehicles passing below, with the road at risk of collapsing from above We spoke to people who travel through this area. Ujjwal Pandey said, "During construction, the soil was not properly compacted and strengthened, nor was sufficient rolling carried out. Proper attention was also not paid to water sprinkling and vibration." In addition, the quality of the asphalt used in the road also appears to be extremely poor. The road has sunk at several places because heavy rainwater seeped in and the soil was not compacted properly. Cracks have appeared in it. There is a risk of the road collapsing about 10-15 feet below the bridge approach. Vehicles are passing below. Road cracked in the middle due to the contractor's negligence Shiva Shankar Prajapati said, “The road has cracked in the middle. One side of the road has completely sunk. A slope has formed beneath the road, making it frightening to pass through here.” He added, "Due to the recent heavy rains and inadequate drainage, water accumulated beneath the road, causing it to sink. Potholes have also developed in several places on the road. It seems that the contractor was negligent during construction or that the work was carried out in haste." BJP leader's brother's company is constructing the road The construction of the Ram Van Gaman Path is being carried out by PNC Infratech. The company is owned by Pradeep Jain, the brother of BJP Rajya Sabha MP Naveen Jain. The same company also constructed the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway. That expressway too had potholes at around 84 locations. After the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway sank, the NHAI declared the company a non-performing entity. The company also removed three officers. PNC’s work is good, poor-quality work was done by SP Infra Developers Suryaprakash, an employee of PNC, said, “The roads that have sunk do not fall under our scope of work. The poor-quality work was not carried out by our company; it comes under SP Infra Developers. Our work starts beyond 49+155, where there are no issues or complaints. PNC’s work is good.” 210-km-long Ram Van Gaman Path being built at a cost of ₹4,400 crore Under the Ram Van Gaman Path Project, a nearly 210-kilometre-long, four-lane road is being constructed from Ayodhya to Chitrakoot. Approximately ₹4,400 crore is to be spent on this project. Its objective is to provide better road connectivity between religious and historical sites such as Ayodhya, Sultanpur, Pratapgarh, Shringverpur Dham, Kaushambi, and Chitrakoot. Lord Shri Ram travelled through these routes during his exile. The project was scheduled to be completed in December 2024, but after a delay of one and a half years, it is now nearly complete. It was being said that PM Modi and CM Yogi could inaugurate it soon. Foundation stone laid in 2022 The foundation stone for the Ram Van Gaman Path project was laid in 2022. Considered extremely important from religious and tourism perspectives, the completion of this project is expected to make travel easier for pilgrims from Ayodhya to Prayagraj and Chitrakoot. Executive Engineer says, ‘Damage caused by heavy rain’ PWD NH Wing Executive Engineer Ravindra Pal Singh said the damaged section does not belong to PNC, but to S and P. However, the damaged section lies at the boundary between the phases being handled by the two companies. He said the damage was caused by heavy rain. Maintenance work is currently underway.
