stories.title: ‘Need to provide holistic education’
Officials, clerks pocket 7% of UP road, drainage funds:CDO gets major share of commission; sting Op captures bribe rate list – Part II
stories.summary: You've seen and read how legislators in Uttar Pradesh are allegedly taking commissions from funds meant for development works. After the legislators’ 35% share, officials also allegedly take a cut from the remaining amount. To expose this, we reached the CDO offices with recommendation letters issued by MLAs. What we found was a complete system of bribery. From junior employees to senior officials, everyone has a fixed rate. Read Part 2 of our biggest expose We had a recommendation letter from BJP MLA Jai Mangal Kannaujia of Maharajganj Sadar, seeking the release of ₹10.50 lakh from the MLA fund. We reached the CDO (Chief Development Officer) office in Maharajganj district with the letter. The MLA had specifically asked us to meet senior clerk Arjun Kumar Gautam. We spoke to him, and Arjun explained the entire system of corruption to us. Senior clerk takes ₹8,000 in bribes Reporter: The MLA has given our NGO the work of installing solar street lights. He asked us to meet you and understand the system. Arjun: We cannot give the money directly to your NGO. We will have to release it through some department. Reporter: You will give it to UPNEDA, and the money will then reach the NGO through them. Arjun: You will get the work done through them? Reporter: Yes. What is the system here? Arjun: There is a 5% commission here. Whichever department you want to take the money through, we will release the funds to them. The MLA fund will be released in two instalments, 60% first and 40% later. Reporter: Reduce the commission a little from 5%. The MLA has already increased his share. Arjun: It is fixed here. It applies to all MLAs. Reporter: Make it 3%. We will give you the money in one go. Arjun: It cannot be 3%. The CDO and PD (Project Director) also get a share. Reporter: The money must go directly to the CDO, right? There cannot be anyone in between. Arjun: There is the CDO, the PD, the technical team, AE (Assistant Engineer), JE (Junior Engineer), the accountant and me. There are so many people involved that what comes to each is just a nominal amount. We cannot decide that you should give this much and take this much. It is fixed, and the fixed amount is paid. Reporter: How much would it be for ₹10.50 lakh and ₹52,500? Arjun: Yes. Whatever proposal comes in, we will get the work done through whoever you are told to use. During this conversation, Arjun Kumar Gautam, the senior clerk at the Maharajganj CDO office, took the first instalment of the bribe, ₹3,000. (The next day, we returned to senior clerk Arjun Kumar Gautam with the work order issued by the MLA.) Reporter: It cannot be that only you and the CDO get a commission and no one else is involved. Arjun: The technical team will definitely go to inspect the work. They have to get their share. We cannot ignore the PD. We cannot ignore the CDO. All the bills go to the accountant. They keep the complete accounts. There is no one else whose share can be cut. Reporter: It is difficult to get any work done here. Arjun: This has been fixed in the DRDO (District Rural Development Office) for a very long time. PDs come and say that it is 7% there and 8% there. They ask why it is only this much here and tell us to increase it. We tell them that we cannot do that. SP MLA’s 7% commission demand in Azamgarh Samajwadi Party MLA Pooja Saroj from Mehnagar in Azamgarh district had issued a recommendation letter seeking the release of ₹81 lakh from the MLA fund after allegedly agreeing to a 35% commission deal. She had asked us to meet assistant accountant Ashok Kumar Srivastava at the CDO office to get the funds released. We reached the CDO office posing as NGO managers. We spoke to assistant accountant Ashok Kumar Srivastava, who explained the entire alleged bribery system to us. Accountant takes ₹5,000 and says, ‘Your work will be done’ Reporter: What is the system? What percentage is being charged? Ashok: Including the AE (Assistant Engineer) and everyone else, the commission will come to 7%. Reporter: There are only three layers, right? You, the engineer, and the AE? Ashok: First, there is the AE. Second, the BDO (Block Development Officer). Third, the CDO. Reporter: What will the system be? How much has to be paid upfront and how much later? Ashok: When the money is released, 60% of the fixed 7% commission will have to be paid in advance. Reporter: 7% is too much. Please see if it can be reduced. Ashok: Bring the letter, then we will talk. Maharajganj CDO not taking bribery allegations seriously Despite all the evidence of alleged bribery, Maharajganj CDO Mahendra Kumar Singh does not appear willing to take the matter seriously. He said, The claim that the CDO office takes a 5% bribe to approve MLA fund works is completely wrong. I do not know who made this statement, but it is rubbish. Nothing like this happens here.

stories.title: Akhilesh wears blue scarf instead of red:SP student wing members to switch to blue T-shirts and jeans; party targeting Dalits or Gen Z?
stories.summary: From Parliament in Delhi to election rallies in Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh Yadav has often been seen wearing a red scarf and red cap. Along with the kurta-pyjama, these have become something of a dress code for Samajwadi Party leaders, giving office-bearers a distinct identity much like the party flag and symbol. But at a meeting of district presidents held in Lucknow on August 31, 2026, Akhilesh was seen wearing a blue scarf around his neck. Six days later, a message reached workers of the Samajwadi Party’s student wing, Samajwadi Chhatrasabha, telling them they would now wear blue T-shirts and jeans. Until now, they had worn maroon shirts and white trousers. The SP organisation has also sent blue T-shirts to student leaders, bearing the Samajwadi Chhatrasabha logo. This is the wing that remains active among students in universities and colleges across Uttar Pradesh. Is the SP using these changes to woo Dalit voters or Gen Z ahead of the elections? Read the report… Understand the change in the SP’s dress code August 31- District presidents’ meeting A meeting of district presidents and metropolitan presidents from all 75 districts was held at the Samajwadi Party office in Lucknow. The agenda was election preparations. Everyone wore red scarves around their necks. When Akhilesh Yadav arrived on stage, Shivpal was with him. Neither was wearing the usual red scarf. Both were wearing blue scarves instead. It was an unspoken message to party office-bearers. However, when Akhilesh was asked about the blue scarf, he replied in a measured tone, “The weaver brothers made it for us. So that we look a little different.” He then laughed. September 6- Message reaches Chhatrasabha workers Samajwadi Chhatrasabha is the SP’s student wing. It too has a dress code, with members wearing maroon shirts and white trousers. This was changed on September 6. Student workers have now been sent blue T-shirts and jeans. The T-shirts feature the Chhatrasabha logo and a bicycle. However, the SP’s official launch of the new dress code is scheduled for September 8. What is Akhilesh trying to achieve with the colour blue? Akhilesh Yadav has been seen wearing blue scarves before, particularly on occasions such as BR Ambedkar’s birth anniversary or at rallies in Dalit-dominated areas. According to political analysts, the SP is pursuing two major objectives through the change: 1. Dalit vote bank - Dalits account for 21.1% of Uttar Pradesh’s voters. Wearing a blue scarf is an attempt to send the message that the SP is now a direct claimant to the politics of Dalit rights. As the BSP’s political base in UP continues to weaken, the SP wants to take over that space completely. In political history, blue has long been a symbol of Ambedkarite ideology and Bahujan politics. Through this, the SP wants to give its PDA (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) slogan a visual identity, rather than leaving it confined to speeches. 2. Gen Z and young voters - Samajwadi Chhatrasabha has units in 80 universities and more than 8,000 colleges across UP. Until now, its members were seen in maroon shirts and white trousers. The party believes blue jeans and T-shirts will make it easier to connect with students on university and college campuses. Message to Dalits through blue, will it help? Until 2022, a large section of Dalits, particularly non-Jatavs, along with non-Yadav OBC voters, remained a strong support base for the BJP. The trend changed in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The ‘Constitution is in danger’ narrative and Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA strategy led to a rapid shift of the BSP’s traditional Dalit vote, along with non-Jatav Dalit and OBC voters who had moved away from the BJP, towards the SP-Congress alliance. As a result, the BJP was reduced to 33 seats in UP, while the SP emerged as the largest party with 37 seats. Akhilesh is once again trying to build the same narrative just before the elections, in an effort to secure Dalit voters’ support in the Assembly polls. Chhatrasabha national president says the change will apply across the organisation Chhatrasabha national president Dr Imran says, Blue is considered a symbol of equality and equal rights. It can also be seen as a symbol of the thinking of Dr Ram Manohar Lohia and Dr BR Ambedkar. This is a student organisation, so changes are being made to increase youth participation. We are not limited to UP; we are also doing good work in Delhi and Madhya Pradesh. This new dress code will apply to the entire Chhatrasabha organisation across the country. Expert says SP-BSP alliance created this atmosphere Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says, Since the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the BSP’s influence has become more deeply embedded in the SP. This was the period when the Samajwadi Party and Bahujan Samaj Party entered into an alliance for the Lok Sabha elections.The alliance broke up after the elections. After that, several prominent BSP leaders left the party and joined the SP. These included major Dalit faces such as Inderjit Saroj, RK Chaudhary and Tribhuvan Dutt. The SP then also began observing the birth and death anniversaries of Dalit icons, including Dr BR Ambedkar and Kanshi Ram.Before long, the backdrop at the Samajwadi Party office changed. Pictures of various Samajwadi leaders replaced the bicycle that had been on the backdrop. Along with green and red, blue was also added. Since then, Akhilesh Yadav has increasingly been seen wearing blue scarves on different occasions. SP spokesperson Manoj Kaka says, Every colour has its own meaning. All Bahujan people identify with the colour blue. As for the dress code, changes happen in everything from time to time, and this is also being changed. It may be premature to link it to vote-bank politics. Our party works in line with what today’s youth and students think.

stories.title: Alliance Air flight engine fails mid-air:Emergency landing in Delhi, all 40 passengers safe; aircraft was coming from Prayagraj
stories.summary: An Alliance Air flight's engine failed mid-air. The flight made an emergency landing at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport using its second engine. There were 40 people on board, including crew members. Everyone is safe. The DGCA has ordered an investigation into the incident. Alliance Air flight 9I-698 took off from Prayagraj for New Delhi at around 12:33 p.m. On reaching the area around Meerut, the pilot detected a technical fault in one of the engines. The pilot immediately informed air traffic control (ATC) and sought permission to make an emergency landing in Delhi. An emergency alert was issued at IGI Airport as soon as the information was received. All necessary arrangements were made at the airport for the aircraft's safe landing. The aircraft was landed safely at around 2:15 p.m. The aircraft had arrived in Prayagraj from Bilaspur in the morning According to sources, the aircraft that developed an engine-related technical fault had departed from Bilaspur for Prayagraj at 10:45 a.m. on Friday. The aircraft reached Prayagraj Airport at around 11:58 a.m. After remaining there for some time, the aircraft took off from Prayagraj for Delhi at 12:33 p.m. The technical fault emerged afterwards. Second incident involving an Alliance Air aircraft in two weeks This is the second serious incident involving a technical fault in an Alliance Air aircraft in about two weeks. Earlier, on 28 August, Alliance Air flight 9I 613, which arrived in Bilaspur from Delhi, narrowly avoided an accident. The aircraft's left tyre burst while it was landing at Bilasa Devi Kevat Airport in Bilaspur. After the tyre burst, sparks flew from the runway and there was intense friction. However, the pilot acted swiftly and brought the aircraft to a safe stop. The aircraft was carrying 37 passengers and four crew members. Everyone remained safe. Following these two incidents, which came to light within two weeks, questions are being raised over the maintenance and safety arrangements of Alliance Air aircraft.

stories.title: BJP core group meeting:UP in-charge Vinod Tawde, organisation general secretary BL Santosh present; strategy being prepared for 2027 polls
stories.summary: After suffering setbacks in the Awadh and Kanpur-Bundelkhand regions in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP is now in no mood to take any risks. To put the party into election mode, BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh reached Lucknow on Friday evening. BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary and state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh welcomed him at the airport. BL Santosh’s visit is being considered politically significant. Major core committee meeting at BJP office BL Santosh will chair an important core committee meeting at the state BJP headquarters on Friday evening. The state’s top leadership will attend the meeting. Who will attend: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, state president Pankaj Chaudhary and state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh. Election roadmap to be discussed: After the core committee meeting, BL Santosh will hold a meeting with all state general secretaries and regional in-charges. The meeting will focus on the strategy for the Assembly elections and the division of organisational responsibilities. Close watch on 134 seats in Awadh-Kanpur The BJP suffered major losses in the 2024 general election in the Awadh region, which has 82 Assembly seats, and the Kanpur-Bundelkhand region, which has 52 seats. This is why the central leadership has now turned its full attention towards these two regions. On Saturday, BL Santosh will visit the Kanpur-Bundelkhand region. An introductory meeting with local leaders will be held to sharpen the election strategy. Nitin Nabin’s programme may change: BJP national president Nitin Nabin is likely to travel directly to Kanpur. However, his proposed Meerut visit on September 12 and 13 has been cancelled. State in-charge Vinod Tawde will again visit Uttar Pradesh between September 15 and 20. Central leadership keeps close watch on UP The BJP’s central organisation has been directly monitoring every major and minor development in Uttar Pradesh for the past few months. July 4 visit: Nitin Nabin and BL Santosh held marathon meetings in Lucknow with the Chief Minister and both Deputy Chief Ministers. A coordination meeting was also held with NDA allies Apna Dal (S), RLD, Nishad Party and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party. September 5 meeting: State in-charge Vinod Tawde reached Lucknow for a two-day visit and reviewed the organisation’s work with regional and state-level office-bearers. Report card on grassroots presence to be reviewed During his visit, BL Santosh will also take a detailed account of the progress of campaigns being run by the organisation. The six-month campaign being held to mark Sant Ravidas Jayanti, from July 29 to February 20, 2027, will be reviewed. stories.title: Chandrashekhar’s former girlfriend returns to India after 6 years:Hindu groups receive her, says MP will be responsible if she is attacked
stories.summary: Dr. Rohini Ghawari, who had accused Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad of sexual exploitation, returned to India from Switzerland on Friday. She was welcomed at Delhi airport by several people, including Shri Rashtriya Rajput Karni Sena national president Surajpal Singh Ammu, Hindutva leader Daksh Chaudhary, and Akku Pandit. Without naming Chandrashekhar, Rohini Ghawari said, "A person who follows Babasaheb Ambedkar believes in justice. Such a person is not exploitative. Why didn't you fight for my dignity? Why did you treat me unjustly? Why? Am I not a daughter of this society? Am I not a daughter of the Dalit community?" Rohini said, "I will visit different states and hold meetings. I am not among those who sit at home out of fear. And unlike you, I will neither beg for security nor be bought. If anything happens to me, you and your Bhim Army will be responsible." Rohini had posted a photo of herself on X while leaving Switzerland. It read: "Goodbye to Switzerland, the country that gave me everything from the title of Doctor to the recognition of delivering a speech at the United Nations. The six years I spent in this country will always be remembered. Six years ago, I went there with three bags; now I am returning with two bags and countless memories."

stories.title: Two youths take horse injections before race to win:Collapse on field in Agra; were preparing for Army recruitment
stories.summary: Two young men injected themselves with a steroid meant for horses to win a 6-kilometer race in Agra. As soon as the race ended, both their conditions deteriorated and they collapsed on the field. Their companions took them to a local hospital, where doctors treated them for two hours. Their condition improved afterward. According to the villagers, Shyamveer Sikarwar (16) came second, and Gaurav (22) came fourth in the competition. Both are also preparing for army recruitment. The race competition was held on Thursday in the Kheragarh police station area, 35 kilometers from the district headquarters. According to the doctor, the two had taken the injection to improve their performance and reduce fatigue. Know the full story... Shyamveer, a resident of Aaila village in the Kheragarh area, is studying in Class 11. His father is a farmer, and his two elder brothers work in private jobs. Gaurav, meanwhile, is an undergraduate student. His father is also a farmer, while his elder brother works in a private job. According to the villagers, both of them regularly run and engage in physical exercise. At around 7 a.m. on Thursday, the Marathon Committee organized a 6-kilometer race in the village. The first prize was set at ₹2,100, the second at ₹1,100, and ₹551 for the participant who finished third. Medals were also to be awarded to the top 10 participants. Gaurav and Shyamveer also took part in the competition. Both said, "To improve our performance, we injected ourselves with 3 ml of an injection meant for horses. After finishing the race, our health deteriorated. Our companions took us to the CHC in Kheragarh. We felt better after receiving treatment there." An empty vial of the injection was also found in the youths' possession. Pushpendra, a member of the organizing committee, said- Competitions are held from time to time to nurture the talents of villagers. As part of this initiative, a 6-kilometer marathon was organized on Thursday. The race concluded successfully. Afterward, Shyamveer Sikarwar and Gaurav Sikarwar felt anxious, following which they were taken to the Kheragarh CHC. Both were sent back after some time. It is not known what they had taken. Doctor says: Taking steroids without medical advice is dangerous According to CHC Superintendent Dr. RK Singh, the two young men had taken steroid injections to improve performance and reduce fatigue. Their health deteriorated afterward. After approximately two hours of treatment, both of them showed improvement. The doctor said that taking any kind of steroid or injection without medical advice can be seriously harmful. Young people preparing for recruitment and physical examinations may put their health at risk by resorting to such practices in the desire to improve their performance quickly.

stories.title: Surveyors made to wear petticoats, garlanded with shoes:MLA Brijbhushan Rajput says ‘Don’t beat them’; Mahoba farmers had accused them of extortion
stories.summary: In Mahoba, farmers caught two crop surveyors and allegedly paraded them through the village after accusing them of extorting money by promising higher crop insurance payouts. The farmers made the two men wear petticoats and blouses, applied lipstick and bindis to them, and put garlands of shoes around their necks. According to the farmers, the surveyors had collected more than ₹2 lakh from villagers, charging each farmer between ₹1,000 and ₹2,000. The farmers caught the two men at around 10 pm on Thursday. Farmers seek BJP MLA’s intervention After catching the surveyors, the farmers spoke to BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput over a video call. The MLA reprimanded the two men and told the villagers to humiliate them before handing them over to the police. The MLA told the villagers to make the men wear petticoats and bangles, put garlands of shoes around their necks, blacken their faces and parade them through the village before handing them over to the police. Both surveyors detained by police The incident took place in Natarra village, around 35 km from the district headquarters. Charkhari police have detained both accused surveyors. The two men work as surveyors for Global Ark, a company that conducts crop surveys for IFFCO-TOKIO. The insurer provides crop insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. See the pictures... Know the full story... Most farmers in Natarra village grow urad, sesame, groundnut and other crops. Heavy rainfall over the past 20 days has damaged most crops during the current kharif season. Farmers claim around 90% of their urad, sesame and groundnut crops have been destroyed. After the crop damage, farmers informed the insurance company in the hope of receiving compensation under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. Two surveyors arrived to assess crop damage According to the farmers, IFFCO-TOKIO provides crop insurance in the area under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. About a week ago, two surveyors from Global Arc, the company contracted to conduct crop surveys, arrived in the village to assess the damage. Both are reportedly residents of Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh. Farmers allege surveyors demanded money for higher payouts Farmer Indrapal Kushwaha said he lodged a complaint with the insurance company’s toll-free number after his crop was damaged. The two surveyors arrived about a week ago and have been conducting surveys since then. Kushwaha alleged that the surveyors took ₹5,000 from him through an online payment. They allegedly told farmers that paying money would lead to a higher assessment of crop damage, which could result in a larger insurance payout. Village representative Ravindra Rajput alleged that the two men collected more than ₹2 lakh from around 200 farmers in the village. Several farmers were also allegedly threatened with losing their insurance compensation if they refused to pay. MLA questions surveyors over alleged extortion on video call Late Thursday night, villagers caught both surveyors and contacted Charkhari BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput over a video call. The MLA spoke to village head representative Ravindra Rajput and other villagers before questioning the two surveyors himself. He strongly reprimanded them over the alleged collection of money from farmers. The MLA then told the villagers to dress the two surveyors in sarees, put garlands of shoes around their necks and parade them through the village before handing them over to the police. Following this, the villagers dressed the two men in women’s clothes and paraded them through the village. The police were later called and the two men were handed over to them. MLA’s representative reaches village, urges farmers not to pay Soon after, MLA representative Suraj Pandey also reached the spot. He said such extortion would not be tolerated. The MLA has asked party workers to visit villages, interact with farmers and spread awareness that no one should pay money in the name of compensation. Agriculture officer arrived; both surveyors in police custody Meanwhile, upon receiving information about the commotion, Agriculture Officer Ram Sajeevan also reached the village. He heard the villagers' complaints and said, “The matter will be brought to the District Magistrate's attention, and action will be taken after an investigation.”

stories.title: Airline fined ₹64,000 in Gorakhpur:Passenger stopped after boarding, gets justice 6 years later
stories.summary: Gorakhpur’s District Consumer Commission has delivered a major verdict in a nearly six-year-old case involving a passenger who was stopped from boarding a flight before its scheduled departure time. After a lengthy legal process and multiple hearings, the victim has finally received justice, with the commission’s decision sending the message that although justice may be delayed, it is ultimately delivered. The case concerns Jaya Upadhyay, a resident of New Shivpuri Colony in Rustampur, Gorakhpur. Her father had booked a SpiceJet Airlines ticket on February 27, 2018, for her journey from Delhi to Gorakhpur. The scheduled departure time of the flight was 9:45 a.m. On the day of the journey, Jaya Upadhyay reached Delhi Airport ahead of time, at 9:05 a.m. She completed all the formalities and also obtained her boarding pass, making it clear that she had fully complied with the prescribed travel rules. Boarding was stopped 20 minutes early Despite completing all the required procedures, when Jaya Upadhyay reached the gate to board the aircraft, SpiceJet Airlines staff stopped her just 20 minutes before the flight. The incident was shocking in itself, as boarding usually continues until the scheduled departure time. She was prevented from boarding the aircraft without any valid reason, disrupting her entire travel plan. Even the money was not refunded The matter did not end there. Even after preventing Jaya Upadhyay from boarding the flight, SpiceJet Airlines did not refund the ticket fare of ₹4,560. As a result, she suffered not only financial loss but also considerable mental distress. On the one hand, her journey was interrupted, and on the other, she did not receive her money back, making the matter even more serious. Filed a complaint with the Consumer Commission for justice After this entire sequence of events, Jaya Upadhyay did not give up and filed a complaint with the District Consumer Commission to seek justice. Her lawyers argued before the commission that the passenger had arrived ahead of time and complied with all the rules, yet she was prevented from boarding the flight and was not even refunded the money, which clearly amounted to a deficiency in service. Airline's Fault Established After Hearing During the hearing, the commission heard arguments from both sides and examined all the facts. Commission President Surendra Kumar Singh and members Krishnanand Mishra and Beena Singh found that SpiceJet Airlines' conduct was entirely irresponsible. They stated that preventing a passenger from boarding before the scheduled time and failing to refund the ticket amount were both violations of consumer rights and would be considered a deficiency in service. Order to Refund the Amount Along with Compensation and Interest In its decision, the Commission issued strict directions to SpiceJet Airlines, ordering it to refund the ticket amount of ₹4,560 along with 10% annual interest. In addition, considering the mental and financial distress suffered by the passenger, the airline was ordered to pay ₹60,000 as compensation. The airline will also have to bear the litigation expenses. Thus, overall, the airline will have to pay approximately ₹64,000. A Strong Message for Consumers This decision sends a strong message to all consumers who remain silent even after falling victim to a company's negligence. The case shows that if you raise your voice for your rights, the law stands with you. Although justice may take time, the truth ultimately prevails, and those at fault have to pay the price. Warning to Companies This decision of the District Consumer Commission has also issued a clear warning to service-providing companies to comply with their rules and responsibilities. If negligence or arbitrary conduct occurs at any level, they will face legal action and financial penalties. This decision will be regarded as a strong precedent for similar cases in the future.

stories.title: Mayawati attacks Akhilesh over blue 'gamacha':Says ‘casteist mindset will not change’; calls Congress, which offered Akash a deal, a sinking ship
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati has hit out at Akhilesh Yadav. Without naming him, she said on Friday that adopting the BSP’s blue colour, wearing a blue scarf around the neck, dressing in blue clothes or putting blue fabric on a stage would not change a party’s casteist mindset. Mayawati wrote on social media platform X: "If you genuinely care about the poor, Dalits, tribals, backward classes and other neglected sections, then all opposition parties, including the SP and Congress, must first cleanse their hearts and minds. Merely adopting the colour blue does not make anyone an Ambedkarite." In fact, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had arrived wearing a blue scarf around his neck during a press conference on August 31. Three days earlier, Akhilesh had launched a new blue uniform for the student wing, the Samajwadi Party Chhatra Sabha. He had said, "Blue is the colour of the Bahujan Samaj as well as its ideology." On the offer to her nephew Akash Anand to join the Congress, Mayawati said, "Congress is like a sinking ship. Why would anyone put their political future in darkness by joining it?" After Akash was expelled from the BSP, Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam had said that the doors of the Congress were open to Akash and that he would receive due respect there. Key points from Mayawati’s post 1. Mayawati said, ‘They say one thing and do exactly the opposite’ Mayawati said, "Opposition parties have continuously changed their colours on issues concerning backward classes and Dalits. These parties say one thing and do exactly the opposite." Questioning the Samajwadi Party’s PDA slogan, referring to backward classes, Dalits and minorities, she said the BSP was the only party fighting the real battle for the Bahujan Samaj. She described the BSP as their only well-wisher and the only Ambedkarite party. 2. ‘Those expelled from BSP are opportunists and loyal to no one’ Mayawati said, "People expelled from the BSP have switched parties several times. This gives an indication of their selfish and opportunistic politics. Such people cannot do good for any party." She said some expelled leaders, while acting at the behest of other parties, even go on to form small parties and organisations. According to her, this cannot serve the collective interests of the Bahujan Samaj. 3. ‘They cannot contest elections without alliances; power is the most important thing’ Mayawati said, "Such parties cannot even contest elections without alliances. At the same time, when a major party forms the government, they cannot stay away from joining it." The BSP chief also targeted parties that advise leaders expelled from the BSP to join them or form separate parties. She said such parties should first look within themselves. 4. ‘Babasaheb had advised the Bahujan Samaj to maintain distance from Congress’ Referring to Dr BR Ambedkar, Mayawati said that during his lifetime, he had warned members of the Bahujan Samaj to maintain distance from the Congress. She said it was important for people associated with the BSP and its movement to understand these points in the current political circumstances. 5. ‘Ashok Siddharth tried several tactics and was forced to retire from politics’ On the political retirement of Akash Anand’s father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, Mayawati said, "On the day I advised Ashok to retire from politics, he tried several tactics. When none of them worked, he was forced to announce his retirement at 6.30 am the next morning because of the compulsion and the fear of greater losses." Ashok Siddharth retired from politics, Akash expelled from BSP Mayawati expelled her nephew Akash Anand from the party again on Thursday morning. At 9 am, she wrote on X, "Akash is more attached to his father-in-law. He has become double-minded. If he wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so. Therefore, from today, he has been freed from the party." A day earlier, on Wednesday, Mayawati had set Ashok Siddharth’s retirement from politics as a condition for restoring Akash’s party position. Around 17 hours after Mayawati set the condition, Ashok Siddharth announced his retirement from politics at 7 am on Thursday. Following the announcement by Akash’s father-in-law, it was believed that Mayawati might forgive Akash. However, surprising everyone, she not only refused to restore his position but also expelled him from the party. This is the second time in three years that Mayawati has expelled Akash from the BSP. Seven days earlier, she had removed him from the post of national coordinator, the party’s number two position. From Akhilesh to Sanjay Nishad, who said what about Akash? At a press conference in Lucknow on September 10, when asked whether Akash Anand could join the SP, Akhilesh Yadav said, "You are a journalist, you tell him to come, we will take him." Nishad Party president Sanjay Nishad said, "Akash Anand should join us. He will be given full respect and a major responsibility. He could even be made national president. The dream of Ambedkar and Kanshi Ram remains incomplete, and we can all work together to fulfil it." Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai had said, "Akash Anand was speaking about his people, which Mayawati did not like." Congress leaders also believe that decisions taken by the party have played a major role in damaging Akash Anand’s political career. Read why Akash was expelled 1. According to sources, a close party leader allegedly provoked Mayawati against Ashok Siddharth, telling her that he was misleading Akash and interfering in party decisions. Mayawati subsequently made Ashok’s retirement from politics a condition for Akash’s return. 2. In a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Ashok had agreed to retire on Wednesday itself. He announced his retirement on Thursday morning. The decision was then in Akash’s hands. A senior party leader told Akash to repost Mayawati’s post and publicly thank her. However, Akash was not willing to do so. 3. Akash said, "Whatever I do, she simply does not trust me. On September 9, Mayawati wrote about Ashok Siddharth and me, including the line ‘your son-in-law...’. Akash was extremely upset over this." 4. This time, Akash was not willing to accept any position in the party. Even his father, Anand Kumar, tried to persuade him, but he refused. Akash said he was willing to work for the party independently and without holding any position. 5. When Mayawati came to know about Akash’s position, she became even more upset. She subsequently decided to expel him from the party.

stories.title: Constable dies by suicide, wife screams after seeing body:Father faints and ASP helps him; body found hanging in Ambedkar Nagar room
stories.summary: A 30-year-old constable died by suicide in Ambedkar Nagar. His body was found hanging from the window grille in his room at 5:30 a.m. on Friday. The door was locked from the inside. The incident came to light when the constable's colleague arrived to collect the mess keys. When he knocked on the door, there was no response. He informed the officers. The police broke open the door and took out the body. No suicide note was found in the room. Sandeep, a resident of Mau, was the mess clerk at the police lines. The incident took place in the Akbarpur Kotwali area, 3 km from the Collectorate. The constable had married Ranjana three years ago. They have a one-and-a-half-year-old daughter. He was the only son in his family. As soon as they were informed of the incident, his father and wife arrived. His wife, Ranjana, screamed upon seeing the body and fainted while crying. His father, Rampyare, collapsed unconscious. The ASP helped him up. Placing a hand on his shoulder, he said, 'Stay strong, please don't worry. We are with you.' ASP Tejveer Singh said: Sandeep had gone home on a two-day leave. He returned to duty on Thursday. The initial investigation suggests family discord. No information about departmental or other work-related stress has emerged. The police are also examining his mobile phone to determine the circumstances before the incident. See 4 pictures- Sandeep had joined the police force 8 years ago Sandeep Kumar was originally a resident of Nav Semar village in Mau. He joined the police force in 2018. He married Ranjana in 2023. He lived alone in a rented accommodation located behind the engineering college in Akbarpur. A fellow constable said, "On Friday, I called him several times to collect the mess keys, but he did not answer. After that, I went to his room. The door was locked from the inside. There was no response even after knocking and calling out. Suspecting something was wrong, I informed the officers. When the police opened the door, they found Sandeep's body."

stories.title: Umesh Pal’s wife says, ‘I am Brahmin, married in temple’:Says she does not know Pooja Pal’s caste; read what Atiq family lawyer asked in court
stories.summary: In the much-discussed Umesh Pal murder case at the Prayagraj District Court, his wife, Jaya Pal, testified. Tarachandra Gupta, the lawyer for Eklakh Ahmed, the accused brother-in-law of mafia don Atiq Ahmed, asked, "How did you and Umesh get married? Was it by your choice, or did someone else arrange it? Is there any record of it?" Jaya Pal replied, "I belong to the Brahmin community. I married Umesh Pal on January 19, 2005. I was an adult at the time, so everything happened with my consent. The wedding rituals were performed at a temple near my in-laws' home. The priest conducted the ceremonies. Therefore, no written record was made. I do not even know the name of the temple." The lawyer asked, "Did Umesh Pal identify himself as an eyewitness in the murder case of former MLA Raju Pal? What caste does Raju Pal's wife, Pooja Pal, belong to? Did she ever have a physical altercation with Umesh Pal?" Jaya replied that she did not know. However, she said that no physical altercation had taken place between Umesh and Pooja Pal in the Dhoomanganj police station area. Actually, the hearing in the Umesh Pal murder case has been underway in court since September 8. During the first two days, witness Jaya Pal's statement was recorded in the Special Judge SC/ST Act Court. Arguments began thereafter. On February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal and his two government gunners were shot and killed and attacked with bombs in broad daylight in Prayagraj. Umesh was the prime witness in the 2005 murder case of BSP MLA Raju Pal. Mafia don and former MP Atiq Ahmed, his brother Ashraf, his son Asad, and their aides were accused in the case. Read what Jaya said in response to the lawyer's questions- Jaya Pal said-she does not know about the relationship between Pooja and Umesh Jaya Pal said-When Umesh testified, the Samajwadi Party government was in power in UP Jaya Pal told the court-I do not know whether the court had issued any order for a CBI investigation into the Raju Pal murder case. When Umesh Pal testified in the Raju Pal murder case, the Samajwadi Party government was in power in Uttar Pradesh. I know that Atiq Ahmed was elected MLA from the City West constituency five times. Atiq Ahmed was also elected as an MP from Allahabad district. "I don't know whether Umesh Pal contested the election from the OBC community or not." Jaya Pal said that it is true that after Umesh Pal testified in the Raju Pal murder case, the district panchayat election was held. I do not know whether Umesh Pal contested that election as a member of the OBC community or not. I also do not know whether Atiq Ahmed's men and vehicles were used in campaigning during that election. Jaya told the media: I am receiving threats to blow me up with RDX Today, I am remembering the scene of my husband's murder Jaya Pal said, "I am reminded of that scene today... My husband had just left after returning from court when he was brutally beaten to death on the way. I too will be murdered, just as my husband was. Jaya Pal showed a poster of Umar, the eldest son of Atiq Ahmed. Umar is pointing a finger and signaling someone to remain silent. Who is this gesture meant for?" It is being circulated on social media every day that Umar will come, Ali will come, and Ahzam is out. My family is being tortured. I want justice. Umesh Pal's wife had reached the court with several lawyers and supporters. Earlier, on September 1 as well, Jaya Pal had recorded her statement in court. Know about the Raju Pal and Umesh Pal murder case- In 2005, BSP MLA Raju Pal was murdered in Prayagraj. Umesh Pal was among the key witnesses in the case. Eventually, this testimony became the reason for the Umesh Pal murder. On February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal was attacked in the Dhoomanganj area of Prayagraj. He was returning home. Umesh Pal and two government gunmen deployed for his security were killed in the attack. After the incident, a case was registered against Atiq Ahmed, Ashraf, Shaista Parveen, Asad, and several others on the complaint filed by Umesh Pal's wife, Jaya Pal.

stories.title: MP spurious liquor case:Main accused shot in leg and arrested after firing 3 rounds at police; wanted in case involving 31 deaths
stories.summary: The main accused in the spurious liquor case in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar was arrested on Friday after police shot him in the leg during an exchange of fire in a forest. The accused, Ravi Lakhera, allegedly opened fire at the police team three times near Khaiwaha village in the Baraytha forest area, close to the Uttar Pradesh border. One bullet hit a police vehicle. Police returned fire after Lakhera allegedly refused to stop despite warnings. One bullet hit his left leg, following which he was arrested. Sagar SP Anurag Sujania confirmed the arrest. Lakhera had a ₹20,000 reward on his arrest. Police said two men accompanying him on a motorcycle fled the spot and are being searched for. So far, 31 people have reportedly died after consuming the illicit liquor. Three more patients admitted to Bundelkhand Medical College died on Thursday. However, the administration has officially confirmed 16 deaths. Bulldozers used against illegal structures at three accused’s properties On Thursday, the administration demolished illegal portions of five houses belonging to three accused in the case. The properties included those of accused Manish Lodhi, Karni Sena divisional president Chandrabhan Singh Rajput and Ashish Sahu. Police have so far named 33 people as accused in the case. Of them, 18, including Lakhera, have been arrested. One accused has died and another is undergoing treatment in hospital. Thirteen accused are still absconding. Police say Lakhera was key figure in illicit liquor network According to the police investigation, several people were involved in the operation, from manufacturing the illicit liquor to supplying it to villages. Ravi Lakhera: Alleged mastermind behind liquor production Lakhera is originally from Mahoba in Chhatarpur district but has been living for a long time in the Gangapuram Colony area of Lalitpur, Uttar Pradesh. Police describe him as an inter-state liquor smuggler. Around 25 criminal cases have reportedly been registered against him in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and other places, most of them under the Excise Act. According to police, Lakhera had detailed knowledge of liquor production and the materials used in it. He allegedly arranged the required materials and supplied them to his network, which was involved in preparing illicit liquor. Investigators have described him as a key link and alleged mastermind of the illicit liquor network. He was also in contact with licensed liquor contractor Manish Lodhi, alias Yashwant Singh. Manish Lodhi: Licensed contractor allegedly linked to illicit liquor trade Manish Lodhi, alias Yashwant Singh, was the licensed contractor for a liquor shop in Barethi. Police said he learnt the method of making illicit liquor from Lakhera and allegedly began the illegal business under the cover of his licensed liquor trade. Eleven criminal cases have been registered against Lodhi, including six under the Excise Act. He also owned a bar on Sagar Road in Banda, which was sealed after the case came to light. Chandrabhan Singh Rajput: Alleged role in manufacturing and supply Chandrabhan Singh Rajput, alias Chandu, a resident of Tatarwara, has been accused of playing a key role in the manufacturing and supply network. He is a relative of liquor smuggler Shivanjay Rajput and allegedly came into contact with Manish Lodhi through him. Police said illicit liquor was prepared in Chandu’s maize field. Five criminal cases have been registered against him. Shivanjay Rajput: Alleged role from production to supply Shivanjay Rajput, a resident of Chhapri, was allegedly active in the network. He is related to Chandu and was in contact with Manish Lodhi. Police said Shivanjay, Lodhi and Chandu were involved in supplying the illicit liquor to nearby villages after it was prepared. Spurious allegedly made in a maize field According to police, the illicit liquor was prepared in Chandu’s maize field in Tatarwara around two days before Janmashtami. Police allege that Lakhera and Manish Lodhi provided the materials required to make the liquor. Chandu, Shivanjay and Lodhi then allegedly prepared around 50 boxes of illicit liquor. The liquor was reportedly supplied to nearby villages under the brand name ‘Sagar Gold’ through salesmen. Accused allegedly tried to destroy evidence after deaths began After people started falling ill and deaths were reported following consumption of the liquor, the accused allegedly tried to destroy evidence. Police said around 20-25 boxes of liquor were taken to the field and burnt. Materials used to prepare the liquor were allegedly disposed of in a drain. Police to question Lakhera about source of materials According to investigators, Lakhera played a key role in procuring the materials used to prepare the illicit liquor. Police allege that he and Manish Lodhi arranged items including materials for liquor production, packaging material, sacks, wrappers, labels, stickers, methanol and ethanol, among other supplies. Investigators are now trying to establish where these materials were purchased and how they were transported to Tatarwara. Police said questioning Lakhera and Lodhi could reveal further details about the network and the people involved in procuring and supplying the materials.

stories.title: Clouds over Varanasi, rain likely:Temperature stays at 30°C since morning, Ganga water level stabilises
stories.summary: Once again, the water level of the Ganga has stabilized in Varanasi. Meanwhile, the skies over Varanasi have been cloudy since Friday morning. The temperature was recorded at 30 degrees Celsius at 8 a.m. Winds are blowing at a speed of 14 kilometers per hour. Meanwhile, the difficulties of people living in the areas along the banks of the Ganga and Varuna rivers are increasing. Dark clouds cover the sky Dark clouds have covered the sky in Varanasi since Friday morning. The weather has become pleasant after rain late last night. According to the Meteorological Department, Varanasi will receive intermittent rain today. Meanwhile, the maximum temperature is expected to reach 33 degrees Celsius. Winds are currently blowing at a speed of 14 kilometers per hour, while humidity has been recorded at 79 percent. Rise in Ganga's water level stopped at 8 p.m According to the Central Water Commission, the rise in the Ganga's water level stopped again at 8 p.m. on Thursday. The Ganga is currently flowing at 69.33 meters. The water level remained stable until 8 a.m. Meanwhile, water is still present in several places in the riverside areas, forcing people to leave their homes and live in camps. 877 families affected by the flood According to the district administration, 877 families in Varanasi are currently affected by the floods. These include families affected by both the Varuna and Ganga rivers. They have been accommodated in relief camps. Meanwhile, some people are staying in private rooms they have rented. Due to the rising water levels of the Ganga and Varuna, 24 villages in Varanasi and 16 localities in the urban area are submerged. People are evacuating these areas.

stories.title: DDU to get AI-powered student assistant:Will work 24 hours a day, resolving students’ problems and providing instant answers
stories.summary: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University plans to develop a 24-hour AI-powered student assistant to address students’ academic and administrative needs. Once developed, the system will provide instant answers to common queries related to admissions, fees, examinations, results, certificates and other university services. The facility is proposed under the “Dean, AI Initiatives and Digital Transformation Office” plan put forward by Vice-Chancellor Prof. K.P. Singh. On Thursday (10 Sept), the Vice-Chancellor conducted a detailed review of preparations for “AI Manthan-2.0”. During the meeting, he assessed the action plan being prepared to use artificial intelligence (AI) to provide students with faster, better and more convenient services. All essential information to be brought under one system The proposal also includes a centralised knowledge base containing accurate and updated information from various departments, examination sections, hostels and the finance branch. This will allow students to access essential information from a single platform while improving the speed and transparency of administrative operations. AI facilities to be made student-friendly Vice-Chancellor Prof. K.P. Singh said technology should be used to make processes more convenient for students and improve the university’s overall functioning. He emphasised that all AI-based facilities should be simple, reliable and completely student-friendly. ‘AI Manthan-2.0’ to be held in Kanpur “AI Manthan-2.0” will be held on September 12 and 13, 2026, at Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University (CSJMU), Kanpur, with universities across Uttar Pradesh participating. The Vice-Chancellor directed officials to complete preparations for the event within the stipulated time and ensure that the university’s use of AI remains focused on student welfare and faster operations. He also instructed officials to submit the information sought by Raj Bhavan in an organised manner. IQAC Coordinator Prof. Ajay Singh, DSW Prof. Anubhuti Dubey, the Registrar and several other officials attended the review meeting.

stories.title: Two youths stripped naked and beaten over theft suspicion:Accused of entering house in Lucknow; police act after video surfaces
stories.summary: A case has come to light in Ambergunj under Lucknow’s Saadatganj area, where two youths were allegedly stripped and beaten with sticks after being suspected of theft. The incident reportedly took place after the two youths allegedly entered a house under construction at around 3 am on Tuesday night. According to the allegations, labourers and a mason sleeping at the site heard a noise, caught the two youths and took them to the Balaganj police outpost. It is alleged that when no action was taken there, they were brought back to the construction site and beaten with sticks. Police launched an investigation after a video of the incident surfaced on social media. Saadatganj Police have detained one person and are questioning him. The video has not been independently verified. Youths accused of stealing motor, mobile phone and ₹10,000 According to Yogendra, officer in charge of the Ambergunj outpost, Kuldeep Gupta owns a traders’ shop in the Thakurganj area and is constructing a building in Ambergunj. Only the mason and labourers stay overnight at the construction site. It was alleged that around 3 am on Tuesday (8 Sept), two youths entered the building under construction and stole a motor, a worker’s mobile phone and around ₹10,000 belonging to a mason. The workers and mason woke up after hearing a noise and caught the two youths at the spot. Youths allegedly brought back after police outpost The two youths were reportedly taken to the Balaganj police outpost by Kuldeep Gupta and an acquaintance. It is alleged that the police personnel present there took no action and sent them back. They were then allegedly taken back to the construction site to recover the stolen money and belongings. Video shows youths allegedly being stripped and beaten It is alleged that the two youths were stripped and severely beaten with sticks at the construction site. Someone recorded the incident, and the video later surfaced on social media. In the video, the two youths can allegedly be seen with their hands folded while apologising. One detained, police search for victims Saadatganj Police Station in-charge Santosh Arya said the case is being investigated on the basis of the video. Police are searching for the youths who were allegedly beaten. One person has been detained and is being questioned. Arya said further action would be taken after a written complaint is received.

stories.title: Kanpur millionaire businessman murder:5 reasons suspicion on son deepens; spoke to contract killer 309 times, went with him thrice
stories.summary: In the murder case of Kanpur's millionaire medicine trader Vineet Minocha, following the daughter-in-law Shalu, police suspicion has now deepened towards his son Subrat as well. Investigation has revealed that Subrat spoke to hitman Vishal Gautam on the phone around 309 times in three months. In the 20 days leading up to the murder, Subrat went out thrice with the contract killer Vishal and his wife Shalu. The biggest question is that despite having more than 20 employees at home and in the business, why was Subrat so close to Vishal? Why did Subrat fail to recognise Vishal, who had worked at his firm for 12 years? The first time he was shown the CCTV footage. These links have raised several questions regarding Subrat, the answers to which are now being sought in the investigation. Read the 5 points based on which the police suspect the son's role… 1. Three house helpers, 17 employees, yet why was Vishal so special? In the Vineet Minocha murder case, the police have already sent the murder accused Vishal, Rajkishore, and daughter-in-law Shalu to jail. The details that have emerged from the surveillance cell's investigation are putting the son in the dock as well. Subrat spoke to hitman Vishal Gautam 309 times on the phone over three months. This was despite Vineet having already fired him from his job. Ever since he was caught stealing, Vineet disliked him immensely. During police questioning, Subrat and Shalu stated that Vishal used to assist with household chores. However, three servants, including a maid, work at Subrat's house. Around 17 employees work at his Pharma Traders firm. In such a situation, the question arises as to what kind of bond Subrat shared with the contract killer, such that Subrat would call only Vishal for every task. 2. Subrat had gone with Vishal three times in 20 days DCP West SM Qasim Abidi stated that up until 20 days prior to the murder, Subrat had also gone to several places alongside Vishal and Shalu. He mentioned that to get duplicate keys to the flat made, Shalu, Vishal, and Subrat had gone together to Gumti No. 5. There, Shalu gave Vishal ₹1200 to get the keys made. During this time, Subrat remained seated in the car, while Shalu and Vishal went to the shop. Meanwhile, prior to this, Subrat had also taken Vishal to Parade to take him shopping. There, Shalu had even helped him with making purchases. A few days earlier, Vishal's health had deteriorated; after he remained down with a viral infection for several days without recovery, Vishal's mother had sought Subrat's help. Subrat had then taken him to a doctor for treatment as well. 3. Why did Subrat fail to recognise a servant who had worked for 12 years? Vineet Minocha was murdered at 11:28 pm on the night of 5 September. When the police reached the flat in the early morning hours, the team began examining the CCTV cameras installed at the apartment's entry gate and outside the flat. In this, Vishal and his accomplice Rajkishore were clearly captured entering and exiting the flat. Following this, the police showed the CCTV footage to Subrat to identify the accused, but he refused to recognise them. Upon insistence by the police, Subrat disclosed that the youth seen in the footage was Vishal, who used to work at his firm. Vishal had worked at Subrat's shop located on Birhana Road from 2010 to 2022. Vineet Minocha had sacked him in 2022. The question arises: why did Subrat fail to recognise a youth who had worked at his shop for 12 years? Why was he still in touch with him despite his father having fired him? Meanwhile, Dheeraj Arora, brother of the accused Shalu, stated during a press conference on Thursday that when he brought this up with his sister during a jail visit, she too was astonished as to why her husband had refused to recognise Vishal in the first place. 4. Subrat spoke to the contract killer 25 times in six days After the murder, Subrat attempted to erase the call records from his mobile phone. Certain numbers were discovered in the Call Detail Record (CDR) that were absent from his call history. An investigation by the Surveillance Team of the West Zone revealed that on the day of the murder, Vishal spoke to Shalu on the phone 14 times. Meanwhile, Vishal spoke to Subrat 25 times via WhatsApp calls between 29 August and the day of the incident. When questioned, Subrat stated that due to a lack of network coverage in the flat, he frequently made WhatsApp calls. The investigation disclosed that Shalu had deleted the call history and WhatsApp messages from the day of the incident, whereas Subrat had deleted three call logs. Following his father's murder, upon learning of his wife's involvement in the conspiracy, no significant change was observed in Subrat's demeanor. He offered no reaction after the police disclosure. The investigation has also revealed that Vineet Minocha paid his son a salary of merely ₹40,000 for his expenses. 5. Party was organised by Subrat, bill paid by medical store proprietor On the night of Vineet Minocha's murder, 5 September, his son Subrat and daughter-in-law Shalu attended a couple's kitty party at the Cosmojin Lounge located in Tilak Nagar. That the party was organised by Subrat himself was revealed on Thursday by Shalu's brother Dheeraj and sister Sonia Mehrotra. Thirty-three people associated with the pharmaceutical trade attended the couple's party. On Wednesday, a video of Subrat and Shalu dancing at the party also surfaced. Records from the restaurant revealed that the duo arrived at the party at 10:30 pm itself, whereas the party was scheduled to begin from 11:30 pm. Additionally, their departure from the lounge at 3:00 am has been confirmed. Police investigation and lounge records brought another detail to light: the party bill came to approximately ₹80,000, which was paid by a medical store proprietor. In light of this, the question arises as to under what circumstances Subrat did not make the payment. Police are now preparing to summon the guests who attended the party and the medical store proprietor who settled the bill for questioning.
