stories.title: Couple Cut LA Home Price: Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr. trim ask; $9.95m tag after $550k cut
stories.summary: Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr. have decided to drop the price of their Mandeville Canyon home, now listed at $9.95 million. This price cut comes only three months after the property was first put on the market. The couple bought this family residence in 2013 and is now eager to find a buyer for their beloved Los Angeles home.

stories.title: Trash Talk Nyc Project: 100-day cleanup sparks gardens; neighbours build a movement
stories.summary: David Clarke took it upon himself to clean a neglected block in New York City using simple tools. His shared updates on social media sparked wider community interest, leading to a collaborative effort. He invested his own funds to create gardens in tree beds, inspiring neighbors to participate in maintaining the area. This grassroots initiative revitalized the block and fostered a sense of community pride in public spaces.

AI Stream Sparks Feud: N3on and Sneako trade insults over Kick clone; friendship called fake
stories.summary: Streamers N3on and Sneako have found themselves in a heated public confrontation surrounding the ethics of artificial intelligence. N3on revealed an AI replica to maintain his streaming presence, while Sneako questioned why N3on needed funds trickling in from gambling ventures. As tensions rose, N3on accused Sneako of betrayal for airing their grievances publicly. Their back-and-forth burgeoned into a flurry of personal attacks, igniting further drama for their followers.

Officer asked to show Outlook or Teams as evidence of working: OPT student shares domestic travel experience to New Mexico
Underwater sensors capture porpoises’ rare distress calls off Cornwall
17 pigs rescued before New Zealand island’s feral population was eradicated
Goods train derails in J&K’s Kathua, no injury or damages
Ladakh groups claim breakthrough in talks with MHA on legislative powers
Chen Ziyi Death Details: Mukbang star dies at 24 after health warning; raises concern over extreme eating
stories.summary: Chen Ziyi, known online as Ganfan Yingying, was a 24-year-old Chinese mukbang creator with about 1.2 million followers. She died on August 17, 2026, days after revealing that her potassium level had dropped to 2.3 mmol/L. Chen had spoken about purging after extreme eating sessions. Her parents confirmed her death but did not disclose an official cause.

stories.title: Dan Houser Net Worth In 2026: Rockstar co-founder hits $250m; GTA success fuels fortune
stories.summary: Dan Houser, a co-founder of Rockstar Games, built an impressive $250 million fortune thanks to the immense popularity of games like Grand Theft Auto, which he helped create. After two decades of leading the studio's creative vision, he departed in 2020. His significant investments in real estate highlight his financial success, and with the anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, additional revenue is expected to flow in.

stories.title: Kesha sells Los Angeles mansion for $6.68 million after two years on the market
stories.summary: Kesha has sold her sprawling Los Angeles mansion for $6.68 million, nearly two years after first listing the property. The singer purchased the Mar Vista home for $4.95 million in 2020 and stands to make almost $1.7 million before expenses. The seven-bedroom estate features a pool, rooftop deck, guest house and music room.

stories.title: Sea otters returned to a California estuary; eelgrass expanded 600%, marsh-edge erosion slowed 69%
stories.summary: Sea otters returned to California’s Elkhorn Slough in 1984 when pollution had severely affected its ecosystem. Their recovery triggered changes across the food web, helping eelgrass beds expand by 600%. A later study found marsh-edge erosion slowed by an average of 69%, as otters reduced populations of root-eating crabs.

stories.title: 144-year-old Indiana train depot being restored after decades of abandonment
British actor Noel Clarke, known for 'Doctor Who', charged with 6 sex offences involving 5 women
Raghav Chadha’s Delhi voter registration approved after due process: Poll body
Anthropic researcher backs ex-employee’s AI warning, says human extinction could come within years
Beyond E20? Only flex-fuel vehicles may have the option, indicates adviser
‘Pilot is a good leader’: Channi backs new Punjab Congress in-charge, says appointment brings ‘new hope’
stories.summary: Sachin Pilot's appointment as Punjab Congress in-charge brings new hope to party workers. He is seen as a capable leader who can unite various factions within the state unit. This move aims to strengthen the Congress party's position before the upcoming 2027 Assembly elections. Leaders like Charanjit Singh Channi and Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa welcomed the decision. The party is planning a statewide yatra to revive its organizational activities.

Indian-origin billionaires lead US immigrant rich list: Who are Forbes 2026’s latest entrants?
A couple bought a cabin over Tennessee river which they later protected for the future
Jazz age-era Connecticut inn reopens after $8 million historic restoration
Baba Neem Karoli’s granddaughters claim their ancestral home illegally occupied by trust
Jeremy Corbyn finds buyer for £700,000 North London home after 19 years, nearly doubling 2007 price
stories.summary: Jeremy Corbyn has found a buyer for his three-bedroom Finsbury Park home after 19 years. The former Labour leader bought the North London property for £363,000 in 2007 and initially listed it for £800,000 this year. The house was later reduced to offers over £700,000 and is now under offer, according to reports.

stories.title: Meet Claire Jiang, 18-year-old NJ student diagnosed with arthritis who built a lab model of the disease
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, eighteen-year-old student Claire Jiang claimed seventh place and a generous seventy thousand dollars for her outstanding research. Motivated by her own struggle with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, Jiang developed an innovative laboratory cell model that promises to enhance the testing of new treatments. Her success underscores the vital role of personal experiences in fostering impactful scientific advancements.

stories.title: India considers it a responsibility, not a favour, to provide aid to Sri Lanka as first responder: Rajnath to president Dissanayake
India launches ORV Sagar Manthan, boosting ocean research fleet
Built in 1917, historic 22-bedroom hotel is up for sale
stories.summary: A historic 22-bedroom Palace Hotel in Odessa, Washington, is now for sale. This landmark building, built in 1917, awaits a new owner. The property spans 4,572 square feet and retains original craftsmanship. After years of vacancy, the hotel needs significant updating and restoration. It offers potential for various redevelopment projects and ventures.

stories.title: ‘Wanted to teach him a lesson’: Accused on assault that killed Manipuri musician
stories.summary: Seven men and a juvenile were arrested for the alleged killing of Chongtham Vikram Singh. The accused reportedly assaulted the musician after he objected to noise outside his home. Singh, a musician, died hours after the assault due to internal injuries. Police are investigating all aspects, including a potential racial angle in the incident. The North Eastern Students' Organisation demanded a swift and impartial probe into the matter.

stories.title: Highway 141 takes Missouri family’s 15 acres; how $238,000 offer became $2.1 million
stories.summary: A Missouri family's 15-acre property, bought in 1904, became the centre of a long eminent domain dispute after St. Louis County acquired it for a highway project. A jury valued the land at $1.3 million, while the court added $650,000 in heritage value and interest, taking the judgment to about $2.1 million. The Missouri Supreme Court later upheld the award.

stories.title: Brics summit in Delhi on September 12-13: Agenda, schedule and other details
Centre clears separate engineering cadre for Delhi PWD
stories.summary: The Centre has approved the Delhi government's proposal to create a separate engineering cadre for the Public Works Department (PWD), a move expected to give the capital greater control over its engineering workforce and help speed up infrastructure projects.

stories.title: MCD demolished 34 structures, sealed 17; over 1,200 PG buildings surveyed
stories.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has sealed seventeen properties and conducted thirty-four demolitions. This action follows a building collapse which tragically killed seven occupants. Authorities are now assessing paying guest accommodations for structural safety concerns. Over twelve hundred buildings are being evaluated for potential vulnerabilities and repairs. The civic body aims to complete this crucial survey by September tenth.

stories.title: ABVP asks PG residents to flag safety gaps after Satya Niketan tragedy
Trump gives Natalie Harp, 2 aides $45,000 each: Why cash gifts are under scrutiny
Ajit Bharti moves Delhi high court against trial court order denying anticipatory bail in SC/ST act case
stories.summary: The trial court had declined Bharti's plea after holding that the material placed on record prima facie disclosed the ingredients of an offence under Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

stories.title: Helsinki recovers 90% of data centre heat to warm 28,000 apartments
'Punjab Dalits, remain vigilant': Rahul demands AAP finance min's resignation over Gulzar Singh's suicide
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has called for the resignation of Punjab minister Harpal Singh Cheema amidst ongoing concerns surrounding the death of Gulzar Singh. The Congress leader emphasized the need for a thorough investigation and cautioned Dalit communities about the potential misuse of power by the AAP government. Family members of Gulzar Singh have accused officials of harassment and making casteist remarks following their inquiries.

stories.title: Couple bought a broken Eichler home; now it’s worth $2.75 million
stories.summary: A magnificent example of midcentury modern architecture, this rare 1971 Eichler home in San Anselmo is listed at $2.75 million. Boasting four bedrooms, it has been tastefully renovated since its acquisition in 2015, showcasing an inviting indoor-outdoor aesthetic, a contemporary kitchen, and a sparkling pool. This home blends vibrant living spaces, making it perfect for families and older adults seeking style and comfort.

stories.title: ‘Making memes’: P Chidambaram says Gen Z is having last laugh over PM Modi’s ‘naraaz fufa’ jibe
stories.summary: Congress leader P Chidambaram proudly embraced the 'Dimagi Naxal' label given by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He also dismissed the 'Naraaz Fufa' remark as meaningless and lacking substance. Chidambaram noted that these comments have sparked widespread discussion and memes online. Prime Minister Modi had urged identifying and isolating those with an ideological Naxal mindset. The exchange highlights ongoing political sparring between the BJP and Congress parties.

stories.title: Colorado man challenges drilling rights beneath his mountain as 400,000 acres head to lease sales
stories.summary: A Colorado landowner and Desert Storm veteran is continuing his legal fight against oil and gas drilling rights beneath Baker’s Peak after the Bureau of Land Management rejected his protest. His appeal comes as the BLM prepares to offer more than 400,000 acres of Colorado land for drilling across six lease sales through December 2026.

Mahmood Farooqui on Storytelling, Survival and the Human Cost of Imprisonment
Meet 22-year-old Utah woman with Down syndrome who became a certified fitness instructor
stories.summary: Aubry Allbridge, 22, has become a certified UpBeat Barre fitness instructor and led her first class with 60 people. She hopes to make everyone feel included while turning her passion for fitness into a full-time job.

stories.title: 10,000 homes were demolished to build world’s heaviest building in Romania; the story behind it
stories.summary: Bucharest’s grand Palace of the Parliament, commissioned by dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu, looms large as a testament to an ambitious and controversial regime. The construction, initiated in 1984, involved the demolition of historic districts, displacing tens of thousands of citizens. Notably, it is the heaviest administrative building worldwide, although much of it remains unoccupied. The colossal structure's fate is precarious as it continues to sink slightly each year.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Vijay-led TVK alliance gets official name; Mayawati puts condition on nephew's party role & more
stories.summary: Vijay has named his new alliance with Congress and other parties the "Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance". Mayawati stated Akash Anand can return to party roles if his father-in-law quits politics. Philippines defence chief rebuked China over its rejection of the South China Sea arbitration ruling. The Supreme Court mentioned all are treated equally after a plea for an early hearing.

stories.title: ‘They want to make CPM a culprit’: Vijayan accuses ED of political targeting over CMRL case
Colorado family protects 684-acre ranch after 90 years; old cabin was ranger post
Vijay-led TVK alliance officially named 'Secular Social Justice Victory Front'
Indian-origin couple donates $20 million to US university to set up AI, advanced analytics college; institute to be named after them
'All treated equally': SC on complainant's 'VVIP' charge against Rahul Gandhi
Paramount’s 2,700-acre film ranch rebuilt after 2018 wildfire destroyed most of it
stories.summary: Paramount Ranch in California, a historic Hollywood filming site, is being rebuilt nearly eight years after the 2018 Woolsey Fire destroyed most of its buildings and sets. The National Park Service is spending $26 million on the project, with new fire-safe structures being built in the footprints of historic Paramount-era buildings. The ranch is expected to reopen in 2027.

stories.title: Indian family deported from Canada after asylum claim fails: 'When Canada needed Harish, he was essential'
New satellite images show major construction surge at Iran’s Pickaxe nuke site
stories.summary: Construction activity has significantly increased at Iran's underground Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site this year. The United States is developing new weapons to target deeply buried facilities. President Trump has repeatedly threatened strikes on the heavily fortified Iranian location. The US military maintains operational plans for potential strikes against the site. This renewed scrutiny occurs as the wider US-Iran conflict intensifies.

stories.title: Brics Summit: Delhi on high alert with 4,800 cops, 35+ roads face curbs
stories.summary: As Delhi gears up for the 18th Brics Summit from September 11 to 13, heightened security protocols have been put in place. Over 4,800 traffic police will oversee the movements of VVIPs and manage traffic diversions. This summit, held at Bharat Mandapam, celebrates two decades of Brics and welcomes foreign leaders and dignitaries from its newly expanded eleven-member coalition.

stories.title: Retired 40-metre dredger sunk off Adelaide to create new artificial reef
stories.summary: South Australia has sunk the 40-metre MV Andrew Wilson six kilometres off Brighton to create an artificial reef. The vessel now rests 20 metres underwater and forms part of a $165 million algal-bloom recovery effort. Fishing is banned within 200 metres of the wreck for 12 months to help local fish stocks recover.

stories.title: This Hawaii startup is making boats from volcanic rock for the military
'Are they adopting Talibanism? 'Satheesan hits back at BJP over action on journalist
Meet the scientist who helped reveal Costa Rica’s mysterious ghost shark
Alaska saw 30,000 ship arrivals in 11 years; their hulls created a hidden invasive species risk
stories.summary: Researchers found that nearly 30,000 commercial vessel arrivals brought 430 sq km of submerged surface area to Alaska between 2012 and 2022. The study says this surface can carry marine organisms through biofouling. Passenger vessels accounted for more than half of the total area, while warming waters and increased Arctic shipping could raise the risk of non-indigenous species reaching Alaska.

stories.title: Britain’s turtle doves rebound after 98% decline as 30 birds are released
‘Unfounded accusations’: China rejects US claims of 'malicious' AI distillation by its firms
SIR row: No notice issued to Prof CNR Rao over name discrepancy, says Bengaluru official
Zuckerberg and Chan gave $4m to save a 600-year-old fishpond for the community
Centre to challenge Allahabad HC order quashing student activist's NSA detention
Meet Franklin Howley-Dumit Serulle, whose online insect photo helped reveal a new hoverfly
stories.summary: An amateur naturalist's photograph on iNaturalist helped scientists identify a new hoverfly species. Researchers later found a specimen in Valle Nuevo National Park, confirming the discovery. This new species, Monoceromyia ndidiae, was formally described after laboratory analysis. The discovery highlights how amateur observations contribute to understanding biodiversity. This finding earned the Swiss Systematics Society’s New Species of the Year 2026 title.

stories.title: Nepal’s flood bill could hit $5 billion. Where will the money come from?
stories.summary: Following the catastrophic floods, Nepal is staring down an enormous reconstruction cost running into billions. To restore infrastructure and homes effectively, both local resources and international assistance will play pivotal roles. The nation is actively pursuing funding opportunities with development banks and climate finance, emphasizing the importance of resilient rebuilding strategies for securing its long-term future.

stories.title: ‘Civilisational twins’: Rajnath Singh meets Sri Lankan president, steps up India’s defence ties with Colombo
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo. They discussed multifaceted partnerships and regional safety, security, peace, and prosperity. Sri Lanka reiterated its commitment to India's security interests and acknowledged India's assistance. Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey Bridges constructed by Indian defence forces. Memorandums of understanding were exchanged to boost defence cooperation between the two nations.

stories.title: Dutch scientists turn office urine into electricity, nutrients and potentially hydrogen
stories.summary: Men in a Dutch office toilet became a small power station using a dedicated urinal. This rig extracted phosphate and ammonia while generating electricity for electric cars. Bacteria break down organic matter in urine, transferring electrons to electrodes for current production. Separately collected urine is a promising feedstock for these bio-electrochemical treatment systems. Research shows urine can be a valuable source for fertilizer and hydrogen gas production.

stories.title: In 2023, LA storms refilled shallow aquifers and reservoirs, but deep groundwater recovered only 25%
stories.summary: In 2023, record-setting storms brought a much-needed boost to Los Angeles's reservoirs and shallow groundwater levels. Yet, deeper aquifers, specifically those lying beneath fifty meters, showed only a slight recovery post-wet season, with just twenty-five percent of lost groundwater replenished. This highlights a crucial disparity; improvements in surface water do not mirror the health of underground reservoirs, a consequence of prolonged drought and aggressive water extraction.

stories.title: ‘South Park’ becomes ‘South America’ in Trump-inspired satirical jab
Before the White House, Carter was a farm boy; his home is now a park
stories.summary: The childhood farm of Jimmy Carter in Archery, Georgia, has been transformed into a historical park to preserve the essence of his early years. This site captures the rural environment and structures that influenced his formative life, where young Jimmy learned the value of hard work through various farm tasks. It was officially designated as part of the National Historical Park in 2000, celebrating his pre-political journey.

stories.title: 17 waste materials tested to make stronger, lower-carbon cement building products
stories.summary: A James Dyson Award project explores using waste for construction materials. Recycled aggregates like eggshells and glass replace conventional materials in cement. This approach reduces reliance on newly extracted natural resources. The project aims to create thinner, stronger cement boards and tiles. Further testing will assess durability and recycling potential for these innovative products.

stories.title: West Bank sanction row: Israel bars 12 British MPs from entering country
Human rights organisations condemn 'racist murder' of Manipuri singer Chongtham Vikram in Delhi
stories.summary: Following the shocking death of a Manipuri music teacher in Delhi, civil society groups have voiced their outrage and called for an in-depth investigation into possible racial motives for the crime. The FIR lodged incorporates serious allegations of group murder based on racial grounds. Advocates pointed out the government’s failure to implement previous recommendations aimed at combating racial biases against Northeast residents.

stories.title: In 2015, Canada sank a 113m warship off British Columbia; 170+ species lived on it by 2020
stories.summary: A former Canadian warship, HMCS Annapolis, now serves as an artificial reef. This vessel was deliberately sunk off British Columbia in 2015. Over five years, more than 170 marine species colonized the sunken ship. The artificial reef provides crucial habitat for various marine organisms. This project demonstrates the ecological value of prepared underwater structures.

stories.title: California cleared 900,000 lbs of debris, but left old telephone poles for purple martins to nest
stories.summary: California crews removed more than 900,000 pounds of human debris while restoring about 40 acres at Sierra Azul Open Space Preserve. They also removed hazardous materials and old septic systems. Some telephone poles were left standing because purple martins use them for nesting. The birds were once thought to have disappeared from Santa Clara County.

stories.title: 'Poster-boy actions': Vijay Mallya's message to those calling him 'bhagoda'
stories.summary: Vijay Mallya has publicly declared that he is legally prevented from leaving the United Kingdom, contending that the Indian government's approach to his situation is unfair. He emphasised that more than fourteen thousand crore rupees have been recovered from him and questioned his ongoing designation as a fraudster while his assets remain inaccessible. The Indian government continues to assert its dedication to extraditing economic offenders.

stories.title: Brazil restored cattle land with native trees; tapirs returned after 100 years
Australian space firms seek deeper India partnerships
stories.summary: An Australian space delegation explored commercial partnerships with Indian firms at Bengaluru Space Expo 2026. Australian companies showcased diverse capabilities complementing India's growing space ecosystem. LatConnect 60 and NewSpace India Limited will access ground-station infrastructure for mission operations. Universities and industry associations intend to collaborate on research and education initiatives. Several Australian firms are advancing agreements for spaceport services and payload recovery.

stories.title: 'Allies should stand with us': Congress calls out Abdullahs after full version of Vande Mataram played
Scientists transform coffee waste into a material that makes concrete stronger by 29%
stories.summary: Researchers transformed used coffee grounds into a valuable construction material. Pyrolysis converted the grounds into biochar, which improved concrete's compressive strength. Replacing fifteen percent of sand with biochar increased concrete strength by nearly thirty percent. This process reduces waste and the need for natural construction resources. Further laboratory testing is needed before widespread commercial application.

stories.title: NIA has not dropped UAPA probe against US citizen VanDyke and other accused: Report
California garbage collector turns trash into a hillside home
Scientists image immune cells without dyes, detecting activation with 94% accuracy in 2 hours
stories.summary: A groundbreaking method has been unveiled by scientists that allows for the natural reading of immune cell data. This approach entails analyzing light emitted from molecules in immune cells, successfully distinguishing between activated and resting states with remarkable precision. By evaluating metabolism at the single-cell level without additional dyes, this technique promises to enhance our understanding of immune cell functionality and health.

stories.title: 'Punjabis don't like politics over dead': CM Mann counters Rahul over Gulzar Singh's suicide
George Harrison revived a forgotten garden and Olivia kept his dream alive
stories.summary: George Harrison purchased Friar Park in 1970 and began restoring its neglected Victorian gardens. He cleared overgrown vegetation and repaired damaged features, making gardening a family activity. After Harrison's death, Olivia Harrison continued preserving the estate's unique character and elaborate topiary. Today, Friar Park's gardens showcase over 160 restored topiary specimens.

stories.title: Volunteers removed 100,000 sea urchins in Norway; kelp and fish nurseries return
stories.summary: Nearly 100,000 sea urchins have been removed from three northern Norway sites by almost 500 volunteers since 2024. The effort has helped kelp and seaweeds return to previously barren seabeds, creating nursery habitat for fish and supporting marine biodiversity. Continued monitoring aims to ensure the underwater forests can recover and persist.

stories.title: Caught on cam: Strike hits close to reporter live on air in Lebanon
In 2023, Australia paved two suburban roads with 135,000 recycled coffee cups and glass bottles, cutting the asphalt’s carbon footprint by 24%
stories.summary: Australia is embracing sustainability by turning discarded coffee cups into road materials. In Penrith, New South Wales, a groundbreaking project resurfaced local roads with a recycled asphalt mixture, incorporating approximately 135,000 coffee cups and countless glass bottles. This innovative use of recycled content has led to a significant twenty-four percent decrease in carbon emissions from the road surface, exemplifying a circular economy that creatively repurposes waste into valuable resources.

stories.title: He spent thirty years transforming his 150-acre property into a wetland, now the former AP biology teacher is creating 'bio supermarkets' for wildlife
stories.summary: A former teacher is restoring Minnesota wetlands on his property. He has spent thirty years transforming his land back to its natural state. This restoration effort aims to combat significant wetland loss across the state. Wetlands provide vital ecological services and support biodiversity. His work is supported by the US Fish and Wildlife Service.

stories.title: Carl Sandburg bought 245-acre estate for wife's goat farm; it became a poet's NPS site
In 1987, Kansas brought bisons back to Konza Prairie; 29 yrs later, native plant richness rose 103%
stories.summary: In 1987, 30 bison were brought back to Kansas’ Konza Prairie as part of a long-term study of grassland ecology. Over the next 29 years, researchers found that bison grazing was linked to a major rise in native plant diversity. Native species richness increased by 103% locally and 86% across catchments, with the gains also recovering after a severe drought.

stories.title: Swiss entrepreneur is drilling the Alps to make 20 mega-bunkers for the super-rich, here's why
stories.summary: Swiss entrepreneur Thomas Gasser is constructing twenty underground mega bunkers deep within Alpine rocks. These secure vaults will safeguard the valuable assets of the world's wealthiest individuals. Each bunker offers a ninety-nine-year lease, with prices beginning at one million Swiss francs. The complex, located near Lungern, is scheduled to open next year after extensive construction. This project aims to provide unparalleled security for art, gold, and other precious possessions.

BJP announces month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to mark PM Modi’s 25 years in public service

Why Vijay's gold ring scheme may miss its September 15 launch
stories.summary: In a surprising move, Tamil Nadu's chief minister has chosen to delay the launch of a gold ring initiative aimed at welcoming newborns. With a pivotal trip to London on the horizon for talks with European industrialists, he underscores the need for fresh investments. Before his departure, he will also oversee important strategy sessions to solidify alliances and boost Tamil Nadu's economic prospects.

Punjab extends cleanliness campaign 2.0 till Sept 12 with 5,000 complaints resolved
stories.summary: The campaign, launched on August 29 across all 166 Urban Local Bodies, including 14 municipal corporations and 152 municipal councils and nagar panchayats, has received 6,459 complaints through the M-Seva app.

stories.title: Researchers turn water-treatment waste into a filter that removes up to 97.1% of microplastics
stories.summary: Researchers are investigating a new method to filter microplastics from water. This approach uses waste generated during water treatment as a filtering material. Tests show this repurposed waste achieved significant microplastic removal efficiencies. The innovative strategy tackles two environmental issues simultaneously. This circular approach could enhance water purification processes in the future.

stories.title: Nearly 4,000 NYC students planted 100,000 plus beachgrass stalks to rebuild dunes and curb flooding
stories.summary: The National Wildlife Federation’s Resilient Schools and Communities programme has brought nearly 4,000 New York City public school students together to restore coastal dunes at Coney Island Creek Park. Since 2022, students, teachers and community members have planted more than 100,000 American beachgrass culms across 2.25 acres. The project aims to stabilise dunes, reduce erosion and build flood protection for more than 50,000 people living near the park.

stories.title: CM Yogi highlights state's textile heritage, industrial potential at UP Textile Conclave in Lucknow
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday highlighted the state's rich textile heritage and industrial potential, saying Uttar Pradesh has skilled manpower, a large market, industry, entrepreneurship and the world's youngest workforce.

stories.title: 240-million-year-old lost fossil revealed a new reptile related to dinosaurs and crocodiles
stories.summary: The discovery of Silescelida acristata, a fossil unearthed in Brazil, provides crucial insights into the origins of early archosauriform reptiles. This remarkable creature thrived at a pivotal time, just before the dawn of dinosaurs. While only partial remains were found, its distinctive bone structures set it apart from contemporaneous Triassic reptiles. Phylogenetic studies classify Silescelida as an early variant of eucrocopodan archosauriforms.

stories.title: The ‘veg-only’ gatekeepers of urban housing in India
stories.summary: From brokers who pre-filter buyers to societies that quietly restrict sales, food rules can shape who gets access to a home — and at what cost

Toxic air after 9/11: Mamdani releases documents showing how New Yorkers were misled
stories.summary: In a significant move, New York City disclosed withheld documents on air quality after 9/11, suggesting that officials may have misrepresented the dangers present post-collapse of the Twin Towers. A memo warned of potential lawsuits for toxic exposure and city liability concerns. There were also fears about asbestos levels and negative public response. This revelation follows a legal challenge from the advocacy group 9/11 Health Watch.

'Festivals are inclusive': Amruta Fadnavis opposes VHP call to bar Muslims from Navratri events
Thousands protest in Germany as far-right AfD eyes first state government since the Nazi Party
Roman cemetery dig reveals Stone Age man buried with 2 skulls, 42 teeth and an axe
stories.summary: In a startling archaeological find, researchers uncovered a burial site dating back to the Stone Age, predating nearby Roman graves by thousands of years. The grave contained a battle axe, striking amber beads, and a unique necklace fashioned from the teeth of 42 animals. Additionally, two human skulls were discovered alongside the skeleton, offering rare insights into the rituals and practices of ancient communities.

stories.title: Napa Art Center Land Deal: di Rosa eases 162 acres into trust; future trail to Milliken Peak
stories.summary: A landmark conservation deal aims to safeguard a large portion of the di Rosa Center's Napa Valley landscape. Effectively shielding about 75% of the estate from future privatization, this agreement also secures vital financial resources for the center's ongoing operations. Exciting plans include a new public trail that will reach the summit of Milliken Peak, fostering an ideal mix of accessibility and artistic preservation.

stories.title: Indians trust the classroom, see better opportunities abroad: Global survey
stories.summary: Across 16 G20 countries covered by an Ipsos survey, Indians are unusually bullish about schools, degrees and the future of the young. Yet 76% say young people would have better opportunities abroad, pointing to a striking gap between faith in education and confidence in opportunity at home.

Motorcyclist Startles IRL Stream: Security rushes in on La Piquiña; viewers debate robbery risk
stories.summary: Kick streamer La Piquiña experienced a frightening moment while livestreaming from the streets of Colombia at night. A motorcyclist suddenly approached his outdoor desktop setup, prompting concerns that a robbery could be underway. His nearby security team quickly intervened, and the rider left before the situation escalated. The encounter later sparked debate online, with fans praising the guards while others questioned the safety of streaming from an exposed public location after dark.

stories.title: Building collapses to fires, 33k died in 5 years from 2020
AI Streamer Feud Escalates: N3on and Sneako trade insults; friendship rift over public criticism
stories.summary: N3on and Sneako’s friendship has taken a dramatic turn after Sneako publicly criticized N3on’s controversial AI streamer project. N3on, who announced an AI version of himself would stream 24/7 on Kick, accused Sneako of being disloyal and seeking views instead of addressing concerns privately. Sneako fired back with personal insults, while N3on defended the project and their friendship. The feud later intensified as both streamers continued trading jabs online.

stories.title: BJP got Rs 1,473 crore to fight Bengal, Assam, 3 other assembly polls
Sri Lanka a close friend, India stands by it: Rajnath Singh
Absorbing unqualified pvt school teachers will ruin students: Supreme Court
Costa Rica maps nearly 500 dominant tree species to protect forest biodiversity
stories.summary: Researchers mapped Costa Rica's diverse forest ecosystems by analyzing tree species composition. Satellite observations and environmental data helped create a national forest map. This map distinguishes forest types, including secondary forests, across varied landscapes. The findings highlight the importance of dominant tree species for understanding forest function. Better field inventories are still needed to improve future forest mapping efforts.

NIA drops UAPA against American, 6 Ukrainians held in 'terror link' case
US strikes Iranian tankers near Kharg Island; Tehran threatens Gulf oil vessels
Endangered Sawfish-Turtle Photo Wins Australia’s Top Nature Prize
North Florida family protects 816 acres while keeping land available for farming
US sanctions all remaining Iranian airlines, with 27 carriers hit in fresh action
Copenhagen’s £200m underground museum opens in 2027 with dinosaurs, 14m specimens and eight galleries
stories.summary: Copenhagen’s new £200 million Natural History Museum will open on March 6, 2027, featuring eight immersive underground galleries and a collection of 14 million specimens. Visitors can explore dinosaur skeletons, 3D exhibits and the spectacular Ocean Hall, as the museum combines historic Botanical Garden buildings with striking new underground architecture inspired by nature.

Klamath River salmon reclaim 88% of historic range after dams are removed
Strategic autonomy in motion as India hosts Brics summit

1st Corps Commander-level India-China talks in eastern sector held over 2 days: MEA; says ties gradually moving in positive direction
Just 1% of asylum seekers in UK genuine, insider says, as UN blasts Britain for allowing bogus claims
Antarctica gained 695 billion tons in 2021-23 as tropical warmth drove heavy snowfall
stories.summary: Between 2021 and 2023, Antarctica experienced a notable gain in ice mass, primarily driven by exceptional snowfall in East Antarctica. This unusual occurrence, influenced by warmer tropical ocean temperatures, caused atmospheric disturbances that transported moisture southward. Although this gain temporarily countered ongoing ice loss in other regions, it does not signify a change in Antarctica's long-term trend of declining ice mass.

stories.title: AI predicts fusion plasma instability 200 ms early, stops it in time
Artist puts Kashmiri poet Lal Ded's mysticism on Pashmina
Ladakh's tourist footfall continues rising; August sees most foreign visitors
Canadian couple donate 187-acre Ontario island sanctuary after protecting its wildlife for 36 years
stories.summary: Jim and Anne Purvis bought 187.4 acres on Ontario’s Wilson Island in 1989 and spent 36 years protecting the land as a family sanctuary. They have now donated the property to the Northumberland Land Trust, ensuring its forests, wetlands, grasslands and habitats for species at risk remain protected as a permanent nature reserve.

stories.title: Village head's appeal drove Ladakh LG's initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation
NCPCR summons Meta India head over alleged child abuse ads
stories.summary: The NCPCR has summoned Meta India's managing director regarding ads linked to child exploitation. This action follows a BBC Eye report and a formal inquiry into Meta's systems. The commission will examine Meta India's role in the s' appearance. The inquiry considers stringent provisions under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Meta stated it has zero tolerance for child exploitation and removed many suspicious accounts.

stories.title: Kharge ‘purification’ row escalates as Congress MPs demand FIR from Delhi Police
US Democrat urges House Speaker to sue Trump admin over triumphal arch, says Congress never approved funds
Meet Rachel Chen, 18, who won $100K for her breakthrough quantum math research using simple diagrams
stories.summary: Rachel Chen, an 18-year-old Los Angeles student, won $100,000 at the Regeneron Science Talent Search for expanding a 1997 mathematical idea involving Temperley-Lieb diagrams. Her research offers a visual way to describe complex quantum particle systems and spin representations, potentially helping researchers better understand connections between different quantum-mechanical states.

NHRC seeks report on hostel facilities for DU students from Delhi chief secretary, UGC
Expelled Bihar Congress functionaries protest outside party office, seek meeting with Rahul
In 1973, Montana released a gall fly to control spotted knapweed; decades later...
stories.summary: Controlling invasive spotted knapweed biologically has initiated an unexpected ecological chain reaction. Gall flies, introduced as a control measure, have turned into a vital winter food source for deer mice, causing a surge in their populations and an uptick in hantavirus spread. Areas dense with knapweed report more infected mice than those with native grasslands.

stories.title: She bought a Maine island to stop clear-cutting; 90 years after Audubon opened its first camp there
stories.summary: Hog Island Audubon Camp marks an impressive ninety years of promoting environmental education and research. Located in Maine, this island was rescued from deforestation by environmentalists Millicent Todd Bingham and Mabel Loomis Todd. The camp is also the birthplace of Project Puffin, which successfully revitalized seabird numbers. Today, it remains a vital training ground for future scientists, educators, and artists, with its influence extending to bird conservation throughout North America.

stories.title: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta found hanging at Noida residence, dies by suicide
Lindsay Clancy murder case: Lawyer asks Trump to pardon Massachusetts mother after mistrial
Scientists seeded clouds over China’s Muz Taw Glacier; fresh snow cut ice loss by 14% to 17%
stories.summary: Scientists tested cloud seeding over China’s Muz Taw Glacier in 2018 to create artificial snowfall and slow ice loss. The experiment used silver iodide generators to encourage snow formation. Researchers found that fresh snow made the glacier surface brighter and reduced the amount of ice lost over a short period. However, they said the results are preliminary and need further testing.

stories.title: Andrew Flintoff lists his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion, bought from Phil Neville in 2021
stories.summary: England cricket legend Andrew Flintoff has put his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion on the market, four years after his life-changing Top Gear car crash. Bought from former Manchester United star Phil Neville in 2021, the 10,000 sq ft luxury property features six bedrooms, six bathrooms, four floors, a pool, gym, cinema and games room.

stories.title: Inside a $29M California mansion no one has ever lived in
stories.summary: A French-style manor in Rancho Santa Fe is now for sale at $29 million. This newly built home features antique materials and custom artisan craftsmanship throughout. The expansive residence includes a main house and a separate guest house on 3.66 acres. It boasts a zero-edge pool, gardens, and breathtaking views from its terraces. The manor comes fully furnished with art and antiques, ready for immediate occupancy.

stories.title: Meet Anvith, Dubai student who watched his brother’s school commute and built a free carpool service
stories.summary: In a bid to tackle traffic congestion, a student from Dubai has launched a unique carpooling website that connects commuters with similar routes through sophisticated algorithmic matching. Community Carpool now boasts over a thousand registered users in Dubai, ensuring user privacy by discreetly matching individuals until they agree to share rides. Notably, a local property developer has embraced this platform for its workforce, facilitating its growth.

stories.title: An 81-year-old US homeowner faced a $17,827.96 lien after a burst-pipe insurance claim was denied
stories.summary: Tyler Perry has made headlines with his philanthropic intervention for an elderly homeowner in Illinois. With her insurance company, Allstate, refusing to cover the damages from burst pipes, she faced the threat of foreclosure. Perry's willingness to pay off a significant property lien and provide additional financial support has saved her from losing her home and brightened her future.

stories.title: Twin girls once given less than 10% chance of survival are now ready for their first day of school
stories.summary: Ruby and Scarlett were given less than a 10% chance of survival after being diagnosed with Twin-to-Twin Transfusion Syndrome at 16 weeks. Following high-risk surgery, premature birth and serious health complications, the twins spent 300 days in hospital. Now, their mother Hanna Brameld is celebrating as her daughters prepare for their first day of school.

stories.title: Glowworms return to Yorkshire after 100 years, with first glowing females bred in a Bristol shed
stories.summary: Glowworms have reappeared at Nosterfield nature reserve after a century-long absence. Conservation efforts, which began with larvae raised in a garden shed, show early success. Volunteers observed up to twelve glowing females this summer, indicating survival and development. Historical records confirm glowworms were once abundant in the area before their disappearance. Further releases of captive-reared larvae are planned for later this year.

stories.title: In 2023, an Australian cattle station sold for $40 million for a carbon project; three years later...
stories.summary: After a disappointing turn of events, Benmara Station, a prominent cattle property in Australia, was sold for A$26 million, significantly lower than its original price of A$40 million. This decline resulted from the cancellation of an ambitious environmental project related to carbon farming, emphasizing traditional pastoral values instead of its former carbon potential as regulatory challenges mounted.

stories.title: Does AfD's big win in Germany signal a 'far right' uprising in Europe?
stories.summary: Many years ago, Otto von Bismarck observed that politics was “the art of the possible”. The modern European establishment appears to have inverted the Iron Chancellor’s maxim. Politics has increasingly become the art of explaining to voters why what they want is impossible, irresponsible, xenophobic, Islamophobic, nativist or, inevitably, far right. And made it impossible to vote for the so-called far-right party that’s actually willing to admit there’s a problem.

stories.title: Satya Niketan building collapse: MCD crackdown begins across Delhi; 24 properties demolished, 7 sealed
Kentfield Home Hits Market: Long-held 1966 Laurel Grove house lists at $3.295m; charter club perk included
stories.summary: Now available on the market is a charming four-bedroom house in Kentfield, originally constructed in 1966. This midcentury gem has been tastefully renovated, featuring an expansive 2,784 square feet of living area set on a spacious lot. With modernized interiors and exclusive access to a local club, this well-established residence awaits its new owner after nearly sixty years of cherished memories.

stories.title: Cheque-bounce case: Actor Rajpal Yadav seeks exemption from surrender, SC says deposit Rs 5 cr first
'Releasing 6,000 cusecs is impossible': Karnataka on Cauvery water order, may move Supreme Court
stories.summary: Karnataka may approach the Supreme Court regarding water release orders. The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee recommended releasing 6,000 cusecs daily. This recommendation was upheld by the Cauvery Water Management Authority. Karnataka officials cited declining water inflows and drinking water needs. The state government is seriously considering filing a petition soon.

stories.title: Panama City school left empty for years is getting a second life
stories.summary: The former Panama City Grammar School will undergo redevelopment into apartments and townhomes. City officials have cleared financial hurdles, waiving fines and providing a grant for the project. Developer Zachary Seymour will purchase the property and begin necessary structural repairs. The agreement mandates completion of critical repairs within one year to preserve the historic structure. Local leaders emphasize saving heritage, especially after Hurricane Michael's significant damage.

stories.title: No rooms, Rs 2.3 lakh a night: BRICS Summit sends Delhi hotel rates soaring
1,800 years ago, a Roman household decorated floor with cat and dog; archaeologists uncover mosaic
stories.summary: Archaeologists in Turkey have uncovered a colourful Roman-era mosaic dating back around 1,800 years. Found inside a villa at ancient Adramytteion, the mosaic features 15 panels showing animals and mythological figures. Two animals are named in Greek: a cat called Emerald and a dog called Ocean.

stories.title: NCPCR summons Meta India chief over alleged child sexual abuse material ads
ABVP seeks MCD chief’s exit, PG audits after Satya Niketan tragedy
stories.summary: The ABVP has demanded safety audits for paying guest accommodations in student areas. They also called for the Municipal Corporation of Delhi commissioner's resignation following a recent tragedy. Thousands of students participated in a march to highlight safety concerns and hostel shortages. The organization urged Delhi University to build more hostels for students. They seek immediate action and structural checks on unsafe accommodations.

stories.title: India, China hold first high-level military flag talks in Arunachal amid LAC tensions
stories.summary: The meeting followed understandings reached during the Special Representatives dialogue between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The talks are part of efforts by the two countries to maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control and gradually improve bilateral ties. MEA spokesperson said meeting was held at Wacha on the Indian side on September 6 and at Damai on the Chinese side on September 7.

stories.title: Channi vs Warring: Why Sachin Pilot may be Congress's best bet in Punjab
stories.summary: In a strategic move to mend internal discord, Congress appointed Sachin Pilot to lead efforts in Punjab, following Bhupesh Baghel's ousting due to his inability to unify the Channi and Warring factions. With a wealth of experience from Rajasthan, Pilot faces the challenging task of overcoming anti-incumbency against the ruling AAP government. His triumph here may pave the way for a more significant role back in Rajasthan.

stories.title: 'Not intended to hurt anyone': CM Vijay clarifies gesture in TN assembly after DMK protest
California town first sold on eBay in 2002, is back on market again
stories.summary: Bridgeville, an 80-acre town in Northern California, made history in 2002 as the first town to be listed on eBay. The auction drew 250 bids, with the highest reaching $1.77 million, but the winner backed out. After several owners and failed plans, the town is set to return to the market this September, with its current owners hoping for someone who can help the community flourish.

stories.title: As El Niño intensifies, scientists in Chile are making a vulnerable penguin species wear copper vests, here's why
stories.summary: In an inspiring initiative, Chilean researchers are designing specialized vests for injured penguins, incorporating copper and zinc to expedite healing. This groundbreaking effort is focused on supporting the struggling Humboldt penguin population by preventing further injury while enhancing recovery. The vests draw on effective treatments that have proven successful for domestic animals, showcasing a creative blend of technology and compassion.

stories.title: 4 members of Florida family missing after plane vanishes en route from Bahamas to Miami
In 1980, conservationists began eradicating feral sheep to restore California's Santa Cruz Island
stories.summary: Conservationists undertook a significant effort to remove feral sheep from Santa Cruz Island, aiming to revive its delicate ecosystem. Over seven years, thousands of these sheep were eliminated, risking the extinction of a unique heritage breed. To counter this, twelve lambs were rescued to spearhead a captive breeding initiative on the mainland, ensuring the preservation of a rare genetic lineage and honoring California's rich agricultural heritage.

stories.title: Digital asset firms seek sovereign funds’ backing at Delhi meet
'Poisonous': Rahul Gandhi targets 'India's most corrupt' MP govt over liquor deaths

Hidden gut bacteria populations linked to ageing, cancer and type 2 diabetes may spread worldwide
stories.summary: Scientists led by the University of Vienna have found hidden populations within common gut bacteria, some of which are linked to ageing, colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease and type 2 diabetes. The study also found evidence that certain bacterial populations can spread between people and across continents within a few decades, suggesting the gut microbiome may be more transmissible and dynamic than previously thought.

stories.title: Man hid inside a Roman storage jar 1,600 years ago; archaeologists uncover his final moments
stories.summary: Archaeologists have unearthed the skeletal remains of a man tucked inside a massive Roman storage jar, offering a chilling glimpse into the past. It appears he sought refuge from a violent raid, as evidenced by the surrounding destruction and signs of fire. Two iron knives discovered alongside him imply a desperate act of self-defense. This city's fate remained enigmatic for an astonishing sixteen centuries before it was eventually rebuilt.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Bruce Lee: "If you always put limits on everything you do, physical or anything else, it will…"
PM Modi holds four-hour review meeting with 20 ministers on governance, welfare
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a four-hour review meeting with ministers. He focused on key government initiatives and their implementation on the ground. Ministers presented progress reports on their respective departmental work. Actionable ideas were sought for a developed India vision by 2047. PM Modi stressed digital engagement and plans more such sessions.

stories.title: 'Rumours of mobile jammers at Satya Niketan site false': Delhi Police reacts to AAP's allegations
Former mayor Giuliani says Mamdani should skip New York’s 9/11 memorial ceremony

Indian envoy meets Bangladesh president, stresses strengthening 'deep-rooted' ties
Why is N3on becoming an AI streamer? Kick star defends controversial never-ending livestream
stories.summary: On September 7, 2026, Kick streamer N3on unveiled a groundbreaking AI streaming initiative that aims to make him the first AI streamer with an uninterrupted broadcast. This pioneering project is designed to operate continuously, even when N3on is offline. He positions this venture as an exciting evolution in content creation while reassuring fans that his traditional streaming will persist alongside this new experiment.

stories.title: SC to consider Satya Niketan case transfer from Delhi HC over PG building collapse
stories.summary: A bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan was hearing a plea seeking urgent intervention after the building housing a boys' paying guest accommodation collapsed near Delhi University's South Campus. Seven students were killed and five others were injured. The court noted that the Delhi high court was already dealing with the incident but said the issues raised appeared to overlap with a broader case before the Supreme Court

stories.title: TN Assembly passes resolution urging Centre to use official OBC names in 2027 Census
stories.summary: The resolution covers Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Denotified Communities listed by the Tamil Nadu and Union governments. It also calls for these official lists to be built into the census portal so that people can select their caste from a fixed list rather than enter names themselves. The resolution said caste details should be collected for these communities in the same manner as data for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

stories.title: New York is building a bridge with recycled glass: $21.2 million project to divert 106 tons of glass from landfills and prevent over 72 tons of CO2 emissions
stories.summary: A New York bridge initiative is making headlines by incorporating recycled glass into its concrete mix. This project effectively diverts waste glass from landfills, significantly cutting down on carbon emissions. By transforming unwanted glass into a sustainable alternative for cement, this pilot demonstrates forward-thinking in construction materials. The expected completion of the project, including accompanying sidewalks, is slated for late 2026.

stories.title: Why Harry and Meghan were caught off guard by King Charles’ latest letter
stories.summary: King Charles III has clarified Prince Harry and Meghan's status as private citizens. The royal family confirmed they remain non-working members, which was previously agreed. This clarification came shortly before a letter was sent to senior officials. Harry and Meghan continue their commercial and charitable work in their private capacity. Their security arrangements remain a separate and ongoing discussion.

Shakespeare’s Globe to replace 30-year-old roof with 14,000 reed bundles in £10m project
stories.summary: Shakespeare’s Globe in London is set for a major roof replacement nearly 30 years after the reconstructed theatre opened. The £10 million project will use traditional thatching and around 14,000 bundles of reed instead of modern roofing materials. The Globe’s original roof used 6,000 bundles of Norfolk reeds. The project comes as traditional thatching in England faces challenges including poor harvests, old machinery and uncertain seasonal labour supplies.

stories.title: She built a 12-by-12-foot cabin with no electricity or road: The woman who chose to live alone in the Adirondack wilderness
stories.summary: Anne LaBastille, an iconic figure in wilderness living, constructed a secluded cabin in the Adirondack wilderness, eschewing all modern perks. Her life there was immortalized in her famous 'Woodswoman' memoir series, capturing the essence of nature. Later, her beloved property was turned over to New York State for conservation, now part of the Forest Preserve, showcasing her lasting impact in inspiring nature lovers and protecting the great outdoors.

stories.title: 'Why bring BJP into this?' Rijiju slams Rahul for targeting Shah over Manipuri musician's murder
Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky: "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and…"
Over 100 eagle rays gather off Malta in largest aggregation ever recorded
Satya Niketan tragedy: ABVP seeks PG safety audit, MCD chief’s suspension
PM Modi-Putin talks: 5th gen Su-57s, nuclear power plants & US sanctions on agenda
'Turned quiet life into chaos': Virginia man sues Amazon over data centre
IISc’s FSID appoints first industry leader as CEO under new model
stories.summary: The Indian Institute of Science's FSID has appointed Omprakash Subbarao as its new CEO, signaling a pivotal transition to an industry-driven governance structure. With aspirations to evolve into a self-sustaining entity, FSID aims to spur innovation and incubation by undertaking a thousand industry initiatives and fostering three hundred deep-tech startups, while enhancing collaboration with corporations and MSMEs for tangible outcomes.

stories.title: Japan’s floating solar farm faced Typhoon Faxai; modules broke loose and 50 panels caught fire
stories.summary: In 2019, a severe typhoon struck Japan's largest floating solar farm, leaving it heavily damaged. This event highlighted the engineering flaws present in floating solar structures when confronted with extreme weather. Investigators identified anchor failures as the main factor contributing to the significant damage. In response, the project was restructured into smaller, more resilient floating modules. Now, it serves as a reference for enhancing solar technology's storm resilience.

stories.title: Bengaluru start up gets US patent for its satellite imaging tech
Dubai teen built AI platform for breast cancer after losing grandmother at 10; took cancer awareness to India
stories.summary: Saiyette Aima’s journey began with her grandmother’s battle against breast cancer, driving her to make a significant impact. She spearheaded community-oriented fundraising and awareness campaigns, which flourished with local backing. Following this, Aima launched Pink for Purpose and started a YouTube channel to enhance her outreach. Her mission extended to India, providing free screening camps, which culminated in the innovative CareCheck, an AI tool for guiding breast health decisions.

stories.title: Another French museum heist: Thieves steal 4 paintings worth Rs 93 cr from Renoir museum; drop one while fleeing
ED detects Rs 60 crore ‘irregularities’ after 24-hour search at TMC MP Nadimul Haque’s premises
As 9/11 attacks collapsed his office, a blind man's guide dog helped him down 78 flights to safety
stories.summary: During the harrowing 9/11 attacks, Michael Hingson's guide dog, Roselle, became his lifeline, leading him down seventy-eight floors from the north tower. Together with his colleague David Frank, they managed to escape the crumbling World Trade Center amid chaos. While firefighters bravely climbed upward, Hingson and Frank made their way to safety. In the aftermath, Hingson found solace through sharing their powerful story of trust and collaboration.

stories.title: Mozart's melodies were less predictable, teen finds
stories.summary: Eighteen-year-old Linus Chen-Plotkin from Philadelphia has created a groundbreaking study on the genius of Mozart. Using statistical tests to evaluate melody predictability, he found that Mozart's music demonstrated significantly lower predictability than that of his contemporaries. This unique characteristic allowed him to both adhere to classical standards and surprise his audience, offering fresh insights into the nature of musical innovation and the essence of artistic excellence.

stories.title: Meet Celine Zhang, 18, who can prove puzzles without revealing answers
'Some can never be happy with India's progress': PM Modi renews 'naraz fufa' jibe at Congress in Vadodara
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated development projects worth over thirty-five thousand crore rupees in Vadodara. He highlighted the successful completion of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor sections connecting key industrial hubs. The Prime Minister also criticised previous governments for significant delays in executing the freight corridor project and emphasised the transformation in the nation's work culture and logistics system since 2014.

'Character assassination must stop': Kangana slams targeting of Tamil Nadu actress 'for her relations'
'To stop love jihad': Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane backs VHP's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events
Mississippi teen who wrote an autism book for her sister finishes second at Miss America’s Teen
stories.summary: Mississippi teen Madalyn Sullivan has finished as first runner-up at Miss America’s Teen after representing her state at the national competition. An Oxford High School student, Sullivan founded Millie’s Mission, an initiative inspired by her sister’s autism diagnosis. She also co-authored the children’s book “Meet Millie” and donated copies to public libraries across all 82 Mississippi counties.

stories.title: Phase Three Expansion: Broad Metro buys final 65 acres for $4.6 million; city backs $200m plan
stories.summary: Broad Metro LLC has successfully acquired sixty-five acres to launch the third phase of Stadium Trace Village. This ambitious expansion will feature a blend of retail spaces, medical facilities, and professional offices, alongside luxury residential options in the upper sections. The Hoover City Council has endorsed this initiative by approving an economic development agreement, marking a pivotal advancement in the long-term growth strategy of the project.

stories.title: Lightning Damages Mansion Turret: Fire chars historic Maple Street landmark; store below stays open
stories.summary: A dramatic lightning strike set the turret of a historic mansion in Georgia ablaze on Saturday night. Firefighters successfully contained the fire to the upper exterior, limiting its impact. The steeple and balcony suffered considerable damage, but thankfully, the business within the mansion emerged largely unscathed. Exterior repairs are scheduled as operations at the store proceed with minimal disruption.

Dam Removal Reopens Habitat: Virginia project reconnects 127 miles; migratory fish return upstream
stories.summary: In 2014, the removal of Harvell Dam revitalized over 120 miles of river, providing essential upstream habitats for migratory fish. Observations from state biologists and anglers confirmed fish migrating upstream post-demolition. This collaborative restoration project united various agencies and organizations, successfully restoring the river's free-flowing state and enhancing benefits for both aquatic life and recreational activities.

stories.title: Six people buried in a rare Viking Age grave reveal violence, family ties, and Baltic ancestry
stories.summary: A rare ninth-century burial in Latvia revealed violence and family connections. Ancient DNA showed father and son relationships among the six individuals. Three men bore sharp-force injuries, suggesting a violent incident occurred. Genetic analysis placed the group closer to local Baltic populations. This unusual grave offers insights into Viking Age Semigallian life and kinship.

stories.title: Punjab minister Arora meets UAEIIC secretary general, pitches state as next investment hotspot for UAE capital
stories.summary: During the meeting, the Industries Minister discussed with Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi Punjab’s vast economic potential and invited UAE investors to tap into high-growth sectors through government, semi-government and private sector partnerships.

stories.title: Suborno Bari: The young maths prodigy who caught Barack Obama’s attention
stories.summary: Suborno Isaac Bari, a 12-year-old student, graduated high school after skipping several grades. He began attending university-level classes and lecturing in India at age seven. Bari entered New York University with plans to complete his degree by age 14. His parents, both educators, inspired his ambition to teach mathematics and physics. He also pursued interests in debate, painting, and playing the piano.

Delhi building collapse: SC appointed amicus curiae seeks safety audit of PGs, hostels across capital
Yemen conflict widens: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi airport, air base and Aramco sites
In 1895, lightning ignited a West Virginia gas well; flames soared 200 feet as crowds watched
stories.summary: In a remarkable display, a West Virginia gas well suffered a fiery explosion triggered by a lightning strike. Discovered in 1895, this vast gas reservoir was tough to control with the limited technology of the era. For two hours, flames leaped 150 to 200 feet into the sky until the force of the escaping gas extinguished itself.

Iran doubles petrol price for heavy users as currency touches record low
stories.summary: Iran has recently increased its petrol price for consumers who surpass a monthly limit of 110 litres. This price hike is intended to boost government revenue, which officials assure will be allocated to support households. Amid ongoing inflation and a declining national currency, experts caution that this rise in fuel costs could exacerbate the existing financial strain on everyday citizens.

Canada released 26 bison into Banff in 2017; 9 years later, the herd has grown rapidly
stories.summary: Parks Canada successfully reintroduced plains bison into Banff National Park starting in 2017. The population grew from sixteen animals to about eighty by autumn 2022. Monitoring showed bison adapted to mountain habitat, preferring higher elevations for forage. Natural mortality remained low, with only two deaths recorded during the pilot. The five-year program achieved a 33% average annual population growth rate.

stories.title: Streamers Debate Emotions And Pain: IShowSpeed insists on nerve signals; Jasontheween says he feels pain daily
stories.summary: IShowSpeed and Jasontheween went viral after a surprising debate about emotions and pain during Jasontheween’s 72-hour collaboration video. Speed argued that emotions involve nerve signals and later suggested that pain is the brain processing physical signals at the atomic level. Jasontheween strongly disagreed with his unusual explanation. Their playful yet heated exchange quickly spread across social media, drawing attention from fans amused by their contrasting views.

Lindsay Clancy Mistrial: Hasan Piker rejects Polymarket ‘support’ claim; says stance miscast
stories.summary: Hasan Piker has denied Polymarket’s claim that he supports Lindsay Clancy, calling the wording a false description of his views. He has discussed Clancy’s postpartum psychosis defense, questioned her criminal responsibility and rejected theories blaming her husband. The case remains unresolved after a mistrial in Massachusetts, with prosecutors yet to decide whether Clancy will face another trial in the case.

Streamer Backlash Over Crash Photo: Kick’s Binx slammed for Miami plane stunt; legal fallout eyed
stories.summary: Kick streamer Binx is facing criticism after footage appeared to show her posing near the wreckage of an Amazon cargo plane that killed five people in Miami. The crash happened on September 6 after the Boeing 767-300 overran the runway and struck vehicles. Authorities are investigating the cause, while it remains unclear whether Binx could face any legal action over her access to the site.

Overdue Book Finally Returned: 1943 San Antonio loan arrives from Oregon; no late fee owed
stories.summary: After 82 years, a library book borrowed in 1943 was finally returned in Oregon, revealing a heartfelt letter detailing its extensive journey. The family inquired about overdue fees, but fortunately, the library had abolished such fines in 2021. The book, still in excellent condition, was briefly showcased before being put up for sale.

In 1876, Jesse James’s gang tried to rob a Minnesota bank for seven minutes; 150 years later...
stories.summary: In a dramatic seven-minute standoff in Northfield, Minnesota, local citizens bravely confronted the notorious James-Younger Gang during a bank heist, ultimately leading to the gang's capture. Today, the Northfield Historical Society preserves fascinating artifacts, including an outlaw's duster and even a mummified ear from that fateful day. The town now honors this brave moment in history with a lively annual festival.

Scientists tagged 14,000 endangered moths with paint and glue; none turned up, and that may be good news
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, researchers have tagged over 14,000 Bogong moths in the Snowy Mountains of Australia. However, after extensive tracking efforts, none have been recaptured, suggesting potential populations larger than previously assumed. Alternatively, these moths might be utilizing undiscovered migration routes. The ongoing project remains crucial for understanding the ecology of these endangered insects.

At 16, an Indiana girl earned 5 cents a day working at a café; her family later bought it
stories.summary: South Bend's Sunny Italy Cafe, established in 1926, is celebrating its centennial anniversary. This historic eatery has remained under family ownership for a full century. The restaurant is renowned for its authentic, scratch-made Italian dishes and traditional recipes. Generations of Notre Dame students and local residents have frequented the establishment. Its enduring legacy highlights a unique culinary tradition in the community.

stories.title: 67-year-old Colombian woman makes money selling neighbourhood gossip; she carries a notebook, collects evidence, also takes payment to keep her mouth shut
Rural area LPG booking period reduced from 45 to 25 days
In 1952, Mary Tsingou programmed a Los Alamos experiment that helped change modern physics
stories.summary: In the 1950s, Mary Tsingou Menzel played a pivotal role in solving a complex physics problem using one of the earliest computers. Initially recognized only in a footnote for her computational work, her contributions to the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam problem have since gained fitting recognition. A true trailblazer in computational physics, she worked silently yet effectively in the realm of national security science.

What happened to Kal Dosanjh, Vancouver cop arrested for alleged fraud? His boss says, 'This officer had a profile in the community and internally, and officers are angry and disappointed'
An Australian woman learned she was pregnant and could give birth ‘any day’ within 24 hours
stories.summary: An Australian mother was shocked to find out she was pregnant just days before giving birth to a very premature baby. Her daughter, Makerita Tanuvasa, entered the world at just 21 weeks and three days, weighing only 351 grams. Remarkably, she became Australia’s most premature surviving infant. After more than four months in intensive care, receiving specialized treatment, she finally returned home, marking a miraculous recovery.

‘Will reduce UP to Orwellian Dystopia’: Allahabad HC raps Noida DM over student’s NSA detention
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court quashed the National Security Act detention of Akriti Chaudhary. The court ordered recovery of five lakh rupees from Gautam Buddha Nagar officials. This compensation will be paid to the Delhi University student activist. The bench criticized the arbitrary invocation of the stringent preventive detention law. Officials' conduct was noted in their service records for their actions.

Fake encounter case: Allahabad HC seeks UP, Rajasthan Police reports over conflicting arrest versions
Scientists covered 200 square metres of a Swiss glacier with sheep’s wool; early tests found...
stories.summary: In an innovative approach, Swiss researchers are experimenting with natural wool blankets to mitigate glacier melting. These eco-friendly coverings have shown results comparable to synthetic options during trials. The initiative makes use of discarded sheep's wool, an agricultural byproduct. Although effective in localized regions, it's important to note that this technique alone won't reverse global warming—tackling greenhouse gas emissions is essential for the long-term preservation of glaciers.

stories.title: Lucknow tops clean air survey 2026 for taking air pollution control measures, none of the big metros met the acceptable limit of PM10 levels in 2025-26
Five Wilderness Bound Features: Mojang details camping-focused update; autumn aesthetic and builds
stories.summary: Mojang's Wilderness Bound update will bring players to a new autumn biome. This update introduces abandoned camps and valuable loot for explorers. Straw beds will allow players to skip nights without changing their spawn point. New furniture, including cushions, will enhance building and roleplaying experiences. Concrete and wool stairs and slabs will offer more architectural options.
